8Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
9 “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked. 10“You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere. 11Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
12The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.”
Then Satan left.
Job Loses Everything
13Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son, 14when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass, 15a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
16That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
17Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
18That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son, 19when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
20When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God 21 and said:
“We bring nothing at birth;
we take nothing
with us at death.
The Lord alone gives and takes.
Praise the name of the Lord!”
22In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_text:
Seetan sɔ Dwobu anlea
1Ɛnee nrenya bie wɔ Ɛɛze maanle nu. Bɛfɛlɛ ye Dwobu. Nrenya ɛhye anwo ɛnlɛ dɛne biala yɛɛ ɔle sonla fɔɔnwo, ɔdi nɔhalɛ ɔmaa Nyamenle, yɛɛ ɔkyi ɛtane. 2Ɔwole mralɛ mrenya nsuu yɛɛ mraalɛ nsa. 3Ɔlɛ mboane apenle nsuu, afunlumu apenle nsa, nlankɛ apenle ko, asoaso ɛya nnu, yɛɛ sonvolɛma dɔɔnwo; nrenya ɛhye le sukoavolɛ kpole tɛla awie biala mɔɔ wɔ Aduduleɛ la.
4Ɔ mra ne mɔ to ɛkponle bɛ ti ngoko. Saa ko biala mekɛ ɛdeɛ ne dwu a, ɔto ɛkponle na ɔfɛlɛvɛlɛ ɔ mediema mrenya ne mɔ nee bɛ mediema mraalɛ ne mɔ na bɛ nee bɛ di, no, dielie bɛ nye. 5Saa bɛto ɛkponle ne toonwo na ɔyia bɛ ti a, Dwobu fɛlɛ bɛ na ɔnua bɛ. Ɔdwazo aleɛbahye na ɔbɔ bɛ ti ngoko ɔfa nane ɔyela ɔbɔ azu, ɔluakɛ Dwobu edwɛkɛ a le kɛ, “Wɔannea a ɛnee me mra ne mɔ ɛyɛ ɛtane wɔ bɛ ahonle nu na bɛdendɛ ɛtane bɛtia Nyamenle.” Dwobu yɛle ɛhye mekɛ biala.
6 Kenle ko Nyamenle anzɛɛ Anwuma amra hɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu kɛ bɛkava bɛ nwo bɛahile ye, na Seetan ɔdaye ɔhɔle ɛkɛ ne bie. 7Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale Seetan kɛ, “Na ɛvi nienwu yɛɛ wɔra ɛke a?”
Seetan buale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Mewɔ akpɔsa nu wɔ aleɛabo. Ewiade anu ala yɛɛ medi ye akɔneaba a.”
8Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Seetan kɛ, “Wɔnwu me sonvolɛ Dwobu, awie biala mɔɔ le kɛ ɔdaye la ɛnle aleɛabo, ɛtane biala ɛnle ɔ nwo yɛɛ ɔdi nɔhalɛ. Ɔsulo Nyamenle yɛɛ ɔtwe ɔ nwo ɔfi ɛtane nwo.”
9 Seetan buale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Na mgbane ala yɛɛ Dwobu sulo Nyamenle a? 10Wɔbɔ ɔdaye, ɔ mra nee debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la anwo bane. Dahuu ɛsinza ye, ye abusua ne nee debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la. Wɔyila ɔ sa anloa gyima zo yɛɛ dahuu ye anwonyia ne, kpole ala a ɔyɛ a. 11Saa ɛkulo a die debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la fi ɔ sa nu na ɛkɛde mgbole mɔɔ ɔkɛheha ɔkɛtietia wɔ la.”
12Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Seetan kɛ, “Nea, debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la wɔ ɛ sa nu, noko mmafa ɛ sa ɛka Dwobu ɛleka biala fee.” Akee Seetan vi Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu ɛkɛ ne hɔle.
Dwobu amra nee ye anwonyia ɛzɛkye
13Kenle ko mɔɔ Dwobu amra ne mɔ, mrenya nee mraalɛ yiale ralɛ nrenya kpanyinli ne sua nu na bɛlɛdi, bɛno nwanye la, 14ɛbɔfoɔ rale Dwobu ɛkɛ razele ye kɛ, “Mɔɔ nlankɛ ne mɔ ɛlɛfundu azɛlɛ ne na asoaso ne mɔ noko ɛlɛdidi bɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne la, 15arɛlevilɛ nu ala, Sabima ralile yɛ nvunu hyehyele nlankɛ ne mɔ na bɛhunle sonvolɛma ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti. Me ngomekye ala a meha mɔɔ menriandi mera mebabɔ wɔ amaneɛ a.”
16Mɔɔ ɔ nloa wɔ zolɛ ɔlɛtendɛ la, ɛbɔfoɔ fofolɛ vindele ɛkɛ razele ye kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛkpakye ɛsɛnlɛmanye ɛhu mboane ne nee sonvolɛma ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti na yeyela bɛ wee. Me ngomekye ala a mevi nu mɔɔ mera mebabɔ wɔ amaneɛ a.”
17Ɔ nloa ampe ɛnee ɛbɔfoɔ bieko anyunlu ɛne. Ɔse, “Kaledima ɛhyɛ bɛ nu ekpunli nsa ɛrali yɛ nvunu, ɛhye afunlumu ne mɔ amuala ɛhɔ, na bɛhu sonvolɛma ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti. Me ngomekye ala a meha mɔɔ mera mebabɔ wɔ amaneɛ a.”
18Mɔɔ ɔ nloa wɔ zolɛ ɔlɛtendɛ la, ɛbɔfoɔ bieko vindele ɛkɛ razele ye kɛ, “Ɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ ne mɔ wɔ bɛ diema nrenya kpanyinli ne sua nu, bɛlɛdi, bɛno nwanye. 19Na nea, ahumu kpole bie vi fienemgbole ne anu lɔ ɛdu ɛrabu sua ne ɛgua bɛ nwo zo, ɛhu bɛ muala. Me ngomekye ala a mevi nu mɔɔ mera mebabɔ wɔ amaneɛ a.”
20Akee Dwobu dwazole, ɔsuosuanle tɛladeɛ mɔɔ ɔwula la anu, ɔkpale ɔ ti, ɔdule ɔdɔle aze na ɔyeyɛle Nyamenle. 21Ɔse, “Meanva bie meamba na mekɔ a meava bie meahɔ. Ɛdɛnkɛma a vale manle me a, yɛɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛlie ye debie a. Ayɛlɛyelɛ ɛha Ɛdɛnkɛma duma ne.”
22Anwubɛnyunlu ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti anu, Dwobu anyɛ ɛtane biala yɛɛ yeanvu Nyamenle.

english_text:
Job Loses His Health
1When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them, 2and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
3Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
4Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive. 5Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
6“All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.” 7Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
8Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery, 9his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
10Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God.
Job's Three Friends
11Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him. 12When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly. 13For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_text:
Seetan sɔ Dwobu anlea bieko
1Kenle ko eza Nyamenle anzɛɛ Anwuma amra hɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu kɛ bɛkava bɛ nwo bɛahile ye, na Seetan eza hɔle ɛkɛ ne bie.
2Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale Seetan kɛ, “Na wɔmɔ, ɛvi nienwu yɛɛ wɔra ɛke a?”
Seetan buale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Mewɔ akpɔsa nu wɔ aleɛabo. Ewiade anu ala yɛɛ medi ye akɔneaba a.”
3Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Seetan kɛ, “Wɔnwu me sonvolɛ Dwobu, awie biala mɔɔ le kɛ ɔdaye la ɛnle aleɛabo, ɛtane biala ɛnle ɔ nwo, ɔdi nɔhalɛ, ɔsulo Nyamenle na ɔtwe ɔ nwo ɔfi ɛtane nwo. Wɔyɛ anrɛɛ ɛmaa meazɛkye ye, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔtɛyɛle ɛhwee la, noko wɔnwu ye wienyi kɛ Dwobu gyi ɔ gyakɛ anu kpundii.”
4Na Seetan buale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Ɔle zɔhane, na ye nwonane ne noko ɛ! Sonla kɛhulo kɛ ɔkɛdɛnla ngoane nu tɛla kɛ ɔkɛminli anwonyia biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la. 5Wɔmɔ, ɛkulo a fa ɛ sa ka ye maa ɔde nyane ekyii, na ɛkɛde mgbole mɔɔ ɔkɛheha ɔkɛtietia wɔ la.”
6Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Seetan kɛ, “Ɔwɔ ɛ sa nu, na anrɛɛ mmafa ɛ sa ɛka ye ngoane ne.”
7Yemɔti Seetan vi Ɛdɛnkɛma anwo ɛkɛ ne hɔle na ɔhɔdele nganlɛ mgbole ɔkpondenle Dwobu anwo. Ɔvi ɔ ti zo mɔɔ dwu ɔ gyakɛ akunlu la yɛle nganlɛ ngome. 8Dwobu hɔdɛnlanle fovolɛ zo yɛɛ ɔfa foandɛkɛ ɔfonvoa ɔ nwo a. 9Na ɔ ye zele ye kɛ, “Ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala ɛtɛgyi ɛ gyakɛ anu, ɛtɛtoa Nyamenle abo zo. Tendɛ ɛtane tia Nyamenle na wu ɛ.”
10Dwobu buale ye kɛ, “Ɛtendɛ kɛ mraalɛ ahɔnwɔne ne mɔ anu ko tendɛ la. Saa Nyamenle kyɛ yɛ ninyɛne kpalɛ a, yemɔ yɛdie. Na saa anwubɛnyunlu to yɛ a, ɛnee duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ yɛkpo ye amunli a?” Wɔ amaneɛnwunlɛ ɛhye mɔ amuala anu Dwobu anloa anvula edwɛkɛ ɛtane antia Nyamenle.
Dwobu agɔnwo mɔ ba
11Mekɛ mɔɔ Dwobu agɔnwo mɔ nsa ne, Ɛlaefaze mɔɔ vi suakpole Tima, Beledade mɔɔ vi Hyua maanle nu, yɛɛ Zofaa mɔɔ vi Neeyama maanle nu la dele ye anwubɛnyunlu ne nganeɛ la, bɛhɛlɛhɛlale bɛ nwo na bɛhilele kenle bɛrale kɛ bɛbakpɔla ye, bɛayɛ ye gyakɔ na bɛakyekye ɔ rɛle. 12Mɔɔ bɛlua adenle zo moa ekyii na bɛnwunle Dwobu la, bɛannwu ye sonla holɛ. Na bɛradole ye la, bɛzunle bɛyele awolɛ. Bɛsuosuanle bɛ adɛladeɛ mɔɔ bɛwula la anu, bɛvale nzonle bɛbɔle bɛ nwo na bɛlile nyane. 13Bɛkpofokpofole azɛlɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne bɛ nee ye dɛnlanle ewiazo nee nɔɔzo toonwo kenle nsuu. Bɛ biala ambuke ɔ nloa anga edwɛkɛkpɔkɛ ko bɔbɔ, ɔboalekɛ bɛnwunle kɛ ɛnee ɔlɛnwu amaneɛ kpole.

english_text:
Job's First Speech
Blot Out the Day of My Birth
1 Finally, Job cursed the day
of his birth
2by saying to God:
3Blot out the day of my birth
and the night when my parents
created a son.
4Forget about that day,
cover it with darkness,
5and send thick, gloomy shadows
to fill it with dread.
6Erase that night from the calendar
and conceal it with darkness.
7Don't let children be created
or joyful shouts be heard
ever again in that night.
8Let those with magic powers
place a curse on that day.
9Darken its morning stars
and remove all hope of light,
10because it let me be born
into a world of trouble.
Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
11Why didn't I die at birth?
12Why was I accepted
and allowed to nurse
at my mother's breast?
13Now I would be at peace
in the silent world below
14with kings and their advisors
whose palaces lie in ruins,
15and with rulers once rich
with silver and gold.
16I wish I had been born dead
and then buried, never to see
the light of day.
17In the world of the dead,
the wicked and the weary rest
without a worry.
* 18Everyone is there—
19where captives and slaves
are free at last.
Why Does God Let Me Live?
20Why does God let me live
when life is miserable
and so bitter?
21 I keep longing for death
more than I would seek
a valuable treasure.
22Nothing could make me happier
than to be in the grave.
23Why do I go on living
when God has me surrounded,
and I can't see the road?
24Moaning and groaning
are my food and drink,
25and my worst fears
have all come true.
26I have no peace or rest—
only troubles and worries.
translation_text:
Dwobu ka ye nyane edwɛkɛ ahile Nyamenle
1 Nzinlii Dwobu bukele ɔ nloa na ɔwale kenle ko ne mɔɔ bɛwole ye la amonle.
Dwobu
2Dwobu hanle kɛ,
3“O Nyamenle, maa abule ɛbu kenle ko ne mɔɔ bɛwole me la;
abule ɛbu nɔe ne mɔɔ bɛnrenzɛle me ralɛ nrenya la!
4Nyamenle, maa awozinli ɛva kenle zɔhane.
Mmakakye kenle zɔhane bieko ɛlɛ;
mmamaa wienyi ta kenle zɔhane anu ɛlɛ.
5Maa awozinli kabii nee awozinli mindomindo ɛva ye.
Maa amungu ɛheda zo;
maa alehyenlɛ ne anu awozinli ɛha ɛzulolɛ.
6Nɔɔzo zɔhane, maa awozinli kabii ɛva ye!
Mmamaa bɛtia ye bɛboka ɛvolɛ ne anu kenle ne mɔ anwo,
mmamaa bɛtia ye bɛboka siane ne mɔ anwo.
7Maa nɔɔzo zɔhane ɛyɛ diinyi,
mmamaa bɛte anyelielɛ ɛnelɛ biala.
8Maa amowama ɛbɔ kenle ne sasa, ɛwa ye amonle;
bɛmɛ yɛɛ bɛze kɛ bɛsi bɛmaa nyevizonle maa ɔ nwo zo a.
9Mmamaa ye aleɛbahye nwɔlɔra ne mɔ ta;
mmamaa nɔɔzo zɔhane mangyee si.
10Ɔluakɛ yeando ɔmɔ awodeɛ ne anu,
na ɔyele me ɔmanle nyanenwunlɛ.
11“Me kunlu a anrɛɛ menwule ɔmɔ akunlu,
anzɛɛ bɛwole me ala la mengale nzule nu.
12Duzu ati a ɔmɔ dedɛle me ɔ gyakɛ azo a?
Duzu ati a ɔmanle me nyɛfonlɛ a?
13Saa menwule a, anrɛɛ mela melie me menle koonwu;
anrɛɛ mela melie me menle bie
14kɛ ewiade arelemgbunli nee nrɛlɛbɛvoma
mɔɔ kyekyele awuke mgbole manle bɛ nwo la.
15Anrɛɛ mela kɛ arelemgbunli mralɛ mrenya
mɔɔ vale ezukoa nvutuke nee dwɛtɛ fufule yile bɛ azua
la.
16Anrɛɛ ɔmɔ ako kpɔnenle, na meanyɛ sonla,
anzɛɛ kɛ adɔma mɔɔ wule ɔ nli akunlu.
17Funli kuma nu yɛɛ amumuyɛma gyakyi ninyɛndane,
na menli mɔɔ ɛvɛ la nyia ɛnwomenlelielɛ a.
18Ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ menli mɔɔ gua efiade la anwo tɔ bɛ,
na bɛnde kpoyokpoyo bieko a.
19Mgbolema nee ahoahweabane wɔ ɛkɛ,
na kanranli nyia ɔ ti fi ɔ menle asa anu.
20“Duzu ati a ɛmaa menli mɔɔ de anwunvɔne nu la nwu wienyi a?
Duzu ati a ɛmaa menli mɔɔ te nyane la ngoane ɛ?
21 Bɛ nwo dɔ ewule, noko ewule ɛmba;
bɛkpondɛ ewule bɛtɛla anwonyia biala.
22Kenle mɔɔ bɛkɛwu na bɛkɛzie bɛ la,
ɛnee bɛ nye ɛlie.
23Duzu ati a sonla mɔɔ ɛnze ye kenlebie la,
Nyamenle ɛbɔ ɔ nwo bane a?
24Me aleɛ a le me ɛzunlɛ,
yɛɛ me nzule a le me ɛkponlenlɛ.
25Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ mesulo ye la ɛra me nwo zo,
yɛɛ mɔɔ tu me ahonle la ɛdo me.
26Menlɛ anzonudwolɛ, yɛɛ ɛdendɛlɛ ɛdɔ me nwo;
menlɛ ɛnwomenlelielɛ, yɛɛ me anwubɛnyunlu ɛnlɛ awieleɛ.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's First Speech
Please Be Patient and Listen
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2Please be patient and listen
to what I have to say.
* 3Remember how your words
4have guided and encouraged
many in need.
5But now you feel discouraged
when struck by trouble.
6You respect God and live right,
so don't lose hope!
7No truly innocent person
has ever died young.
8In my experience, only those
who plant seeds of evil
harvest trouble,
9and then they are swept away
by the angry breath of God.
10They may roar and growl
like powerful lions.
But when God breaks their teeth,
11they starve, and their children
are scattered.
A Secret Was Told to Me
12A secret was told to me
in a faint whisper—
13 I was overcome by sleep,
but disturbed by dreams;
14I trembled with fear,
15and my hair stood on end,
as a wind blew past my face.
16It stopped and stood still.
Then a form appeared—
a shapeless form.
And from the silence,
I heard a voice say,
17“No humans are innocent
in the eyes of God
their Creator.
18He finds fault with his servants
and even with his angels.
19Humans are formed from clay
and are fragile as moths,
so what chance do you have?
20Born after daybreak,
you die before nightfall
and disappear forever.
21Your tent pegs are pulled up,
and you leave this life,
having gained no wisdom.”
translation_text:
Alumua Adwelielilɛ ne
(4.1—14.22)
Ɛlaefaze
1Ɛlaefaze buale ye kɛ,
2“Dwobu, saa awie ka edwɛkɛ a ɛkɛva ɛya ɔ?
Sonla ɛnrɛhola ɛnrɛdɛnla ɛke koonwu zɛhae.
3Wɔhilehile menli dɔɔnwo
na wɔmaa menli mɔɔ ɛngola bɛ nwo la anwosesebɛ.
4Saa awie kpo aze, ɔ nwo golo ye na ɔfɛ a,
wɔ ɛdendɛlɛ maa ye akɛnrazilɛ maa ɔdwazo.
5Na kɛkala mɔɔ yedo wɔ la, ɛnnyia nwolɛ abotane;
yeha wɔ la, wɔ adwenle ɛbɔ nu.
6Wɔ Nyamenle ɛzulolɛ manle wɔ adwenle zile pi,
yɛɛ wɔ ndenle kpalɛ zo ɛvalɛ manle wɔ anyelazo.
7Dwenle nwo, nwane a ɛnze nwolɛ bie na ɔwule,
anzɛɛ nienwu yɛɛ bɛhunle tenlenema a?
8Mɔɔ meze la a le kɛ, menli mɔɔ so ninyɛndane ɛya,
na bɛdua amumuyɛ la bu munzule.
9Nyamenle ɛnwomenle ɛgulɛ ku bɛ,
na ye ɛya ne bɔ bɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ.
10Amumuyɛma kpo na bɛtea kɛ awenade,
na Nyamenle tudu bɛ gye na ɔmaa bɛyɛ koonwu.
11Bɛle kɛ awenade mɔɔ ɛnnyia debie ɛngu ɛnli,
bɛwu na bɛ mra ne mɔ bɔ asande.
12“Mekɛ bie ɛnelɛ bie hanle nrɛlaleɛ hilele me,
ɛnelɛ ne dule me azukue.
13 Ɔrale kɛ ɛlalɛ ɛzulolɛ bie,
mɔɔ menli ka wɔ bɛ nafelɛ nu la.
14Ɛzulolɛ hanle me, me nwo wozole me,
na me mbowule nu wozole.
15Debie pɛle me nye zo,
na me nwo bɔle me nyee.
16Deɛ ne gyinlanle koonwu,
na meannwu ye sɔhovolɛ;
ɛnee debie gyi me nyunlu ɛkɛ;
ɛkɛ ne yɛle diinyi,
akee mendele ɛnelɛ, ɔse:
17Asoo sonla kola yɛ tenlene tɛla Nyamenle
anzɛɛ ɔ nwo kɛde kɛdɛla ye Bɔvolɛ?
18Ye sonvolɛma bɔbɔ, ɔnlie bɛ ɔnli,
yɛɛ anwuma soanvolɛma bɔbɔ, ɔnyia bɛ nwo nvonleɛ.
19Na akee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvale ndɛtɛlɛ a bɛbɔle bɛ,
mɔɔ bɛvi ndɛtɛlɛ nu,
na bɛti bɛ kɛ ngɛkɛba la!
20Ɔvi nwonlomɔ kɔdwu aledwolɛ, bɛsɛkye bɛ,
bɛ bo zo minli bɔkɔɔ, awie ɛngakye bɛ.
21Saa bɛ ahonle nyɛma te a, ɛnee bɛwu,
bɛwu mɔɔ nrɛlɛbɛ biala ɛnle nu a.

english_text:
Eliphaz Continues
Call Out for Help
1Job, call out for help
and see if an angel comes!
2Envy and jealousy
will kill a stupid fool.
3I have seen fools take root.
But God sends a curse,
suddenly uprooting them
4and leaving their children
helpless in court.
5Then hungry and greedy people
gobble up their crops
and grab their wealth.
6Our suffering isn't caused
by the failure of crops;
7it's all part of life,
like sparks shooting skyward.
8Job, if I were you,
I would ask God for help.
9 His miracles are marvelous,
more than we can count.
10God sends showers on earth
and waters the fields.
11He protects the sorrowful
and lifts up those
who have been disgraced.
* 12God swiftly traps the wicked
13 in their own evil schemes,
and their wisdom fails.
14Darkness is their only companion,
hiding their path at noon.
15God rescues the needy
from the words of the wicked
and the fist of the mighty.
16The poor are filled with hope,
and injustice is silenced.
Consider Yourself Fortunate
17 Consider yourself fortunate
if God All-Powerful
chooses to correct you.
18 He may cause injury and pain,
but he will bandage and heal
your cuts and bruises.
19God will protect you from harm,
no matter how often
trouble may strike.
20In times of war and famine,
God will keep you safe.
21You will be sheltered,
without fear of hurtful words
or any other weapon.
22You will laugh at the threat
of destruction and famine.
And you won't be afraid
of wild animals—
23they will no longer be fierce,
and your rocky fields
will become friendly.
24Your home will be secure,
and your sheep will be safe.
25You will have more descendants
than there are blades of grass
on the face of the earth.
26You will live a very long life,
and your body will be strong
until the day you die.
27Our experience has proven
these things to be true,
so listen and learn.
translation_text:
1“Ɛkulo a fɛlɛ, saa ɛkɛnyia awie kɛlie wɔ zo a;
anwondelɛma ne mɔ boni yɛɛ ɛfa ɛ nye wɔado ɔ nwo zo a?
2Nɔhalɛ, ɛya ku koasea,
yɛɛ anyebolo ku kɔnwɔne.
3Menwu kɛ koasea ɛzɔ ndinli,
noko arɛlevilɛ nu, membɔle ye awuke ne sasa.
4Ɔ mra nee munzule avinli anwa,
bɛku bɛ wɔ anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa,
bɛnlɛ dievolɛ biala.
5Menli mɔɔ ɛhɔne ku bɛ la di bɛ bɛyɔba ne,
kanza bɛgua mbowule nu bɔbɔ a, bɛbu,
yɛɛ anyeboloma anye bolo bɛ anwonyia.
6Anwubɛnyunlu ɛnvi azɛlɛ nwo,
yɛɛ ngyegyelɛ ɛnfifi ndɛtɛlɛ nu.
7Bɛwo sonla bɛmaa ngyegyelɛ,
ɔle kɛ senle mɔɔ tudu kɔ anwuma la.
8“Saa medame a, anrɛɛ mebadoa Nyamenle abo zo,
na meava me edwɛkɛ meawula ɔ sa nu;
9yemɔ mɔɔ ɔyɛ ninyɛne mgbole, mɔɔ ɛnlɛ nvedenu,
ye nwanwane nyɛleɛ ɛnlɛ ɔ nloa.
10Ɔmaa ezule tɔ azɛlɛ ye azo
na ɔgugua nzule wɔ ɛbɔ ne mɔ azo.
11Ɔmaa bɛlɛvoma zo,
na ɔye nyanelilɛma ɔfi nyane nu.
12Ɔsɛkye agyibatovoma mɛlɛbɛla,
na ɔmaa bɛfua asakpane.
13 Ɔkye nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma wɔ bɛdabɛ bɛ agyibadolɛ nu,
na agyibadolɛma ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ pɛ sinli ndɛndɛ.
14Awozinli fa bɛ alehyenlɛ nu,
na bɛdi nvuovua ewiazo ketekete kɛ nɔɔzo.
15Ɔdie menli mɔɔ ɛhyia la ɔfi dadeɛ nloa,
na ɔdie bɛ ɔfi mgbolema asa anu.
16Yemɔti ehyianvolɛma lɛ anyelazo,
na menli mɔɔ ɛnli pɛlepɛle la ka bɛ nloa to nu.
17 “Nyilalɛ ɛha sonla ne mɔɔ Nyamenle twi ɔ nyunlu la,
yemɔti mmakpo Nyamenle Bɛdevinli ne ndeanlɛ.
18 Ɔluakɛ ɔbo wɔ a, ɔsia ɔdwu wɔ,
yɛɛ ɔtea wɔ a, ɔfa wɔ ɔbɔ ye ɛbolɛ.
19Ɔbaye wɔ yeavi ngyegyelɛ fane nsia anu,
nsuu ne azo, munzule biala ɛnrɛdo wɔ.
20Wɔ ɛhɔne nu, ɔbaye wɔ yeavi ewule nu;
wɔ konle nu, ɔbaye wɔ yeavi dadeɛ nloa.
21Ɔbaye wɔ yeavi dumanzɛkyelɛ nu,
yɛɛ saa ewule ba a ɛnrɛzulo.
22Ɛbazele ewule nee ɛhɔne,
yɛɛ ɛnrɛzulo aleɛabo nanemgbole biala.
23Ɔluakɛ ɛ nee ɛbɔ nu awolɛ mgbole bali ngitanwo,
na aleɛabo nanemgbole nee wɔ adɛnla anzonudwolɛ nu.
24Ɛbanwu kɛ anzonudwolɛ wɔ wɔ sua nu,
yɛɛ ɛnrɛminli debie biala wɔ wɔ mboane tunli nu.
25Eza ɛbanwu kɛ ɛ bo zo amra bada,
na ɛ kunlu mralɛ anyenle kɛ ɛbɔ nu ndile.
26Ɛbayɛ nwosonwoso kolaa na wɔawu,
kɛmɔ ɛlobɔ dwu na bɛava ma bɛahɔ ma ɛwozolɛ
ɛleka la.
27Nea, yɛvedevede ɛhye anu, na ɔle nɔhalɛ.
Yemɔti Dwobu, tie na die to nu.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
It's Impossible
1Job said:
2It's impossible to weigh
my misery and grief!
3They outweigh the sand
along the beach,
and that's why I have spoken
without thinking first.
4The fearsome arrows
of God All-Powerful
have filled my soul
with their poison.
5Do oxen and wild donkeys
cry out in distress
unless they are hungry?
6What is food without salt?
What is more tasteless
than the white of an egg?
7That's how my food tastes,
and my appetite is gone.
* 8How I wish that God
would answer my prayer
9and do away with me.
10Then I would be comforted,
knowing that in all of my pain
I have never disobeyed God.
11Why should I patiently hope
when my strength is gone?
12I am not strong as stone
or bronze,
13and I have finally reached
the end of my rope.
My Friends, I Am Desperate
14My friends, I am desperate,
and you should help me,
even if I no longer respect
God All-Powerful.
* 15But you are treacherous
16like streams that swell
with melting snow,
17then suddenly disappear
in the summer heat.
18I am like a caravan,
lost in the desert
while searching for water.
19Caravans from Tema and Sheba
20thought they would find water.
But they were disappointed,
21just as I am with you.
Only one look at my suffering,
and you run away scared.
What Have I Done Wrong?
22Have I ever asked any of you
to give me a gift
23or to purchase my freedom
from brutal enemies?
24What have I done wrong?
Show me,
and I will keep quiet.
25The truth is always painful,
but your arguments
prove nothing.
26Here I am desperate,
and you consider my words
as worthless as wind.
27Why, you would sell an orphan
or your own neighbor!
28Look me straight in the eye;
I won't lie to you.
29Stop accusing me falsely;
my reputation is at stake.
30I know right from wrong,
and I am not telling lies.
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Dwobu buale ye kɛ,
2“O, anrɛɛ bɛazuzu me nyane ne,
nee me amaneɛnwunlɛ ne wɔ tone zo!
3Anrɛɛ bɛkɛnwu kɛ ɔyɛ ɛnlomboɛ ɔtɛla ɛnweazo ɛnwea,
ɛhye ati a me mgbolehanlɛ ne ɛyɛ nwanwane a.
4Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne ɛda mbaka ne ɛwowɔ me,
na ye bɔlɔ ɛwie me wolowolo,
yɛɛ Nyamenle ɛya mgbole ne mɔ ɛra me nwo zo.
5“Asoo asoaso nyia ndile na ɔlɛdi a ɔsu,
anzɛɛ ɛnlankɛ gyi aleɛ nwo a ɔsu?
6Asoo aleɛ tatabɛ, bɛdi a ɔdi?
Asoo kolonvia aleɛ fufule ne yɛ fɛ?
7Me tiakunlu ɛmba zo bɔbɔ;
bɛle aleɛ mɔɔ ka me ya.
8“O, anrɛɛ meanyia mɔɔ mebiza la,
na Nyamenle akponle mɔɔ mekpondɛ la azo!
9Anrɛɛ ɛnee Nyamenle kɛhu me pɛneko,
na ɔkɛpɛ me ngoane zo.
10Anrɛɛ ɛhye bakyekye me rɛle;
na meali fɛlɛko wɔ me nyane nu,
ɔluakɛ metɛtule Nwuanzanwuanza Ko ne anloa.
11Duzu anwosesebɛ a melɛ, mefa mekendɛ a?
Yɛɛ kɛ menwɔwie ye mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ mesi abotane a?
12Ɛnee me anwosesebɛ le kɛ awolɛ ɔ?
Anzɛɛ me nwonane le kɔbele ɔ?
13Nɔhalɛ nu, menlɛ anwosesebɛ biala me nu,
yɛɛ menlɛ ɛleka mɔɔ moalɛ vi bara a.
14“Awie biala mɔɔ ɛnyɛ atiakunlukɛnlɛma la
ɛnzulo Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne.
15Me mediema ne mɔ le ngunzi;
bɛle kɛ azuboazɛlɛ mɔɔ azule se zo bobobobo,
16na ezukɔtweaba kɔfea nu
yɛ azule ne anye fii, kyengye ye.
17Wuluwulu melɛ nu bɛkolo,
na bɛ bo zo minliminli bɔkɔɔ.
18Adenduvoma di ɛkɛ ne akɔneaba
bɛkɔkpondɛ nzule ne toonwo bɛwu.
19Tima adenduvoma neɛnlea,
Hyiba adenduvoma anye da.
20Bɛ anyelazo bɔ bɛ, ɔboalekɛ ɛnee bɛdie bɛdi;
bɛkɛhɔdwu la, ɛnee nzule ne ɛsesa.
21Zɛhae yɛɛ bɛle bɛmaa me a;
bɛnwu me anwubɛnyunlu la, ɛzulolɛ ɛha bɛ.
22Meha kɛ bɛhyɛ me debie ɔ?
Anzɛɛ bɛva bɛ anwonyia ne bie bɛdua me ti ndoloboa ɔ?
23Meha kɛ bɛlie me bɛvi kpɔvolɛ ne asa anu ɔ?
Anzɛɛ bɛkpɔne me bɛvi nzisima asa anu ɔ?
24“Bɛhilehile me, na menwɔyɛ koonwu;
bɛmaa menwu ɛtane mɔɔ meyɛ la.
25Nɔhalɛ edwɛkɛ nu mia!
Na bɛ ndeanlɛ ye, duzu anwo ndeanlɛ ɔ?
26Ɛnee bɛdwenle kɛ bɛkola bɛtea edwɛkɛ ɔ,
wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ sonla mɔɔ ɛnlɛ anyelazo la
edwɛkɛ ɛhanlɛ le anwoma la?
27Bɛnyia arisa a, bɛkɛgua ɔ ti nzeleba,
na bɛkɛdɔne agɔnwolɛma.
28Na kɛkala, mebodo bɛ, bɛnlea me,
ɔluakɛ menrɛbɔ adalɛ wɔ bɛ nyunlu.
29Mebodo bɛ, bɛgyakyi, bɛmmabua me mgbɔvodɛne;
bɛgyakyi, na medi benle.
30Anzɛɛ meha ɛtane ɔ?
Menze kpalɛ menze ɛtane ɔ?

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
1“Sonla ɛbɛlabɔlɛ yɛ se wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo,
sonla mekɛ kɔsɔɔti le kɛ ɛkpanli.
2Ɔle kɛ kanranli mɔɔ kpondɛ alubo nu adɛnla,
ɔle kɛ ɛkpanli mɔɔ anye la ye ahatualɛ zo.
3Zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛhyehyɛ mekɛ mgbane
nee aledwolɛ anu nyane bɛmaa me a.
4Saa meda a mebiza kɛ,
‘Kenlenzu yɛɛ mebadwazo a?’
Aledwolɛ ne wale,
mekɔsɔ mekɔ, mekɔsɔ meba,
mepe toonwo alehyenlɛ.
5Melɔ azonlɛ, me nwo ɛzi bile,
me nwo nwoma di wulate.
6Me mekɛ se ndɛndɛ
tɛla ɛdanlɛnwovolɛ agbuyiaba,
na ɔba awieleɛ mɔɔ anyelazo ɛnle nu a.
7“Kakye kɛ me ngoane le anwoma;
me nye ɛnrɛnwu debie kpalɛ bieko.
8Ɛnyelɛ mɔɔ nwu me la ɛnrɛnwu me bieko;
mɔɔ bɛ nye dua me ala la, mebado ɛbɛla ne aze.
9Kɛmɔ amungu kpa na ɔpɛ nu ɔse la,
zɔhane ala yɛɛ mɔɔ kɔ Ɛbolɔ la ɛnzia ko a.
10Ɔnzia ɔmba ye awuke nu bieko,
yɛɛ ye awuke nu amra ɛnze ye ko.
11Yemɔti menrɛmua me nloa;
mebaha mɔɔ wɔ me kunlu la;
mebaha mɔɔ wɔ me ahonle nu la.
12“Mele nyevile, anzɛɛ nyevizonle,
mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛmaa me sinzavolɛ a?
13Saa meka kɛ, ‘Me ɛkpa bakyekye me rɛle,
me ebia mɔɔ meda nu la bamaa me anwofofolɛ aha aze’ a,
14ɛnee bɛfa ɛlalɛ bɛnwunlonwunla me,
na bɛfa ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ bɛka me ɛzulolɛ.
15Yemɔti menwɔhulo kɛ bɛkɛmia me kɔmenzia bɛkɛhu me
tɛla kɛ ɔkɛha me mbowule.
16Mekpo me ngoane; menrɛhakyi bolɛ.
Bɛgyakyi me, ɔluakɛ kɛkala, me ngoane ɛnle ɛhwee.
17 “Na Nyamenle, sonla le duzu, mɔɔ ɔhyia wɔ zɛhae a,
mɔɔ ɛ nye wɔ ɔ nwo zɛhae a?
18Mɔɔ nwolomɔ biala ɛkpɔla ye,
na mekɛ biala ɛsɔ ye ɛnea ɛ?
19Kenlenzu yɛɛ ɛkɛye ɛ nye me nwo,
anzɛɛ ɛkɛgyakyi me ɛkɛmaa menwɔme nyɛlɛ a?
20Saa meyɛ ɛtane a, ɛnee duzu a meyɛ wɔ a,
wɔmɔ menli sinzavo?
Duzu ati a ɛ nye gyi me nyunlu zɛhae a?
Duzu ati a meyɛ adesoa memaa wɔ a?
21Duzu ati a ɛnrɛva me mɛladonlɛ ɛnrɛhyɛ me,
na ɛnrɛva me amumuyɛ ɛnrɛhyɛ me ɛ?
Ɔluakɛ mebala azɛlɛ ye abo;
ɛbakpondɛ me, na ɛnrɛnwu me.”

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
Beledade
1Na Beledade hanle kɛ,
2“Na kenlenzu a ɛkɛwie tendɛ a?
Ɛ nloa edwɛkɛ le kɛ anwoma kpole bie la.
3Ɛnea a ɛnee Nyamenle kyi nɔhalɛ,
anzɛɛ Tumivolɛ ne kyi pɛlepɛlelilɛ ɔ?
4Saa ɛ mra ɛyɛ ɛtane ɛtia ye a,
yeye bɛ yemaa bɛdabɛ bɛ ɛtane.
5Saa ɛkɛkpondɛ Nyamenle abo zo,
na ɛkɛbodo ɛkɛzɛlɛ Tumivolɛ ne,
6saa ɛmaa ɛ nwo te na ɛbɔ ɛbɛla mɔɔ tenrɛ,
nɔhalɛ, ɔbaheha ɔ nwo na yeakyekye wɔ awuke ne bieko,
7amaa saa mɔlebɛbo ne ɛle ekyi a,
wɔ awieleɛ nu wɔayɛ sonlakpole.
8“Mesɛlɛ wɔ, biza mɔɔ ɛze ɛhɔ la,
na dwenle mɔɔ ɛ ze mɔ ɛnwu ye la anwo.
9Ɔluakɛ anoma ala a bɛwo yɛ a, yɛnze ɛhwee,
yɛ mekɛ wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo le kɛ ɛlawolɛ.
10Bɛbahilehile wɔ,
na bɛaha mɔɔ bɛnwunle ye la bɛahile wɔ.
11Asoo ndɔ fifi ɛleka mɔɔ azia ɛnle la,
anzɛɛ ɔnyi ɔtɛlɛdɛlɛ wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ nzule ɛnle la?
12Mɔɔ bɛkɛgyinla dedɛkɛɛ na bɛtɛpepɛle bɛ la,
bɛkyengye bɛwu kolaa na baka biala awu.
13Kɛ menli mɔɔ arɛle fi Nyamenle la
ndenle nu de la ɛne;
sonla mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la anyelazo bawie.
14Ye adwenle ɛnzi pi,
yɛɛ ye diedi le kɛ kɛdɛba ndenda.
15Ɔtudu ɔkisia ye sua, noko sua ne golo;
ɔsɔ nuhua, noko sua ne ɛngyinla.
16“Sɛnzɛne ne ɛtɛtudule a ɔnyi ɔtoto ɔ sa,
na ɔtende ɔgua ye tola ne bane ne mɔ azo.
17Ye ndinli beba awolɛ edukue ne,
na ɔgyinla awolɛ ne mɔ avinli.
18Saa bɛtu ye bɛfi ɔ bo zo ne a,
ɔkpo ye na ɔka kɛ, ‘Metɛnwunle wɔ ɛlɛ!’
19Ɛhɛe, kɛ ye fɛlɛkolilɛ adenle ne de la ɛne;
bie mɔ noko fifi ɔ bo zo ne.
20“Noko, Nyamenle ɛnrɛkpo mɔɔ ɛnze nwolɛ bie la,
yɛɛ ɔnrɛzɔ ɛtanevolɛma asa.
21Ɔbamaa ɛ nloa anwo ayɛ ɛzelekɛ ɛzelekɛ,
na wɔava fɛlɛkolilɛ wɔadeɛdea nu.
22Menli mɔɔ kpɔ wɔ la baheda anyiemgba ɛdanlɛ,
na amumuyɛma awuke ne mɔ abɔ tɔɔ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Na Dwobu buale ye kɛ,
2 “Nɔhalɛ, meze kɛ ɔle zɔ.
Noko nwane a di benle wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu a?
3Saa awie se kɛ ɔ nee ye yeye ɛnloanlɛ a,
ɔnrɛhola ye kpuyia apenle ko anu ko bɔbɔ anloa ye.
4Ɔle nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ, yɛɛ ye anwosesebɛ le bedevinli;
nwane a nee ye ɛdwudwu na yenyia gyinlagyakɛ a?
5Saa ɔfa ɛya a ɔdwulu awoka,
na ɔtudu bɛ mɔɔ ɔngakye awie a.
6Ɔkpusu azɛlɛ ɔtudu ye ɔ bo zo ne,
na ɔmaa ye mpila ne mɔ kpusu.
7Ɔsisi sɛnzɛne ne anwo zo, ɔmmaa ɔndudu,
na ɔkeda nwɔlɔra nyunlu.
8Ɔdaye ɔ ngome a ɔbɔle anwomanyunlu tɛtɛlɛ ye,
na ɔtietiale nyevile azɛlɛkye zo a.
9 Ɔbɔle nwɔlɔra Ɛrelera nee ɔ mra nee Apeansa,
Nwɔlɔra Nsuu nee nyiakɛ nwɔlɔra.
10Ɔyɛ ninyɛne mgbole mɔɔ bo sonla ndelebɛbo zo,
ɔyɛ nwanwane ninyɛne mɔɔ ɛnlɛ ɔ nloa a.
11“Nea, ɔse me nwo ɛkɛ, noko mennwu ye;
ɔlɛkɔ bɔbɔ a mennwu ɔ nwo.
12Saa Nyamenle ɛlɛfa debie a, nwane a kɛhola ye aze si a?
Nwane a kɛhola kɛbiza ye kɛ, ‘Duzu a ɛlɛyɛ la?’
13Nyamenle ɛnrɛhwe ye ɛyavalɛ ne ɛnrɛzia;
Releehabe boavolɛma bɔ bɛ ti aze ɔ nyunlu.
14Ɛnee kɛ menzi membua ye ɛ,
duzu edwɛkɛkpɔkɛ a meka a?
15Menli fɔlɛ, noko menrɛhola ye bua;
ɔwɔ kɛ mesɛlɛ me ndɛnebuavolɛ ne anwunvɔnezelɛ.
16Saa menvɛlɛle ye yɛɛ ɔliele me zo a,
anrɛɛ menrɛlie menrɛli kɛ yedie me ne.
17Ɔluakɛ ɔfa ahumu ɔbɛlɛ me aze,
na mgbane ne ala ɔmaa me nwo nganlɛ yɛ dɔɔnwo.
18Ɔmmaa menlie me ɛnwomenle,
na ɔmaa ɛbɛlabɔlɛ yɛ ɛnwonle.
19Saa ɔba anwosesebɛ ɛzulɛ a, ɔle bedevinli;
saa ɔba pɛlepɛlelilɛ a, nwane a kɛhola ye a?
20Menze nwolɛ bie, medi nɔhalɛ,
noko me nloa bua me ewule fɔlɛ;
menli fɔlɛ, noko yehile kɛ menle kpalɛ.
21Menli fɔlɛ; membu me nwo;
me kunlu bɔbɔ a anrɛɛ mewu.
22Ɔ muala wie ko; yemɔti mese,
ɔsɛkye kpalɛma, ɔsɛkye amumuyɛma.
23Saa esiane fa arɛlevilɛ nu ewule ba a,
ɔsi anzenwolɛbiema anwubɛnyunlu amgbu.
24Bɛva azɛlɛ ye bɛwula amumuyɛma asa anu;
ɔkedɛheda ndɛnebuavolɛma anyunlu,
na saa tɛ ye a, ɛnee nwane ɔ?
25“Me mekɛ se waa tɛla sonla mɔɔ ɛlɛnriandi la;
ɔse ɔkɔ, ɔnnwu kpalɛ biala.
26Ɔpɛ nu ɔkɔ kɛ ndɔ mɔɔ la azule nye,
ɔto kɛ kɔleɛ ɛlɛto ahye nane.
27Saa meka kɛ, ‘Memaa me rɛle avi me nyane,
meagyakyi me nyunlu alɔbɔlɛ ɛyɛlɛ,
meamaa me nye alie’ a,
28me nyanenwunlɛ ne ka me ɛzulolɛ,
ɔluakɛ meze kɛ ɛbabua me fɔlɛ.
29Bɛbabua me ewulefɔlɛ,
duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ mefonla me nwo a?
30Saa mefa saminla mebia,
na mefa anatele meyɛ me sa anwo a,
31ɛbavuandi me wɔado ewula nu,
na medame me nwo ndanlɛ bɔbɔ bahyi me.
32Ɔluakɛ ɔnle sonla kɛ medame la na meabua ye,
na yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛaye ndɛne.
33Kpɔdavolɛ biala ɛngyi yɛ avinli,
mɔɔ kɛkpɔda yɛ mu nwiɔ a.
34Bɛmaa ɔva me nwo empele ne ɔhɔ,
na ɔmmafa ɔ nwo ɛzulolɛ ne ɔnwunlonwunla me.
35Amaa meanzulo ye na meandendɛ,
ɔluakɛ menle kɛ mɔɔ bɛmɛ bɛdwenle kɛ mele la.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
1“Me kunlu a anrɛɛ mewu;
akee mebaha me nyane kɔsɔɔti;
mebaha me ahonle nu nyane muala.
2Mebaze Nyamenle kɛ, mmabua me ewule fɔlɛ,
maa menwu deɛ mɔɔ yemɔti ɛ nee me ɛlɛsi la.
3Anzɛɛ ɛ kunlu dwo kɛ ɛkɛsisi me,
kɛ ɛkɛkpo ɛ sa anloa gyima,
na ɛ nye kɛlie amumuyɛma ɛbɛla nwo ɔ?
4Asoo ɛ nye le kɛ sonla ɛdeɛ ne,
na ɛnea debie kɛ sonla la?
5Asoo wɔ mekɛ le kɛ sonla ɛdeɛ ne la?
Anzɛɛ wɔ ɛvolɛ dodo le kɛ dasanli ɛdeɛ,
6mɔɔ ɛneɛnlea me nu wɔanwu me munzule mɔɔ mebɔ,
na wɔaza me ɛtane ne mɔ wɔagua zo a?
7Ɛze kɛ menli fɔlɛ,
yɛɛ awie biala ɛngola ɛnlie me ɛnvi ɛ sa nu.
8“Ɛdawɔ a ɛbɔle me ɛzieziele me a,
yɛɛ kɛkala wɔpɛ ɛ nwo kɛ ɛsɛkye me a.
9Kakye kɛ ɛvale ndɛtɛlɛ a ɛbɔle me a;
na eza ɛmaa meazia meahɔ ndɛtɛlɛ nu bieko ɔ?
10Na wɔanwola me kɛ meleke,
wɔambɔ me kunguma kɛ kyiisi ɔ?
11Ɛvale mbowule nee ndinli ɛbɔle me,
na ɛvale nwonane nee nwoma ɛhedale zo.
12Wɔmaa me ngoane nee ɛhulolɛ kpundii,
yɛɛ wɔli me sunsum ne adane.
13Noko wɔva ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti wɔzie wɔ ahonle nu;
meze kɛ ɛhye a le wɔ kpɔkɛ mɔɔ ɛgyi zo a.
14Saa meyɛ ɛtane a, ɛnee wɔva wɔzie,
ɛnva me nvonleɛ ɛngyɛ me.
15Saa meyɛ amumuyɛ a, munzule doa me!
Saa medi pɛlepɛle a, mengola me ti zo ma,
ɔluakɛ menea amaneɛ mɔɔ melɛnwu ye la a,
ɛnee nyiane ɛkpɔlɔ me betaa.
16Saa memaa me nwo zo a, ɛfoa me kɛ awenade,
na ɛyɛ nwanwane ninyɛne ɛtia me.
17Dahuu ɛlɛ alasevolɛ ka tia me,
me nwo ɛya mɔɔ wɔ ɛ kunlu la dahuu yɛ kpole,
yɛɛ dahuu ɛfa ɛlɔnema fofolɛ ɛba me nwo zo.
18“Duzu ati a ɛmanle bɛwole me a?
Me kunlu a anrɛɛ menwule kolaa na ɛnyelɛ anwu me.
19Anrɛɛ mevi ɔmɔ akunlu ala la
bɛ nee me hɔle aziezo.
20Me mekɛ mɔɔ ɛha la le ezinraa.
Bɛgyakyi me, amaa me rɛle akyekye ekyii.
21Ɔnrɛhyɛ biala na meahɔ ɛleka mɔɔ
bɛkɔ a bɛnzia la,
maanle anu kisii, anu awozinli kabii ne,
22maanle anu kisii,
anu begyebegye ne,
mɔɔ ye wienyi le kɛ awozinli.”

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Zofaa
1Zofaa hanle kɛ,
2“Yemɔti ɔnle kɛ awie bua edwɛkɛ bebelebe ye anwo,
anzɛɛ ɛdendɛlɛ dɔɔnwo dɔɔnwo bua sonla benle ɔ?
3Ɛ nloa beɛbeɛ, awie mmaka bie ɔ,
yɛɛ wɔ amgbuzilɛ ne, ɛngulo kɛ bɛtwi ɛ nyunlu ɔ?
4Ɛse wɔ ngehanleɛ ne le fɔɔnwo,
yɛɛ ɛ nwo te wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu.
5Anrɛɛ Nyamenle adendɛ,
na yeabuke ɔ nloa wɔ ɛ nwo,
6anrɛɛ ɔkɛze wɔ kɛ nrɛlɛbɛ ndenle zonle;
ninyɛne dɔɔnwo wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ dasanli ɛnde bɛ bo a.
Nwu ye kɛ Nyamenle ɛndua wɔ kakɛ, kɛmɔ ɛfɛta la.
7“Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛnwu Nyamenle abo ɔ?
Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛnwu Tumivolɛ ne awieleɛ ɔ?
8Ye tumi ne kpole wɔ anwuma tɛla anwomanyunlu,
duzu a ɛkɛhola ɛkɛyɛ a?
Yɛɛ ɔle kuloonwu ɔtɛla Ɛbolɔ kuma,
na wɔmɔ, ɛkɛhola ɛkɛnwu ye ɔ?
9Ɔwale ɔtɛla azɛlɛ ye,
yɛɛ ɔtɛlɛ ɔtɛla nyevile.
10Saa ɔba, ɔse kɛ ɔgua menli efiade,
ɔ nee bɛ kɔ ndɛnebualɛ ɛleka a,
nwane a kɛhola ɔ nwo zo sisi a?
11Ɔluakɛ ɔze kpamgbanvolɛma ne mɔ;
saa ɔnwu ɛtane a, ɔnrɛdwenle nwo ɔ?
12Saa bɛwo asoaso kokonyinli sonla a,
ahɔnwɔne bɔbɔ bade ɔ bo.
13“Saa ɛfa wɔ ahonle ɛmaa Nyamenle a,
ɛbamaa ɛ sa zo wɔamaa ye.
14Saa ɛle ɛtanevolɛ a, gyakyi ɛtaneyɛlɛ,
mmadie amumuyɛ azie wɔ wɔ awuke nu.
15Ɛhye bamaa wɔamaa ɛ ti zo, ɛnrɛze nyiane;
bɛbabɔ ɛ nwo bane na ɛnrɛzulo.
16Ɛ rɛle bavi wɔ anwubɛnyunlu ne;
ɛbahakye ye ala kɛ azuyilɛ mɔɔ ɛhwe.
17Na wɔ ɛbɛla bada adɛla ewiazo sɛnzɛne;
nuhua awozinli ne bayɛ kɛ nwonlomɔ sɛnzɛne.
18Wɔ adwenle bagyinla, ɔboalekɛ ɛlɛ anyelazo;
bɛbabɔ ɛ nwo bane,
amaa wɔalie wɔ ɛnwomenle anzonudwolɛ nu.
19Ɛbala koonwu, yɛɛ awie biala ɛnrɛha wɔ ɛzulolɛ;
na menli dɔɔnwo babiza wɔ moalɛ.
20Amumuyɛma ɛnrɛnwu ɛhwee;
ɛnriandilɛ adenle biala baminli bɛ nye zo,
bɛ anyelazo a le ewule.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
16just as he rules over liars
and those they lie to.
17God shames counselors,
turns judges into fools,
18and makes slaves of kings.
19God removes priests and others
who have great power—
20he confuses wise,
experienced advisors,
21puts mighty kings to shame,
and takes away their power.
22God turns darkness to light;
23he makes nations strong,
then shatters their strength.
24God strikes their rulers senseless,
then leaves them to roam
through barren deserts,
25lost in the dark, staggering
like someone drunk.
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Dwobu buale ye kɛ,
2“Ɔnyɛ nwanwane, menli ne a le bɛmɛ,
yɛɛ bɛ nee nrɛlɛbɛ bawu.
3Noko melɛ ndelebɛbo kɛ bɛdabɛ ala la;
mendɔ sinli wɔ bɛ nu.
Nwane a ɛnze ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ a?
4Me nwo ɛyɛ me gɔnwo mɔ ɛzelekɛ;
medame mɔɔ menvɛlɛle Nyamenle memanle ɔliele me zo,
sonlakpalɛ mɔɔ me nwo ɛnlɛ ngehanleɛ,
ɛnɛ medo ɛzelekɛ aleɛ.
5Sonla mɔɔ arɛle ɛdɔ aze la adwenle nu a
anwubɛnyunlu ɛnle debie biala;
ɔwɔ ɛkɛ ɔmaa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ ɔngyɛ na bɛatele bɛadɔ la.
6Anzonudwolɛ wɔ nwule awuke nu,
yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛka Nyamenle
ɛya la anwo kɔlɔnwo,
bɛmɛ, bɛ nyamenle a le bɛ anwosesebɛ.
7“Na biza nane ne mɔ, na bɛkɛhilehile wɔ;
biza anwomanyunlu nloma, na bɛkɛze wɔ;
8anzɛɛ biza azɛlɛ ye azo mbaka,
na bɛkɛhilehile wɔ;
biza nyevile nu fɛlɛ,
na bɛkɛha bɛkɛhile wɔ.
9Na ɛhye mɔ, bɛ nuhua boni a ɛnze
kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛyɛ ɛhye a?
10Abɔdeɛ biala ngoane wɔ ɔ sa nu,
yɛɛ dasanli biala ngoane wɔ ɔ sa nu.
11Ɛnzonlɛ te edwɛkɛ,
kɛmɔ ɛtafinlimalɛ sɔ aleɛ nea la.
12“Nrɛlɛbɛ hale mgbanyinli,
yɛɛ ɛkyɛ a ɛnyia ndelebɛbo.
13Nyamenle lɛ nrɛlɛbɛ, ɔlɛ tumi;
folɛdulɛ nee ndelebɛbo le ye ɛdeɛ.
14Saa ɔbubu debie a, awie ɛngola ye boɛ yɛ bieko;
saa ɔto sonla efiade a, awie ɛngola ye tukue.
15Saa ɔsisi ezuledɔlɛ zo a, azule sesa;
saa ɔtukue ezule a, azɛlɛ sia.
16Anwosesebɛ nee nrɛlɛbɛ le ye ɛdeɛ;
mɔɔ bɛlɛbɛla nee mɔɔ bɛbɛlɛbɛla ye la le ye ɛdeɛ.
17Ɔsa folɛdulɛma ɔdie nrɛlɛbɛ,
na ɔmaa ndɛnebuavolɛma yɛ ahɔnwɔne.
18Ɔsa arelemgbunli ɔdie bɛ abɔtile,
na ɔmo bɛ abɛlako.
19Ɔkpolo sɛlɛvolɛma adɛladeɛ na ɔfoa bɛ,
na ɔbɛlɛ mgbolema aze.
20Ɔmaa menli mɔɔ bɛdie bɛ bɛdi la tɔ mumule,
na ɔsa mgbanyima ɔdie bɛ nrɛlɛbɛ.
21Ɔbɔ arelemgbunli mralɛ mrenya anyiemgba,
na ɔdie anwosesebɛma anwosesebɛ.
22Ɔsa awozinli nu ninyɛne ɔgua zo,
na ɔmaa awozinli kabikabi kakyi wienyi.
23Ɔmaa maanle maanle zo, yɛɛ eza ɔsɛkye bɛ.
Ɔmaa maanle maanle pi, yɛɛ eza ɔbɔ bɛ asande.
24Ɔdie azɛlɛ ye azo arelemgbunli ndelebɛbo,
na ɔmaa bɛduolua ye ɔ nye ɔ nye.
25Bɛdi nvuovua wɔ awozinli nu,
na ɔmaa bɛtotɔ kɛ nzanli.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Know and Understand
1I know and understand
every bit of this.
2None of you are smarter
than I am;
there's nothing you know
that I don't.
3But I prefer to argue my case
with God All-Powerful—
4you are merely useless doctors,
who treat me with lies.
5The wisest thing you can do
is to keep quiet 6and listen
to my argument.
7Are you telling lies for God
8and not telling the whole truth
when you argue his case?
9If he took you to court,
could you fool him,
just as you fool others?
10If you were secretly unfair,
he would correct you,
11and his glorious splendor
would make you terrified.
12Your wisdom and arguments
will blow away like dust.
Be Quiet While I Speak
13Be quiet while I speak,
and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
1“Nea, me nye ɛnwu ɛhye mɔ amuala,
me nzo ɛde na mede ɔ bo.
2Mɔɔ bɛmɛ bɛze la, medame noko meze;
mendɔ sinli wɔ bɛ nu.
3Me nee Tumivolɛ ne badendɛ,
mekulo kɛ mekilehile edwɛkɛ nu mekile Nyamenle.
4Na bɛmɛ, bɛfa adalɛ bɛkye bɛ nwo ɛhane,
bɛ muala bɛle ninsivoma mɔɔ anwo ɛnlɛ nvasoɛ a.
5Saa bɛyɛ koonwu a,
anrɛɛ ɛnee bɛze nrɛlɛbɛ.
6“Akee bɛdie me edwɛkɛ,
bɛdie mɔɔ vi me nloa anu finde la.
7Bɛbɔ adalɛ bɛamaa Nyamenle,
na bɛabɛlɛbɛla ye ɔ?
8Bɛdi bɛahɔ Nyamenle anzi ɔ?
Bɛka Nyamenle tendile bɛamaa ye ɔ?
9Saa ɔneɛnlea bɛ nuhua a, bɛkɛvi nu ɔ?
Asoo bɛkɛhola ye bɛlɛbɛla kɛ bɛbɛlɛbɛla sonla la?
10Kanza bɛwɔ ye afoa awozinli nu bɔbɔ a,
ɔbahwi bɛ nyunlu.
11Asoo ye tumi ne ɛnrɛha bɛ ɛzulolɛ,
yɛɛ ɔ nwo ɛzulolɛ ne ɛnrɛdɔ bɛ nwo zo?
12Bɛ mrɛlɛbulɛ le mgbane kɛ nzonle,
bɛ nwo banebɔlɛ le kɛ ndɛtɛlɛ.
13Bɛyɛ ngungoonwu, na metendɛ,
bɛmaa mɔɔ ba me nwo zo la ɛrɛla.
14“Melɛ me ngoane ne me sa nu,
mebava me nwonane ne meado nzeleba.
15Ɛhɛe, ɔbahu me, menlɛ anyelazo;
noko mebahɔha me edwɛkɛ meahile ye.
16Ɛhye bayɛ me ngoanelielɛ,
ɔluakɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la ɛnrɛra ɔ nyunlu.
17Bɛdie me edwɛkɛ ne kpalɛ,
na bɛmaa mɔɔ meka la ɛhɔ bɛ nzo nu.
18Bɛnlea, meziezie me edwɛkɛ ne pɛpɛ,
meze kɛ me nwo bavi nu.
19“Nwane bɔbɔ a kɛhola kɛze me kɛ meyɛ ɛtane a?
Anrɛɛ menwɔyɛ koonwu na menwɔwu.
20Maa membiza wɔ ninyɛne nwiɔ,
na menrɛvea me nwo wɔ ɛ nyunlu.
21Ye ɛ sa wɔ me nwo zo,
yɛɛ mmamaa ɛ nwo ɛzulolɛ ne nwunlonwunla me.
22“Akee fɛlɛ, na menwɔlie zo;
anzɛɛ maa mendendɛ, na bua me.
23Me ninyɛndane nee me ɛtane ne mɔ le nyɛ?
Maa menwu me mɛladonlɛ nee me ɛtane ne mɔ.
24“Duzu ati a ɛfa ɛ nye ɛfea,
na ɛbu me wɔ kpɔvolɛ ɛ?
25Asoo ɛkɛnwunlonwunla nya mɔɔ anwoma ɛlɛbɔ ye ahɔ la,
na ɛkɛnriandi ɛkɛdoa ma abonle?
26Ɔluakɛ ɛkɛlɛ ɛtane ɛtane ɛtia me,
na ɛmaa medi me mgbavolɛ nu ɛtane ne mɔ anwo fɔlɛ.
27 Ɛbɔ me kpanwu, ɛnea me adenle biala anu;
egyakɛ biala mɔɔ metu la, ɛ nye gyi me nwo.
28Sonla sɛkye yɛ mgbane kɛ debie kpɔlɔlera,
ɔle kɛ ɛdanlɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛtɛba ɛli la.

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
1“Sonla dasanli mɔɔ raalɛ ɛwo ye la mekɛ le ezinraa,
yɛɛ nuhua le amaneɛ ngome.
2Ɔkpakye kɛ ndotolo, na ɔnwoso;
ɔpɛ nu kɛ ɛlawolɛ, na ɔminliminli.
3Sonla zɛhae, ɔdaye ɛnea ye,
ɛdi ye edwɛkɛ, ɛbua ye ndɛne?
4Nwane a kɛhola kɛye debie bɔkɔbɔkɔ kɛvi evinli nu a?
Awie biala ɛnle ɛkɛ.
5Kɛmɔ bɛhile ye mekɛ mɔɔ ɔbali la, bɛwie,
siane dodo mɔɔ ɔbali la,
wɔhyehyɛ wɔdo ɛkɛ, na ɔnrɛhakyi ɛlɛ.
6“Ye ɛ nye ɔ nwo, na gyakyi ye,
amaa yealie ɔ nye, yeali ye mekɛ kɛ ɛkpanli.
7Ɔluakɛ baka bɔbɔ lɛ anyelazo,
kɛ bɛpɛ ye bɔbɔ a, ɔbafifi bieko,
ɔ nye ɛnrɛgyakyi ɛwɔlɔlɛ ɛlɛ.
8Kanza ye ndinli ne mɔ kyɛ aze,
ye dosinli ne wu azɛlɛ bo a,
9kɛ ɔnyia ezule la ɛnee yefifi
yeyeye ngane kɛ baka ekyi la.
10Sonla wu, na bɛsie ye;
sonla gua ɛnwomenle aze a ɛnee ɔwɔ nienwu?
11“Kɛmɔ tandane we,
na azudenle sesa la,
12zɔhane ala yɛɛ sonla wu na ɔndwazo ko a.
Saa anwuma ɛtɛpɛle nu ɛtɛsenle a,
bɛnrɛdwazo bieko,
bɛvi nafelɛ nu bɛnrɛdunwue.
13“Anrɛɛ wɔava me wɔavea ɛbolɔ,
wɔava me wɔavea toonwo wɔ ɛya ne adwo,
anrɛɛ wɔahile me mekɛ, na ɔdwu a wɔahakye me.
14Saa sonla wu a, ɔkɛdɛnla ngoane nu bieko ɔ?
Wɔ me ɛzonlenlɛ mekɛ nu mebahendɛ,
toonwo me ɛkpɔnelɛ mekɛ adwu.
15Ɛbavɛlɛ, na mebalie wɔ zo;
ɛ nwo balɔ ɛdawɔ ɛ sa anloa gyima.
16Na akee ɛbanlea me gyakɛ ɛdudulɛ nu,
na ɛnrɛnlea me ɛtane ne mɔ;
17ɛbawula me mɛladonlɛ ne kodoku nu wɔakyekye ɔ nloa,
na wɔaheda me ninyɛndane zo.
18“Na boka bɔbɔ dwulu gua aze,
yɛɛ bodane tudu fi ɔ bo zo ne;
19azule kundohundo awolɛ,
yɛɛ ɛzezeane pia anwea kɔ;
yemɔti ɛmaa sonla anyelazo bɔ ye.
20Ɛkolo ɔ nwo zo dahuu na ɔwu bɔkɔɔ;
ɛkakyi ɔ nyunlu na ɛye ye ɛfi ɛ nye zo.
21Ɔ mra mrenya nyia bɛ nyunlu, na ɔnnwu ye;
bɛ nyunlu gua aze, noko ɔnnwu ye.
22Ɔdaye mumua ne ye nwonane nu nyane ne ala a ɔte a,
na ɔsu ɔdaye ɔ ngome ɔ nwo.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Adwelielilɛ mɔɔ tɔ zo nwiɔ
(15.1—21.34)
Ɛlaefaze
1Na Ɛlaefaze hanle kɛ,
“Edwɛkɛ funli, Dwobu!
Edwɛkɛ funli a wɔha la!
2Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ biala ɛnrɛha edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛka la
na ɔnrɛva edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ndelebɛbo ɛnle nu la
ɔnrɛhye ɔ nwo ɛhane.
3Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛsu kpolera mɔɔ nvasoɛ biala ɛnle zo la,
anzɛɛ bɛsu edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛnle nɔhalɛ la anwo kpolera ɔ?
4Nea, ɛlɛmaa Nyamenle ɛzulolɛ avi ɛkɛ,
na wɔazi Nyamenle anyunlu nzɛlɛlɛ aze.
5Wɔ ɛdendɛlɛ bɔbɔ kile wɔ adwenle ɛtane,
na ɛfa ɛ nloa ɛkye ɛ nwo ɛhane.
6Ɛdawɔ ɛ nloa a bu wɔ fɔlɛ a, tɛ me ɔ;
ɛdawɔ wɔ ɛdendɛlɛ di daselɛ tia wɔ.
7“Ɛdwenle kɛ wɔmɔ a ɛle sonla mɔɔ bɛlumuale bɛbɔle wɔ a?
Anzɛɛ bɛbɔle wɔ kolaa na bɛabɔ awoka ɔ?
8Wɔdie Nyamenle adwenle ngyehyɛlɛ ne ɔ?
Na ɛdwenle kɛ ɛ ngomekye a ɛze nrɛlɛbɛ a?
9Duzu yɛɛ wɔmɔ ɛze mɔɔ yɛmɛ yɛnze a?
Duzu a wɔmɔ ɛte ɔ bo mɔɔ yɛmɛ yɛnde ɔ bo a?
10Egyɛnema nee mgbanyinli wɔ yɛ avinli,
menli mɔɔ le mgbanyinli tɛla ɛ ze la.
11“Ɛnee Nyamenle arɛlekyekyelɛ ne le ekyi maa wɔ,
anzɛɛ ye bɛlɛvolɛ edwɛkɛ ne a le ekyi a?
12Duzu ati a wɔ ahonle gyegye wɔ,
na ɛkpa yɛ anyehoanlɛ zɛhae ɛ?
13Duzu ati a ɛkakyi ɛ nzi ɛsi Nyamenle,
na ɛtendɛ ɛdendɛlɛ ɛhye a?
14 “Sonla le duzu, mɔɔ ɔ nwo kola te a?
Anzɛɛ sonla boni yɛɛ raalɛ ɛwo ye
mɔɔ kola sɔ Nyamenle anye a?
15Nea, Nyamenle ɛnlie ye
anwondelɛma bɔbɔ ɛnli,
yɛɛ anwuma ɛnde ɔ nye zo;
16na akee sonla mɔɔ sie munzule na ye subane ɛkpɔlɔ,
sonla mɔɔ no ɛtane kɛ nzule la.
17Tie maa menga mengile wɔ,
mɔɔ menwu ye la yɛɛ meka a;
18nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma ɛha,
bɛ ze mɔ anva anvea bɛ,
19kɛ bɛmɛ bɛ ngome yɛɛ bɛvale azɛlɛ ne bɛmanle bɛ a,
yɛɛ ɛyɛvolɛ biala andɛnla bɛ nu.
20“Amumuyɛnli te nyane dahuu,
ɛvolɛ dodo mɔɔ ɔbali la, awie ɛnrɛze ye anwunvɔne.
21Ɛnelɛ ɛzulolɛ ɛmkpa ɔ nzo nu;
saa ɔkpazi a, sɛkyevolɛ ne bara ɔ nwo zo.
22Ɔnlie ɔnli kɛ ɔbavi awozinli nu,
ye awieleɛ wie dadeɛ nloa.
23Ɔkpɔsɛkpɔsa wɔ aleɛ duma nu,
na ɔse kɛ, ‘Aleɛ wɔ ni?’
Ɔze kɛ awozinli kenle ne asɛɛ ɛdo ye.
24Nyanenwunlɛ nee arɛlebɔlɛ nwunlonwunla ye;
bɛba ɔ nwo zo kɛ belemgbunli mɔɔ ɛboɔboa ɔ nwo ɛlɛkɔ konle la.
25“Kɛmɔ yedende ɔ sa Nyamenle anyunlu,
na yedu Tumivolɛ ne anloa yedo,
26yeva bɛ sa nu enyinlike ɛnlomboɛ yegyela,
na yememaa ɔ nwo zo Nyamenle anyunlu la ati,
27kɛmɔ yeyɛ belane na ye dwongu nu ɛmia,
28na ɔdɛnlanle azuadu zo,
azua mɔɔ menli ɛnde nu, mɔɔ bɛhyehyɛle bɛdole ɛkɛ,
kɛ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ ewula edukue edukue la anu la ati,
29ɔnrɛnyia ɔ nwo ɛlɛ, ye anwonyia ɛnrɛhyɛ,
yɛɛ ɔ bo ɛnrɛzɔ ndinli ɛlɛ,
30awozinli ɛnrɛkpa ɔ ti ɛlɛ;
sendɔlɔra bayela ye ngane kɔsɔɔti,
na ahumu akpoɔkpoa ye ndotolo ne mɔ bɔkɔɔ.
31Ɔmmamaa ɔ nye da, ɔbɛlɛbɛla ɔ nwo;
ɔluakɛ anyelazo mgbane a bayɛ ye ahatualɛ a.
32Bɛbadua ye kakɛ bɔkɔɔ na yeawu,
yɛɛ ye nya ɛnrɛyɛ amunli bieko.
33Ɔbayɛ kɛ vanye baka mɔɔ kpolo ye ma amunli gua,
kɛ ɔlivi baka mɔɔ kpolo ye ndotolo la.
34“Menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la ɛnrɛnyia bɛ bo zo amra,
yɛɛ senle bayela ndanlɛ azua
mɔɔ bɛvale ndoloboa bɛsisile la.
35Bɛsua nwondomgbɔ ɛhane bɛkye akɛsakɛsa,
yɛɛ mɛlɛbɛla ɛyi bɛ ahonle ne mɔ tɛkɛɛ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Na Dwobu buale ye kɛ,
2“Edwɛkɛ ɛhye mɔ, menyia bɛ nde;
bɛle arɛlekyekyevolɛma anwo anwunvɔne.
3Edwɛkɛ mgbane mgbane ɛnrɛwie ɛlɛ ɔ?
Duzu bɔbɔ a yɛ wɔ ɛya mɔɔ yemɔti ɛtendɛ zɔhane a?
4Saa wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛgyi me gyinlabelɛ a,
anrɛɛ medame mebahola tendɛ kɛ ɛdawɔ la;
anrɛɛ mebawola edwɛkɛ meagua ɛ nwo zo,
na meakpusukpusu me ti meahile wɔ.
5Anrɛɛ mebadendɛ meamaa wɔ anwosesebɛ,
na me nloa edwɛkɛ amaa wɔ anwofofolɛ ne aha aze.
6“Metendɛ a me anwofofolɛ ne ɛnga aze,
meyɛ koonwu noko a me anwofofolɛ ne azo ɛnde.
7Nɔhalɛ, Nyamenle ɛmaa mekponzo;
yebɔ me bo zo bɔkɔɔ.
8Yebɔ me kɔtɔlɔba, na ɛhye di daselɛ tia me;
menwa kanzakanza, medame mumua ne medi nwolɛ daselɛ.
9“Yehyi me, yeva ɛya yetete me nu;
yenrese ɔ gye yehile me;
me kpɔvolɛ koloholo ɔ nye kile me.
10Menli ɛdendɛ mgbane mgbane ɛhile me,
bɛbobɔ me nzo nu koasea nu;
bɛkye bɛ nwo file bɛko bɛtia me.
11Nyamenle ye me maa anzenyamenlema,
na ɔye me ɔwula amumuyɛma asa anu.
12Ɛnee mede anzonudwolɛ nu, na ɔtetele me nu;
ɔtalele me kɔme ɔfinle me aze ɔmanle mentetele,
na ɔvale ɔ nye ɔwulale me nyunlu.
13Ye menli mɔɔ to ɛda la bɔ yia me.
Ɔkpukekpuke me ɛzizira, ɔnze anwunvɔne;
ɔtulu me bɔnyema ɔgua aze.
14Ɛbodalɛ ala a ɔbodɛboda me a,
na ɔba me nwo zo kɛ sogyanli.
15Mekpomgba ɛrele meheda,
na mekpofo ndɛtɛlɛ nu.
16Ɛzunlɛ ngome ɛmaa me nye ɛyɛ ngengaanwo,
na me nye anzi ɛyɛ dudukuu,
17noko menli mgbondedolɛ biala anwo fɔlɛ,
yɛɛ me nzɛlɛlɛ le fɔɔnwo.
18“O azɛlɛ, mmakeda me mogya zo,
yɛɛ mmamaa me ɛzunlɛ ne yɛ mgbane.
19 Nea, kɛkala bɔbɔ, me dasevolɛ ne wɔ anwuma,
yɛɛ mɔɔ di me edwɛkɛ maa me la wɔ anwuma.
20Me gɔnwo mɔ si me amgbu;
metwi monle mekile Nyamenle,
21kɛ ɔkɛmaa sonla nee Nyamenle avinli kɛzɛ,
kɛmɔ sonla nee ɔ gɔnwo bɛ avinli sɛ la.
22Ɔluakɛ yeha mekɛ ekyi bie
na meahɔ ɛleka mɔɔ mekɔ a menrɛzia la.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
1Me ɛkɛla ɛnriandi me, me mekɛ ɛwie,
me nye gyi ewule kuma nu.
2Nɔhalɛ, amgbuzilɛma ɛbɔ ɛyia me,
yɛɛ me nye ala a gyi bɛ nyunlu a.
3Ɛdawɔ fa ɛ nwo di agyinlanu maa me;
nwane a kɛva ɔ nwo kɛli agyinlanu kɛmaa me a?
4Kɛmɔ wɔdo bɛ adwenle nu na bɛnlɛ ndelebɛbo la,
ɛnrɛmaa bɛnrɛli konim ɛlɛ.
5Awie biala mɔɔ pepɛ ɔ gɔnwo mɔ agyakɛ anzi
die bɛ agyadeɛ ne bie la,
ɔ mra anye bazi.
6Yemaa meyɛ agolobɛnwo sonla wɔ menli nyunlu,
na bɛtoto me nyunlu nyɛlɛ.
7Alɔbɔlɛ ngome ɛzi me nye,
me nvɛyeba ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti ɛwie tuto.
8Menli mɔɔ di nɔhalɛ la nwu ɛhye a ɔsi bɛ nwo,
na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnze nwolɛ bie la
ko tia anzenyamenlema.
9Noko tenlenenli die to nu kɛ ɔle fɔɔnwo,
yɛɛ mɔɔ ɛnle ɛtanevolɛ la nyi anwosesebɛ nu.
10Na bɛmɛ, bɛ muala bɛba bieko bɔbɔ a,
menrɛnwu nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ ko bɔbɔ wɔ bɛ nu.
11“Me mekɛ ɛkpa nwo, me adwenle ngyehyɛlɛ ɛkpa nwo,
me ɛhulolɛdeɛ ɛwie.
12Bɛfa aledwolɛ bɛkakyi alehyenlɛ;
bɛse, ‘Wienyi bikye awozinli.’
13Saa mefa Ɛbolɔ kɛ me sua zo,
na metoto me ɛkpa wɔ awozinli nu,
14saa mese funli kuma kɛ, ‘Ɛle me ze’,
na mese sonlɛ kɛ, ‘Ɛle me nli,’
anzɛɛ ‘Me diema raalɛ a,’
15ɛnee me anyelazo wɔ ni?
Nwane a kɛnwu me anyelazo a?
16Asoo ɔ nee me kɛhɔ ɛbolɔ?
Asoo ɔ nee me kɛhɔ ndɛtɛlɛ ne anu?”

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Beledade
1Beledade hanle kɛ,
2“Dwobu, na kenlenzu yɛɛ ɛ nloa kɛpe a?
Dwenle nwo, na maa yɛdayɛ yɛha bie.
3Duzu ati a ɛbu yɛ nane a?
Duzu ati a ɛbu yɛ menli mgbane a?
4Wɔmɔ mɔɔ ɛya maa ɛkile ɛ nwo nyane la,
ɛnee wɔmɔ ɛ ti, sonla vi azɛlɛ ye azo ɛdu,
anzɛɛ bɛdu bodane bɛvi ɔ bo zo ne ɔ?
5 “Ɛhɛe, bɛnua amumuyɛnli ne kɛnlaneɛ,
ye senle le monzomonzo.
6Wienyi le awozinli wɔ ye ndanlɛ sua nu,
na bɛnua ye kɛnlaneɛ ne mɔɔ henda ye sua ne anu la.
7Ye ɛdialɛ anu ɛsesebɛ ne ɛdo,
yɛɛ ɔdaye ye adwenle ngyehyɛlɛ maa ɔkpo aze.
8Ɔluakɛ ɔdaye ɔ gyakɛ fa ye kɔto ɛhane nu,
na ɔkɔtɔ kuma nu.
9Ɛhane sɔ ɔ gyakɛ na ɔkye ye ɔsie ɛkɛ.
10Bɛsua ye azɛlɛ bo ɛhane,
bɛsua ye adevinli ɛhane.
11“Ɛzulolɛ bɔ ye mgbɔlɔka,
na ɔfoa ye ndinlizo.
12Ɛhɔne ngome ɛkpɔlɔ ye,
yɛɛ munzule ɛlɛkendɛ ye azedɔlɛ.
13Ewule ɛzɛkye ye nwonane,
ewule ara kpanyinli bubu ye agbɔkɛ.
14Bɛte ye bɛfi ye ndanlɛ sua ne
mɔɔ ɔvale ɔ rɛle ɔwulale nu la anwo,
na bɛfa ye bɛkɔmaa belemgbunli ewule anwo ɛzulolɛ.
15Bɛfa sɔlefe bɛkpondekponde ye sua ne anu a,
awie gyɛne biala kola tɛnla ye ndanlɛ sua ne anu.
16Ye ndinli kpɔlɔ, yɛɛ ye ngane ne mɔ kyengye.
17Ye duma minli azɛlɛ ye azo,
yɛɛ bɛmbɔ ye duma wɔ mgbata biala azo.
18Bɛye ye bɛfi wienyi nu bɛfuandi ye bɛto awozinli nu,
na bɛtu ye ewiade ye anu.
19Ɔnlɛ mralɛ anzɛɛ ɔ bo zo amra wɔ ye menli avinli,
yɛɛ awie ɛnga ɛleka mɔɔ anrɛɛ ɔde la.
20Ɔvi aduduleɛ mɔɔ kɔ adɔleɛ la,
awie biala mɔɔ kɛde ye edwɛkɛ la,
ɛzulolɛ ka ye na ɔ nwo wozo ye.
21Nɔhalɛ, kɛ anzenyamenlema wie ye la ɛne,
mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la tɛnlabelɛ nu kɛ wie ye la ɛne.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Na Dwobu buale ye kɛ,
2“Duzu ati a ɛlɛfa ɛdendɛlɛ ngome wɔahu me ɛvɛlɛ ɛ?
3Fane kɛyɛ bulu ɛ, aholoba ala a ɛbɔ me a;
ɔnyɛ wɔ nyiane bɔbɔ kɛ ɛkɛvo me ɔ?
4Na saa ɔle nɔhalɛ bɔbɔ kɛ meyɛ ɛtane a,
me ɛtane ne doa me.
5Saa ɛbu ɛ nwo ɛtɛla me,
na ɛfa me anwubɛnyunlu kɛ me ɛtane nwo ndeanlɛ a,
6ɛnee nwu ye kɛ Nyamenle a ɛbua me fɔlɛ,
na yegua me asawu a.
7Nea, metea nu, ‘Kɔdiawu o!’
noko awie ɛmbua me; metea nu ɛsesebɛ,
na pɛlepɛlelilɛ ɛnle ɛkɛ.
8Yedua me adenle, yemɔti mennyia ɛleka mempe,
yemaa awozinli ɛva me.
9Yelie me anyunlunyia,
na yedu me belemgbunli kyɛlɛ ne.
10Ɔbɛlɛ me aze wɔ adenle biala anu,
na ɔmaa mewu, na yedu me anyelazo kɛ baka.
11Yeva me nwo ɛya,
na ɔtia me ɔboka ye kpɔvolɛma anwo.
12Ye ɛlɔnema bɔ nu ba me nwo zo;
bɛbɔ bɛyia me na bɛyɛ azokoɛleɛ
wɔ me ndanlɛ sua ne anwo.
13“Yemaa me nee me mediema yɛ avinli ɛde,
na meyɛ ɛyɛvolɛ wɔ manivolɛma anye zo.
14Me nwo amra nee agɔnwolɛma kpalɛ
ɛye me rɛle ɛdo me sa nu.
15Me sua nu nyɛvolɛ arɛle ɛvi me;
me sonvolɛ mraalɛ bu me ɛyɛvolɛ;
meyɛ bɛ nye zo ɛyɛvolɛ.
16Mefɛlɛ me sonvolɛ, na ɔmbua me;
ɔwɔ kɛ mekpa ye kyɛlɛ bɔbɔ kolaa.
17Me ye bɔbɔ ɛmkpondɛ me nyunlu ɛnnea,
ɔmɔ akunlu mralɛ bɔbɔ kyi me.
18Ngakula bɔbɔ kyi me;
memaa me nwo zo a bɛtendɛ bɛtia me.
19Agɔnwolɛma kpalɛ kpalɛ kyi me,
yɛɛ menli mɔɔ ɛnee mekulo bɛ la ɛhakyi bɛ nzi ɛzi me.
20Mewie nwa, me mbowule ɛza ɛgua zo,
me gye a maa metɛsɔho sonla a.
21“Bɛnwu me anwunvɔne, bɛnwu me anwunvɔne,
ayi mɔ, bɛnwu me anwunvɔne,
ɔluakɛ Nyamenle ɛva ɔ sa ɛha me!
22Duzu ati a bɛhakyi bɛ nwo Nyamenle bɛdoa me ndinlizo a?
Duzu ati a bɛ kunlu ɛndwo me nwonane ne anwo a?
23“O, me edwɛkɛ fɛta kɛlata!
O, anrɛɛ bɛahɛlɛ ye buluku nu!
24O, anrɛɛ bɛava bulalɛ pɛne nee sumi
bɛahɛlɛ ye wɔ bodane zo mɔɔ ɔnkyikyi ɛlɛ a!
25Ɔluakɛ meze kɛ me Dievolɛ ne de aze,
na ɔka kenle ko a ɔbalie me;
26nzinlii mɔɔ bɛkɛzɛkye me nwonane ye la,
mevi nwonane ɛhye anu mebanwu Nyamenle,
27Mebanwu kɛ ɔgyi me foa ko,
me nye banwu ye, menrɛnwu sonla gyɛne biala.
Akee me ɛbolɛ ɛlɛte
28Saa ɛbiza kɛ, ‘Kɛ yɛbazi yɛavoa ye ɛ?’
na bɛse kɛ, ‘Edwɛkɛ ne abo wɔ ye ɛkɛ’ a,
29ɛnee bɛzulo konle dadeɛ ne,
ɔluakɛ konle dadeɛ ne nee ɛya ɛvalɛ ndeanlɛ a lua a,
amaa wɔanwu kɛ ndɛnebualɛ wɔ ɛkɛ.”

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
Zofaa
1Zofaa hanle kɛ,
2“Dwobu, tie maa menze wɔ,
yera me nu kɛ membua wɔ ndɛndɛ,
ɔboalekɛ me nwo ɛlɛyelɛyela me.
3Mete wɔ aholoba ne mɔɔ ɛlɛbɔ la,
yɛɛ melɛ nwolɛ ngakyibɛnzi.
4“Ɛdawɔ, ɛnze ye wienyi kɛ ɔvi tete,
mɔɔ bɛbɔle sonla bɛdole azɛlɛ ye azo la,
5amumuyɛnli ɛkpazilɛ ɛndwu moa,
yɛɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la fɛlɛkolilɛ le sinli?
6Kanza ye tendenle dwu anwuma anwuma,
ɔ ti kpula Nyamenle ko abo bɔbɔ a,
7ɔbakpɔlɔ kɛ ɔdaye ye ebinli;
na menli mɔɔ ɛnwu ye ɛlɛ la babiza kɛ, ‘Ɔwɔ ni?’
8Ɔbapɛ nu yeaze kɛ ɛlalɛ, na bɛnrɛnwu ye ko;
bɛbavoa ye kɛ nɔɔzo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ.
9Ɛnyelɛ mɔɔ nwunle ye la ɛnrɛnwu ye ko,
menli mɔɔ ɔ nee bɛ dɛnlanle la ɛnrɛnwu ye ko.
10Ɔ mra babiza ehyianvolɛma moalɛ,
na yeakpu ye anwonyia ne.
11Ɔlɛ kpavolɛ anwosesebɛ wɔ ye nu,
noko ɔnrɛhyɛ biala na yeahakyi ndɛtɛlɛ.
12“Munzule ɛbɛla yɛ ye fɛ,
ɔfa ɔfea ɔ tafinlima abo,
13ɔngulo kɛ ɔgyakyi nu,
ɔnoko ye ɔ tafinlima abo,
14noko ye aleɛ dwu ɔ kunlu a
ɔle kɛ ndianwu bɔnyema.
15Ɔmeme anwonyia na ɔkpu bɛ bieko;
Nyamenle yeye bɛ fi ɔ kunlu.
16Ɔbanlo ndianwu bɔnyema;
bɔna baha ye ahu ye.
17Ɔnrɛnwu azule,
azule mɔɔ se kɛ wolɛ nee meleke.
18Ɔbaye mɔɔ yenyia ye gyima nu la yeamaa,
bie ɛnrɛha ɔ nloa;
nvasoɛ mɔɔ ɔbanyia ye gualilɛ nu la,
ɔnrɛli nuhua fɛlɛko.
19Ɔluakɛ yesisi ehyianvolɛma na yekpo bɛ,
yelie sua mɔɔ tɛ ɔdaye a ɔzile la.
20Kɛmɔ ye angomedi ɛmmaa ɔ kunlu ɛndwo ɔ nwo la,
debie biala mɔɔ ɔ nye die nwo la, ɔdi ɔ muala.
21Ɔdi a, ɔngyakyi bie,
yemɔti ɔnrɛkpazi.
22Mɔɔ ye anyiabɛnwo ne kɛgyinla zo kpalɛ la,
ɛnee munzule doa ye,
anwubɛnyunlu bali ye akpanebɛ.
23Kanza maa ɔli ɔ ko ɛyi tɛkɛɛ,
Nyamenle bava ye ɛya kpole ne agua ɔ nwo zo,
yeamaa yeali ye kɛ aleɛ.
24Ɔbanriandi konle bulalɛ biala,
noko kɔbele ɛda bawɔ ye avinde ɔ nzi.
25Bɛtwe ye bɛfi sonlabaka ne anu,
ɔ ti memeamemea ne fi ye bɔnyema ne anu finde;
na ɛzulolɛ kpole ka ye.
26Awozinli kabii keda ye anwonyia zo;
senle mɔɔ tɛ sonla a wudale la bayela ye;
ye sua nu debie biala badɔ nzonle.
27Anwuma baza ye ninyɛndane agua zo,
na azɛlɛ adwazo atia ye.
28Bɛbazoa ye awuke nu ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti bɛahɔ,
bɛbawua debie biala wɔ Nyamenle ɛya kenle ne.
29“Amumuyɛnli afoa nu ɛdeɛ mɔɔ ɔnyia
ye Nyamenle ɛkɛ ne la ɛne,
agyadeɛ mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛhyehyɛ ɛmaa ye la ɛne!”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Na Dwobu buale ye kɛ,
2“Yɛ ɛnzonlɛ tie me edwɛkɛ ye kpalɛ,
na maa ɔyɛ arɛlekyekyelɛ ɔmaa wɔ.
3Maa me adenle maa mendendɛ,
saa mewie na ɛkulo a, golo me nwo.
4“Mame, me nee dasanli biala ɛnlɛ butule,
yemɔti menzi abotane biala.
5Wɔmɔ nea me tɛnlabelɛ nu, ɔnyɛ wɔ nyiane
mɔɔ maa ɛfa ɛ sa ɛsɔ ɛ nloa a?
6Saa medwenle nwo a ɛnee me rɛle ɛbɔ,
na me nwo wozo me.
7“Duzu ati a ɛtanevolɛma tɛnla aze,
yɛ mrelera na bɛnyia tumi mgbole ɛ?
8Bɛ mra bo tila,
na bɛ bo zo amra nyi to bɛ.
9Ɛzulolɛ ɛnle bɛ awuke nu,
yɛɛ Nyamenle ndeanlɛ ɛmba bɛ nwo zo.
10Bɛ nlankɛ nyinli yɛ dɔɔnwo;
bɛ nlankɛ mbelɛ wo mralɛ, bɛ ko ɛmkpɔne.
11Bɛ mra anwo tɛ bɛ kɛ mboane,
yɛɛ bɛ mra di wulupe, si agole.
12Bɛto aweɛne nee getaa edwɛne,
na bɛsi fulutu nloa agole.
13Bɛkpazi, bɛdi bɛ mekɛ,
na bɛfa anzonudwolɛ bɛkɔ ɛbolɔ.
14“Bɛka bɛkile Nyamenle kɛ, ‘Ɛvi yɛ nwo ɛke kɔ!
Yɛmkpondɛ wɔ ɛzonlenlɛ nwo ngilehilelɛ biala.
15Tumivolɛ ne a le nwane, mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛsonle ye a?
Yɛɛ saa yɛsonle ye a, duzu nvasoɛ a yɛnyia a?’
16Bɛdwenle kɛ bɛ ɛkpazilɛ vi bɛ mɔdenlebɔ.
Metua me nzo kɛ menwɔdie amumuyɛma folɛdulɛ!
17“Fane nyɛ yɛɛ ɛtanevolɛma kɛnlaneɛ ɛnlu a?
Fane nyɛ yɛɛ munzule ɛdo bie a?
Fane nyɛ yɛɛ Nyamenle ɛva ɛya ɛdua bie kakɛ a?
18Fane nyɛ yɛɛ ɔbɔ bɛ ɔkɔ kɛ abonle lua anwoma nu,
anzɛɛ nya mɔɔ ahumu ɛlɛfa ye ahɔ la a?
19“Wɔmɔ ɛse, ‘Nyamenle fa bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ tea bɛ mra.’
Maa ɔdua bɛdabɛ mumua ne kakɛ, amaa bɛanwu ye.
20Maa bɛdabɛ bɛ nye ɛnwu bɛ ndeanlɛ,
na bɛnwu kɛ Tumivolɛ ne ɛya si de la.
21Ɔluakɛ saa sonla wu a, duzu adwenle bieko
yɛɛ ɔlɛ wɔ ye awuke nwo a?
22Asoo awie kɛhola kɛhile Nyamenle nrɛlɛbɛ,
yemɔ mɔɔ ɔbua mgbolema ndɛne la?
23-24“Menli ne bie mɔ kpazi toonwo bɛwu,
bɛkye, bɛyɛ mbelane tutoboo,
na bɛwu fɛlɛkolilɛ nee anzonudwolɛ nu.
25Bie mɔ noko ɛnde fɛlɛko ɛlɛ,
bɛfa nyane ngome bɛkɔ ɛbolɔ.
26Noko bɛ muala bɛkɔ azɛlɛ ye abo,
na azonlɛ di bɛ muala.
27“Nea, meze bɛ adwenle,
nee me nwo adwenle ɛtane mɔɔ bɛlɛ la,
28ɔluakɛ bɛse, ‘Sonlakpole zɔhane sua wɔ ni?
Yɛɛ amumuyɛnli ne noko sua wɔ ni?’
29Bɛtɛbizale adendulɛma mɔɔ fa ndenle ne mɔ azo la,
anzɛɛ bɛnlie bɛ daselɛlilɛ ne mɔ bɛndo nu,
30kɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ mekɛ nu, bɛgyakyi amumuyɛnli ne,
na bɛye ye bɛfi ɛya kenle ne anu ɔ?
31Nwane a kola fa amumuyɛnli ɛtane si ɔ nyunlu a,
yɛɛ nwane a kola ye kakɛ tua wɔ mɔɔ yeyɛ la anwo a?
32Saa bɛ nee ye kɔ asie a,
menli sinza ye nla ne.
33Bɔnza ne anu anwea yɛ ye fɛ;
menli kɔsɔɔti kɔsɔho ye,
menli mɔɔ kɔsɔho ye la le pemgbenleamgbe.
34“Na duzu edwɛkɛ kpaziwɔkɛ bɔbɔ
yɛɛ ɛfa wɔakyekye me rɛle a?
Ɛnlɛ mualɛ kpalɛ biala kɛ adalɛ ala.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
Adwelielilɛ mɔɔ tɔ zo nsa
(22.1—27.23)
Ɛlaefaze
1Ɛlaefaze hanle kɛ,
2 “Asoo sonla nwo le nvasoɛ maa Nyamenle?
