Sonla mɔɔ ze nrɛlɛbɛ la
le nvasoɛ maa ɔdaye ɔ nwo?
3Saa ɛdi pɛlepɛle a, duzu bolɛ yɛɛ ɛsonle ɛmaa Tumivolɛ ne a,
anzɛɛ ɛbɔ wɔ ɛbɛla ne fɔɔnwo a, duzu nvasoɛ a ɔnyia a?
4Anzɛɛ wɔ ɛzulolɛ mɔɔ ɛsulo ye la ati
yɛɛ ɛyɛ ɛtane a ɔtea wɔ, ɔbua wɔ ndɛne a?
5Asoo wɔ amumuyɛ ne ɛnle kpole?
Wɔ ɛtane ne mɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ.
6Ɔluakɛ wɔlie ɛ mediema awoba mgbane gyɛne ne ala,
na wɔkpa bɛ nwo ndanlɛ.
7Ɛtɛmanle menli mɔɔ ɛvɛ la nzule bɛtɛnonle,
yɛɛ ɛtɛmanle menli mɔɔ ɛhɔne ɛlɛku bɛ la aleɛ.
8Sonla mɔɔ lɛ tumi la vale azɛlɛ ne,
na mɔɔ ɔkulo ye edwɛkɛ la dɛnlanle zo.
9Wɔmaa ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ ɛlɛ bɛ sa mgbane,
yɛɛ wɔsisi nrisa wɔwua bɛ.
10Yemɔti ngane ɛbɔ wɔ mgbɔlɔka ɛyia,
na sulosulo gyegye wɔ.
11Awozinli ɛva wɔ, ɛnnwu aze,
yɛɛ azule ɛyi ɛva wɔ ɛleka biala.
12Asoo Nyamenle ɛnde anwuma hwehwe lɔ?
Nea anwomanyunlu nwɔlɔra, kɛ bɛ ngɛnlɛma si de la!
13Yemɔti a ɛse ‘Duzu a Nyamenle ze a?
Asoo ɔkɛhola ndɛne bua wɔ awozinli kabikabi ye anu?
14Amungu kabii keda ɔ nye, yemɔti ɔnnwu ɛhwee,
na ɔzinze anwuma nee aze bɛ avinli,’ la.
15“Adenle dɛba ne mɔɔ amumuyɛma ɛva nu la,
asoo yemɔ ala a ɛdawɔ ɛbava nu a?
16Bɛpianle bɛ bɛhɔle kolaa na bɛ mekɛ adwu;
azuyilɛ pianle bɛ hɔle, ɔminlinle bɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ.
17Bɛzele Nyamenle kɛ, ‘Ɛvi yɛ nwo ɛke kɔ!
Duzu yɛɛ Tumivolɛ ne kɛhola kɛyɛ kɛmaa yɛ a?’
18Noko yemɔ yɛɛ ɔmanle bɛ ninyɛne kpalɛ a,
na mame, metua me nzo wɔ ɛtanema folɛdulɛ nwo.
19Pɛlepɛlelilɛma nwu ɛhye na bɛdi fɛlɛko,
menli mɔɔ ɛnze nwolɛ bie la sele bɛ maa bɛ ti si aze.
20Bɛse kɛ, ‘Nɔhalɛ, bɛbɔ yɛ kpɔvolɛma abo zo,
yɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛgyakyile la,
senle ɛmaa bɛdɔ nzonle.’
21“Ɛ nee Nyamenle ɛbɔ nu na nyia anzonudwolɛ,
na ɛbakpazi bieko.
22Tie ɔ nloa edwɛkɛ,
na fa ye edwɛkɛ sie wɔ ahonle nu.
23Saa ɛsia ɛkɔ Tumivolɛ ne ɛkɛ bieko,
ɛbɛlɛ ɛ nwo aze ɛmaa ye,
saa wɔ awuke nu amra gyakyi ɛtanelilɛ,
24saa ɛbu ezukoa nvutuke kɛ munlutu,
na ɛbu ezukoa nvutuke awolɛ ‘ɔfɛ’ kɛ azule bo awolɛ,
25na ɛmaa Tumivolɛ ne yɛ wɔ ezukoa nvutuke,
nee wɔ dwɛtɛ fufule mɔɔ sonle bolɛ la a,
26ɛbanyia anyelielɛ wɔ Tumivolɛ ne anu,
na wɔakpogya ɛ nye zo wɔanlea Nyamenle.
27Ɛbavɛlɛ ye, na ɔbadie wɔ;
na wɔadua wɔ ɛwɔkɛbɔlɛ muala.
28Debie biala mɔɔ ɛkɛdwenle nwo la bayɛ zɔ,
na wienyi bada wɔ adenle nu.
29Ɔluakɛ Nyamenle bɛlɛ mgbanyizonlema aze,
na ɔmaa bɛlɛvoma zo.
30Ɔpepɛ ɔdie sonla mɔɔ ɛnze nwolɛ bie;
saa ɛnli fɔlɛ ɛdeɛ a, ɔbapepɛ yealie wɔ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Na Dwobu buale ye kɛ,
2“Ɛnɛ noko me somolɛ ne le kpole kpalɛ,
mɔɔ melɛkponle ala la ɛnee Nyamenle ɛlɛtinli me nu.
3Anrɛɛ meanwu ɛleka mɔɔ ɔwɔ la,
amaa meahɔvinde ɔ nyunlu.
4Anrɛɛ menwɔva me edwɛkɛ menwɔdo ɔ nyunlu
na meahilehile me edwɛkɛ nu meahile ye.
5Anrɛɛ menwɔzukoa ye mualɛ mɔɔ ɔkɛva ɔkɛmaa me la,
na meade mɔɔ ɔkɛha ɔkɛhile me la abo.
6Asoo ye tumi ne kpole nwo yɛɛ ɔnea ɔ nee me ali a?
Kyɛkyɛ, anrɛɛ ɔkɛgyele ɔ nzo ɔkɛdie me somaa.
7Ɛkɛ ne, tenlenenli kola nee ye fa adwenle,
na me ndɛnebuavolɛ ne kɛbua me benle dahuu.
8“Noko nea, mekɔ me nyunlu, na ɔnle ɛkɛ;
mekɔ me nzi, noko mennwu ye;
9mekpondɛ ye me bɛne zo, noko mennwu ye;
yɛɛ mekpondɛ ye me fema zo, noko mennwu ye.
10Noko yemɔ, ɔze adenle mɔɔ mefa zo la;
saa ɔsɔ me ɔnea a, mebavi kɛ ezukoa nvutuke.
11Melua ɔ gyakɛ abo zo ne fɔɔnwo;
melua ye adenle ne anu, metɛfonle adenle.
12Metɛtule ɔ nloa edwɛkɛ metɛtole;
ɔ nloa edwɛkɛ sonle bolɛ maa me.
13“Ɔngakyi ɛlɛ; nwane a kɛhola kɛhakyi ye adwenle a?
Ɔyɛ mɔɔ ɔdaye ɔkulo la.
14Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ ɔhyehyɛle ɔmanle me la, ɔbayɛ,
yɛɛ ngyehyɛlɛ ɛhye mɔ dɔɔnwo wɔ ɔ ti anu.
15Yemɔti mekɔ ɔ nyunlu a, ɛnee me ahonle ɛdu;
saa medwenle ɔ nwo a, ɛnee ɛzulolɛ ɛha me.
16Nyamenle ɛmaa me nwo mɔra ɛdu;
Tumivolɛ ne ɛha me ɛzulolɛ;
17ɔluakɛ awozinli ɛva me,
na awozinli kabii ɛheda me nwo zo.

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
1“Duzu ati a Tumivolɛ ne ɛnzie ndɛnebualɛ mekɛ,
na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛze ye la ɛnnwu ye mekɛ ne ɛ?
2Menli kakyi azɛlɛ ɛweɛne;
bɛwua mboane bɛyɛne bɛ.
3Bɛkyehye nrisa mralɛ asoaso bɛkɔ;
bɛdie ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ nlankɛ nyinli awoba.
4Bɛtua ehyianvolɛma ɛkpazilɛ adenle;
na bɛkpuokpua bɛ bɛmaa bɛnriandi bɛfea.
5“Bɛle kɛ ɛsɛlɛ zo asoaso nyinli,
bɛdwazo ndɛ bɛkɔ aleɛkpondɛlɛ
wɔ fienemgbole nu bɛmaa bɛ mra.
6Bɛbu ɛya mɔɔ tɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ ɔ la anu aleɛ,
na bɛtete amumuyɛma vanye egyinli nu ma.
7Nɔɔzo bɛdɛ bɛ nwo zɔ bɛda,
bɛnlɛ debie bɛnzɔ bɛ ɛyɛlɛ.
8Awoka zo ezule bo bɛ,
na bɛbetɛbeta awolɛ kɛ bɛkpondɛ feabelɛ.
9“Menli bie mɔ te nrisa mralɛ fi nyɛfonlɛ nloa,
na bɛdie ehyianvolɛma amra nlɔma awoba.
10Noko bie mɔ dɛ bɛ nwo zɔ finde,
bɛngeda bie;
na bɛfa ɛhɔne bɛsoa bɛyɔba.
11Bɛtwihwi ɔlivi ma bɛyɛ nwole,
wɔ atisesebɛma egyinli nu;
bɛtwihwi vanye ma bɛyɛ nwanye,
noko nwolɛ nzuhɔne ku bɛ.
12Suakpole ne azo, wuleravolɛma kponle,
menli mɔɔ ɛbodɛboda la su fɛlɛ moalɛ,
noko Nyamenle ɛndie bɛ nzɛlɛlɛ.
13“Bie mɔ wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ ko tia wienyi ne a;
bɛtɛnwunle ye ndenle ne mɔ yɛɛ bɛnlua nuhua.
14Alehyenlɛ nu, kɔdiawu ne dwazo
kɔsia ku ehyianvolɛma;
aledwolɛ nu, ɔle awule.
15Nrenya mɔɔ fa awuvolɛ raalɛ la kendɛ aledwolɛ,
ɔkeda ɔ nyunlu na ɔka kɛ, ‘Awie ɛnrɛnwu me.’
16Awozinli nu bɛbubu awie mɔ azua,
na alehyenlɛ nu bɛtoto bɛ nwo nlenkɛ nu;
bɛnze wienyi ne deɛ holɛ.
17Awozinli kabikabi le bɛ alehyenlɛ,
ɔluakɛ bɛ gɔnwo mɔ a le awozinli nu amundubɛ ne mɔ.”
Zofaa
18Zofaa hanle kɛ,
“Wɔmɔ ɛse ‘Azuyilɛ pia amumuyɛma kɔ ndɛndɛ,
na bɛ afoa nu azɛlɛ ɛdeɛ ne, bɛwa ye amonle;
yɛɛ awie ɛnyɛ gyima wɔ ye vanye egyinli nu.
19Ewia pe a wuluwulu maa ezukɔtweaba kolo na ɔsesa,
zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɛtanevolɛma minli ɛbolɔ a.
20Mrɛladane arɛle fi bɛ; bɛdɔ azonlɛ;
bɛ aluma bɔbɔ, bɛngakye;
yemɔti amumuyɛnli bu tɔ kɛ baka la.’
21Bɛfo bɛgyinla mota mraalɛ akɔme zo,
yɛɛ bɛnze ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ anwunvɔne.
22Noko Nyamenle fa ye tumi ne maa mgbolema mekɛ tendenle;
bɛ anyelazo wie a, bɛmaa bɛ nwo zo bieko.
23Ɔbɔ bɛ nwo bane, ɔmaa bɛgyinla boɛ;
yɛɛ ɔ nye wɔ bɛ ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu.
24Ɔkpogya bɛ zo ekyii, noko ɔngyɛ ɛnee bɛ bo zo ɛminli;
bɛnwoso na bɛwu kɛ ndile; bɛbu bɛ kɛ abɛlɛ.
25Saa ɔnle zɔ a, nwane a kɛha kɛ mele adalɛ,
kɛhile kɛ mɔɔ meha la ɛnle nɔhalɛ a?”

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
Beledade
1Beledade hanle kɛ,
2“Tumi nee ɛzulolɛ le Nyamenle ɛdeɛ,
ɔmaa anzonudwolɛ ba ye anwuma ɛleka ne.
3Nwane a kɛhola ye ɛlɔnema tia a?
Nwane a ye wienyi ne ɛnda ɔ nwo a?
4Ɛnee kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na sonla ayɛ tenlenenli wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu ɛ?
Anzɛɛ kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na dasanli mɔɔ raalɛ ɛwo ye la anwo ade ɛ?
5Nea, siane ne bɔbɔ ɛnda,
yɛɛ nwɔlɔra bɔbɔ anyunlu ɛnde wɔ ɔ nye zo;
6na akee sonla mɔɔ le kɛkɛba sonlɛ la,
sonla ra, mɔɔ le sone la!”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Na Dwobu hanle kɛ
2“Kɛ wɔzi wɔboa sonla mɔɔ ɛnlɛ tumi,
anzɛɛ wɔlie sonla mɔɔ ɛnlɛ anwosesebɛ la ɛ?
3Wɔdu sonla mɔɔ ɛnze nrɛlɛbɛ la folɛ kpalɛ,
na wɔva wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ ne bie wɔmaa ye ala ɛne!
4Nwane a ɛboa wɔ ɛmaa wɔha edwɛkɛ ɛhye mɔ a,
yɛɛ nwane a manle wɔ anwosesebɛ ɛhye mɔɔ wɔva wɔdendɛ la a?”
Beledade
5Beledade hanle kɛ,
“Azɛlɛ bo lɔ, mɔwuamra anwo wozo bɛ,
azule nee bɛ nuhua ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti.
6Ɛbolɔ la zolɛ wienyi wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu,
yɛɛ Abadɔn nwenle zolɛ wɔ ɔ nyunlu.
7Ɔtɛlɛ sɔlɔ anwomanyunlu ɔdwu
ɛleka mɔɔ debie biala ɛnle la,
na ɔmaa azɛlɛ noko sinze mɔɔ debie ɛnlɛ nu a.
8Ɔmaa nzule gyinla amungu nu,
noko amungu ne ɛnkpuke.
9Ɔkeda siane ne anyunlu,
na ɔfa amungu ɔkeda siane ne anye.
10Yepɛ sɛma yedo nzule ne mɔ anye,
yeva yegya wienyi nee awozinli ɛweɛne.
11Saa ɔtea mpila mɔɔ dedɛ anwomanyunlu la nu a,
ɛzulolɛ ka bɛ maa bɛkpusu.
12Ɔvale ye tumi ɔmanle nyevile guale diinyi;
ɔvale ye nrɛlɛbɛ ɔhunle nane sɛkyeravolɛ Releehabe.
13Ɔvale ye ɛnwomenle ɔmanle anwomanyunlu dele wienyi;
ɔvale ye tumi ne ɔhunle nyevile nu nane anwo ɛzulolɛ ne.
14Nea, ɛhye mɔ bɔbɔ le ye tumi ne anu ekyi bie;
ɔ ne ekyi bie a yɛte a,
na nwane a kɛhola kɛgyinla ye tumi kpole ne anloa a?”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
Dwobu
1Dwobu hanle kɛ,
2“Meka tease Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne mɔɔ ɛmaa mewie ye zɛ,
na yemaa me ɛkɛla ɛli nyane la kɛ,
3sumunli kenle ala mɔɔ mede ngoane nu,
na Nyamenle maa medie ɛnwomenle la,
4me nloa ɛnrɛkpula munzule edwɛkɛ,
na meava me tafinlima meabɔ adalɛ.
5Ɔkɛbɔ me tɔ kɛ menwɔha kɛ bɛle nɔhalɛ a;
mebagyinla kpundii kɛ menze nwolɛ bie
kɔkpula kɛ menwɔwu.
6“Melɛ me tenleneyɛlɛ ne anu kpundii,
menrɛgyakyi nu ɛlɛ;
me adwenle ɛmbu me fɔlɛ kenle bie maanle nu.
7“Bɛmaa me kpɔvolɛ ɛyɛ kɛ amumuyɛnli,
na mɔɔ ko tia me la ɛyɛ kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛnle tenlene la.
8Ɔluakɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la anyelazo wɔ ni,
saa Nyamenle ye ye zo a?
9Asoo ɔyia ngyegyelɛ na ɔfɛlɛ a
Nyamenle badie ye ɛzunlɛ?
10Asoo ɔ nye balie Tumivolɛ ne anwo?
Asoo ɔbazu yeavɛlɛ Nyamenle mekɛ biala?
11Mebahilehile wɔ kɛ Nyamenle tumi ne si de la;
debie biala mɔɔ fane Tumivolɛ ne anwo la, menrɛva menrɛvea.
12Bɛnlea, bɛ muala bɛnwu ye bɛ nye zo;
na duzu ati a akee bɛ muala bɛyɛ mgbane a?”
Zofaa
13Na Zofaa hanle kɛ,
“Kɛ Nyamenle si tea amumuyɛnli ne la ɛne,
yɛɛ agyadeɛ mɔɔ nzisima nyia fi Tumivolɛ ne ɛkɛ la ɛne.
14Saa ɔ mra so dɔɔnwo a, bɛwie dadeɛ nloa;
yɛɛ ɔ mra ɛnrɛli bɛ ko ɛnrɛyi.
15Menli mɔɔ kɛha ɔ nzi la, ewule tɔ bɛ avinli sɛkye bɛ;
yɛɛ bɛ ye mɔ ɛnrɛzu ɛnrɛye bɛ awolɛ.
16Ɔbahuohua dwɛtɛ fufule nloa kɛ anwea,
na yeahuohua ndakpa nloa kɛ ndɛtɛlɛ edukue,
17noko mɔɔ di nɔhalɛ la a baheda a,
na menli mɔɔ ɛnze nwolɛ bie la ahyɛ ye dwɛtɛ fufule ne ava.
18Ye sua mɔɔ ɔsi la le kɛ kɛdɛba ndenda,
ɔle kɛ sinzavolɛ kpɔda.
19Kenle ko ɔbala kɛ sukoavolɛ, noko ɔnrɛla zɔ bieko;
ɔkatete ɔ nye zo la ɛnee ye anwonyia ne ɛwie.
20Ɛzulolɛ monla ye kɛ azuyilɛ;
nɔɔzo, ahumuakyima fa ye kɔ.
21Aduduleɛ anwoma kpogya ye zo kɔ;
ɔtu ye ɔfi ye tɛnlabelɛ ne.
22Ɔfuandi ye ɔto; ɔnze ye anwunvɔne,
ɔnriandi ɔfi ye tumi ne abo.
23Ɔnriandi la ɛnee ɔ nwo anwoma ne ɛlɛsu huu,
na anwoma ne ane ne ka ye ɛzulolɛ.

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
Nrɛlɛbɛ ɛhanvolɛ
1“Kuma wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛtu dwɛtɛ fufule nu,
yɛɛ ɛleka wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛtu ezukoa nvutuke nu a.
2Bɛtu bulalɛ wɔ azɛlɛ bo,
yɛɛ bɛtwe kɔbele bɛfi awolɛ nu.
3Menli ɛndie awozinli kabikabi ne,
bɛfunvu azɛlɛ bo ahuma kuloonwu
bɛtu awolɛ wɔ awozinli kabikabi ne anu.
4Bɛfunvu ahuma wɔ bɔnza mɔɔ menli ɛnle nu la anu,
ɛleka mɔɔ adendulɛma ɛnze la,
bɛkenda nyɛma nwo na bɛdi ehono bɛkɔ bɛba.
5Aleɛ vi azɛlɛ nu a ba a,
na ɔ bo lɔ, ɔtu ɔfonyia kɛ senle la nu.
6Ezukoa awolɛ anye buluwu wɔ ye awolɛ ne mɔ anu,
yɛɛ ezukoa nvutuke wɔ ye ndɛtɛlɛ ne mɔ anu.
7Adenle zɔhane, anloma mɔɔ di nane la ɛnze ye,
yɛɛ kyɛnyema nye ɛtɛnwunle ɛkɛ ne ɛlɛ.
8Nane anwo ɛzulolɛ biala agyakɛ ɛtɛtiale ɛkɛ,
yɛɛ awenade bɔbɔ ɛtɛpɛle nu ɛkɛ.
9“Sonla funvu awolɛ mɔɔ yɛ se la anu,
na ɔfunvu awoka ne mɔ abo.
10Ɔpepɛ ndenle wɔ awolɛ ne mɔ anu,
na ɔnwu debie biala mɔɔ sonle bolɛ la.
11Ɔsi azudenle ne mɔ, amaa bɛanzenze,
na ɔtwe debie mɔɔ vea la ɔfinde wienyi nu.
12Noko nienwu yɛɛ yɛkɛnwu nrɛlɛbɛ a,
yɛɛ ndelebɛbo wɔ ni?
13“Dasanli ɛnze ye adenle,
yɛɛ bɛnnwu ye wɔ anyewɔzoma anu.
14Buma se, ‘Ɔnle me lɔ’,
yɛɛ nyevile se, ‘Ɔnle me lɔ’.
15Bɛnzu ezukoa nvutuke bɛndɔ,
yɛɛ bɛnzu dwɛtɛ fufule bɛndɔ.
16Ezukoa nvutuke tagyee bɔbɔ bolɛ nee ye ɛnzɛ,
ezukoa awolɛ ‘ɔnekese’ nee ‘safaya’ nee ye ɛnzɛ bolɛ.
17Ezukoa nvutuke nee neanleɛ nee ye ɛnzɛ,
yɛɛ bɛfa bɛsenza anwodeɛ nee ezukoa nvutuke tagyee a ɔnyɛ boɛ.
18Ezukoa awolɛ kɔkɔlɛ anzɛɛ fufule anye nwohyee,
bɛmɛ, bɛmbɔ bɛ aluma;
nrɛlɛbɛ sonle bolɛ tɛla ezukoa bolɛ biala
mɔɔ sonle bolɛ la.
19Yiteɔpea ezukoa bolɛ topaze nee ye ɛnzɛ,
yɛɛ bɛfa bɛto ezukoa nvutuke tagyee nwo a bɛnzɛ.
20“Na ɛnee akee nrɛlɛbɛ bo vi ni?
Nienwu a ndelebɛbo wɔ a?
21Bɛva bɛvea anyewɔzoamra kɔsɔɔti,
anwomanyunlu nloma bɔbɔ ɛnze.
22Ɛbolɔ nee Ewule se, ‘Yɛde ye bɛse bɛse.’
23“Nyamenle a ze ye adenle,
nee ɛleka mɔɔ ɔwɔ la a.
24Ɔluakɛ ɔnwu azɛlɛ ti nee ɔ bo,
yɛɛ ɔnwu debie biala mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la.
25Mɔɔ ɔvale tumi ɔmanle anwoma,
na ɔzuzule nzule ne mɔ kpole;
26mɔɔ ɔhyehyɛle ɛleka mɔɔ ezule tɔ dwu,
na ɔhilele ɛsɛnlɛmanye adenle ne la,
27akee ɔnwunle ye na ɔbɔle ye nolo;
ɔnwunle bolɛ mɔɔ ɔsonle la, na ɔliele ye ɔdole nu.
28 “Na ɔzele sonla kɛ,
‘Nrɛlɛbɛ a le kɛ ɛkɛzulo Awulae;
yɛɛ ndelebɛbo a le kɛ ɛkɛhwe ɛ nwo ɛkɛvi ɛtane nwo!’ ”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
Dwobu edwɛkɛ mɔɔ li amozi
1Dwobu bɔle ɔ bo dendɛle bieko.
Dwobu
2Ɔse, “O, anrɛɛ meazia meayɛ kɛ me dɛba ne,
mɔɔ ɛnee Nyamenle sinza me la;
3mɔɔ ɛnee ye kɛnlaneɛ ne ta me nwo zo,
na ɔmanle menwunle aze wɔ awozinli nu;
4kɛmɔ ɛnee me anwonyia ɛyɛ kpole,
na Nyamenle agɔnwolɛyɛlɛ ne wɔ me awuke nu;
5mɔɔ ɛnee Tumivolɛ ne nee me de,
na me mra ɛbɔ ɛyia me;
6mɔɔ ɛnee meleke ɛbu me nwo zo,
na bodane manle nwole bule kɛ azudenle manle me la.
7Mɔɔ mengɔle suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa,
mɔɔ menzieziele me ebia na mendɛnlanle aze,
8mgbavolɛ ne mɔ nwunle me na bɛhwenle bɛ nwo,
na mgbanyinli ne mɔ dwazole gyinlanle.
9Mgbanyima gyakyile ɛdendɛlɛ,
na bɛvale bɛ sa bɛsosɔle bɛ nloa;
10mgbanyima bɔbɔ yɛle ngungoonwu,
na awie biala muanle ɔ nloa.
11“Awie biala mɔɔ diele me la hanvole me,
yɛɛ awie biala mɔɔ nwunle me la liele me dole nu;
12ɔboalekɛ menliele ehyianvolɛma mɔɔ zunle vɛlɛle me,
na memboale nrisa mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awie ɛmboa bɛ la.
13Menli mɔɔ asɛɛ ɛdɔ nzonle la yileyilale me,
na memanle ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ dole anyelielɛ edwɛne.
14Membule pɛlepɛlelilɛ tɛladeɛ menwulale,
na me nɔhalɛlilɛ yɛle kɛ tɛladeɛ nee abɔtile.
15Menyɛle anyenzinliravolɛma anye,
na menyɛle abuburama agyakɛ.
16Menyɛle ehyianvolɛma bɛ ze,
na memkpondɛle mɔɔ menze ye la anzi adenle.
17Mendudule mɔɔ ɛnli pɛlepɛle la agye,
memanle ɔdole mɔɔ ɔlɛ ye ɔ gye nu la aze.
18“Akee mendwenlenle kɛ mebanyi meahyɛ,
na meawu meala me sua nu koonwu.
19Me ndinli dendenle dwule nzule nu,
na me nya ne mɔ nyianle nɔɔzo ɛbɔlɛ,
20anyunlunyia yɛle me ɛdeɛ dahuu,
yɛɛ dahuu me ɛda le amolɛ wɔ me sa nu.
21Menli hendɛle diele me,
na bɛyɛle ngungoonwu bɛdiele me folɛdulɛ.
22Metendɛ mewie a bɛmbuke bɛ nloa bieko,
na me edwɛkɛ dɔle bɛ nwo zo.
23Bɛhendɛle me kɛ bɛkendɛ ezule;
na bɛbukebukele bɛ nloa kɛ asɛɛ bɛkendɛ nyenyesuo.
24Kɛmɔ bɛnlie bɛ nwo bɛnli la ati, menzelele;
na me nloa anwo ɛzelekɛ yɛle akɛnrazilɛ manle bɛ.
25Mengilele bɛ adenle na mendɛnlanle kɛ belemgbunli,
mendɛnlanle kɛ belemgbunli de ye ɛlɔnema avinli,
menzɔle bɛ kɛ sonla mɔɔ kyekye nyanelilɛma arɛle.

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1“Noko nea, me sa nu nlɔma ɛnɛ golo me nwo,
bɛ ze mɔ bɔbɔ anrɛɛ nee me ahwea ɛnrɛbɔ nu ɛnrɛzinza me mboane.
2Duzu nvasoɛ yɛɛ menwɔnyia ye bɛ nwo zo a?
Bɛdabɛ mumua ne bɛ anwosesebɛ ɛwie.
3Ehyia nee ɛhɔne maa bɛdi ɛsɛlɛ zo ɛva ketekete ne.
4Bɛnrenlenrenle ɛsɛlɛ zo mbaka nwo bɛtete nya nya bɛdi,
na bɛdi mbaka bo ndinli bɛmaa bɛ nwo yɛ wuluwulu.
5Bɛtu bɛ bɛfi menli avinli;
bɛwudo bɛ kɛ asɛɛ bɛwudo awule.
6Bɛda ɛzezeane ahuma mgbole nu,
yɛɛ azɛlɛ bo nee awolɛ mbɔne nu.
7Bɛsu kɛ nane wɔ kpɔkɛ ne mɔ abo;
na bɛnyenya bɛ nwo bɛda mbowumbaka bo.
8Bɛle gyibivolɛma ekpunli mɔɔ anwo ɛnlɛ nvasoɛ,
na bɛbo bɛ bɛdu bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo.
9“Kɛkala bɛfa me bɛto edwɛne,
na meyɛ bɛ agolobɛnwo sonla.
10Bɛkyi me, bɛmbikye me;
bɛnwu me a bɛto me nwo nyɛlɛ.
11Kɛmɔ Nyamenle ɛbɛlɛ me aze la,
yemaa bɛva bɛ ɛya bɛgua me nwo zo.
12Kpamgbanvolɛma ɛhye mɔ dwazo me fema zo,
bɛtu me mgbaliko, bɛfoa me ndinlizo,
na bɛboɔboa bɛ nwo kɛ bɛsɛkye me bɔkɔɔ.
13Bɛtua me adenle bɛtinli me nyane nu;
noko awie biala ɛnze bɛ kɛ bɛgyakyi.
14Bɛbɔ bɛfa me ɛvealeka bane ne anu,
na bɛtietia me nwo zo bɛkɔ.
15Ɛzulolɛ kpole ɛha me;
me enililɛ ɛze kɛ anwoma,
yɛɛ me anwonyia ne ɛminli kɛ amungu.
16“Kɛkala me ɛkɛla bɔbɔ vi me nu ɛnriandi;
nyane ngome ɛva me aze.
17Nɔɔzo me mbowule nu bu me,
yɛɛ me nwo ɛngyakyi me ɛfofolɛ.
18Nyamenle ɛva ɛya ɛzɔ me nu,
ye ɛya ne kyekye me kɛ me anwuma tɛladeɛ kɔme.
19Nyamenle ɛvuandi me ɛdo azia nu,
yemaa meyɛ kɛ ndɛtɛlɛ nee nzonle.
20“Mesu mefɛlɛ wɔ, na ɛnlie me zo;
mesɛlɛ, noko ɛndie me.
21Wɔyɛ me atisesebɛ;
ɛfa wɔ tumi kpole ne ɛyɛ me kpɔdekpɔde.
22Ɛkpogya me zo wɔ anwoma gye nu,
ɛmaa medua zolɛ,
na wɔamaa ahumu ne ali me fuandisɔ.
23Ɛhɛe, meze kɛ ɛbamaa meawu,
na meahɔ ɛleka mɔɔ teasema amuala wɔ la.
24Noko asoo sonla mɔɔ de ewula edukue nu la
ɛndende ɔ sa, na ɔnzɛlɛ moalɛ wɔ ye nyanenwunlɛ nu ɔ?
25Asoo meanzu meammaa menli ne mɔɔ alehyenlɛ ne anu yɛ se maa bɛ la?
Asoo me ɛkɛla anli nyane ammaa ehyianvolɛma?
26Noko mɔɔ memkpondɛle kpalɛ la, ɛtane a rale a;
yɛɛ mengendɛle wienyi, na awozinli a rale a.
27Me ahonle ɛlɛdi nyane, yɛɛ ɔngyakyi;
kɛ nyanelilɛ ne doɔdoa zo ala ɛne.
28Dahuu melua awozinli nu, menze sɛnzɛne deɛ holɛ;
medwazo menli nu, na mesu mebiza moalɛ.
29Me mediema mrenya a le ɛzonlɛ,
yɛɛ me gɔnwo mɔ a le soholo.
30Me nwonane kpunli na ɔtete ɔgua,
yɛɛ me mbowule nu dɔ kɛ ɔgyi senle zo.
31Me getaa edwɛne ɛhakyi awolɛyelɛ,
yɛɛ me fulutu edwɛne ɛhakyi ɛzunlɛ.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
1“Me nee me nye ɛyɛ ngyekyeleɛ;
kɛ menrɛnlea bɛlɛra mɔɔ ɛnze nrenya la menrɛhulo ye.
2“Me kyɛfoa mɔɔ vi anwuma Nyamenle ɛkɛ ne la a le duzu,
yɛɛ me agyadeɛ mɔɔ wɔ anwuma Tumivolɛ ne ɛkɛ la a le duzu?
3Asoo munzule ɛndo menli mɔɔ ɛnle tenlene la,
yɛɛ nyane ɛndo amumuyɛma?
4Asoo ɔnnwu me ndenle ne mɔ,
na ɔnnea me gyakɛ ɛdudulɛ ne mɔ ɔ?
5“Saa membɔ adalɛ wɔ me ɛlualɛ nu,
na menli mɛlɛbɛla nzi a,
6ɛnee Nyamenle ɛzuzu me wɔ nɔhalɛ tone zo,
na ɔbanwu kɛ menze nwolɛ bie.
7Saa mengyakyi nɔhalɛ adenle ne,
memaa me nye ɛbɛlɛbɛla me ahonle,
na menli ɛtane nwo fɔlɛ a,
8ɛnee maa menlua, na sonla gyɛne ɛli;
mɔɔ melua la, maa bɛdudu bɛgua.
9“Saa raalɛ ɛhwe me ahonle,
na medɛ ye me gɔnwo anlenkɛ nloa a,
10ɛnee maa me ye ɛdo nrenya fofolɛ aleɛ,
na maa nrenya gyɛne ɛvo ye ɛzɔlɛ zo.
11Ɔluakɛ ɛhye le munzule kpole,
mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ ndɛnebuavolɛma nea
maa bɛtua menli nwolɛ kakɛ a;
12ɔluakɛ ɔle kɛ ɛbolɔ senle,
na ɔbayela mɔɔ melɛ la amuala.
13“Saa me sonvolɛ nrenya anzɛɛ raalɛ
ɛrabɔ me somolɛ, na mekpo ye,
14na saa Nyamenle dwazo a, duzu a mebayɛ a?
Saa ɔbizebiza nuhua a, kɛ menwɔzi menwɔye ɔ nloa ɛ?
15Na tɛ mɔɔ bɔle me dole ɔmɔ akunlu la a bɔle ɔdaye ɔ,
yɛɛ yeambɔ yɛ wɔ ɛkolɛ nu ɔ?
16“Metɛkpole kɛ menrɛboa ehyianli,
anzɛɛ menrɛmaa kunlanvolɛ raalɛ ɛnrɛzu ɔ nye ɛnrɛbɔ nu,
17anzɛɛ me ngomekye menrɛli me aleɛ,
na menrɛmaa nrisa bie ɛnrɛli a.
18Ɔluakɛ ɔvi me ngakula nu, menyɛle nrisa bɛ ze,
mevi ɔmɔ akunlu ala la, meneanle ahunlanvolɛ.
19“Saa menwu kɛ awie ɛnlɛ ɛdanlɛ la ati ɔlɛwu,
anzɛɛ ehyianvolɛ bie ɛnlɛ bie ɛngua ɔ nwo a,
20memaa ye kundu mɔɔ meva me mboane enrinli menwo la,
na ɔyeye ye ahonle nu ɔyileyila me.
21“Saa mesisi arisa ɛlɛ,
ɔluakɛ melɛ moalɛ wɔ mgbanyima ne mɔ ɛkɛ a,
22ɛnee maa me awane vi me bati ɛkpane,
na maa me sa baka ne ɛdu ɛdɔ.
23Ɔluakɛ ɛnee mesulo Nyamenle ndeanlɛ ne,
yɛɛ eza anrɛɛ menrɛhola ɔ nyunlu gyinla.
24“Saa menva ezukoa menyɛ me nyamenle,
anzɛɛ menva me rɛle menwula ezukoa nvutuke tagyee nu;
25saa menli fɛlɛko kɛ me anwonyia ɛyɛ kpole,
anzɛɛ kɛmɔ me sa ɛyi tɛkɛɛ la;
26saa ewia ne fi la meneanle ye,
anzɛɛ siane ne ɛdalɛ kɛnlɛma ne,
27na bɛhwe me ahonle,
bɛmaa me sa ɛha me nloa menzonle bɛ a,
28ɛhye noko ɛyɛ munzule ɛmaa me,
na ndɛnebuavolɛma ɛdua me nwolɛ kakɛ,
ɔluakɛ ɛnee meanli nɔhalɛ
meammaa Nyamenle mɔɔ wɔ anwuma la.
29“Metɛdile me kpɔvolɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ nwo fɛlɛko,
anzɛɛ metɛdile fɛlɛko kɛ munzule dole ye;
30metɛfale me nloa metɛkanle ɛtane,
metɛwale me kpɔvolɛ amonle kɛ ɔwu;
31asoo me awuke nu amra ɛtɛkanle kɛ,
‘Nwane a ɛtɛdile ye debie ɛlɛ a?’
32Adendulɛma ɛtɛsokoɛle gua zo ɛlɛ,
mebuke me nlenkɛ memaa nyɛvolɛ.
33“Saa menva me ɛtane ne mɔ menvea kɛ ebia mɔ,
menva me munzulebɔlɛ menvea me nwo,
34kɛmɔ ɛnee mesulo menli pemgbenleamgbe ne,
na menzulole kɛ mbusua ɛnrɛbu me la ati,
menyɛle koonwu, meanvinde alie nwo a.
35“O, anrɛɛ meanyia awie adie me!
Me edwɛkɛ ne amuala ɛne!
Bɛmaa Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne ɛbua me.
“O, anrɛɛ me kpɔvolɛ ne ahɛlɛ
me munzule mɔɔ mebɔ la kɔsɔɔti amaa meanwu ye.
36Nɔhalɛ, anrɛɛ menwɔzoa ye me kɔme zo;
anrɛɛ menwɔzoa ye kɛ belemgbunli kyɛlɛ;
37anrɛɛ menwɔbu me nwo mgbonda menwɔhile ye,
na meahɔ ɔ nyunlu kɛ mele belemgbunli ra.
38“Saa memaa azɛlɛ ne azo gyimayɛvoma
ɛhwi monle ɛgua kɔfie ne mɔ azo,
39kɛ meli zolɛ aleɛ ne
na meandua bɛ kakɛ memaa bɛwu a,
40ɛnee kɛmɔ hwiiti kɛfifi zolɛ la, mbowule ɛfifi zolɛ,
yɛɛ kɛmɔ baale kɛfifi zolɛ la, ndile ɛfifi zolɛ.”

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
Ɛlaehu Edwɛkɛ ne
(32.1—37.24)
1Dwobu nea ɔ nwo a ɔle tenlenenli, yemɔti menli nsa ne angola ambua ye edwɛkɛ ne anwo. 2Na Buzinli Baleekɛle mɔɔ vi Relam abusua nu la ara nrenya Ɛlaehu vale ɛya. Ɔvale Dwobu anwo ɛya, ɔboalekɛ Dwobu buale ɔ nwo benle na ɔvale ɛzonle ɔdole Nyamenle anwo zo. 3Eza ɔvale Dwobu agɔnwo mɔ nsa ne anwo ɛya, ɔboalekɛ bɛhanle kɛ Dwobu le ɛtanevolɛ bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko bɛanyia nu kile kpalɛ biala. 4Kɛmɔ Ɛlaehu le kakula la ati, ɔhendɛle ɔmanle bɛwiele tendɛ kolaa na ɔdaye yeadendɛ yeahile Dwobu. 5Ɛlaehu hendɛle toonwo na ɔnwunle kɛ bɛnlɛ mualɛ kpaziwɔkɛ biala bɛmbua Dwobu la, ɔvale ɛya, 6na ɔbɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔtendɛ. Ɔse,
Ɛlaehu
“Mele kakula, bɛmɛ bɛle mgbanyinli,
yemɔti menyɛle foanvoanle, na menzulole
kɛ menwɔva me adwenle menwɔdo gua wɔ bɛ nyunlu.
7Menzele me nwo kɛ bɛmaa mgbanyinli ɛdendɛ,
na egyɛnema ɛhile bɛ nrɛlɛbɛ ne.
8Noko sunsum ne mɔɔ wɔ sonla nu,
Tumivolɛ ne ɛnwomenle ne
yɛɛ maa sonla nyia ndelebɛbo a.
9Tɛ mgbanyinli ngome yɛɛ ze nrɛlɛbɛ a,
yɛɛ tɛ egyɛnema angome a te mɔɔ le fɔɔnwo la abo a.
10Yemɔti mese, bɛdie me;
bɛmaa medame mengile me adwenle.
11“Bɛnlea, mengendɛle toonwo memanle bɛwiele tendɛ,
mendiele bɛ nrɛlɛbɛ edwɛkɛ ne mɔ amuala,
wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛlɛdwenle mɔɔ bɛka la anwo la.
12Menzile abotane mendiele bɛ, na bɛnlea,
bɛ nuhua biala angola ambua Dwobu angile kɛ ɔdi fɔlɛ,
bɛ biala ambua Dwobu edwɛkɛ ne anwo kpaziwɔkɛ nu biala.
13Bɛnlea boɛ na bɛanga kɛ, ‘Yɛnwu nrɛlɛbɛ;
anzɛɛ Nyamenle a bali ɔ nwo zo konim a, tɛ dasanli ɔ’.
14Ɔtɛkanle edwɛkɛ biala ɔtɛtiale me,
yemɔti menrɛbua ye, kɛmɔ bɛmɛ bɛbuale ye la.
15“Dwobu, mɔɔ bɛka la ɛwie, bɛnlɛ mualɛ bieko;
bɛnlɛ edwɛkɛkpɔkɛ ko bɔbɔ bɛnga.
16Kɛmɔ bɛndɛ bɛ nloa anu,
na bɛgyigyi ɛkɛ ne, na bɛnlɛ mualɛ biala la ati,
ɛnee ɔnle kɛ metendɛ ɔ?
17Medame noko mebabua nwolɛ,
na meahile me adwenle.
18Ɔluakɛ edwɛkɛ ɛyi me ti tɛkɛɛ,
sunsum ne mɔɔ wɔ me nu la se mendendɛ.
19Bɛnlea, me ahonle ɛyɛ kɛ nwanye mɔɔ bɛdua zo
wɔ toba nu la,
me ahonle le kɛ nwanye nwoma fofolɛ,
ɔkpondɛ yeakpuke.
20Ɔwɔ kɛ metendɛ, na me ahonle adɔ me azule nu;
ɔwɔ kɛ mebuke me nloa mebua wɔ.
21Menrɛli mɔguazo biala,
yɛɛ menrɛva ɛtafinlimalɛ menlemenle
menrɛbɛlɛbɛla awie biala.
22Ɔluakɛ menze adalɛ bɔ,
meyɛ ye zɔ a me Bɔvolɛ ne kɛhu me.

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
1“Na kɛkala, Dwobu, akee tie me ɛdendɛlɛ,
na tie mɔɔ meka la amuala.
2Nea, mebuke me nloa;
akee mebadendɛ meahile wɔ.
3Me edwɛkɛ ne vi me ahonle nu fɔɔnwo,
yɛɛ mɔɔ melɛka la le nɔhalɛ.
4Nyamenle sunsum ne ɛbɔ me,
yɛɛ Tumivolɛ ne ɛnwomenle ne maa me ngoane.
5“Saa ɛkola a, bua me;
siezie wɔ edwɛkɛ ne mɔ agbɔkɛ; na gyinla boɛ.
6Nea, melua Nyamenle adenle ne anu kɛ ɛdawɔ ala la,
medame noko bɛvale ndɛtɛlɛ a bɛbɔle me a.
7Nea, mmamaa wɔ ahonle tu na ɛsulo me,
menrɛmia wɔ kpole biala menrɛmaa ɛ nwo ɛnrɛhyele wɔ.
8“Nɔhalɛ, wɔdendɛ wɔmaa mede,
yɛɛ mede wɔ edwɛkɛ ne.
9Ɛse, ‘Me nwo te, metɛyɛle ɛtane biala;
me ɛbɛla le bɔkɔbɔkɔ, metɛyɛle ninyɛmunli biala.
10Nea, ɔkpondɛ edwɛkɛ yeatia me,
ɔbu me kɛ mele ye kpɔvolɛ.
11 Ɔbɔ me gyakɛ kpanwu,
na ɔnea me gyakɛ biala mɔɔ metu la.’
12“Nea, ɛhye ɛnle nɔhalɛ. Mebabua wɔ.
Nyamenle le kpole tɛla dasanli.
13Duzu ati a ɛbɔ ye somolɛ kɛ
ɔnrɛbua wɔ edwɛkɛ ne mɔ ko bɔbɔ anwo a?
14Ɔluakɛ Nyamenle tendɛ ko ala,
ɔka ye nwiɔ, noko dasanli ɛndie ye.
15 Wɔ ɛlalɛ nu, nɔɔzo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ nu,
mɔɔ nafelɛ kɛdɔ menli nwo zo,
na bɛdeda bɛ mgba ne mɔ azo la,
16akee ɔbuke menli nzo,
ɔbɔ bɛ kɔkɔ, ɔmaa ɛzulolɛ ka bɛ,
17amaa yeahwe sonla yeavi ye nyɛleɛ nwo,
na yeaye mgbanyizonle yeavi ye nu.
18Ɔtwe sonla ɛkɛla ɔfi ewule kuma nu,
na ɔdie ye ɔfi dadeɛ nloa.
19Bɛfa nyanenwunlɛ bɛtea sonla,
na ɔte nyane wɔ ye mbowule nu,
20amaa ɔ nloa anu ado,
na yeakpo ye atiakunluwɔzo aleɛ.
21Ɔnwa ɔyɛ nrenzenrenze mɔɔ bɛnnwu ye sonla holɛ,
na ye mbowule sa gua zo sanrɛlaanye.
22Ye ɛkɛla bikye ewule,
ye ngoane dwu ewule soanvolɛma asa anu.
23“Saa ɔnyia Nyamenle soanvolɛma
apenle apenle ne mɔ anu kamaavolɛ ko,
mɔɔ maa yeanwu mɔɔ le kpalɛ maa ye,
24mɔɔ yɛ ahunlunyele amaa ye, yeaze kɛ,
‘Die ye fi ewule nu,
menyia ɛkpɔnedeɛ,
25maa ye nwonane ɛzia ɛyɛ kɛ ye mgbavolɛ nu,
na ɔnyia ye mgbavolɛ nu anwosesebɛ ne bieko’ a,
26anrɛɛ sonla sɛlɛ Nyamenle a, ɔtie ye;
na ɔfa fɛlɛkolilɛ ɔba Nyamenle anyunlu bieko.
Ɔbɔ ye ngoanelielɛ ne nolo ɔkile menli,
27na ɔto edwɛne ɔkile menli, ɔse kɛ,
‘Menyɛle ɛtane, na mengyile nɔhalɛ,
na meannyia nwolɛ ndeanlɛ.
28Yelie me yevi ewule nu,
na mezia mera ngoane nu.’
29“Nea, Nyamenle yɛ ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ amuala
fane kɛyɛ nyɛ maa sonla,
30amaa yealie ye yeavi ewule nu,
na yeava ye yeara ngoane nu.
31“Dwobu, gyele ɛ nzo tie mɔɔ melɛka la;
yɛ koonwu maa mendendɛ!
32Saa ɛlɛ edwɛkɛ a, ka maa mendie;
tendɛ, ɔluakɛ mekulo kɛ mebua wɔ benle.
33Saa ɛnlɛ edwɛkɛ a, ɛnee tie me;
yɛ koonwu maa mengile wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
translation_text:
1-2“Bɛdie me, bɛmɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma,
bɛmɛ mɔɔ bɛze deɛ, bɛmaa bɛ nzo ɛrɛla ɛke;
3 ɔluakɛ ɛnzonlɛ te edwɛkɛ,
kɛmɔ ɛtafinlimalɛ te aleɛ fɛlɛko la.
4Bɛmaa yɛva nuhua mɔɔ le nɔhalɛ,
na yɛhile kpalɛ mɔɔ wɔ nu la.
5Ɔluakɛ Dwobu se, ‘Menli fɔlɛ,
Nyamenle ɛbua me mgbɔvodɛne.
6Mɔɔ melɛka nɔhalɛ bɔbɔ la,
ɛnee bɛse mele adalɛ;
menyɛ ninyɛndane,
noko me hanlɛ ɛngɔ ɛlɛ.’
7“Duzu sonla bɔbɔ a le Dwobu,
mɔɔ tendɛ ɛtane zɛhae,
8mɔɔ nee ɛtanevolɛma tu,
na ɔ nee amumuyɛma tu fane a?
9Ɔluakɛ ɔse, ‘Nvasoɛ biala ɛnle zo
kɛ dasanli anye kɛlie Nyamenle anwo.’
10“Yemɔti, bɛmɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛ ndelebɛbo la, bɛdie me,
ɔle bɛkyi kɛ Nyamenle kɛyɛ amumuyɛ,
anzɛɛ Tumivolɛ ne kɛyɛ ɛtane.
11 Ɔluakɛ kɛ sonla kɛzi kɛyɛ ye gyima la,
nwolɛ yɛɛ ɔbanlea yeadua ye kakɛ a,
yɛɛ kɛ ɔkɛzi ɔkɛbɔ ye ɛbɛla ne la,
yɛɛ ɔwie ye a.
12Nɔhalɛ, Nyamenle ɛnrɛyɛ amumuyɛ,
yɛɛ Tumivolɛ ne ɛnrɛli mɔguazo.
13Nwane a vale azɛlɛ ye wulale ye tumi bo a,
yɛɛ nwane a vale ewiade ye wulale ɔ sa nu a?
14Saa ɔdie ye sunsum ne
nee ye ɛnwomenle ne a,
15menli kɔsɔɔti bawu,
na sonla azia ahɔ ndɛtɛlɛ nu.
16“Saa bɛlɛ ndelebɛbo a, bɛdie ɛhye;
bɛdie mɔɔ meka la.
17Asoo sonla mɔɔ kyi pɛlepɛlelilɛ la sie maanle?
Asoo ɛkɛbua sonla mɔɔ di pɛlepɛle
na ɔle katakyie la ewule fɔlɛ,
18yemɔ mɔɔ ɔkola ɔse belemgbunli kɛ, ‘Sonlamgbane,’
na ɔse mgbolema kɛ, ‘Amumuyɛma’ la.
19Ɔnnea mgbanyima nyunlu ɔnli mɔguazo,
yɛɛ ɔmbu sukoavolɛma ɔndɛla ehyianvolɛma,
ɔluakɛ bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛle ɔ sa anloa gyima.
20Ɔngyɛ ɛnee bɛwu;
alevinli mu nwiɔ avinli bɛ ahonle tu na bɛwu,
yɛɛ tɛ sonla a ku mgbolema a.
21Ɔluakɛ ɔnwu sonla ndenle nu,
yɛɛ ɔnwu ɔ gyakɛ biala mɔɔ ɔtu la.
22Awozinli ɛnle ɛleka biala
mɔɔ ɛtanevolɛma fea nu a ɔyɛ boɛ a.
23Ɔluakɛ ɔtɛkilele sonla biala mekɛ
kɛ ɔhɔ Nyamenle anyunlu ɔmaa bɛbua ye ndɛne.
24Ɔngyia nvedenvedenu na yeadu mgbolema,
yeava fofolɛ yeazie bɛ gyakɛ anu.
25Kɛmɔ ɔze mɔɔ bɛyɛ la ati,
ɔtu bɛ nɔɔzo na ɔyɛ bɛ kpasakpasa.
26Bɛ amumuyɛ ti, ɔtea bɛ bagua nu,
27ɔboalekɛ bɛkpole kɛ bɛnrɛdoa ɔ bo zo,
yɛɛ bɛanli ye mɛla ne mɔ biala azo.
28Ɔlua zo ehyianvolɛma ɛzunlɛ dwule ɔ nzo nu,
na ɔdele nyanenwunlɛma ɛzunlɛ.
29“Saa ɔyɛ koonwu a, nwane a kɛbu ye fɔlɛ a,
yɛɛ ɔfea ɔ nwo a, nwane a kɛnwu ye a,
saa maanle o anzɛɛ sonla ko o?
30Ɔnle kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la di belemgbunli
anzɛɛ yɛ ɛhane maa maanlema.
31“Asoo awie ɛha ɛhile Nyamenle kɛ,
‘Menyia ɛtane nwo ndeanlɛ; menrɛyɛ ɛtane ko;
32kilehile me mɔɔ mennwu ye la;
saa meyɛ ɛtane a, menrɛyɛ ko?’
33Kɛmɔ wɔkpo ɛtane la ati,
ɔwɔ kɛ Nyamenle yɛ mɔɔ wɔmɔ ɛkulo la ɔ?
Ɛdawɔ yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ ɛka a, tɛ mame ɔ;
yemɔti mɔɔ ɛlɛ ye la, ka maa yɛdie.
34“Menli mɔɔ lɛ ndelebɛbo la baze me,
yɛɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma mɔɔ tie me la baze kɛ,
35‘Dwobu ɛndendɛ nrɛlɛbɛ nu,
edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ ɔkɛha la, ndelebɛbo ɛnle nu.’
36Anrɛɛ bɛazɔ Dwobu bɛanlea bɛahɔ awieleɛ,
ɔboalekɛ ɔye edwɛkɛ nloa kɛ amumuyɛma.
37Ɔluakɛ ɔfa atuadelɛ ɔboka ye ɛtane ne mɔ anwo;
yɛ avinli ɛke, ɔbɔ ɔ sa nu
na ɔka mgbole ɔtia Nyamenle!

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
13If God All-Powerful refuses
to answer their empty prayers,
14he will surely deny
your impatient request
to face him in court.
15Job, you were wrong to say
God doesn't punish sin.
16Everything you have said
adds up to nonsense.
translation_text:
1-2“Dwobu, ɛdwenle kɛ ɛhye le fɔɔnwo,
kɛ ɛkɛha kɛ ɛdi benle wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu,
3mɔɔ yemɔti ɛbiza kɛ, ‘Duzu nvasoɛ a menyia a?
Saa meyɛ ɛtane a anrɛɛ kɛ mezi mekpazi ɛ?’
4Mebabua wɔ nee ɛ gɔnwo mɔ.
5“Bɛdo bɛ nye anwuma,
na bɛnlea amungu ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ bɛ ti zo anwuma la.
6 Saa bɛyɛ ɛtane a, duzu a bɛnyia ye
mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛnlɛ bie a?
Yɛɛ saa bɛ ninyɛmunli ne mɔ yɛ mɔnwo a,
duzu a bɛyɛ bɛmaa ye a?
7Saa ɛle tenlenenli a, duzu a ɛfa ɛmaa ye,
anzɛɛ duzu a ɔnyia ye ɔfi ɛ sa nu a?
8Wɔ amumuyɛ ne mɔ ka sonla mɔɔ le kɛ ɛdawɔ la,
yɛɛ wɔ tenleneyɛlɛ ka sonla ala.
9“Ɛsisilɛ bebelebe ti menli tea nu su;
bɛsu kɛ awie ɛlie bɛ ɛvi nzisi tumi bo.
10-11Na bɛ biala ɛnga kɛ,
‘Nyamenle me Bɔvolɛ,
mɔɔ maa meto edwɛne nɔɔzo,
mɔɔ kilehile yɛ tɛla azɛlɛ ye azo nane,
na ɔmaa yɛyɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma
yɛtɛla anwomanyunlu nloma la wɔ ni?’
12Bɛtea nu bɛsu, na ɔmbua bɛ,
ɔboalekɛ ɛtanevolɛma le mgbanyizonle.
13Nɔhalɛ, Nyamenle ɛndie ɛzunlɛ mgbane mgbane,
yɛɛ Tumivolɛ ne ɛmbu ye bɔbɔ.
14Dwobu, ɛse ɛnnwu Nyamenle;
noko wɔzi abotane ɛlɛkendɛ,
na wɔ edwɛkɛ ne la ɔ nyunlu.
15Kɛmɔ ɔnva ɛya ɔndwi sonla nyunlu,
na ɔntinli mɛladonlɛ ndeanlɛ zo ɛsesebɛ la ati,
16Dwobu buke ɔ nloa tendɛ ɛdendɛlɛ biala,
na ɔkeha edwɛkɛ mɔɔ nrɛlɛbɛ biala ɛnle nu la.”

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Be Patient a While Longer
1Elihu said:
2Be patient a while longer;
I have something else to say
in God's defense.
3God always does right—
and this knowledge
comes straight from God.
4You can rest assured
that what I say is true.
5Although God is mighty,
he cares about everyone
and makes fair decisions.
6The wicked are cut down,
and those who are wronged
receive justice.
7God watches over good people
and places them in positions
of power and honor forever.
8But when people are prisoners
of suffering and pain,
* 9God points out their sin
and their pride,
10then he warns them
to turn back to him.
11And if they obey,
they will be successful
and happy from then on.
12But if they foolishly refuse,
they will be rewarded
with a violent death.
Godless People Are Too Angry
13Godless people are too angry
to ask God for help
when he punishes them.
14So they die young
in shameful disgrace.
15Hard times and trouble
are God's way
of getting our attention!
16And at this very moment,
God deeply desires
to lead you from trouble
and to spread your table
with your favorite food.
17Now that the judgment
for your sins
has fallen upon you,
18don't let your anger
and the pain you endured
make you sneer at God.
19Your reputation and riches
cannot protect you
from distress,
20nor can you find safety
in the dark world below.
21Be on guard! Don't turn to evil
as a way of escape.
22God's power is unlimited.
He needs no teachers
23to guide or correct him.
Others Have Praised God
24Others have praised God
for what he has done,
so join with them.
25From down here on earth,
everyone has looked up and seen
26how great God is—
God is more than we imagine;
no one can count the years
he has lived.
* 27God gathers moisture
into the clouds
28and supplies us with rain.
29Who can understand
how God scatters the clouds
and speaks from his home
in the thunderstorm?
30And when God sends lightning,
it can be seen
at the bottom of the sea.
31By producing such rainstorms,
God rules the world
and provides us with food.
32Each flash of lightning
is one of his arrows
striking its target,
33and the thunder tells
of his anger against sin.
translation_text:
1-2“Dwobu, si abotane ekyii,
maa menga mengile wɔ,
megyi Nyamenle agyakɛ anu
melɛka edwɛkɛ meahile wɔ.
3Me adwenle ne abo vi moa,
me Bɔvolɛ ne di pɛlepɛle.
4Ɔluakɛ me edwɛkɛ ne ɛnle adalɛ;
sonla mɔɔ ye adwenle ɛdi la gyi ɛ nyunlu ɛke.
5“Nea, Nyamenle le bedevinli, ɔmkpo bie;
yɛɛ ye ndelebɛbo nu mia kpole kpalɛ.
6Ɔmmaa amumuyɛma ɛndɛnla aze ɛngyɛ,
na ɔmaa amaneɛnwunlɛma nyia bɛ gyinlabelɛ.
7Ɔnye ɔ nye wɔ tenlenema anwo zo,
ɔsiezie bɛ kɛ arelemgbunli na ɔkpogya bɛ zo dahuu.
8Saa bɛgua bɛ anga na anwubɛnyunlu kyekye bɛ a,
9ɛnee Nyamenle ɛmaa bɛnwu bɛ nyɛleɛ
nee bɛ ninyɛmunli ne mɔ;
kɛ bɛlɛyɛ mgbanyizonle.
10Ɔbuke bɛ nzo ɔmaa bɛte folɛ,
ɔmaa bɛtwe bɛ nwo bɛfi bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ anwo.
11Saa bɛtie ye na bɛsonle ye a,
bɛdi bɛ mekɛ ne anwonyia nu,
bɛdi bɛ ɛvolɛ ne mɔ wɔ anzonudwolɛ nu.
12Na saa bɛandie ye a, bɛbawu dadeɛ nloa,
na bɛawu ewule mɔɔ bɛnde ɔ bo a.
13“Menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la fa ɛya sie bɛ ahonle nu,
kanza bɛwɔ ngyianlɛ nu bɔbɔ a,
bɛnzu bɛnvɛlɛ Nyamenle moalɛ.
14Bɛwu bɛ mgbavolɛ nu,
yɛɛ bɛ awieleɛ wie anyiemgba nu.
15Nyamenle dua nyanenwunlɛma nyane zo die bɛ,
na ɔdua bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ zo ɔbuke bɛ nzo.
16“Eza Nyamenle yele wɔ vile nyanenwunlɛ nu
hɔle ɛleka wienyi mɔɔ anwodɔlɛ wɔ la,
na wɔ ɛkponle zo yɛle sosɔɔ.
17Na kɛkala, bɛva amumuyɛma ndeanlɛ bɛdea wɔ;
ndɛnebualɛ nee pɛlepɛlelilɛ ɛbɔ wɔ kpanwu.
18Nea boɛ anrɛɛ ɛyavalɛ kɛmaa bɛkɛgolo ɛ nwo;
yɛɛ mmamaa ɛkpɔnedeɛ ne kpole ti ɛfo adenle.
19Asoo wɔ ɛzunlɛ kɛye wɔ kɛvi nyanenwunlɛ nu,
anzɛɛ wɔ anwosesebɛ kɛhola kɛboa wɔ?
20Mmamaa ɛ nwo dɔ aledwolɛ ne,
mekɛ mɔɔ maanle maanle bo zo bɔ la ɛne.
21Nea boɛ, mmakakyi ɛkɔyɛ ɛtane,
ɔluakɛ wɔhulo ɛhye wɔdɛla amaneɛnwunlɛ.
22“Nea, Nyamenle tumi ne le kpole,
nwane a le kilehilevolɛ kɛ ɔdaye a?
23Nwane a ɛhola ɛhile ye adenle,
anzɛɛ nwane a kɛhola kɛze ye kɛ, ‘Wɔyɛ ɛtane’ a?
24Bɛhakye kɛ bɛkɛhanvo ye gyima ne,
mɔɔ menli ɛdo nwolɛ edwɛne la.
25Menli kɔsɔɔti ɛnwu ye;
sonla nwu ye moa moa.
26Bɛnlea, Nyamenle le kpole, noko yɛnze ye;
ye ɛvolɛ dodo, bɛnrɛnwu ye ɛlɛ.
27“Ɔluakɛ ɔtwe ezule mɔɔ pepe la ɔkɔ anwuma,
ɔtwe ezule ɔfi kpukpuke nu,
28na ɔvi anwomanyunlu ɔtɔ
ɔmaa sonla nyia bie dɔɔnwo.
29Asoo awie kɛhola kɛde kɛ amungu si tɛlɛdɛlɛ,
nee kɛ anwomanyunlu si kuluhulu la abo?
30Bɛnlea, ɔkpakye ɛsɛnlɛmanye ɔbɔ ɔ nwo mgbɔlɔka,
na ɔkeda nyevile buma bo azo.
31Ɔluakɛ ɛhye mɔ azo yɛɛ ɔdua ɔbua
maanle maanle ndɛne na ɔmaa aleɛ bu a.
32Ɔfa ɔ sa ɔsɔ ɛsɛnlɛmanye,
na ɔmaa ɔpe ɛleka mɔɔ ɔkpondɛ la.
33Ye ɛpenlɛ ne kile kɛ ɔsi ɔde la,
kɛ ye nungule ɛya ne tia ninyɛndane.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
I Am Frightened
1I am frightened
and tremble all over,
2when I hear the roaring voice
of God in the thunder,
3and when I see his lightning
flash across the sky.
4God's majestic voice
thunders his commands,
5creating miracles too marvelous
for us to understand.
6Snow and heavy rainstorms
7make us stop and think
about God's power,
8and they force animals
to seek shelter.
9The windstorms of winter strike,
10and the breath of God
freezes streams and rivers.
11Rain clouds filled with lightning
appear at God's command,
12traveling across the sky
13to release their cargo—
sometimes as punishment for sin,
sometimes as kindness.
Consider Carefully
14Job, consider carefully
the many wonders of God.
15Can you explain why lightning
flashes at the orders
16of God who knows all things?
Or how he hangs the clouds
in empty space?
17You almost melt in the heat
of fierce desert winds
when the sky is like brass.
18God can hammer out the clouds
in spite of the oppressive heat,
but can you?
19Tell us what to say to God!
Our minds are in the dark,
and we don't know how
to argue our case.
20Should I risk my life
by telling God
that I want to speak?
21No one can stare at the sun
after a breeze has blown
the clouds from the sky.
22Yet the glorious splendor
of God All-Powerful
is brighter by far.
23God cannot be seen—
but his power is great,
and he is always fair.
24And so we humans fear God,
because he shows no respect
for those who are proud
and think they know so much.
translation_text:
1“Ɛhye bɔbɔ maa me ahonle tu,
na ɔsi me kunlu.
2Tie kɛ ɔ ne ɛlɛsi ahulu bie a,
nee kpomgbanyekpomgbanye mɔɔ ɔlɛyɛ la.
3Ɔdwu aleɛabo ɛleka biala,
yɛɛ ye ɛsɛlɛmanye kpakye a
ɔdwu aleɛabo muleɛ biala azo.
4Ɛhye anzi, ɔ ne kulu;
ɔfa ye belemgbunli tumi ɛnelɛ ne ɔkulu,
yɛɛ kɛ bɛte ɔ ne ala la
ɛnee ɛvedelɛ ne doa ye.
5Nyamenle fa ɔ ne kulu ɛzulolɛ nu bie;
ɔyɛ ninyɛne mgbole mɔɔ yɛnrɛhola yɛnrɛde bɛ bo a.
6Ɔluakɛ ɔka ɔkile ezukɔtweaba kɛ,
‘Tɔ azɛlɛ ye azo’;
na ɔse ezule kɛ, ‘Mia nuhua.’
7Ɔkpɔne menli gyima,
amaa menli kɔsɔɔti anwu ye gyima.
8Akee nane ne mɔ kɔ bɛ nla ɛleka,
na bɛboa bɛ tunli nu.
9Ahumuakyima vi ye ekpumgbunli ne anu finde,
yɛɛ ɛyɛlɛ vi anwoma mɔɔ ɛlɛbɔ la anu ba.
10Nyamenle die ɛnwomenle a ɔtɔ ayese,
na ɔmaa azule ne mɔ bɔ kunguma ndɛndɛ.
11Ɔmaa nzule gyinla amungu nu;
na amungu ne mɔ maa ezule fedevede.
12Ɔmaa bɛpɛ bɛ nwo fɛlɛnvɛlɛ,
ɔmaa bɛyɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɔkɛze bɛ la,
wɔ ewiade ye anu ɛleka biala.
13Saa bɛ nvonleɛ ɛdenrɛlɛ o, ye azɛlɛ ye ati o,
anzɛɛ ye ɛhulolɛ ti o, ɔmaa ɔsi zɔ.
14O Dwobu, tie ɛhye;
gyinla na dwenle Nyamenle nwanwane gyima ne mɔ anwo.
15Asoo ɛze kɛ Nyamenle si
maa ɛsɛnlɛmanye kpakye amungu ne anu la?
16Asoo ɛze kɛ amungu ne mɔ
si sinze anwomanyunlu la?
Ɔle nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ kpole, ɔyɛ nwanwane gyima.
17Wɔmɔ saa nyiakɛ anwoma ne maa ewiade gyinla a,
wɔ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ dɔ.
18Asoo ɛkɛhola ɛkɛyɛ kɛ ɔdaye,
ɛkɛdɛlɛdɛlɛ anwomanyunlu ne,
ɛkɛmaa ɔkɛyɛ ɛsesebɛ kɛ neanleɛ la?
19Kile yɛ mɔɔ yɛha yɛhile ye la;
awozinli ti, yɛnrɛnwu yɛ edwɛkɛ ne dwula.
20Asoo bɛha bɛhile ye kɛ mebadendɛ ɔ?
Asoo sonla kɛhulo kɛ bɛkɛme ye?
21“Kɛkala, wienyi kpakye anwomanyunlu,
mɔɔ anwoma ne ɛye ɔ nyunlu la,
menli ɛnrɛhola wienyi ne nea.
22Ɛdɔlɔlɛ guanye kɛ ezukoa nvutuke vi sɔlɔ ba;
tumi bedevinli ɛbɔ Nyamenle ɛyia.
23Tumivolɛ ne, yɛnrɛhola yɛnrɛnwu ye;
ye tumi nee ye pɛlepɛlelilɛ le kpole,
yɛɛ ɔnrɛbu ɔ nye ɔnrɛgua ye tenleneyɛlɛ zo.
24Yemɔti menli sulo ye,
ɔmbu menli mɔɔ dwenle kɛ bɛze nrɛlɛbɛ
na bɛbɛlɛbɛla bɛ nwo la bie.”

english_text:
The Lord Speaks
From Out of a Storm
1From out of a storm,
the Lord said to Job:
2Why do you talk so much
when you know so little?
3Now get ready to face me!
Can you answer
the questions I ask?
4How did I lay the foundation
for the earth?
Were you there?
5Doubtless you know who decided
its length and width.
6What supports the foundation?
Who placed the cornerstone,
7 while morning stars sang,
and angels rejoiced?
8 When the ocean was born,
I set its boundaries
9and wrapped it in blankets
of thickest fog.
10Then I built a wall around it,
locked the gates, 11and said,
“Your powerful waves stop here!
They can go no farther.”
Did You Ever Tell the Sun To Rise?
12Did you ever tell the sun to rise?
And did it obey?
13Did it take hold of the earth
and shake out the wicked
like dust from a rug?
14Early dawn outlines the hills
like stitches on clothing
or sketches on clay.
15But its light is too much
for those who are evil,
and their power is broken.
16Job, have you ever walked
on the ocean floor?
17Have you seen the gate
to the world of the dead?
18And how large is the earth?
Tell me, if you know!
19Where is the home of light,
and where does darkness live?
20Can you lead them home?
21I'm certain you must be able to,
since you were already born
when I created everything.
22Have you been to the places
where I keep snow and hail,
23until I use them to punish
and conquer nations?
24From where does lightning leap,
or the east wind blow?
25Who carves out a path
for thunderstorms?
Who sends torrents of rain
26on empty deserts
where no one lives?
27Rain that changes barren land
to meadows green with grass.
28Who is the father of the dew
and of the rain?
29Who gives birth to the sleet
and the frost
30that fall in winter,
when streams and lakes
freeze solid as a rock?
Can You Arrange Stars?
31 Can you arrange stars in groups
such as Orion
and the Pleiades?
32Do you control the stars
or set in place the Big Dipper
and the Little Dipper?
33Do you know the laws
that govern the heavens,
and can you make them rule
the earth?
34Can you order the clouds
to send a downpour,
35or will lightning flash
at your command?
36Did you teach birds to know
that rain or floods
are on their way?
37Can you count the clouds
or pour out their water
38on the dry, lumpy soil?
39When lions are hungry,
do you help them hunt?
40Do you send an animal
into their den?
41And when starving young ravens
cry out to me for food,
do you satisfy their hunger?
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma bua Dwobu
1Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle ahumu ne anu hilele Dwobu.
2Ɔse,
Ɛdɛnkɛma
“Nwane noko a ɔdaye ɔlɛfa edwɛkɛ mgbane mgbane
yeazɛkye adwenle la?
3Bɛza kɛ nrenya,
mebiza wɔ meamaa wɔaye ɔ nloa.
4Mɔɔ mewula azɛlɛ ye adiabo aze la ɛnee ɛwɔ ni?
Saa ɛse wɔ adwenle ɛdi, ɛlɛ ndelebɛbo a, ka kile me.
5Nwane a hyehyɛle kɛ ye kpole ɔwɔ kɛ si yɛ la a?
Ɔwɔ kɛ ɛnwu ye!
Anzɛɛ nwane a dole ye nyɛma zuzule a?
6Duzu azo a ye mpila ne mɔ gyigyi,
anzɛɛ nwane a dole ye mgbɛnezo bolɛ ne a?
7Kenle ko ne aleɛbahye nwɔlɔra bɔle nu dole edwɛne,
na Nyamenle amra kɔsɔɔti vale fɛlɛkolilɛ deɛdeanle nu.
8 Anzɛɛ nwane a dole nyevile ne anlenkɛ nu,
wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔvi azɛlɛ ti anu ɔkpukele,
9mɔɔ menvale amungu menyɛle ye ɛdanlɛ,
na menvale awozinli kabikabi menyɛle ye tabule,
10mengyale ye ɛweɛne,
na menduoduale ye nlenkɛ, menguale mbulalɛ bɛ nzi,
11na menzele kɛ, ‘Ɛke ala a ɔwɔ kɛ ɛba ɛbadwu a,
ɛngɔ ɛ nyunlu ko,
na ɛke yɛɛ wɔ azɛlɛkye mgbole babu adwu’ la,
ɛnee ɛwɔ nienwu?
12Sumunli kɛ bɛwole wɔ la,
kenle ko bɔbɔ wɔmaa aleɛ ɛhye
yɛɛ wɔmaa aleɛbahye ɛnwu ɔ bo zo,
13amaa yeazɔ azɛlɛ ye anloa ne mɔ yeahegye ye,
yeamaa amumuyɛma vi bɛ feabelɛ avinde ɔ?
14Ɔmaa azɛlɛ ye yɛ kɛ ɛva mɔɔ bɛzi zo,
na ɔmaa ɔ nye da ɛkɛ kɛ ɛdanlɛ.
15Amumuyɛma ɛngola wienyi ne nea
yɛɛ bɛ sa ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛmaa bɛ zo la dwɔlɔdwɔlɔ.
16“Asoo wɔnloma nyevile ne abo lɔ
wɔdwu ɛleka mɔɔ nzule ne vi ba la,
anzɛɛ wɔdia nyevile bo azɛlɛ ne azo ɛlɛ?
17Asoo bɛye ɛbolɔ nlenkɛ ne mɔ bɛhile wɔ ɛlɛ,
anzɛɛ wɔnwu awozinli kabikabi nlenkɛ ne mɔ ɛlɛ?
18Asoo wɔnwu kɛ ewiade kpole si de la?
Saa ɛze ɛhye mɔ amuala a, ka kile me.
19“Nienwu yɛɛ wienyi sua zo adenle ne la a,
yɛɛ awozinli sua zo wɔ nienwu,
20amaa wɔava zo wɔahɔ ye maanle nu
na wɔanwu adenle ne mɔɔ kɔ ye sua zo la a?
21Ɛze, ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛwo wɔ,
yɛɛ wɔhyɛ kɛ kpanwenle!
22“Asoo wɔwolo ezukɔtweaba ninyɛnezielɛ sua ne anu,
anzɛɛ wɔnwu ezuawolɛ ninyɛnezielɛ sua ne,
23mɔɔ meva mezie memaa ngyegyelɛ
nee konle mekɛ la?
24Ɛleka mɔɔ wienyi vi ba la adenle,
anzɛɛ ɛleka mɔɔ aduduleɛ anwoma vi bɔ
azɛlɛ ye azo la wɔ ni?
25“Nwane a ɛye ɛzezeane ɛmaa ezule,
na yekpakye adenle yemaa ɛsɛnlɛmanye bolɛ,
26kɛ ɔmaa ezule adɔ ɛleka mɔɔ awie ɛnle
nee ɛsɛlɛ mɔɔ awie ɛnde ɛkɛ la azo;
27kɛ ɔmaa azɛlɛ mɔɔ le resee na yehwie la
ayɛ azɛlɛ mɔɔ fifi ndile la a?
28Asoo ezule lɛ ɔ ze,
anzɛɛ nwane a ɛwo ɛbɔlɛ a?
29Nwane akunlu a ayese vi rale a,
yɛɛ nwane a ɛwo ayese ne mɔɔ vi anwuma ba la a?
30Ɔmaa nzule ne mɔ yɛ se kɛ bolɛ,
yɛɛ buma nye yɛ ketekete.
31 “Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛgua ‘Nwɔlɔra nsuu’ ne nwɔnzɔnwɔnzɔ
anzɛɛ ɛkɛhola ɛkɛzanyi nyɛma mɔɔ kyekye ‘Apeansa’ la ɔ?
32Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛhile nwɔlɔra ne mɔ ɛlobɔ,
anzɛɛ ɛkɛhola ɛkɛhile ‘Ɛrelera nee ɔ mra’ adenle ɔ?
33Ɛze anwuma maamɛla ne mɔ ɔ?
Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛmaa bɛkɛli zolɛ wɔ aleɛabo ɔ?
34“Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛmaa ɛ ne zo ɛkɛze amungu kɛ
azuyilɛ ɛmonla wɔ ɔ?
35Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛzoa ɛsɛlɛmanye ne mɔ ɛkɛmaa bɛkɛhɔ,
na bɛkɛraze wɔ kɛ, ‘Yɛmɛ ɛne?’
36Nwane a ɛhile amungu ne mɔ nrɛlɛbɛ,
anzɛɛ ɛmaa ɛbɔlɛ ɛnyia ndelebɛbo a?
37Nwane a ye nrɛlɛbɛ kɛhola amungu ne mɔ tia a?
Anzɛɛ nwane a kɛhola anwuma nzule ahodoku ne mɔ
kyeɛhyea butu bɛ
38wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ munlutu kɛbo bama
na ɔkɛbɔ ɛdɔkɛ la a?
39“Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛhu nane ɛkɛmaa awenade
na ɛkɛmaa awenade mralɛ akunlu kɛdwo bɛ nwo,
40wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛsise ngoko wɔ bɛ tunli nloa,
anzɛɛ bɛkɛhɔ nzia anyebolo nu la?
41Saa aleɛ ti ahɔhɔsɛlɛ mralɛ duolua nu su
fɛlɛ Nyamenle a, nwane a maa bɛ aleɛ a?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
When Do Mountain Goats Give Birth?
1When do mountain goats
and deer give birth?
Have you been there
when their young are born?
* 2How long are they pregnant
3before they deliver?
4Soon their young grow strong
and then leave
to be on their own.
5Who set wild donkeys free?
6I alone help them survive
in salty desert sand.
7They stay far from crowded cities
and refuse to be tamed.
8Instead, they roam the hills,
searching for pastureland.
9Would a wild ox agree
to live in your barn
and labor for you?
10Could you force him to plow
or to drag a heavy log
to smooth out the soil?
11Can you depend on him
to use his great strength
and do your heavy work?
12Can you trust him
to harvest your grain
or take it to your barn
from the threshing place?
An Ostrich Proudly Flaps Her Wings
13An ostrich proudly
flaps her wings,
but not because
she loves her young.
14She abandons her eggs
and lets the dusty ground
keep them warm.
15And she doesn't seem to worry
that the feet of an animal
could crush them all.
16She treats her eggs as though
they were not her own,
unconcerned that her work
might be for nothing.
17I myself made her foolish
and without common sense.
18But once she starts running,
she laughs at a rider
on the fastest horse.
Did You Give Horses Their Strength?
19Did you give horses their strength
and the flowing hair
along their necks?
20Did you make them able
to jump like grasshoppers
or to frighten people
with their snorting?
21Before horses are ridden
into battle,
they paw at the ground,
proud of their strength.
22Laughing at fear, they rush
toward the fighting,
23while the weapons of their riders
rattle and flash in the sun.
24Unable to stand still,
they gallop eagerly into battle
when trumpets blast.
25Stirred by the distant smells
and sounds of war, they snort
in reply to the trumpet.
26Did you teach hawks to fly south
for the winter?
* 27Did you train eagles to build
28their nests on rocky cliffs,
29where they can look down
to spot their next meal?
30 Then their young gather to feast
wherever the victim lies.
translation_text:
1Ɛze mekɛ mɔɔ awoka zo mbɔnkye wo a?
Wɔnwu kɛ weɛlɛ si wo la ɔ?
2Ɛze siane dodo mɔɔ bɛfa bɛfia bɛ mra a,
yɛɛ ɛze bɛ awolɛ mekɛ ɔ?
3Ɛze mekɛ mɔɔ bɛse ngoko kɛ bɛwo,
na bɛwo bɛ mra la ɔ?
4Bɛ mra nyi kpɔkɛ bo wienyi nu,
na bɛ nwo mia;
bɛkpakye bɛ nwo, yɛɛ bɛnzia bɛmba bieko.
5“Nwane a ɛmaa ɛbɔ nu asoaso ɛva ɔ nwo dwɔɔ a?
Nwane a ɛzanyi asoaso mɔɔ anwo yɛ ndɛ la nyɛma,
6mɔɔ meva ɛsɛlɛ zo memaa ye kɛ ye sua nu,
na meva ngyenle azɛlɛ memaa ye kɛ ɔdɛnla zo la a?
7Ɔkyi suakpole zo alɛra ne mɔ;
ɔnde nanekavolɛ ne ane.
8Awoka ne mɔ azo a le ye adidileka a,
na ɔkpondɛ ndile amolɛ ɔdi.
9“Asoo ɛbɔ nu ɛnlankɛ nyinli bazonle wɔ?
Asoo nɔɔzo ɔbala wɔ tunli ne anu?
10Asoo ɛkɛhola ye kyekye, ɛkɛmaa ɔkɛvundu azɛlɛ,
anzɛɛ ɔkɛva bulalɛ ɔ nee wɔ kɛyɛ gyima wɔ mbɔnza nu?
11Ɔ nwo yɛ se la ati, ɛkɛva ɛ rɛle ɛkɛwula ye nu,
na ɛkɛva wɔ gyima muala ɛkɛgua ɔ nwo zo ɔ?
12Ɛdie ye ɛdi kɛ ɔbazia yeara
yearava wɔ ma ne yeara ma ɛwozolɛ ɛleka ne?
13“Soholo kola bɔ ɔ ndɛba anu kpalɛ kpalɛ;
noko asoo bɛfa bɛto azuazuanloma nwo a ɔkɛyɛ boɛ ɔ?
14Ɔluakɛ ɔgyakyi ye aholonvia anwea nu,
ɔmaa bɛ nwo yɛ wuluwulu.
15Ɔ rɛle fi kɛ egyakɛ kola gelegele bɛ,
yɛɛ ɛbɔ nu nanemgbole kola tietia zo.
16Ɔ nee ɔ mra di ye ketekete,
kɛ asɛɛ tɛ ɔ mra ɔ;
kanza ye ɛvɛlɛ yɛ mgbane bɔbɔ a, ɔnvane ɔ nwo;
17ɔboalekɛ Nyamenle ɛmaa ɔ rɛle ɛvi nrɛlɛbɛ,
yɛɛ yeammaa ye ndelebɛbo nretee zɛ.
18Saa ɔbɔ ɔ ndɛba anu kɛ ɔtu a,
ɔsele ɛkpɔnwɔ ne nee ye kavolɛ ne.
19“Asoo ɛdawɔ a ɛmaa ɛkpɔnwɔ anwosesebɛ a?
Ɛdawɔ a ɛmaa ye ɔ kɔme nu enrinli ne a?
20Asoo ɛdawɔ a ɛmaa ɔwuluwulu kɛ abɛbɛ a?
Ye ɛnwomenlelielɛ bedevinli ne yɛ ɛzulolɛ.
21Ɔfunvu bɔnza ne anu, na ɔdi ye anwosesebɛ nwo fɛlɛko;
ɔfa ye anwosesebɛ muala ɔkɔ konle nloa.
22Ɔnze ɛzulolɛ deɛ holɛ, yɛɛ ɔ rɛle ɛmbɔ,
ɔnwu dadeɛ a ɔnnriandi.
23Ɔ kɛnra azo a ɛda mbaka rede,
yɛɛ atwɛ nee ɛtweneɛ pɛ memeamemea a.
24Ɔfa atisesebɛ nee ɛya yɛɛ ɔnriandi a;
saa ɔte aweɛne tendenle ne ane a,
ɔgyinla a, ɔngyinla.
25Saa ɔte aweɛne tendenle ne ane a, ɔtea nu, ‘Ɛhɛɛ!’
Ɔte konle ne nganeɛ wɔ moa moa,
ɔte safohyenlema ɛhululɛ nee bɛ ɛdeanlɛ ne.
26Asoo wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ ti yɛɛ kyɛnyema tu,
na ɔtɛlɛdɛlɛ ɔ ndɛba wɔ nyiakɛ a?
27Asoo ɛdawɔ a ɛmaa kɔleɛ tu,
na ɔyɛ ye sane wɔ anwuma hwehwe lɔ a?
28Ɔfa boka ne azo ɔyɛ ye sua nu,
na ɔfa bolɛ tokule nu ɔyɛ ye feabelɛ.
29Ɔde ɛkɛ ne a ɔtoto ɔ nye ɔkpondɛ mɔɔ ɔkɛli;
ɔ nye die ye moa moa nehane.
30 Ɔ mra no mogya;
na ɛleka mɔɔ bɛku menli bɛgua la,
ɛkɛ ne a ɔkɔ a.

english_text:
The Lord Continues
I Am the Lord All-Powerful
* 1I am the Lord All-Powerful,
2but you have argued
that I am wrong.
Now you must answer me.
3Job said to the Lord:
4Who am I to answer you?
5I did speak once or twice,
but never again.
6Then out of the storm
the Lord said to Job:
7Face me and answer
the questions I ask!
8Are you trying to prove
that you are innocent
by accusing me of injustice?
9Do you have a powerful arm
and a thundering voice
that compare with mine?
10If so, then surround yourself
with glory and majesty.
* 11Show your furious anger!
Throw down and crush
12all who are proud and evil.
13Wrap them in grave clothes
and bury them together
in the dusty soil.
14Do this, and I will agree
that you have won
this argument.
I Created You
15I created both you
and the hippopotamus.
It eats only grass like an ox,
16but look at the mighty muscles
in its body 17and legs.
Its tail is like a cedar tree,
and its thighs are thick.
18The bones in its legs
are like bronze or iron.
19I made it more powerful
than any other creature,
yet I am stronger still.
20Undisturbed, it eats grass
while the other animals
play nearby.
* 21It rests in the shade of trees
along the riverbank
22or hides among reeds
in the swamp.
23It remains calm and unafraid
with the Jordan River rushing
and splashing in its face.
24There is no way to capture
a hippopotamus—
not even by hooking its nose
or blinding its eyes.
translation_text:
1-2“Dwobu, asoo sonla mɔɔ nvonleɛ ala a ɔkpondɛ la
nee Tumivolɛ ne su kpolera?
Awie mɔɔ nee Nyamenle su kpolera la,
bɛmaa ɔye ɔ nloa.”
Dwobu
3-4Na Dwobu buale kɛ,
“Ɛdɛnkɛma, mendwu bie;
kɛ menzi membua wɔ ɛ?
Meva me sa mezɔ me nloa.
5Meha ko, menga bieko;
fane nwiɔ ɛ, mendɛ me nloa anu ko.”
6Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma buale Dwobu wɔ ahumuakyima ne anu.
Ɛdɛnkɛma
7Ɔse,
“Bɛza kpalɛ kɛ nrenya;
mebiza wɔ edwɛkɛ, na ye me ɔ nloa.
8Yemɔti ɛdawɔ bɔbɔ ɛbua me fɔlɛ ɔ?
Ɛbua me fɔlɛ na wɔali benle ɔ?
9Asoo ɛlɛ anwosesebɛ kɛ Nyamenle,
yɛɛ ɛkɛhola ɛkɛva ɛnelɛ ɛkɛhulu kɛ ye ɛdeɛ ne la?
10Fa mgboleyɛlɛ nee dibilɛ siezie ɛ nwo;
na fa anyunlunyia nee kɛnlɛma yɛ ɛ nwo hyeleenyi.
11Wola wɔ ɛya kpole ne gua,
na bɛlɛ awie biala mɔɔ ɛnea a
ɔle mgbanyizonle la aze.
12Bɛlɛ awie biala mɔɔ le mgbanyizonle la aze,
na tietia amumuyɛma anwo zo
wɔ ɛleka biala mɔɔ bɛwɔ la.
13Fu bɛ kɔsɔɔti wula azɛlɛ bo;
na kyekye bɛ nye wɔ ɛbolɔ.
14Na menwɔlie menwɔdo nu kɛ,
ɛdawɔ wɔ anwosesebɛ kola maa ɛdi konim.
15“Nea nane kɔliadunli;
membɔle ye kɛ membɔle wɔ la;
ɔdi ndile kɛ ɛnlankɛ nyinli.
16Nea anwosesebɛ mɔɔ ɔlɛ ye ɔ nze nu,
nee anwosesebɛ mɔɔ wɔ ye ndinli nu la.
17Ɔsa ɔ dua ketee kɛ sida baka,
ɔ gyakɛ ndinli ne mɔ to bɛka nu.
18Ye mbowule yɛ se kɛ kɔbele,
ye agbɔkɛ le kɛ mbulalɛ agbɔma.
19“Yemɔ a ɔle Nyamenle asa anloa gyima mɔɔ lumua;
ye Bɔvolɛ ne ala a kola twe ɔ nwo dadeɛ a.
20Ɔluakɛ ɔnyia aleɛ wɔ awoka ne mɔ azo,
ɛkɛ ne a ɛbɔ nu nanemgbole kɔsɔɔti di nwɔhoa a.
21Atoatɛlɛ ne mɔ abo yɛɛ ɔda a,
na ɔfea ndɔ ne mɔ abo wɔ azia ne anu.
22Atoatɛlɛ ne mɔ maa ye alubo;
azia nloa ndile bɔ yia ye.
23Nea, saa azule ne tu kpole bɔbɔ a, ɔnzulo;
azule Dwɔdan hu gua ɔ nyunlu bɔbɔ a, ye ahonle gyi pi.
24Asoo awie kɛhola koba to kye ye,
anzɛɛ kɛhola kɛva ɛhane kɛzɔ ɔ bonyi?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
Can You Catch a Sea Monster?
1 Can you catch a sea monster
by using a fishhook?
Can you tie its mouth shut
with a rope?
2Can it be led around
by a ring in its nose
or a hook in its jaw?
3Will it beg for mercy?
4Will it surrender
as a slave for life?
5Can it be tied by the leg
like a pet bird
for little girls?
6Is it ever chopped up
and its pieces bargained for
in the fish-market?
7Can it be killed
with harpoons or spears?
8Wrestle it just once—
that will be the end.
9Merely a glimpse of this monster
makes all courage melt.
10And if it is too fierce
for anyone to attack,
who would dare oppose me?
11I am in command of the world
and in debt to no one.
12What powerful legs,
what a stout body
this monster possesses!
13Who could strip off its armor
or bring it under control
with a harness?
14Who would try to open its jaws,
full of fearsome teeth?
* 15Its back is covered
with shield after shield,
16firmly bound and closer together
17than breath to breath.
When This Monster Sneezes
18When this monster sneezes,
lightning flashes, and its eyes
glow like the dawn.
19Sparks and fiery flames
explode from its mouth.
20And smoke spews from its nose
like steam
from a boiling pot,
21while its blazing breath
scorches everything in sight.
22Its neck is so tremendous
that everyone trembles,
23the weakest parts of its body
are harder than iron,
24and its heart is stone.
25When this noisy monster appears,
even the most powerful
turn and run in fear.
26No sword or spear can harm it,
27and weapons of bronze or iron
are as useless as straw
or rotten wood.
28Rocks thrown from a sling
cause it no more harm
than husks of grain.
This monster fears no arrows,
29it simply smiles at spears,
and striking it with a stick
is like slapping it with straw.
30As it crawls through the mud,
its sharp and spiny hide
tears the ground apart.
31And when it swims down deep,
the sea starts churning
like boiling oil,
32and it leaves behind a trail
of shining white foam.
33No other creature on earth
is so fearless.
34It is king of all proud creatures,
and it looks upon the others
as nothing.
translation_text:
1 “Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛva fɛlɛ koba ɛkɛhye ɛlɛnrɛne,
anzɛɛ ɛkɛva nyɛma ɛkɛkyekye ɔ tafinlima ɔ?
2Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛva nyɛma ɛkɛzinla ɔ bonyi nu,
anzɛɛ ɛkɛva koba ɛkɛbɔ ye awudwolɛ ɔ?
3Asoo ɔkɛzu ɔkɛbodo wɔ?
Asoo ɔkɛdendɛ bɛtɛɛ ɔkɛhile wɔ?
4Asoo ɔ nee wɔ bayɛ ngyekyeleɛ,
kɛ ɛva ye ɛyɛ wɔ sonvolɛ dahuu?
5Asoo ɛ nee ye bali nwɔhoa kɛ ɛ nee anloma la,
anzɛɛ ɛbazɔ ye nyɛma kɛ wɔ mbɛlɛra ne mɔ ɛva ɛli nwɔhoa?
6Asoo gualilɛma bali ye bolɛ?
Asoo gualilɛma bahyɛ amaa bɛ nwo?
7Asoo ɛkɛhola ɛkɛva atwɛ ɛkɛwɔ ye nwoma ne,
anzɛɛ ɛkɛva fɛlɛhyelɛ atwɛ ɛkɛwɔ ɔ ti?
8Fa ɛ sa ka ye nea;
konle mɔɔ ɔ nee wɔ baho la, ɛnrɛyɛ ko ɛlɛ!
9“Nea, saa sonla nye bobɔ ye mgbane bɔbɔ a,
ye anyelazo yɛ mgbane na ɔ nwo bubu ye.
10Awie fee anwo ɛnyɛ ɛzulolɛ mɔɔ kɛhola kɛha ye a.
Na ɛnee akee nwane a kɛhola me nyunlu gyinla a?
11Nwane a ɛva debie ɛvɛne me mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ metua a?
Debie biala mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la le me ɛdeɛ.
12“Menrɛyɛ koonwu wɔ ɔ gyakɛ ne mɔ,
ye anwosesebɛ bedevinli ne,
anzɛɛ ɔdaye mumua ne ye kɛnlɛma ti.
13Nwane a kɛhola kɛkpa ɔ nwo tɛladeɛ a?
Nwane a asa kɛhola kɛfiti ye konle tɛladeɛ ndazo ne a?
14Nwane a kɛhola kɛzɔ ɔ nloa kɛbuke ye a?
Ɔ gye mɔɔ gua ɔ nloa anu la yɛ ɛzulolɛ.
15Ɔ nzi le kɛ enyinlike ɛhonlone,
bɛbetɛbeta nwo kɛ bɛholo sumi bɛsosɔ bɛ.
16Ko beta ko kpalɛ kpalɛ
mɔɔ anwoma bɔbɔ ɛngola ɛnze bɛ avinli a.
17Ko beta ko; bɛsosɔ bɛ nwo
mɔɔ ɛkpɔkye ko bɔbɔ a ɔnyɛ boɛ a.
18Ye ɛnwuasinlɛ sɔ kɛ tɛkɛ,
yɛɛ ɔ nye le kɛ mangyee sɛnzɛne.
19Senle gɔhyee vi ɔ nloa anu finde;
ɔ nloa anu kpa senle.
20Ɔ bonyi nu kpu esike,
kɛ nzule mɔɔ gyi senle zo la kpukpuke.
21Ɔ bonyi nu anwoma kola maa senle sɔ,
yɛɛ senle tafinlima vi ɔ nloa anu finde.
22Ɔ kɔme baka ne anu yɛ se,
ɔ nwo ka ɛzulolɛ.
23Ye nwonane belebele gua zo;
ɔkyekye ɔ nwo ketekete mɔɔ
ɛsianyi nu a ɔnyɛ boɛ a.
24Ye ahonle yɛ se kɛ bolɛ,
ye ɛsesebɛ le kɛ ɛdibolɛ.
25Saa ɔmaa ɔ nwo zo a, anwosesebɛma sulo;
ɔka ɔ nwo a, bɛtɔ gyebilisanza.
26Saa dadeɛ ka ye bɔbɔ a, ɔnyɛ ye tanye;
na yeayɛ atwɛ, ɛda, anzɛɛ ɛtweneɛ.
27Bulalɛ le ɔ nye zo ɛdɛkɛ,
yɛɛ kɔbele le ɔ nye zo baka kpɔlɔlera.
28Ɛda ɛngola ɛmmaa ɔnriandi,
totoabɔ bolɛ le kɛ abonle.
29Ahoholombaka le kɛ abɛlɛ baka welera,
yɛɛ ɛtweneɛ wɔ ye a ɔsele.
30Ɔ kɛnra zo abonle ne le kɛ foandɛkɛ anloa nlane;
ɔtɛlɛdɛlɛ ɔ nwo kɛ ma ɛwozolɛ taboa wɔ azia nu.
31Ɔmaa buma wu kɛ ɛzɛne mɔɔ gyi senle zo;
ɔmaa nyevile yɛ kɛ nwole mɔɔ gyi siase nu.
32Ɔtu ɔtenrɛ a ɔgyakyi adenle fufule ɛdenraa ɔ nzi;
ɔmaa sonla dwenle kɛ nyevile ne ɛvi egyɛne.
33Aleɛabo, ye ɛsaso biala ɛnle ɛke,
ɔle abɔdeɛ mɔɔ ɛnzulo ɛhwee a.
34Ɔmbu debie biala mɔɔ tu ɔ nwo la ɛhwee;
ɔdi mgbanyizonlema kɔsɔɔti belemgbunli.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to the Lord
No One Can Oppose You
1Job said:
2No one can oppose you,
because you have the power
to do what you want.
3 You asked why I talk so much
when I know so little.
I have talked about things
that are far beyond
my understanding.
4 You told me to listen
and answer your questions.
5I heard about you from others;
now I have seen you
with my own eyes.
6That's why I hate myself
and sit here in dust and ashes
to show my sorrow.
The Lord Corrects Job's Friends
7The Lord said to Eliphaz:
What my servant Job has said about me is true, but I am angry with you and your two friends for not telling the truth. 8So I want you to go over to Job and offer seven bulls and seven goats on an altar as a sacrifice to please me. After this, Job will pray, and I will agree not to punish you for your foolishness.
9Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar obeyed the Lord, and he answered Job's prayer.
A Happy Ending
10 After Job had prayed for his three friends, the Lord made Job twice as rich as he had been before. 11Then Job gave a feast for his brothers and sisters and for his old friends. They expressed their sorrow for the suffering the Lord had brought on him, and they each gave Job some silver and a gold ring.
12The Lord now blessed Job more than ever; he gave him 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pair of oxen, and 1,000 donkeys.
13In addition to seven sons, Job had three daughters, 14whose names were Jemimah, Keziah, and Keren Happuch. 15They were the most beautiful women in that part of the world, and Job gave them shares of his property, along with their brothers.
16Job lived for another 140 years—long enough to see his great-grandchildren have children of their own— 17and when he finally died, he was very old.
translation_text:
1Akee Dwobu buale Ɛdɛnkɛma.
Dwobu
2Ɔse,
“Meze kɛ ɛkola ɛyɛ ninyɛne muala,
yɛɛ awie ɛngola ɛnzɛkye wɔ ngyehyɛlɛ biala.
3 Ɛbizale kɛ me ndelebɛbo le nyɛ,
mɔɔ mefedevede wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ nu a?
Yemɔti medendɛ ɛdendɛlɛ mɔɔ mende ɔ bo a,
meha edwɛkɛ mɔɔ menze a, na ye ɛzulolɛ bo me nwo zo.
4 Ɛzele me kɛ mendie na ɛtendɛ,
ɛbiza me edwɛkɛ na menye ɔ nloa.
5Me nzo yɛɛ menvale mendele wɔ nganeɛ a,
na kɛkala, yemɔ menwu ɛ nyunlu;
6yemɔti mebɔ anyiemgba
na menlu me nwo; mebɔ ndɛtɛlɛ nee nzonle.”
Adwulaleɛ
7Mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle edwɛkɛ ɛhye mɔ hilele Dwobu la, akee ɔzele Timanli Ɛlaefaze kɛ, “Meva wɔ nee ɛ gɔnwo mɔ nwiɔ ne anwo ɛya, ɔluakɛ bɛanga nɔhalɛ ne mɔɔ fane me nwo la, kɛmɔ me sonvolɛ Dwobu hanle la. 8Yemɔti bɛva nlankɛ nyinli nsuu nee mboane nyinli nsuu bɛhɔ me sonvolɛ Dwobu anwo ɛkɛ ne bɛhɔbɔ ɛyelalɛ azu wɔ bɛdabɛ bɛ ti, na me sonvolɛ Dwobu bazɛlɛ amaa bɛ, ɔluakɛ mebadie ye nzɛlɛlɛ ne, na me nee bɛ ɛnrɛli ye kɛ mɔɔ bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ de la, ɔboalekɛ bɛanga me nwo edwɛkɛ kpalɛ kɛ mɔɔ me sonvolɛ Dwobu hanle la.”
9Yemɔti Ɛlaefaze, Beledade, yɛɛ Zofaa hɔyɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele bɛ la, na Ɛdɛnkɛma diele Dwobu nzɛlɛlɛ ne.
10 Mɔɔ Dwobu zɛlɛle manle ɔ gɔnwo mɔ la, Ɛdɛnkɛma akee manle ɔnyianle ye anwonyia ne mɔɔ ɔlɛ ye dɛba la mɔnwo. 11Akee ɔ mediema mrenya nee mraalɛ rale ye sua nu nee ye radole ɛsalɛ; bɛyɛle ye gyakɔ na bɛkyekyele ɔ rɛle wɔ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa yezi ɔ nwo zo la anwo, na bɛ nuhua ko biala manle ye ezukoa nee ezukoa nvutuke kpɔdelera.
12Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma yilale Dwobu kpole kpalɛ dɛlale alumua ne; ɔnyianle mboane apenle ngoko bulu nee nna, afunlumu apenle nsia, nlankɛ nyinli apenle nwiɔ, yɛɛ asoaso mbelɛ apenle ko. 13Eza ɔwole mralɛ mrenya nsuu nee mraalɛ nsa. 14Ɔdonle raalɛ kpanyinli kpalɛ ne Gyimaema, ɔdonle mɔɔ doa ye la Kɛzia, yɛɛ mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa la, ɔdonle ye Kɛlɛn Hapɛke. 15Wɔ aleɛabo, mraalɛ ɛnle ɛleka biala mɔɔ nee Dwobu amra mraalɛ ne mɔ sɛ anwofɛlɛko a; bɛ ze gyakyile bɛ agyadeɛ kɛ bɛ mediema mrenya ne mɔ ala la.
16Ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti anzi, eza Dwobu dɛnlanle aze lile ɛvolɛ ɛya ko abulanla, ɔnwunle ɔ mra, ye nlɔnra, nee ye angabɛnzo. 17Dwobu wule wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee akee yeyɛ ɛrelera nwosonwoso la.

english_text:
BOOK I
(Psalms 1–41)
The Way to Happiness
1God blesses those people
who refuse evil advice
and won't follow sinners
or join in sneering at God.
2Instead, they find happiness
in the Teaching of the Lord,
and they think about it
day and night.
3 They are like trees
growing beside a stream,
trees that produce
fruit in season
and always have leaves.
Those people succeed
in everything they do.
4That isn't true of those
who are evil—
they are like straw
blown by the wind.
5Sinners won't have an excuse
on the day of judgment,
and they won't have a place
with the people of God.
6The Lord protects everyone
who follows him,
but the wicked follow a road
that leads to ruin.
translation_text:
BULUKU MƆƆ LUMUA
(Edwɛndolɛ 1—41)
Nyilalɛ kpalɛ
1Nyilalɛ ɛha sonla ne mɔɔ
ɛndie amumuyɛma folɛdulɛ,
na ɔnyɛ mɔɔ ɛtanevolɛma yɛ la;
ɔnva amgbuzilɛma agɔnwolɛ.
2Ɔ nye die Ɛdɛnkɛma Mɛla ne anwo,
na ɔdwenledwenle nwolɛ alehyenlɛ nee aledwolɛ.
3 Ɔle kɛ azule nloa baka,
mɔɔ so ma wɔ ye ɛlobɔ nloa,
ye nya ɛmkpolo ɛlɛ,
yɛɛ ɔkpazi debie biala anu.
4Amumuyɛma ɛnle zɔ,
bɛle kɛ abonle mɔɔ anwoma bɔ ye kɔ la.
5Yemɔti amumuyɛma ɛnrɛnyia gyinlagyakɛ
wɔ ndɛnebualɛ ne anu,
yɛɛ ɛtanevolɛma ɛnrɛnyia gyinlagyakɛ
wɔ tenlenema avinli.
6Ɛdɛnkɛma ze pɛlepɛlelilɛnli adenle;
amumuyɛnli adenle fa ye kɔ munzule nu.

english_text:
The Lord's Chosen King
1 Why do the nations plot,
and why do their people
make useless plans?
2The kings of this earth
have all joined together
to turn against the Lord
