but a sensible leader
restores law and order.
3When someone poor takes over
and mistreats the poor,
it's like a heavy rain
destroying the crops.
4Lawbreakers praise criminals,
but law-abiding citizens
always oppose them.
5Criminals don't know
what justice means,
but all who respect the Lord
understand it completely.
6It's better to be poor
and live right,
than to be rich
and dishonest.
7It makes good sense
to obey the Law of God,
but you disgrace your parents
if you make friends
with worthless nobodies.
8If you make money by charging
high interest rates,
you will lose it all to someone
who cares for the poor.
9God cannot stand the prayers
of anyone who disobeys
his Law.
10By leading good people to sin,
you dig a pit for yourself,
but all who live right
will have a bright future.
11The rich think highly
of themselves,
but anyone poor and sensible
sees right through them.
12When an honest person wins,
it's time to celebrate;
when crooks are in control,
it's best to hide.
13If you don't confess your sins,
you will be a failure.
But God will be merciful
if you confess your sins
and give them up.
14The Lord blesses everyone
who is afraid to do evil,
but if you are cruel,
you will end up in trouble.
15A ruler who mistreats the poor
is like a roaring lion
or a bear hunting for food.
16A heartless leader is a fool,
but anyone who refuses
to get rich by cheating others
will live a long time.
17Don't give help to murderers!
Make them stay on the run
for as long as they live.
18Honesty will keep you safe,
but everyone who is crooked
will suddenly fall.
19Work hard, and you will have
a lot of food;
waste time, and you will have
a lot of trouble.
20God blesses his loyal people,
but punishes all who want
to get rich quick.
21It isn't right to be unfair,
but some people can be bribed
with only a piece of bread.
22Don't be selfish
and eager to get rich—
you will end up worse off
than you can imagine.
23Honest correction
is appreciated
more than flattery.
24If you cheat your parents
and don't think it's wrong,
you are a common thief.
25Selfish people cause trouble,
but you will live a full life
if you trust the Lord.
26Only fools would trust
what they alone think,
but if you live by wisdom,
you will do all right.
27Giving to the poor
will keep you from poverty,
but if you close your eyes
to their needs,
everyone will curse you.
28When crooks are in control,
everyone tries to hide,
but when they lose power,
good people are everywhere.
translation_text:
1Amumuyɛma nriandi mekɛ mɔɔ awie ɛndoa bɛ la, na tenlenema akɛnra yɛ se kɛ awenade.
2Saa maanle yɛ ɛtane a, ye arelemgbunli so dɔɔnwo; maanle mɔɔ lɛ menli mɔɔ lɛ ndelebɛbo nee adwenle la gyinla kyɛ.
3Ehyianli mɔɔ sisi ehyianli la le kɛ ezule mɔɔ tɔ bilididi sɛkye aleɛ la.
4Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkpo mɛla la yeyɛ amumuyɛma, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛdi mɛla zo la ko tia amumuyɛma.
5Menli mɔɔ di ɛtane la ɛnde pɛlepɛlelilɛ bo, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛsonle Ɛdɛnkɛma la te ɔ bo kpalɛ.
6Ehyianli mɔɔ fa adwenle to ye ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nwo la le kpalɛ tɛla sukoavolɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ subane la.
7Ralɛ nrenya mɔɔ di mɛla zo la ze nrɛlɛbɛ, na ralɛ nrenya mɔɔ nee adidikpokuma a tu la gua ɔ ze anyunlu aze.
8Sonla mɔɔ dua awie mɔ ngyianlɛ zo fa nzinwo nyia ɔ nwo la ezukoa pɛ di menli mɔɔ se ehyianvolɛma anwunvɔne la ɛkɛ.
9Saa sonla tuodua ɔ nzo kɛ ɔnrɛdie mɛla ne a, ye nzɛlɛlɛ bɔbɔ le kyibadeɛ.
10Sonla mɔɔ kɛbɛlɛbɛla sonlakpalɛ kɛmaa ɔkɛbɔ ɛbɛla ɛtane la badɔ ɔdaye ye kuma mɔɔ yevu la anu.
Sonla mɔɔ ɛnli ɛzonle la banyia agyadeɛ kpalɛ.
11Sukoavolɛ dwenle kɛ ɔze nrɛlɛbɛ, na ehyianli mɔɔ lɛ ndelebɛbo la maa ɔ nwo da zolɛ.
12Saa tenlenenli di konim a, menli di fɛlɛko kpole, na saa amumuyɛnli dwazo a, menli nriandi fea.
13Sonla mɔɔ fea ye mɛladonlɛ zo la ɛnrɛkpazi, na sonla mɔɔ ka ye ɛtane na ɔgyakyi ye ɛyɛlɛ la, bɛse ye anwunvɔne.
14Nyilalɛ ɛha sonla ne mɔɔ sulo Ɛdɛnkɛma dahuu la, na sonla mɔɔ le anzosesebɛ la badɔ munzule nu.
15Maanlebuvolɛ mɔɔ le amumuyɛ na ɔsie ehyianvolɛma la le kɛ awenade mɔɔ ɛlɛkpo anzɛɛ bedi mɔɔ ɛnwu nane na ɔlɛkye ye la.
16Maanlebuvolɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ ndelebɛbo la ati yɛ se yɛɛ ɔdi nzisi, na sonla mɔɔ kyi nzisi la nyi kyɛ.
17Bɛmaa sonla mɔɔ di fɔlɛ kɛ yehu sonla la ɛyɛ nriandivolɛ toonwo ɛhɔ ewule nu; awie biala mmaboa ye.
18Sonla mɔɔ fa nɔhalɛ dua la, bɛbalie ye ngoane, na mɔɔ ye adenle nu kyeɛhyea la badɔ kuma nu.
19Sonla mɔɔ so ɛya la banyia aleɛ dɔɔnwo, na mɔɔ di ninyɛne mgbane mgbane nzi la, ehyia bahu ye kpole kpalɛ.
20Nyilalɛ dɔɔnwo baha sonla mɔɔ di nɔhalɛ la, na mɔɔ pele nyia ɔ nwo ndɛndɛ la ɛnrɛva ɔ nwo dwɔɔ.
21Mɔguazolilɛ ɛnle kpalɛ, noko aleɛ duma nu ti, sonla ne bie bali mɔguazo ayɛ ɛtane.
22Sonla mɔɔ le akyɛbɛ la pele anwonyia nwo, ɔndwenle nwolɛ kɛ kenle bie ɔbahyia.
23Sonla mɔɔ twi mɔɔ kɛyɛ ɛtane la anyunlu la nzinlii sɔ ɛnyelɛ tɛla mɔɔ kanvo ye bɛ gye zo la.
24Sonla mɔɔ wua ɔ ze anzɛɛ ɔ nli na ɔka kɛ “Ɔnle mɛladonlɛ” la, le sonla mɔɔ sɛkye ninyɛne la agɔnwo.
25Sonla mɔɔ le angomedi la twehwe konle, na mɔɔ fa ɔ rɛle wula Ɛdɛnkɛma anu la banyia ɔ nwo.
26Sonla mɔɔ fa ɔ rɛle to ɔ ngome ɔ nwo zo la le koasea, na mɔɔ fa nrɛlɛbɛ dua la, bɛbalie ye ngoane.
27Sonla mɔɔ nyia ye a ɔmaa ehyianvolɛma bie la ɛnrɛli ehyia, na mɔɔ ɔnyia ye a ɔfa ɔ nye ɔfea la, menli dɔɔnwo bawa ye amonle.
28Saa amumuyɛma dwazo a, menli nriandi fea, na saa bɛ bo zo minli a, tenlenema kpazi.

english_text:
Use Good Sense
1If you keep being stubborn
after many warnings,
you will suddenly discover
you have gone too far.
2When justice rules a nation,
everyone is glad;
when injustice rules,
everyone groans.
3If you love wisdom
your parents will be glad,
but chasing after bad women
will cost you everything.
4An honest ruler
makes the nation strong;
a ruler who takes bribes
will bring it to ruin.
5Flattery is nothing less
than setting a trap.
6Your sins will catch you,
but everyone who lives right
will sing and celebrate.
7The wicked don't care
about the rights of the poor,
but good people do.
8Sneering at others is a spark
that sets a city on fire;
using good sense can put out
the flames of anger.
9Be wise and don't sue a fool.
You won't get satisfaction,
because all the fool will do
is sneer and shout.
10A murderer hates everyone
who is honest
and lives right.
11Don't be a fool
and quickly lose your temper—
be sensible and patient.
12A ruler who listens to lies
will have corrupt officials.
13The poor and all who abuse them
must each depend on God
for light.
14Kings who are fair to the poor
will rule a long time.
15Correct your children,
and they will be wise;
children out of control
disgrace their mothers.
16Crime increases
when crooks are in power,
but law-abiding citizens
will see them fall.
17If you correct your children,
they will bring you peace
and happiness.
18Without guidance from God
law and order disappear,
but God blesses everyone
who obeys his Law.
19 Even when servants are smart,
it takes more than words
to make them obey.
20There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who speaks
without thinking.
21Slaves that you treat kindly
from their childhood
will cause you sorrow.
22A person with a quick temper
stirs up arguments
and commits a lot of sins.
23Too much pride brings disgrace;
humility leads to honor.
24If you take part in a crime
you are your worst enemy,
because even under oath
you can't tell the truth.
25Don't fall into the trap
of being a coward—
trust the Lord,
and you will be safe.
26Many try to make friends
with a ruler,
but justice comes
from the Lord.
27Good people and criminals
can't stand each other.
translation_text:
1Sonla mɔɔ bɛtwi ɔ nyunlu a ɛnee anzosesebɛ ala a ɔyɛ la banwu ɔ nyunlu arɛlevilɛ nu mɔɔ ɔnrɛhola ɔ nloa gyinla a.
2Saa tenlenema ɛlɛbu maanle a, menli ne anye die, na saa amumuyɛma ɛlɛbu maanle a, menli ne su bɛ kunlu.
3Sonla mɔɔ kulo nrɛlɛbɛ la maa ɔ ze di fɛlɛko, na sonla mɔɔ nee tuutuuma a tu la sɛkye ye debie biala.
4Belemgbunli mɔɔ di pɛlepɛle la fa anzonudwolɛ ba ye maanle ne anu, na mɔɔ dahuu kpondɛ ahyɛlɛdeɛ la sɛkye maanle ne.
5Sonla mɔɔ dahuu kanvo ɔ gɔnwo adalɛ nu la sua ɔ gɔnwo ne ɛhane.
6Sonla mɔɔ di ɛtane la mɛladonlɛ kakyi ɛhane kye ye, na sonla mɔɔ di boɛ la to edwɛne na ɔ nye die.
7Tenlenenli ze kpalɛ mɔɔ di wɔ ehyianvolɛma la, na mɔɔ ati yɛ se la ɛnde zɛhae adwenle ne abo.
8Agolobɛnwoma maa senle tɔ suakpole zo, na nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma maa ɛya dwo.
9Saa nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ nee koasea su kpolera a, koasea ne teɛdea nu sele mgbole mgbole; ɔmmaa bɛnnyia bɛ nzo fee.
10Menli mɔɔ ku menli mgbane mgbane la kyi sonla mɔɔ di pɛlepɛle la, na menli mɔɔ le tenlene la kpondɛ zɔhane sonla ne nee ngoane.
11Koasea fa ɛya a, ɔye ɔkile, na nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ fa ɛya a, ɔkomo ɔ nwo zo.
12Saa maanlebuvolɛ di adalɛ ngehanleɛ nzi a, ye mgbanyima yɛ amumuyɛ.
13Ehyianli nee nzisinli sɛ debie ko anwo, Ɛdɛnkɛma maa bɛ mu nwiɔ ɛnyelɛ.
14Saa belemgbunli bua ehyianvolɛma ndɛne pɛpɛ a, ɔbali ye ebia ne yeahyɛ.
15Empele nee ndeanlɛ maa kakula nwu nrɛlɛbɛ, na kakula mɔɔ bɛkɛdu ɔ nwo bɛkɛhyɛ ye la gua ɔ nli anyunlu aze.
16Saa amumuyɛma bu maanle a, mɛladonlɛ so dɔɔnwo, na tenlenema banwu bɛ azedɔlɛ nu.
17Saa ɛ ra nrenya yɛ ɛtane a tea ye, ɔbamaa ɛ nzo nu adwo wɔ na ɛ nye alie.
18Ɛleka mɔɔ bɛnga Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ la, menli yɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛkulo la; nyilalɛ ɛha sonla ne mɔɔ di mɛla zo la.
19Bɛnva bɛ nloa mgbane bɛndea akɛlɛ, ɔluakɛ ɔbade ɔ bo bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko ɔnrɛpili.
20Wɔnwu sonla mɔɔ anloa yɛ ndɛ la ɛlɛ ɔ? Koasea lɛ anyelazo dɔɔnwo tɛla ye.
21Sonla mɔɔ kɛdɛfɛdɛfɛ ye sonvolɛ vi ye ngakula nu la, ɔ nye zo katete ye la ɛnee yeli ye agya.
22Sonla mɔɔ ɛngyɛ na yeava ɛya la twehwe mgbonde nee konle, yɛɛ mɔɔ ɛya wɔ ye ahonle zo la fa mɛladonlɛ dɔɔnwo ba.
23Sonla mɔɔ tu ɔ nwo la adubɛnwo ne gua ɔ nyunlu aze, na mɔɔ le bɛlɛvo la banyia ɔ nyunlu.
24Sonla mɔɔ nee awule tu la kyi ɔdaye mumua ne ye ngoane; ɔte amowa ne, noko ɔngola ɔnga nɔhalɛ ne.
25Sonla mɔɔ le sulosulo la sua ɔ nwo ɛhane, na mɔɔ arɛle wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anu la anwo le kɔlɔnwo.
26Menli dɔɔnwo kulo kɛ bɛsɔ maanlebuvolɛ ne anye, noko Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ sonla nyia pɛlepɛlelilɛ a.
27Sonla mɔɔ le tenlene la kyibadeɛ a le sonla mɔɔ ɛnli boɛ la, yɛɛ mɔɔ ye ɛbɛlabɔlɛ ne le fɔɔnwo la le kyibadeɛ maa amumuyɛnli.

english_text:
The Sayings of Agur
1These are the sayings
and the message
of Agur son of Jakeh.
Someone cries out to God,
“I am completely worn out!
How can I last?
2I am far too stupid
to be considered human.
3I never was wise,
and I don't understand
what God is like.”
4 Has anyone gone up to heaven
and come back down?
Has anyone grabbed hold
of the wind?
Has anyone wrapped up the sea
or marked out boundaries
for the earth?
If you know of any
who have done such things,
then tell me their names
and their children's names.
5Everything God says is true—
and it's a shield for all
who come to him for safety.
6Don't change what God has said!
He will correct you and show
that you are a liar.
7There are two things, Lord,
I want you to do for me
before I die:
8Make me absolutely honest
and don't let me be too poor
or too rich.
Give me just what I need.
9If I have too much to eat,
I might forget about you;
if I don't have enough,
I might steal
and disgrace your name.
10Don't tell a slave owner
something bad about one
of the slaves.
That slave will curse you,
and you will be in trouble.
11Some people curse their father
and even their mother;
12others think they are perfect,
but they are stained by sin.
13Some people are stuck-up
and act like snobs;
14others are so greedy
that they gobble up
the poor and homeless.
15Greed has twins,
each named “Give me!”
There are three or four things
that are never satisfied:
16The world of the dead
and a childless wife,
the thirsty earth
and a flaming fire.
17Don't make fun of your father
or disobey your mother—
crows will peck out your eyes,
and buzzards will eat
the rest of you.
18There are three or four things
I cannot understand:
19 How eagles fly so high
or snakes crawl on rocks,
how ships sail the ocean
or people fall in love.
20An unfaithful wife says,
“Sleeping with another man
is as natural as eating.”
21There are three or four things
that make the earth tremble
and are unbearable:
22A slave who becomes king,
a fool who eats too much,
23a hateful woman
who finds a husband,
and a slave who takes the place
of the woman who owns her.
24On this earth four things
are small but very wise:
25Ants, who seem to be feeble,
but store up food
all summer long;
26badgers, who seem to be weak,
but live among the rocks;
27locusts, who have no king,
but march like an army;
28lizards, which can be caught
in your hand,
but sneak into palaces.
29Three or four creatures
really strut around:
30Those fearless lions
who rule the jungle,
31those proud roosters,
those mountain goats,
and those rulers
who have no enemies.
32If you are foolishly bragging
or planning something evil,
then stop it now!
33If you churn milk
you get butter;
if you pound on your nose,
you get blood—
and if you stay angry,
you get in trouble.
translation_text:
Egɛ anloa edwɛkɛ
1Gyeki mɔɔ vi Masa la ara Egɛ anloa edwɛkɛ ɛne.
Nrenya ne hanle hilele Ayeteɛle,
ɛhɛe, ɔhanle ɔhilele Ayeteɛle nee Yukale kɛ:
2“Medame, nɔhalɛ, meyɛ mgbane.
Menlɛ ndelebɛbo mɔɔ sonla ɔwɔ kɛ nyia la.
3Metɛsukoale nrɛlɛbɛ,
yɛɛ menlɛ Nwuanzanwuanza Ko ne anwo adwenle.
4Nwane a ɛvo ɛhɔ anwuma ɛzia ɛra a?
Nwane a ɛhola ɛhye anwoma ɔ sa nu a?
Nwane a ɛva ye tɛladeɛ ɛkyekye nzule a?
Nwane a ɛhyehyɛ azɛlɛ ye muleɛ ne mɔ a?
Kɛ bɛfɛlɛ ye ɛ, yɛɛ kɛ bɛfɛlɛ ɔ ra ne ɛ?
Nɔhalɛ, ɛze!
5“Nyamenle anloa edwɛkɛ biala yɛ nɔhalɛ; ɔle enyinlike ɔkeda bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnriandi bɛba ye ɛkɛ ne la anwo zo. 6Mmafa edwɛkɛ ɛboka ye edwɛkɛ nwo, anrɛɛ ɔkɛdea wɔ ɔkɛmaa bɛkɛnwu kɛ ɛle adalɛ.”
Mrɛlɛbulɛ bieko
7Ninyɛne nwiɔ yɛɛ mebiza ye wɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne a, Nyamenle, yɛ maa me kolaa na meawu: 8Ye adalɛbɔlɛ nee adalɛ ɛbɛla biala fi me nu bɔkɔɔ; mmamaa medi ehyia anzɛɛ menyia me nwo. Maa menyia aleɛ mɔɔ menwɔhyia nwolɛ la ala, 9anrɛɛ me ko yi a, menwɔkpo wɔ na menwɔbiza kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma a le nwane?” Anzɛɛ anrɛɛ menwɔli ehyia, menwɔwua, na menwɔgua me Nyamenle ne duma ne anwo evinli.
10Mmatoɔdoa sonvolɛ ɛkile ɔ menle, anrɛɛ ɔkɛwa wɔ amonle ɔkɛmaa ɛkɛli fɔlɛ.
11Menli bie wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛwa bɛ ze mɔ amonle yɛɛ bɛmbu mɔɔ bɛ nli mɔ yɛ maa bɛ la.
12Menli bie wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛnea a bɛ nwo te, noko bɛ nwo le evinli ngome.
13Menli bie wɔ ɛkɛ, bɛ nwo yɛ fɛ, bɛ nye ma le nzenzɛɛnye, bɛtwehwe bɛ nye anzi.
14Menli bie wɔ ɛkɛ, bɛ gye le konle dadeɛ; bɛ gye nlane le kɛ dadeɛ, bɛfa bɛsɛkye menli mɔɔ yɛ anwunvɔne wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo, na bɛsɛkye menli mɔɔ ehyia na bɛwɔ menli avinli la.
15Nrenya bie mɔɔ ɛyɛ ɔ nwo mimike la lɛ ɔ mra mraalɛ nwiɔ, bɛ ɛzunlɛ a le, “Fa maa me, fa maa me!”
Ninyɛne nsa wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛ kunlu ɛndwo bɛ nwo; mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la bɔbɔ ɛnga kɛ, “Yeyɛ boɛ!”
16Bɛmɛ a le: Ɛbolɔ sua zo,
raalɛ mɔɔ le mota,
azɛlɛ ye mɔɔ nzule ɛnyi ye ɛlɛ,
yɛɛ senle mɔɔ ɛlɛsɔ mɔɔ bɛnnua ye ɛlɛ.
17Awie biala mɔɔ si ɔ ze amgbu na ɔmbu ɔ nli bie la, mbɔnza nu ahɔhɔsɛlɛ badudu ɔ nye na mgbɔtɛ arali.
18Ninyɛne nsa a wɔ ɛkɛ ne mɔɔ yɛ me nwanwane a; mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la, mende ɔ bo.
19Bɛmɛ a le:
Kɛ kɔleɛ si tu dua anwomanyunlu,
kɛ ɛwɔlɛ si dua bodane zo,
Kɛ meli si dua nyevile kunlu,
yɛɛ kɛ nrenya nee raalɛ adwenle si yia ɛhulolɛ nu la.
20Awuvolɛ raalɛ mɔɔ to awuvolɛvalɛ mɛla ne la subane ɛne: ɔdi, ɔkyikyi ɔ nloa anwo na yeaha kɛ, “Medame, metɛyɛle nyɛleɛ ɛtane biala!”
21Ninyɛne nsa yɛɛ azɛlɛ ye zo mɔɔ ɔngola bɛ a, mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la maa ɔgyinla a ɔnyɛ boɛ.
22Bɛmɛ a le:
Kanranli mɔɔ kɛli ebia,
Koasea mɔɔ kɛli ɔ ko kɛyi,
23raalɛ mɔɔ awie ɛngulo ye na ɔkɛnyia ɔ hu,
yɛɛ sonvolɛ raalɛ mɔɔ kɛli ɔ menle raalɛ agya la.
24Ninyɛne nna wɔ aleɛabo mɔɔ le ngyikyi kpalɛ, na bɛze nrɛlɛbɛ kpole kpalɛ a. Bɛmɛ ɛne:
25Ngyigyilira: Bɛ nwo ɛnyɛ se, noko wawaa
nu bɛkpondɛ bɛ aleɛ biala mɔɔ bɛbahyia nwolɛ la.
26Azulenupema: Bɛnle katakyiema,
noko bɛ alaleɛ wɔ bodane ne mɔ anu.
27Abɛbɛ: Bɛnlɛ belemgbunli, noko bɛse kɛ bɛkɔ a,
bɛkɔ ye ɛhonlone ɛhonlone.
28Kekelebetile: Sonla kola kye bɛ ɔ sa nu,
noko bɛwɔ arelemgbunli azua nu.
29Ninyɛne nsa a bɛ ɛdialɛ le kɛnlɛma a, mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la agyakɛ ɛdudulɛ bɔbɔ le kɛnlɛma bo zolɛ.
30Bɛmɛ a le:
Awenade,
ɔle nane kɔsɔɔti bɛ katakyie.
Ɔnzulo ɛhwee.
31Abɔnkye nyinli
nee akɔlɛ nyinli mɔɔ ɛlɛtudu bɛ gyakɛ,
yɛɛ belemgbunli mɔɔ ɛlɛtudu ɔ gyakɛ wɔ
ye maanlema anyunlu la.
32Saa wɔyɛ koasea, wɔmemaa ɛ nwo zo, anzɛɛ wɔbɔ adwenle ɛtane a, ɛnee kakyi wɔ adwenle. 33Ɔluakɛ saa ɛka ɛnlankɛ nyɛfonzule nu somasoma a, ɔpɛ mgbokɛ, ɛmia ebonyile somasoma a, mogya vi nu finde, yɛɛ ɛka sonla ɛya somasoma a, ɔwie konle.

english_text:
What King Lemuel's Mother Taught Him
1These are the sayings
that King Lemuel of Massa
was taught by his mother.
2My son Lemuel, you were born
in answer to my prayers,
so listen carefully.
3Don't waste your life
chasing after women!
This has ruined many kings.
4Kings and leaders
should not get drunk
or even want to drink.
5Drinking makes you forget
your responsibilities,
and you mistreat the poor.
6Beer and wine are only
for the dying or for those
who have lost all hope.
7Let them drink and forget
how poor and miserable
they feel.
8But you must defend
those who are helpless
and have no hope.
9Be fair and give justice
to the poor and homeless.
In Praise of a Good Wife
10A truly good wife
is the most precious treasure
a man can find!
11Her husband depends on her,
and she never
lets him down.
12She is good to him
every day of her life,
13and with her own hands
she gladly makes clothes.
14She is like a sailing ship
that brings food
from across the sea.
15She gets up before daylight
to prepare food for her family
and for her servants.
16She knows how to buy land
and how to plant a vineyard,
17and she always works hard.
18She knows when to buy or sell,
and she stays busy
until late at night.
19She spins her own cloth,
20and she helps the poor
and the needy.
21Her family has warm clothing,
and so she doesn't worry
when it snows.
22She does her own sewing,
and everything she wears
is beautiful.
23Her husband is a well-known
and respected leader
in the city.
24She makes clothes to sell
to the shop owners.
25She is strong and graceful,
as well as cheerful
about the future.
26Her words are sensible,
and her advice
is thoughtful.
27She takes good care
of her family
and is never lazy.
28Her children praise her,
and with great pride
her husband says,
29“There are many good women,
but you are the best!”
30Charm can be deceiving,
and beauty fades away,
but a woman
who honors the Lord
deserves to be praised.
31Show her respect—
praise her in public
for what she has done.
translation_text:
Bɛtu Belemgbunli folɛ
1Edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Masa Belemgbunli Lɛmuwɛle ɔ nli vale dule ye folɛ la ɛne:
2“Duzu ɔ, me ra nrenya? Me ko ɛzɛne, duzu ɔ? Duzu ɔ, me ra nrenya mɔɔ menluale ɛwɔkɛbɔlɛ zo a menwole ye a? 3Mmasɛkye wɔ anwosesebɛ wɔ mraalɛ nwo. Mmafa wɔ adwenle ɛmaa menli mɔɔ sɛkye arelemgbunli la. 4Ɔnle kpalɛ ɔmmaa arelemgbunli, O Lɛmuwɛle. Ɔnle kpalɛ ɔmmaa arelemgbunli kɛ bɛkɛnlo nwanye anzɛɛ maanlebuvolɛma kɛ bɛ ti akunlu kɛra nza ɛsesebɛ zo, 5anrɛɛ bɛkɛbo na bɛ rɛle kɛvi mɛla ne mɔɔ bɛli bɛdo ɛkɛ la, na bɛkɛzɛkye menli mɔɔ ɛlɛnwu amaneɛ la edwɛkɛ. 6Fa nza ɛsesebɛ maa sonla mɔɔ anye gyi ewule nu la, na fa nwanye maa menli mɔɔ arɛle ɛbɔ kpole la. 7Maa bɛnlo na bɛ rɛle ɛvi bɛ ehyia, na bɛangakye bɛ anwubɛnyunlu ne bieko.
8“Ka maa menli mɔɔ le mumule la, na di menli mɔɔ ɛnlɛ bie la edwɛkɛ maa bɛ. 9Buke ɛ nloa, bua ndɛne tenlene nu, na gyinla maa ehyianvolɛma nee menli mɔɔ ɛhyia la.”
Yelɛ kpalɛ
10Yelɛ kpalɛ, nwane a kɛnyia ye a? Ɔsonle bolɛ ɔtɛla anwoneɛ.
11Ɔ hu fa ɔ rɛle wula ye nu, yɛɛ ɔnrɛhyia ɛhwee.
12Yelɛ ne yɛ ɔ hu boɛ, ɔngyegye ye wɔ mekɛ tendenle muala mɔɔ ɔde ngoane nu la.
13Ɔkpondɛ mboane enrinli nee bolɔfodɔ dwɛsɛ na ɔfa ɔnwo ninyɛne.
14Ɔle kɛ gualilɛ meli, ɔfa aleɛ ɔfi moa moa ɔba.
15Ɔdwazo ndɛ mɔɔ aleɛ ɛtɛwiele kye la ɔkpondɛ aleɛ ɔmaa ye sua nu amra, na ɔkile ye sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ gyima ɔmaa bɛyɛ.
16Ɔkpondɛ azɛlɛ ɔtɔ, na ɔfa ɔdaye ye ezukoa ɔtɔ ma ɔyɛ vanye egyinli.
17Dahuu ɔmaa ɔ nwo yɛ se na ɔyɛ gyima ɛsesebɛ.
18Ɔnea ɔnwu kɛ ye gualilɛ zo ɛra nvasoɛ. Ye kɛnlaneɛ ɛnnu nɔɔzo.
19Ɔdaye ɔbɛka ye nyɛma, ɔnwo ye ndanlɛ.
20Ɔbuke ɔ sa nu ɔmaa ehyianvolɛma, na ɔmaa ɔ sa dwu menli mɔɔ ɛhyia la anwo zo.
21Saa ezukɔtweaba ɛlɛtɔ a ɔ kunlu ɛndu wɔ ye sua nu amra ati, ɔluakɛ ye sua nu amra amuala wula mboane enrinli kɔkɔlɛ adɛladeɛ.
22Ɔnwo ɔdaye ye ɛkpa zo ndanlɛ, na ɔwula lenen adɛladeɛ nee adɛladeɛ ngɛnlɛma anye buluwu nee kɔkɔlɛ afonla.
23Ɔ hu kɔtɛnla bagua ne anu wɔ anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa a, awie biala nwu ye wɔ mgbanyima ne mɔ avinli.
24Ɔnwo lenen adɛladeɛ ɔtɔne bɛ; ɔnwo ndabule ɔtɔne bɛ ɔmaa gualilɛma.
25Ɔ nwo yɛ se, yɛɛ bɛdi ye eni; ɔnzulo mekɛ mɔɔ bara la.
26Ɔtendɛ nrɛlɛbɛ nu, yɛɛ ye ngilehilelɛ fane kpalɛyɛlɛ nwo.
27Ɔnea ye sua nu amra boɛ wɔ bɛ ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu, yɛɛ ɔnli ɔ sa anzi aleɛ.
28Ɔ mra dwazo na bɛyileyila ye. Ɔ hu noko zɔhane ala, na ɔye ye ayɛlɛ.
29Ɔ hu ka kɛ, “Mraalɛ dɔɔnwo ɛbɔ mɔdenle kpalɛ wɔ bɛ hu mɔ anwo, na wɔmɔ, ɛtɛla bɛ kɔsɔɔti.”
30Sili le mɛlɛbɛla, yɛɛ anwofɛlɛko le debie mgbane, na raalɛ mɔɔ sulo Ɛdɛnkɛma la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛye ye ayɛlɛ.
31Kanvo yelɛ kpalɛ wɔ ye gyima mɔɔ ɔyɛ la anwo, na maa bɛye ye ayɛlɛ bagua nu wɔ ɔ sa anloa gyima nwo.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
Ɛbɛlabɔlɛ le mgbane
1Nolobɔvo ne, Devidi ara nrenya ne, mɔɔ le Gyɛlusalɛm belemgbunli ne edwɛkɛ ne ɛne.
2Nolobɔvo ne se, ɔle mgbane, mgbane, ɛbɛlabɔlɛ le mgbane, ɔ muala le mgbane. 3Duzu nvasoɛ a sonla nyia ye wɔ ɛvɛlɛ kpole ye mɔɔ ɔfɛ aleɛabo la anwo a? 4Awolɛndoazo ko kɔ, awolɛndoazo ko ba, noko kɛ ewiade ne de ala la a ɔde a. 5Sɛnzɛne ne tudu, sɛnzɛne ne tɔ, na ɔka ɔ nwo waa ɔkɔ ɛleka mɔɔ ɔtudu la. 6Anwoma ne bɔ kɔ nyiakɛ, ɔpɛne ɔ nwo ɔkɔdi sɔlɔ; ɔpɛnepɛne ɔ nwo toonwo na eza ɔbadua ɔ bo zo ne bieko. 7Azule kɔsɔɔti se gua nyevile nu, noko nyevile ne ɛnyi ɛlɛ; bɛsia bɛkɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛbɔ bɛ bo la, na bɛbɔ ɔ bo bɛse bieko. 8Ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti wie ɛvɛlɛ, ɛvɛlɛ mɔɔ dasanli ɛnrɛhola ye ka a. Ɛnyelɛ nea a ɔnvɛ, yɛɛ ɛnzonlɛ tie a ɔnyi. 9Mɔɔ ɛzi la yɛɛ bazi a, yɛɛ mɔɔ bɛyɛ la yɛɛ bɛbayɛ a; debie fofolɛ biala ɛnle aleɛabo. 10Asoo debie wɔ ɛkɛ ne mɔɔ bɛha kɛ, “Bɛnlea, ɛhye le fofolɛ” ɔ? Ɔwɔ ɛkɛ ne dɛbadɛba kolaa na bɛawo yɛ. 11Awie biala ɛngakye mɔɔ ɛze ɛhɔ la, yɛɛ awie biala ɛnrɛhakye ninyɛne mɔɔ nzinlii basisi menli mɔɔ bara la mekɛ zo la.
Adwenlekilevo ne anwubielɛ
12Medame Nolobɔvo, medɛnla Gyɛlusalɛm meli Yizilayɛ belemgbunli. 13Membɔle mɔdenle kɛ mefa nrɛlɛbɛ meavedevede ninyɛne nu meazukoa debie biala mɔɔ bɛyɛ ye ewiade ye anu la. Na menwunle kɛ ɔle gyima mɔɔ ye ɛyɛlɛ ɛnyɛ fɛ na Nyamenle ɛva ɛmaa menli kɛ bɛyɛ a. 14Menwu debie biala mɔɔ bɛyɛ ye aleɛabo la, na nea, ɔ muala le mgbane. Ɔle kɛ ɛlɛkye anwoma la. 15Debie mɔɔ kyea la bɛtenrɛ ye a ɔndenrɛ, yɛɛ debie mɔɔ ɛnle ɛkɛ la bɛndia.
16 Menganle mengilele me nwo kɛ, “Menwu nrɛlɛbɛ kpole kpalɛ medɛla belemgbunli biala mɔɔ ɛli ebia wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm la; yɛɛ me ti ɛdi nrɛlɛbɛ nee adwenle nu.” 17Membɔle mɔdenle kɛ menea ngakyile mɔɔ wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ, ɛzɛlɛde, yɛɛ ngoaseade nu la. Na menwunle kɛ ɛhye noko le kɛ ɛlɛkye anwoma la. 18Ɔluakɛ nrɛlɛbɛ dɔɔnwo nee abodelɛ dɔɔnwo a lua a, yɛɛ awie biala mɔɔ ye adwenle kɛbuke dɔɔnwo la twehwe nyanelilɛ dɔɔnwo maa ɔ nwo.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
1Menganle mengilele me nwo kɛ, “Medielie me nye meanlea kɛ fɛlɛkolilɛ si de la.” Na nea, ɛhye noko le debie mgbane. 2Menganle ye wɔ ɛzelekɛ nwo kɛ, “Ɔle ɛzɛlɛde” yɛɛ menganle ye wɔ anyelielɛ noko nwo kɛ, “Duzu nvasoɛ a wɔ zolɛ a?” 3Memanle me nrɛlɛbɛ zinzale me na menvale me adwenle memkpondɛle adenle mɔɔ medua zolɛ meava nwanye mealielie me nye, na meazɔ ngoaseadeyɛlɛ nu kɔkpula kɛ menwɔnwu mɔɔ le kpalɛ maa menli, mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ wɔ aleɛabo wɔ bɛ ngoane mekɛ ekyi ye anu la.
4 Menyɛle ninyɛne mgbole; mensisile azua na menzonle me ti anwo vanye egyinli. 5Mengyele me ti anwo tola nee ma tola na menluale mbaka mɔɔ so ma ngakyile ngakyile la wɔ nu. 6Membɔle nzule bula mɔɔ mesa nuhua nzule megugua mbaka mɔɔ menwɔlua la azo. 7 Mendɔle ahanra, mrenya nee mraalɛ, na menyianle ahanra mɔɔ bɛwole bɛ medame me awuke nu la. Eza menyianle nlankɛ nee nyɛmoa mendɛlale awie biala mɔɔ ɛdɛnla Gyɛlusalɛm ɛlɛ la. 8 Memboɔboale dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke yɛɛ arelemgbunli nee maanzinli maanzinli gyadeɛ nloa. Menyianle mrenya nee mraalɛ edwɛndolɛma, yɛɛ debie mɔɔ sonla nrenya anye die nwo la, mgbɔnla dɔɔnwo.
9 Yemɔti menyɛle sonlakpole mendɛlale menli mɔɔ li me nyunlu wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm la, yɛɛ me nrɛlɛbɛ ne ammaa meamkpo aze. 10Debie biala mɔɔ mekpondɛle la, menyianle ye. Meambɔ me nwo abolɛ wɔ anyelielɛ nu. Debie biala mɔɔ menyɛle gyima menyianle ye la me nye liele nwolɛ. Ɛhye a le me ɛvɛlɛ nwo ahatualɛ a. 11Akee mendwenlenle mɔɔ meyɛ la amuala nee ɛvɛlɛ mɔɔ mevɛ bɛ ɛyɛlɛ nu la anwo, na menwunle kɛ ɛhye mɔ amuala le mgbane. Ɔle kɛ ɛlɛkye anwoma la. Debie biala anwo ɛnlɛ nvasoɛ wɔ aleɛabo.
12Yemɔti membɔle ɔ bo kɛ medwenle nrɛlɛbɛ, ɛzɛlɛde, yɛɛ ngoaseade nwo meade bɛ bo, ɔluakɛ duzu a sonla mɔɔ bali belemgbunli agya la kɛhola kɛyɛ a? Kyesɛ mɔɔ belemgbunli ne ɛyɛ ye dɛba la ala. 13Akee menwunle kɛ nrɛlɛbɛ le kpalɛ tɛla ngoaseade, kɛmɔ wienyi le kpalɛ tɛla awozinli la. 14Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ anye gyi ɔ ti anwo, na koasea dua awozinli nu. Noko akee menwunle kɛ bɛ muala bɛ awieleɛ le ko. 15Akee menganle mengilele me nwo kɛ, “Mɔɔ si koasea nwo zo la a bazi medame noko me nwo zo a. Duzu ati yɛɛ akee menwu nrɛlɛbɛ kpole zɛhae a?” Na menganle mengilele me nwo kɛ ɛhye noko le mgbane. 16Ɔluakɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ o, koasea o, bɛnrɛhakye biala dahuu. Mekɛ bara amaa bɛ rɛle avi bɛ bɔkɔɔ. Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ wu yɛɛ koasea wu. 17Yemɔti mengyile ɛbɛlabɔlɛ, ɔboalekɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛyɛ ye aleɛabo la twe edwɛkɛ nyane maa me, ɔluakɛ ɔ muala le mgbane, yɛɛ ɔle kɛ ɛlɛkye anwoma la.
18Mengyile me ɛvɛlɛ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ mevɛ aleɛabo la, ɔluakɛ menwunle kɛ ɔwɔ kɛ megyakyi debie biala memaa me kɔliagya; 19na nwane a ze a, saa ɔle nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ anzɛɛ ɔle koasea a? Noko akee ɔbahendehende debie biala mɔɔ meva me nrɛlɛbɛ mevɛ mekpondɛ la azo. Ɛhye noko le mgbane. 20Yemɔti menvule me nwo kɛ mevɛ ɛvɛlɛ kpole ɛhye wɔ aleɛabo a, 21ɔboalekɛ ɔdwu mekɛ ne bie a, ɔwɔ kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛva nrɛlɛbɛ, adwenle, nee ɔ sa anloa gyima ɛkpondɛ debie la gyakyi ɔ muala maa sonla mɔɔ anvɛ fee la maa ɔfa ɔyɛ ɔ nwo kutukɛtɛɛ. Ɛhye noko le mgbane yɛɛ ɔle munzule kpole. 22Duzu nvasoɛ yɛɛ sonla nyia ye wɔ gyima ɛsesebɛ mɔɔ ɔyɛ nee ɛvɛlɛ mɔɔ ɔfɛ aleɛabo la azo a? 23 Ɔluakɛ ye mekɛ kɔsɔɔti le nyanedelɛ ngome, yɛɛ ye gyimayɛlɛ nu le abodelɛ ngome. Nɔɔzo bɔbɔ ɔda a ye adwenle ɛnla. Ɛhye noko le mgbane.
24 Debie kpalɛ biala ɛnle ɛkɛ ɛmmaa sonla ɛndɛla kɛ ɔkɛli na ɔkɛnlo, na ɔkɛlielie ɔ nye wɔ ye ɛvɛlɛ nwo. Menwunle kɛ ɛhye noko vi Nyamenle ɛkɛ, 25ɔluakɛ saa ɛkoati yemɔ a nwane a kɛnyia ye kɛli anzɛɛ kɛhola kɛlie ɔ nye a? 26 Ɔluakɛ Nyamenle maa sonla ne mɔɔ sɔ ɔ nye la nrɛlɛbɛ, adwenle, yɛɛ anyelielɛ, na ɛtanevolɛ ne ɛdeɛ, ɔmaa ɔsesa ɔkuohua bɛ nloa ɔmaa mɔɔ sɔ Nyamenle anye la. Ɛhye noko le mgbane; ɔle kɛ ɛlɛkye anwoma la.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.

1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
1Eza menwunle nzisi mɔɔ ɔlɛkɔ zolɛ wɔ aleɛabo la. Na nea, bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛsisi bɛ la, monle ebia bɛ, yɛɛ bɛnlɛ awie ɛnkyekye bɛ rɛle. Menli mɔɔ ɛlɛsisi bɛ la lɛ tumi, yemɔti bɛnlɛ awie ɛnkyekye bɛ rɛle. 2Na mendwenlenle nwolɛ kɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwu la ɛli ye moavolɛ ɛdɛla bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛde ngoane nu la. 3Na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnyia ye boɛ kpalɛ bɛdɛla mɔwuamra nee anyewɔzoamra la a le bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛwole bɛ na bɛanwu munzule ɛbɛla mɔɔ bɛlɛbɔ ye aleɛabo la.
4Akee menwunle kɛ ɛvɛlɛ muala nee sonla asa anloa gyima kɔsɔɔti gyi sonla agɔnwo anwo anyebolo zo. Ɛhye noko le mgbane; ɔle kɛ ɛlɛkye anwoma la. 5Koasea yɛɛ fa ɔ sa sia ye ɛzɔlɛ avinli na ɔkye ɛhɔne a. 6Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛkɛnyia ekyi na ɛkɛnyia anzonudwolɛ tɛla kɛ ɛkɛva ɛ sa nwiɔ ɛkɛhu ɛ nwo ɛvɛlɛ na ɛkɛpele kɛ ɛkye anwoma.
7Eza menwu kɛ debie bieko le mgbane wɔ aleɛabo. 8Sonla ne bie ɛnlɛ ye awie, ɔnlɛ ralɛ, ɔnlɛ adiema nrenya, noko ye ɛvɛlɛ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ, ɔ kunlu ɛndwo ye anwonyia nwo, yɛɛ ɔmbiza ɔ nwo kɛ, “Na nwane ati bɔbɔ yɛɛ melɛku me nwo ɛvɛlɛ na mekpo anyelielɛ a?” Ɛhye noko le debie mgbane na ɔle gyima funli.
9Menli nwiɔ le kpalɛ tɛla sonla ko, ɔboalekɛ bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛbɔ nu a bɛkola bɛyɛ gyima bɛnyia zolɛ nvasoɛ. 10Ɔluakɛ saa ko tɔ aze a, ko ne badwazo ye. Na munzule ɛha mɔɔ le baholɛ la, ɔ ngome la ati saa ɔtɔ aze a, awie bieko ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔboa ye yeamaa yeadwazo a. 11Bieko, saa menli nwiɔ da a bɛ nwo yɛ wuluwulu, na kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na sonla ko ahola amaa ɔ nwo ayɛ wuluwulu ɛ? 12Saa awie teta menli nwiɔ a, bɛkɛhola bɛkɛgyinla bɛ gyakɛ anu bɛkɛdɛla sonla ko. Nyɛma bɔ nwolɛ nsa a nuhua ɛdelɛ ɛnla aze.
13-14Ehyianli kola fi ye ehyia ne anu ɔbadi belemgbunli wɔ ye maanle nu, anzɛɛ awie kola fi efiade nla badi belemgbunli. Na saa ye mgbanyinli nu ɔyɛ koasea mɔɔ ɔnde folɛ la a, ɛnee kpavolɛ ehyianli mɔɔ ze nrɛlɛbɛ la tɛla ye ɛkpɔyɛɛ. 15Meneanle menli kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la, na menwunle kɛ kpavolɛ egyegyebaa bie wɔ bɛ avinli mɔɔ bali belemgbunli a. 16Menli ne zonle kpalɛ, yɛɛ ɔdaye a ɔsie bɛ muala a. Noko bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛrale amozi la, biala anye anlie ɔ nwo. Nɔhalɛ, ɛhye noko le debie mgbane. Ɔle kɛ ɛlɛkye anwoma la.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
Mmabɔ ɛwɔkɛ mɔɔ wɔandwenle nwolɛ la
1Saa ɛkɔ Nyamenle Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu a anrɛɛ nea boɛ. Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛkɛhɔ ɛkɛ ɛkɛhɔdie tɛla kɛ ɛkɛbɔ azu, kɛmɔ ahoasea yɛ la, ɔluakɛ bɛnze kɛ bɛlɛyɛ ɛtane. 2Dwenle nwolɛ kolaa na wɔabuke ɛ nloa, yɛɛ mmabɔ Nyamenle ɛwɔkɛ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛtɛdwenlenle nwolɛ la. Ɔluakɛ Nyamenle wɔ anwuma yɛɛ wɔmɔ ɛwɔ azɛlɛ ye azo, yemɔti maa wɔ edwɛkɛ ɛyɛ nzinrenzinra. 3Gyimayɛlɛ dɔɔnwo maa bɛka ɛlalɛ, yɛɛ koasea tendɛ dɔɔnwo. 4 Saa ɛbɔ Nyamenle ɛwɔkɛ a mmakyɛ na wɔaye, ɔluakɛ ɔ nye ɛnlie ahoasea nwo. Ye wɔ ɛwɔkɛ ne mɔɔ ɛkɛbɔ la. 5Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛnrɛbɔ ɛwɔkɛ fee tɛla kɛ ɛkɛbɔ na ɛnrɛye. 6Mmamaa ɛ nloa fa wɔ kɔ ɛtane nu na akee wɔaha wɔahile Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne kɛ tɛ ɛ nye fuu ɔ. Duzu ati a ɛkɛyɛ ɛkɛmaa Nyamenle kɛva ɛ nwo ɛya, na ɔkɛzɛkye ɛ sa anloa gyima mɔɔ wɔyɛ la ɛ? 7Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ wɔ ɛlalɛhanlɛ ɛlɛso la, ɛnee wɔ ɛdendɛlɛ mgbane mgbane ne mɔ ɛlɛso; wɔmɔ sulo Nyamenle.
Ɛbɛlabɔlɛ le mgbane
8Saa ɛnwu kɛ maanzinli bie anu bɛlɛsisi ehyianvolɛma, bɛnli pɛlepɛle bɛmmaa bɛ, yɛɛ bɛmmaa bɛ nwo ɛndɔ bɛ a, mmamaa ɔyɛ wɔ azibɛnwo, ɔluakɛ kpanyinli biala lɛ kpanyinli mɔɔ sie ɔdaye, yɛɛ bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛlɛ mgbanyinli mɔɔ sie bɛ a.
9Noko ɛhye mɔ amuala bɔbɔ, belemgbunli ati zɔ egyinli ne mɔ anu bɛyɔba ne mɔ.
10Sonla mɔɔ anye bolo ezukoa la akunlu ɛndwo ye ezukoa nwo ɛlɛ; yɛɛ mɔɔ anye bolo anwonyia la akunlu ɛndwo mɔɔ yenyia ye la anwo. Ɛhye noko le debie mgbane. 11Saa aleɛ bu a, menli dɔɔnwo nyia bie di. Nvasoɛ mɔɔ aleɛ menle ne nyia ye la a le kɛ ɔnwu kɛ bɛlɛdi. 12Saa gyimayɛvo nyia aleɛ dɔɔnwo di anzɛɛ yeannyia ye dɔɔnwo yeanli bɔbɔ a, ɔdafe botoo; na sukoavolɛ, kanza aleɛ bu ɔ nwo zo bɔbɔ a, adwenleadwenle ɛmmaa ɔnla.
13Menwu munzule kpole bie wɔ aleɛabo: sonla fa ye ezukoa sie toonwo maa ezukoa ne kakyi ɔ kɔme nu munzule. 14Ɔyɛ ezukoa ne mgbane mgbane ɔmaa ɔ muala fi ɔ sa; ɔle selɛ, ɔlɛ ɔ ra nrenya, noko ɔ sa nu fuenyi. 15 Kɛ sonla zile vi ɔ nli akunlu rale la yɛɛ ɔbazia yeahɔ a. Ɔlɛ ɔ nwo zɔhane a ɔrale a, yɛɛ ɔnrɛva ye gyima mɔɔ yeyɛ la anu debie ɔnrɛlɛ ɔ sa nu ɔnrɛhɔ. 16Ɛhye noko le munzule kpole. Kɛ sonla zile rale la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔbahɔ a. Na duzu nvasoɛ yɛɛ ɔnyia ye kɛ ɔkye anwoma a? 17Sonla bɔ ye ɛbɛla ne kɔsɔɔti wɔ awozinli nee nyane, akpule, ɛya nee anwonyane nu.
18Nea, debie mɔɔ menwu ye la a le kɛ: mekɛ ezinraa ɛhye mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛva ɛmaa sonla la, ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɔkɛli, ɔkɛnlo na ɔkɛlielie ɔ nye wɔ ɔdaye ɔ sa anloa gyima mɔɔ yeyɛ la anwo, ɔluakɛ ɛhye a le sonla afoa nu ɛdeɛ a. 19Saa Nyamenle maa sonla anwonyia nee agyadeɛ nee tumi kɛ ɔva ɔlie ɔ nye, na ɔzɔ ye kyɛfoa nu, ɔnyia anyelielɛ wɔ ye gyima nwo a, ɛnee nwu ye kɛ ɔle Nyamenle ahyɛlɛdeɛ. 20Ɔluakɛ sonla zɛhae ɛnrɛdwenle ye ngoane mekɛ nwo dɔɔnwo, ɔboalekɛ Nyamenle bamaa yeahɔ zolɛ yealie ɔ nye.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
7We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied. 8We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right. 9It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
10Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us. 11The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk? 12Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_text:
1Menwu munzule bie wɔ aleɛabo, na ɔgyi menli nwo zo kpalɛ kpalɛ. 2Nyamenle maa sonla ne bie nyia anwonyia, agyadeɛ, yɛɛ enililɛ, nɔhalɛ, ɔlɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɔkpondɛ la, noko Nyamenle ɛmmaa ye tumi ɛmmaa ɔnlidi nwolɛ ɔnva ɔnlie ɔ nye. Ɛyɛvolɛ bie yɛɛ badi a. Ɛhye le debie mgbane; ɔmaa sonla edwɛkɛ yɛ nyane kpalɛ. 3Saa sonla wo mralɛ ɛya ko, ɔnyi ɔdi ɛvolɛ dɔɔnwo, ɔyɛ kpanyinli kpalɛ na yeanlie ɔ nye wɔ ɛbɛla nu ninyɛne kpalɛ nwo, na ɔwu na ye ɛzielɛ nu anyɛ kɛnlɛma a, ɛnee ralɛ mɔɔ kɛkpɔne la tɛla ye ɛkpɔyɛɛ. 4Ɔluakɛ yemɔ ɔba mgbane na ɔdua awozinli nu ɔkɔ, na awozinli ne keda ye duma zo. 5Eza yemɔ yeannwu sɛnzɛne ne anzɛɛ debie biala, noko ɔnyia ɛnwomenlelielɛ ɔtɛla sonla ne mɔɔ kɛli ɛvolɛ dɔɔnwo la. 6Saa sonla di ɛvolɛ apenle nwiɔ bɔbɔ na yeanli ɔ ti ɛlɛ a, bɛ muala bɛkɔ ɛleka ko.
7Sonla ɛvɛlɛ kɔsɔɔti wie aleɛlilɛ ko ye ala, noko ɔ ti akunlu ɛnye aleɛ zo ɛlɛ. 8Ɛnee duzu a nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ fa tɛla koasea a? Yɛɛ saa ehyianli nwu kɛ bɛsi bɛsɔ ɛbɛla sa la a, duzu a ɔnyia ye a? 9Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛ kunlu kɛdwo mɔɔ ɛlɛ la anwo tɛla kɛ dahuu ɛkɛbɔ mɔdenle kɛ ɛkpondɛ fofolɛ. Ɛhye noko le debie mgbane na ɔle kɛ ɛlɛkye anwoma.
10Debie biala mɔɔ ɛzi la ɛnee bɛha bɛdo ɛkɛ dɛba, yɛɛ yɛ muala yɛze kɛ sonla si de la, bɛ nee sonla mɔɔ anwo yɛ se tɛla bɛ la ɛnli butule. 11Ɛdendɛlɛ dɔɔnwo maa bɛka mgbane mgbane, yɛɛ ɔmmaa sonla ɛbɛla ɛngakyi. 12Nwane a kɛhola kɛnwu debie mɔɔ le kpalɛ maa sonla wɔ ye ngoane mekɛ ezinraa ɛhye mɔɔ se waa kɛ ɛlawolɛ la anu a? Saa sonla wu a, kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na yeanwu mɔɔ bazi ɔ nzi wɔ aleɛabo la ɛ?

english_text:
The Best in Life
1 A good reputation
at the time of death
is better than loving care
at the time of birth.
2It's better to go to a funeral
than to attend a feast;
funerals remind us
that we all must die.
3Choose sorrow over laughter
because a sad face
may hide a happy heart.
4A sensible person mourns,
but fools always laugh.
5Correction from someone wise
is better by far
than praise from fools.
6Foolish laughter is stupid.
It sounds like thorns
crackling in a fire.
7Corruption makes fools
of sensible people,
and bribes can ruin you.
8Something completed is better
than something just begun;
patience is better
than too much pride.
9 Only fools get angry quickly
and hold a grudge.
10It isn't wise to ask,
“Why is everything worse
than it used to be?”
11Having wisdom is better
than an inheritance.
12Wisdom will protect you
just like money;
knowledge with good sense
will lead you to life.
13Think of what God has done!
If God makes something crooked,
can you make it straight?
14When times are good,
you should be cheerful;
when times are bad,
think about what it means.
God makes them both
to keep us from knowing
what will happen next.
Some of Life's Questions
15I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper. 16So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart! 17Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool. 18Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
19Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
20No one in this world always does right.
21Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you. 22Haven't you cursed many others?
23I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me. 24The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep. 25So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
26Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for. 27With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together, 28but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman. 29I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_text:
Ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nwo adwenleadwenle
1 Dumamɔlɛ kpalɛ le kpalɛ tɛla nwole evuanlɛ mɔɔ sonle bolɛ la; yɛɛ ewule kenle le kpalɛ tɛla awolɛ kenle.
2Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛkɛhɔ awuke mɔɔ bɛlɛdi nyane nu la anu tɛla kɛ ɛkɛhɔ awuke mɔɔ bɛlɛto ɛkponle wɔ nu la anu, ɔluakɛ menli kɔsɔɔti awieleɛ ɛne, na anyewɔzoamra bava azie bɛ ti anu.
3Nyanelilɛ le kpalɛ tɛla ɛzelekɛ, ɔluakɛ ɔmaa sonla nyunlu yɛ alɔbɔlɛ ɛdeɛ, noko ɔmaa wɔ ndelebɛbo yɛ kpole.
4Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ dwenle awuke mɔɔ nyanelilɛ wɔ nu la anwo. Koasea dwenle awuke mɔɔ fɛlɛkolilɛ wɔ nu la anwo.
5Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ sonla kɛmaa nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma kɛhwi ɔ nyunlu tɛla kɛ ɔkɛdie ahoasea edwɛndolɛ.
6Saa koasea sele a, ɔle kɛ mbowule ɛyɛne ɛlɛtite senle nu la. Ɛhye noko le debie mgbane.
7Nɔhalɛ, nzisi maa nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ yɛ koasea, yɛɛ ndoloboa ɛlielɛ sɛkye subane.
8Debie biala awieleɛ le kpalɛ tɛla ye mɔlebɛbo; yɛɛ abotanezilɛ le kpalɛ tɛla mgbanyizonleyɛlɛ.
9 Mmafa ɛya ndɛndɛ, ɔluakɛ koasea a fa ɛya sie ye nu a.
10Mmabiza kɛ, “Duzu ati a mekɛ mɔɔ ɛze ɛhɔ la le kpalɛ tɛla adwuleso mekɛ ye ɛ?” Ɔluakɛ nrɛlɛbɛ biala ɛnle nu kɛ ɛkɛbiza ɛhye.
11Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ sonla mɔɔ lɛ agyadeɛ la kɛnwu nrɛlɛbɛ; ɔle nvasoɛ ɔmaa menli mɔɔ de ngoane nu la. 12Ɔluakɛ nrɛlɛbɛ kola bɔ sonla nwo bane kɛ ezukoa la. Yɛɛ adwenlebukelɛ nwo nvasoɛ a le kɛ nrɛlɛbɛ bɔ mɔɔ lɛ ye la anwo bane.
13Dwenle mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛyɛ la anwo. Nwane a kɛhola mɔɔ yehyeɛhyea ye la tenrɛdenrɛ a? 14Wɔ ɛkpazilɛ mekɛ nu, di fɛlɛko, yɛɛ saa ehyia to wɔ a, dwenle na kakye kɛ Nyamenle a maa gyinlabelɛ nwiɔ ne ba a, amaa sonla annwu debie biala mɔɔ bazi ɔ nzi la.
15Wɔ me ɛbɛla mekɛ mgbane ɛhye anu, menwu debie biala; sonla tenlene wu ye tenleneyɛlɛ nu, yɛɛ amumuyɛnli ngoane wa wɔ ye munzule ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu. 16Yemɔti mmayɛ kpalɛ somasoma, yɛɛ mmanwu nrɛlɛbɛ somasoma; duzu ati a ɛkɛzɛkye ɛ nwo a? 17Mmayɛ amumuyɛ somasoma, yɛɛ mmayɛ koasea. Duzu ati a ɛkɛhu ɛ nwo na wɔ ewule mekɛ adwu a? 18Saa ɛsɔ debie ɛhye anu a, mmagyakyi ko ne anu, ɔluakɛ sonla mɔɔ sulo Nyamenle la bavi ɔ muala anu.
19Nrɛlɛbɛ maa nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ anwosesebɛ tɛla menli bulu mɔɔ sie suakpole ko la.
20Nɔhalɛ, tenlenenli biala ɛnle azɛlɛ ye azo mɔɔ kpalɛ ngome ala a ɔyɛ na ɔnyɛ ɛtane ɛlɛ a.
21Mmafa wɔ adwenle ɛkɔ edwɛkɛ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ menli ka la azo anrɛɛ ɛkɛde kɛ wɔ sonvolɛ ɛlɛbɔ wɔ sasa; 22ɛze ye wienyi kɛ mekɛ dɔɔnwo ne ala ɛdawɔ wɔbɔ menli sasa.
23Meva nrɛlɛbɛ mezɔ ɛhye mɔ amuala menlea. Menganle kɛ, “Menyɛle kɛ meyɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ, noko meannwu nrɛlɛbɛ.” 24Mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ la, wɔ moa, yɛɛ mɔɔ le kuma la, le kuma kuloonwu; nwane a kɛhola kɛde ɔ bo a? 25Menyɛle me adwenle kɛ menea, meavedevede nu na meakpondɛ nrɛlɛbɛ yɛɛ ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti abo, na meanwu atisesebɛ mɔɔ le ngoaseadeyɛlɛ nee koaseayɛlɛ mɔɔ le ɛzɛlɛde la.
26Menwunle debie mɔɔ yɛ ɛzulolɛ tɛla ewule la; yemɔ a le raalɛ mɔɔ ye ɛhulolɛ le kɛ ɛhane anzɛɛ avonle, na ɔ sa mɔɔ ɔfa ɔbɛla ye kulovolɛ la le kɛ nwɔnzɔnwɔnzɔ la. Sonla mɔɔ sɔ Nyamenle anye la kola die ɔ nwo; na ɛtanevolɛ ɛdeɛ ɔkye ye. 27Bɛdie, kɛ Nolobɔvo ne se la ɛne, menwunle ɛhye ngyikyi ngyikyi wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee melɛkpondɛ bɛ nyelebɛnloa la. 28Mekpondɛkpondɛ nyelebɛnloa fofolɛ, noko metɛnyianle bie. Menwunle nrenya ko wɔ mrenya apenle avinli mɔɔ medi ye eni a, na wɔ mraalɛ ne mɔ avinli, meannyia bie. 29Debie mɔɔ mezukoa la ala ɛne: Nyamenle bɔle sonla fɔɔnwo, na sonla ɛbɔ adwenle dɔɔnwo ɛmaa ɛbɛla ɛyɛ kpomgbondee.

english_text:
1Who is smart enough
to explain everything?
Wisdom makes you cheerful
and gives you a smile.
Obey the King
2If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise. 3Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind. 4The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?” 5If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it. 6Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything, 7though no one can tell the future. 8We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil. 9I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another?
Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
10I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense. 11When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime. 12They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying:
Everyone who lives right
and respects God
will prosper,
13but no one who sins
and rejects God
will prosper or live very long.
14There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens. 15So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
16Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world. 17I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_text:
1Nwane a le kɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ ne a, yɛɛ nwane a ze ninyɛne bo kile a? Sonla nrɛlɛbɛ maa ɔ nyunlu yɛ gyakogyako na ɔ nyunlu ɛmunlanlɛ kakyi ɛzelekɛ.
Yɛ tieyɛ maa belemgbunli
2Di edwɛkɛ mɔɔ belemgbunli kɛha la azo, na mmamaa wɔ adwenle sɛkye kɛ wɔbɔ Nyamenle ɛwɔkɛ a. 3Belemgbunli ne kola yɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɔdaye ɔkulo la, yemɔti saa edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛba la ɛnle kpalɛ a fi ɔ nyunlu ɛkɛ ne kɔ. 4Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ belemgbunli kɛha la le tumi, yɛɛ nwane bɔbɔ a kɛhola kɛze ye kɛ, “Na duzu a ɛlɛyɛ la?” 5Awie biala mɔɔ di mɛla zo la anwo ɛnrɛbu ɛbonle, yɛɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ ze mekɛ ne nee adenle mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ ɔdua nu ɔyɛ la. 6Ɔluakɛ debie biala lɛ ye mekɛ nee ye adenle noko akee sonla ɔdaye ye munzule doa ye kpalɛ kpalɛ. 7Awie biala ɛnze edwɛkɛ mɔɔ bazi la, ɔluakɛ awie biala ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔbaha kɛ ɔbazi yeazi la yeahile ye a. 8Awie biala ɛnlɛ tumi mɔɔ ɔkola ɔmaa ye sunsum ne tɛnla ye nu dahuu, anzɛɛ awie biala ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ lɛ tumi wɔ ye ewule mekɛ zo; ɔle konle mɔɔ bɛkɔ a bɛnzia a, yɛɛ amumuyɛ ɛyɛlɛ ɛnlie bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛyɛ amumuyɛ la ɛnvi nu.
Amumuyɛma nee tenlenema
9Menwunle ɛhye mɔ amuala wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee melɛdwenle ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛyɛ wɔ aleɛabo, mekɛ mɔɔ bie mɔ lɛ tumi ɛlɛsisi bie mɔ bɛamaa bɛanwu amaneɛ la anwo la. 10Akee menwunle kɛ bɛzie amumuyɛma; ɛnee bɛdi ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne anu wolofinde, na menli kanvo bɛ wɔ suakpole ne azo, ɛleka mɔɔ bɛyɛle bɛ ninyɛndane ne mɔ la. Ɛhye noko le debie mgbane.
11Kɛmɔ bɛndua amumuyɛyɛlɛ nwo kakɛ ndɛndɛ la ati, menli fa sie bɛ nyunlu yɛ amumuyɛ dahuu. 12Ɛtanevolɛ yɛ ninyɛmunli fane ɛya na ye ngoane yɛ tendenle, noko meze kɛ ɔbayɛ boɛ yeamaa menli mɔɔ sulo Nyamenle la, ɔboalekɛ ɔ nyunlu, bɛsulo ye; 13na amumuyɛma ɛdeɛ, ɔnrɛyɛ boɛ ɔnrɛmaa bɛ, yɛɛ bɛ ngoane ɛnrɛwa kɛ ɛlawolɛ, ɔboalekɛ bɛnzulo Nyamenle. 14Debie mgbane bie kɔ zolɛ wɔ ewiade ye anu, tenlenema nyia amumuyɛma ndeanlɛ, yɛɛ amumuyɛma nyia tenlenema ahatualɛ. Na menganle kɛ ɛhye noko le debie mgbane.
15Yemɔti menwu ye wienyi kɛ ɔwɔ kɛ sonla dielie ɔ nye, ɔboalekɛ ye fɛlɛkolilɛ mɔɔ ɔlɛ ye wɔ ye ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu la a le kɛ ɔkɛli, ɔkɛnlo na ɔkɛlielie ɔ nye. Yeanyɛ boɛ bɔbɔ a, mekɛ mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛva ɛmaa ye wɔ ewiade, mɔɔ ɔlɛyɛ gyima la, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔdielie ɔ nye.
16Mekɛ biala mɔɔ mendwenlenle nwolɛ kɛ mesukoa nrɛlɛbɛ, na meanwu mɔɔ ɛlɛsisi ewiade, mɔɔ yemɔti sonla si epe nɔɔzo nee ewiazo la, 17menwunle kɛ sonla ɛnrɛde Nyamenle gyima mɔɔ ɛlɛdi wɔ ewiade la abo. Sonla babɔ mɔdenle kɛ duzu bɔbɔ ala a, ɔnrɛde ɔ bo ɛlɛ. Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma baha kɛ bɛze, noko bɛnze.

english_text:
One Day at a Time
1I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad. 2But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
3It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die. 4As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion. 5We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten. 6Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
7So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do. 8Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best. 9Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth. 10Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
11Here is something else I have learned:
The fastest runners
and the greatest heroes
don't always win races
and battles.
Wisdom, intelligence, and skill
don't always make you healthy,
rich, or popular.
We each have our own share
of misfortune.
12None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap.
Better To Be Wise than Foolish
13Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me. 14It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls. 15But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten. 16So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
17Words of wisdom spoken softly
make much more sense
than the shouts of a ruler
to a crowd of fools.
18Wisdom is more powerful
than weapons,
yet one mistake can destroy
all the good you have done.
translation_text:
1Mendwenlenle ɛhye anwo na meneɛnleanle ɔ muala anu kɛ menea kɛ Nyamenle si nea nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma nee tenlenema nee bɛ nyɛleɛ zo la, saa ɛhulolɛ o, saa ɛkpɔlɛ o, awie biala ɛnze. Debie biala mɔɔ gyi bɛ nye zo la le mgbane, 2ɔboalekɛ bɛ muala bɛ awieleɛ le ko: tenlenema nee amumuyɛma, kpalɛma nee ɛtanevolɛma, bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛ nwo te nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛ nwo ɛnde, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛbɔ azu nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛmbɔ azu la, bɛ muala bɛbawu. Sonla mɔɔ le kpalɛ la ɛndɛla ɛtanevolɛ; sonla mɔɔ ka ndane la ɛndɛla sonla mɔɔ ɛnga ndane la. 3Awieleɛ ko ne ala a wɔ ɛkɛ maa bɛ muala a, na ɛhye noko le munzule mɔɔ ka debie biala mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la. Sumunli kenle ala mɔɔ sonla de ngoane nu la, ɛtane nee ɛzɛlɛsɛm ɛyi bɛ adwenle tɛkɛɛ. Bɛyɛ ɛhye mɔ na bɛwu. 4Noko akee awie biala mɔɔ de ngoane nu la lɛ anyelazo, ɔluakɛ twea anyewɔzo tɛla awenade funli. 5Ɔluakɛ anyewɔzoamra ze kɛ bɛbawu, na mɔwuamra ɛnze ɛhwee, yɛɛ bɛnlɛ ahatualɛ bieko; awie ɛngakye bɛ bieko. 6Bɛ ɛhulolɛ, bɛ ɛkpɔlɛ, nee bɛ anyebolo muala ɛwie, yɛɛ bɛ afoa nu ɛdeɛ ɛnle debie biala mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la anu bieko.
7Kɔ zolɛ, di wɔ aleɛ anyelielɛ nu, na fa anyelielɛ no wɔ nza, ɔluakɛ Nyamenle ɛlie debie biala mɔɔ ɛyɛ la ɛdo nu. 8Dahuu maa wɔ adɛladeɛ anye ɛyɛ bɔkɔbɔkɔ; yɛɛ mmamaa nwole kpa ɛ ti zo ɛlɛ. 9Mekɛ tendenle biala mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛva ɛmaa wɔ, mɔɔ ɛdi ye wɔ ewiade ɛbɛlabɔlɛ mgbane ye anu la, fa ɛ ye ne mɔɔ ɛkulo ye la dielie ɛ nye, ɔboalekɛ ɛvɛlɛ totohyia ye mɔɔ ɛlɛfɛ aleɛabo la, wɔ afoa nu ɛdeɛ ne ala ɛne. 10Debie biala mɔɔ ɛkɛzɔ nu kɛ ɛyɛ la, fa wɔ anwosesebɛ yɛ, ɔluakɛ gyima anzɛɛ ndwenlenwo anzɛɛ adwenle anzɛɛ nrɛlɛbɛ biala ɛnle Ɛbolɔ mɔɔ ɛlɛkɔ la.
11Eza menwunle kɛ aleɛabo, tɛ menli mɔɔ anwo yɛ ndɛ la a dahuu di konim wɔ ɛnriandilɛ nu a, yɛɛ tɛ anwosesebɛma angome a dahuu di konim wɔ konle nu a. Tɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma angome a dahuu asa kɔ bɛ nloa a, tɛ sonla mɔɔ lɛ adwenle la angome a nyia ɔ nwo a, yɛɛ tɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛze debie yɛ kpalɛ la angome a nyia gyinlabelɛ kpole a. Tɛ mekɛ ne amuala a bɛdi ye moavolɛ a. 12Sonla ɛnze ye mekɛ; kɛmɔ avonle kola yɛ munzule kye fɛlɛ, yɛɛ ɛhane kola kye anloma la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɛhane kola kye dasanli wɔ munzule mekɛ mɔɔ ɔ nye ɛnla la a.
Nrɛlɛbɛ nee Koaseayɛlɛ nwo adwenleadwenle
13Eza menwu nrɛlɛbɛ nwo ndonwo ɛhye wɔ aleɛabo, na ɔyɛ me azibɛnwo kpole. 14Suakpole ekyi bie wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ menli ekyi bie a wɔ zolɛ a. Belemgbunli kpole bie ratetale ye, ɔvale ye ɛlɔnema ɔbɛnrale ɔyiale ye na ɔboɔboale ɔ nwo kɛ ɔbubu nwolɛ bane ne yeagua. 15Na nrenya ehyianli nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ bie mɔɔ wɔ suakpole ne azo la vale ye nrɛlɛbɛ ne pepɛle liele suakpole ne. Noko awie biala angakye mɔɔ ehyianli ne yɛle la. 16Bɛanwu nrenya ehyianli ne nrɛlɛbɛ ne, yɛɛ bɛandie ye edwɛkɛ, noko mese, nrɛlɛbɛ le kpalɛ tɛla anwosesebɛ. 17Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔkɛha ye bɛtɛɛ la le kpalɛ tɛla belemgbunli ɛdeɛdeanlɛ wɔ ahoasea avinli. 18Nrɛlɛbɛ le kpalɛ tɛla konle adu, na ɛtanenli kokye sɛkye ninyɛne kpalɛ dɔɔnwo.

english_text:
1A few dead flies in perfume
make all of it stink,
and a little foolishness
outweighs a lot of wisdom.
2Sensible thoughts lead you
to do right;
foolish thoughts lead you
to do wrong.
3Fools show their stupidity
by the way they live;
it's easy to see
they have no sense.
4Don't give up your job
when your boss gets angry.
If you stay calm,
you'll be forgiven.
5Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair: 6They honor fools, but dishonor the rich; 7they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
8 If you dig a pit,
you might fall in;
if you break down a wall,
a snake might bite you.
9You could even get hurt
by chiseling a stone
or chopping a log.
10If you don't sharpen your ax,
it will be harder to use;
if you are wise,
you'll know what to do.
11The power to charm a snake
does you no good
if it bites you anyway.
12If you talk sensibly,
you will have friends;
if you talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
13Fools begin with nonsense,
and their stupid chatter
ends with disaster.
14They never tire of talking,
but none of us really know
what the future will bring.
15Fools wear themselves out—
they don't know enough
to find their way home.
16A country is in for trouble
when its ruler is childish,
and its leaders
party all day long.
17But a nation will prosper
when its ruler is mature,
and its leaders
don't party too much.
18Some people are too lazy
to fix a leaky roof—
then the house collapses.
19Eating and drinking
make you feel happy,
and money can buy
everything you need.
20Don't let yourself think about
cursing the king;
don't curse the rich,
not even in secret.
A little bird might hear
and tell everything.
translation_text:
1Nrɛzenra avunli maa mɔɔ yɛ sakyeɛ la nwole evuanlɛ bɔ nvoanle, yɛɛ koaseayɛlɛ ekyi sɛkye nrɛlɛbɛ kpole nee enililɛ.
2Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ adwenle tɔ fema zo, na koasea adwenle tɔ bɛne zo. 3Koasea lua adenle zo bɔbɔ a, ɔkile ɔ nwo kɛ ɔnlɛ adwenle, yɛɛ ye nyɛleɛ ka kile awie biala kɛ ɔle koasea.
4Saa wɔ belemgbunli fa ɛ nwo ɛya a, mmagyakyi gyima ɛkɛ ne ala; saa ɛsie ɛ nwo diinyi a, wɔannea a wɔ ɛtane mgbole mɔɔ wɔyɛ bɔbɔ la, bɛbava bɛahyɛ wɔ.
5Menwu munzule bie wɔ aleɛabo, kɛ ɔle nvonleɛ mɔɔ vi belemgbunli ɛkɛ a ba a. 6Bɛmaa menli mɔɔ ɛnze nrɛlɛbɛ la tumi gyinlabelɛ na bɛkpo sukuavolɛma. 7Menwu kɛ ahanra dede mgbɔnwɔ zo na menli mɔɔ le arelemgbunli la lua aze kɛ ahanra.
8 Sonla mɔɔ fu awie mɔ anwo kuma la bahoati adɔ nuhua; sonla mɔɔ bɔ bane nu finde la, ɛwɔlɛ ka ye. 9Sonla mɔɔ kpukekpuke awolɛ la, bolɛ boda ye, yɛɛ sonla mɔɔ kpakyekpakye mbaka la, bie boda ye. 10Saa akuma tili na wɔanzi a, ɛfa ɛ nwonane ɛyɛ gyima; na nrɛlɛbɛ boa sonla maa ɔko ɔtɔ zolɛ 11Saa sonla mɔɔ ze ɛwɔlɛ sili kye la maa ɛwɔlɛ dumua ka ye kolaa na yeahye ɛwɔlɛ ne sili a, ɛnee nvasoɛ biala ɛnle silikyevolɛ ne anwo zo. 12Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ nloa edwɛkɛ maa menli di ye eni, na koasea ka edwɛkɛ a ɔsɛkye ɔdaye mumua ne ɔ nwo. 13Ɔfa ngoaseasɛm ɔbɔ ye edwɛkɛ bo na yeava amumuyɛ ɛzɛlɛsɛm yeadwula ye. 14Koasea tendɛ a ɔ nloa ɛmpe.
Awie ɛnze mɔɔ bazi a, yɛɛ awie ɛngola ɛnga mɔɔ bazi ye ewule nzi la ɛngile ye.
15Koasea ɛvɛlɛ gyegye ye adwenle, yemɔti ɔngola ɔnnwu suakpole ne adenle.
16Maanle mɔɔ ye belemgbunli ne le kakula, na ye mgbanyima to ɛkponle nɔɔzo toonwo alehyenlɛ la, ye gyakɔ! 17Na maanle mɔɔ lɛ belemgbunli mɔɔ bɛtete ye na ɔdaye ɔkola ɔfa adwenle, na ye mgbanyima to ɛkponle wɔ mekɛ kpalɛ nu nyia anwosesebɛ, na bɛnno bɛmbo la anwo le moavolɛ.
18Saa sonla yɛ mgbovonle toonwo ye sua tete a, sua ne nwu, na ɔfolo ɔgua nu.
19Aleɛ maa sonla sele, nza maa sonla nye die, na ezukoa pɛ debie biala azo.
20Mmaka ɛ ne aze ɛbɔ belemgbunli ne anwo tokule, yɛɛ mmafea wɔ suakunlu bɔbɔ ɛbɔ sukoavolɛ anwo tokule. Anloma anzɛɛ kɛkɛba biala mɔɔ lɛ ndɛbalɛ la bahola ahɔha mɔɔ wɔha la ahile bɛ.

english_text:
It Pays To Work Hard
1Be generous, and someday
you will be rewarded.
2Share what you have
with seven or eight others,
because you never know
when disaster may strike.
3Rain clouds always bring rain;
trees always stay
wherever they fall.
4If you worry about the weather
and don't plant seeds,
you won't harvest a crop.
5No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
6Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce.
Youth and Old Age
7Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun. 8Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
9Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
10Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_text:
Mɔɔ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ yɛ la
1Fuandi wɔ kpanwo ne to azule ne anye, na kenle bie ɛ sa baha ye. 2Bubu bie maa menli nsuu anzɛɛ mɔtwɛ bɔbɔ, ɔluakɛ ɛnze munzule mɔɔ kenle bie bazi azɛlɛ ye azo a.
3Saa ezule munla a, ɔtɔ ɔgua azɛlɛ ye azo, yɛɛ baka tudu tɔ nyiakɛ anzɛɛ sɔlɔ a, ɛleka mɔɔ ɔkɛdɔ la, ɛkɛ ne ala a ɔbala a. 4Sonla mɔɔ dahuu nea anwoma ne la ɛnrɛlua debie biala, yɛɛ mɔɔ nea kɛ anwomanyunlu si de la, ɛnrɛbu ye bɛyɔba. 5Kɛmɔ sonla ɛnze anwoma adenle na ɔnze kɛ ɔyɛ mɔɔ mogya kakyi sonla wɔ nrenzɛvolɛ kunlu la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ sonla ɛnze Nyamenle mɔɔ yɛ debie biala la gyima a. 6Dua wɔ ma ne nwonlomɔ, na eza dua bie nɔsolɛ nu. Ɔluakɛ ɛnze mɔɔ kɛyɛ kpalɛ a, saa bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛkɛyɛ kpalɛ anzɛɛ ko kɛyɛ kpalɛ kɛdɛla ko a, ɛnze.
7Wienyi le kɛnlɛma, yɛɛ ɔyɛ anyelielɛ kɛ sonla kɛnwu sɛnzɛne ne. 8Saa sonla tɛnla ngoane nu ali ɛvolɛ dɔɔnwo a, bɛmaa ɔlie ɔ nye wɔ ɔ muala anu; noko bɛmaa ɔhakye kɛ munzule kenle ne mɔ bazo. Mɔɔ ba la amuala le debie mgbane.
Mgbavolɛ nee mbɛlɛra folɛdulɛ
9Mgbavolɛ nee mbɛlɛra, bɛlie bɛ nye wɔ bɛ ngakula nu. Bɛli fɛlɛko wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛde mgbavolɛ nee mbɛlɛra la. Bɛli bɛ atiakunluwɔzo nzi, na bɛyɛ mɔɔ bɛkulo la. Noko bɛhakye kɛ Nyamenle babua bɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛkɛyɛ la anwo ndɛne.
10Bɛye ɛyavalɛ bɛvi bɛ adwenle nu na bɛye anwofofolɛ biala bɛvi bɛ nwonane nu, ɔluakɛ mgbavosɛm nee mbɛlɛrasɛm nee ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu fɛlɛkolilɛ le debie mgbane.

english_text:
1Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
2Someday the light of the sun
and the moon and the stars
will all seem dim to you.
Rain clouds will remain
over your head.
3Your body will grow feeble,
your teeth will decay,
and your eyesight fail.
4The noisy grinding of grain
and the voices of singers
will be shut out
by your deaf ears,
but even the song of a bird
will keep you awake.
5You will be afraid
to climb up a hill
or walk down a road.
Your hair will turn as white
as almond blossoms.
You will feel lifeless
and drag along
like an old grasshopper.
We each go to our eternal home,
and the streets here are filled
with those who mourn.
6The silver cord snaps,
the golden bowl breaks;
the water pitcher is smashed,
and the pulley at the well
is shattered.
7So our bodies return
to the earth,
and the life-giving breath
returns to God.
8Nothing makes sense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense.
Respect and Obey God
9I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied. 10Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
11Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together. 12My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these.
There is no end to books,
and too much study
will wear you out.
13Everything you were taught can be put into a few words:
Respect and obey God!
This is what life
is all about.
14God will judge
everything we do,
even what is done in secret,
whether good or bad.
translation_text:
1Eza mekɛ mɔɔ bɛle mgbavolɛ nee mbɛlɛra la, bɛhakye bɛ Bɔvolɛ ne kolaa na munzule mekɛ ne mɔɔ ɛnee bɛbikye mgbanyifoa la adwu, na bɛaha kɛ, “Me nye ɛnlie ɛbɛla nu.” 2Bɛhakye ye kolaa na sɛnzɛne ne, anzɛɛ wienyi ne, siane ne, yɛɛ nwɔlɔra ne mɔ ayɛ bɛ nye zo monzomonzo, mɔɔ ezule pe bɔbɔ a amungu ne mɔ ɛmpɛ nuhua ɛnze ɛlɛ la. 3Mekɛ zɔhane, ɛsalɛ ne mɔɔ sɔ awuke ne la bawozowozo, mrenya mɔɔ anwo yɛ se la bakpo. Egyele mɔɔ bɛfa bɛkposa aleɛ la badudu aha ekyi bie, yɛɛ bɛ nye bayɛ monzomonzo. 4Bɛ nzo badi mɔɔ bɛnrɛde gua ne azo alɛra biala a. Saa bɛlɛti ma bɔbɔ a bɛnrɛde melahyinli ne ane, noko anloma ɛzunlɛ badunwue bɛ avi nafelɛ nu, na menli mɔɔ kulo edwɛne la ɛnrɛde edwɛndolɛ bieko. 5Eza bɛbazulo ɛleka mɔɔ wɔ anwuma la, yɛɛ ɛzulolɛ bara bɛ adenle nu, bɛ ti enrinli bayɛ egyɛne; ɛdialɛ bɔbɔ bayɛ se amaa bɛ na bɛ atiakunluwɔzo aye, ɔboalekɛ sonla ɛlɛkɔ ye ɛkɛla nzi, na nyanelilɛma bazu akpɔsa gua bile ne mɔ azo.
6Bɛhakye Bɔvolɛ ne kolaa na bɛ dwɛtɛ fufule ndweabane ne ade, anzɛɛ bɛ ezukoa nvutuke bonkuma ne abɔ; anzɛɛ bɛ dwora abɔ nzufeanvea bula ne azo anzɛɛ nyɛma ne mɔɔ bɛfa bɛto bula ne la ade. 7Munlutu bazia ahɔ ndɛtɛlɛ nu kɛ ye dɛba ne ala la, na sunsum ne azia ahɔ Nyamenle mɔɔ vale manle la ɛkɛ.
8Nolobɔvo ne se, mgbane nu mgbane ɔ. Ɔ muala le mgbane.
Edwɛkɛ ne sikalɛ
9Ɛye kɛ Nolobɔvo ne si ze nrɛlɛbɛ la ɛsie ahane a, eza ɔhilehilele menli ne adwenle nu ɛbukelɛ, debie ɛzuzulɛ nee debie ɛzukoalɛ na ɔdɔle alagye kpalɛ ɔzieziele mrɛlɛ mɔɔ ɔbule la. 10Nolobɔvo ne bɔle mɔdenle kɛ ɔkpondɛ edwɛkɛ agbɔkɛ mɔɔ yɛ fɛ la na edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ ɔhɛlɛle la le nɔhalɛ. 11Nrɛlɛbɛvoma edwɛkɛ le kɛ mboaneneavolɛma agbɔma ati ndwondwɔɔnwo ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛka mboane la, yɛɛ mrɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛboɔboa bɛ nloa la kyɛ kɛ agbɛlɛko mɔɔ bɛva bɛbobɔ debie nu la. Nyamenle ne mɔɔ le kɛ mboaneneavolɛ mɔɔ nea yɛ kɔsɔɔti yɛ nwo zo la a ɛva ɛmaa yɛ a.
12Me ra nrenya, nea boɛ wɔ debie bieko mɔɔ li ɛhye mɔ anzi la anwo. Mbuluku ɛhɛlɛlɛ ɛnlɛ ye awieleɛ, yɛɛ ɛzukoalɛ dɔɔnwo maa ɛvɛlɛ.
13Bɛmaa yɛdie edwɛkɛ ne adwulaleɛ: Bɛzulo Nyamenle, na bɛli ye mɛla ne mɔ azo, ɔboalekɛ sonla gyima mɔɔ la ɔ nwo zo la ala ɛne. 14Ɔluakɛ Nyamenle babua debie biala mɔɔ yɛyɛ, nee awozinli nu nyɛleɛ biala anwo ndɛne, kpalɛ o, ɛtane o.

english_text:
Love Is Better than Wine
1 This is Solomon's
most beautiful song.
She Speaks:
2Kiss me tenderly!
Your love is better than wine,
3and you smell so sweet.
All the young women adore you;
the very mention of your name
is like spreading perfume.
* 4Hurry, my king! Let's hurry.
Take me to your home.
The Young Women Speak:
We are happy for you!
And we praise your love
even more than wine.
She Speaks:
Young women of Jerusalem,
it is only right
that you should adore him.
5My skin is dark and beautiful,
like a tent in the desert
or like Solomon's curtains.
6Don't stare at me
just because the sun
has darkened my skin.
My brothers were angry with me;
they made me work in the vineyard,
and so I neglected
my complexion.
7My darling, I love you!
Where do you feed your sheep
and let them rest at noon?
Don't let the other shepherds
think badly of me.
I'm not one of those women
who shamelessly follow
after shepherds.
He Speaks:
8My dearest, if you don't know,
just follow the path
of the sheep.
Then feed your young goats
near the shepherds' tents.
9You move as gracefully
as the pony that leads
the chariot of the king.
10Earrings add to your beauty,
and you wear a necklace
of precious stones.
11Let's make you some jewelry
of gold, woven with silver.
She Speaks:
12My king, while you
were on your couch,
my aroma was a magic charm.
13My darling, you are perfume
between my breasts;
14you are flower blossoms
from the gardens of En-Gedi.
He Speaks:
15My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
your eyes are those of a dove.
She Speaks:
16My love, you are handsome,
truly handsome—
the fresh green grass
will be our wedding bed
17in the shade of cedar
and cypress trees.
translation_text:
1 Edwɛne nu edwɛne mɔɔ yɛ fɛ kpalɛ kpalɛ mɔɔ bɛdole bɛmanle Sɔlɔmɔn.
Edwɛne mɔɔ lumua
Raalɛ ne
2O, anrɛɛ wɔavo me nloa anwo!
Ɔluakɛ wɔ ɛhulolɛ ne le kpalɛ tɛla nwanye.
3Wɔ nwole ne mɔɔ ɛkpokpa la bɔ evuanlɛ,
Wɔ duma le kɛ nwole mɔɔ bɛlɛwola,
yemɔti mbɛlɛra ne mɔ kulo wɔ.
4Fa me bɔ ɛ nwo na maa yɛnriandi yɛhɔ.
Belemgbunli ne ɛva me ɛra ye sua kunlu.
Yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛ nye balie,
yɛbahanvo wɔ ɛhulolɛ fɛlɛko ne yɛadɛla nwanye.
Ɔnyɛ ɛzulolɛ kɛ mraalɛ kɔsɔɔti kulo wɔ a.
5Gyɛlusalɛm mraalɛ,
mele bile duhuduhu, na me nwo yɛ fɛ,
mele duhuduhu kɛ Kidaa ndanlɛ azua,
me kɛnlɛma le kɛ Sɔlɔmɔn suakunlu mgbɛnu ndanlɛ.
6Mmafa ɛ nye foa ko ɛnea me kɛ medu a,
ɔboalekɛ sɛnzɛne ne a ɛmaa melu a.
Me mediema mrenya ne mɔ vale me nwo ɛya,
bɛmanle menyɛle gyima wɔ bɛ vanye egyinli ne mɔ anu;
mengyakyile medame me vanye egyinli ɛdeɛ ne.
7Me kulovolɛ, ka kile me,
nienwu a ɛbava wɔ nyɛmoa wɔahɔ adidi a?
Ɔdwu sɛnzɛnegyinla a nienwu a bɛbalie bɛ ɛnwomenle a?
Duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ mekpɔsa mekpondɛ wɔ
wɔ ɛ gɔnwo mɔ nyɛmoa avinli a?
Nrenya ne
8Wɔmɔ mɔɔ ɛ nwo yɛ fɛ tɛla mraalɛ kɔsɔɔti,
ɛnze ɛleka ne ɔ?
Dua nyɛmoa ne mɔ agyakɛ abo zo ne,
na maa wɔ mbɔnkye ne mɔ ɛdidi
mboaneneavolɛma ndanlɛ azua ne mɔ anwo.
9Me kulovolɛ, mefa wɔ meto Yigyibiti belemgbunli
ɛkpɔnwɔ belɛ mɔɔ twe ye ehwili ne mɔ la anwo.
10Ɛ nzo tɛba nu nee anwoneɛ le kɛnlɛma,
ɛ kɔme nee ndweabane kɛnlɛma bɛnga.
11Yɛbayɛ ezukoa nvutuke anwoneɛ yɛamaa wɔ,
yɛava dwɛtɛ fufule yɛaduodua nu.
Raalɛ ne
12Mekɛ mɔɔ belemgbunli ne la ye ebia ne anu la,
me nwo anatele ne evuanlɛ yile sua ne tɛkɛɛ.
13Me kulovolɛ ne le kɛ alufuanlɛ kodoku
mɔɔ la me kanra anu la.
14Me kulovolɛ ne le kɛ “hɛna” ndotolo siakɛ
mɔɔ kpakye Ɛngidae vanye egyinli ne mɔ anu la.
Nrenya ne
15Nea, ɛ nwo yɛ fɛ, me kulovolɛ;
nea, ɛ nwo yɛ fɛ;
ɛ nye ma le kɛ abubule nye.
Raalɛ ne
16Nea, ɛ nwo yɛ fɛ kpole, me kulovolɛ;
nɔhalɛ nu, ɛmaa me nye die kpole!
Yɛ ɛkpa mɔɔ yɛda zo la le asuomenle.
17Yɛ sua ne aakɔ ne mɔ le sida mbaka,
yɛɛ sepelɛse mbaka a yɛva yɛzɛ ɔ nye a.

english_text:
Love Makes Everything Beautiful
She Speaks:
1I am merely a rose
from the land of Sharon,
a lily from the valley.
He Speaks:
2My darling, when compared
with other young women,
you are a lily among thorns.
She Speaks:
3And you, my love,
are an apple tree
among trees of the forest.
Your shade brought me pleasure;
your fruit was sweet.
4You led me to your banquet room
and showered me with love.
5Refresh and strengthen me
with raisins and apples.
I am hungry for love!
6Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
7Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Winter Is Past
She Speaks:
8I hear the voice
of the one I love,
as he comes leaping
over mountains and hills
9like a deer or a gazelle.
Now he stands outside our wall,
looking through the window
10and speaking to me.
He Speaks:
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
11Winter is past,
the rain has stopped;
12flowers cover the earth,
it's time to sing.
The cooing of doves
is heard in our land.
13Fig trees are bearing fruit,
while blossoms on grapevines
fill the air with perfume.
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
14You are my dove
hiding among the rocks
on the side of a cliff.
Let me see how lovely you are!
Let me hear the sound
of your melodious voice.
15Our vineyards are in blossom;
we must catch the little foxes
that destroy the vineyards.
She Speaks:
16My darling, I am yours,
and you are mine,
as you feed your sheep
among the lilies.
17Pretend to be a young deer
dancing on mountain slopes
until daylight comes
and shadows fade away.
translation_text:
1Mele kɛ Hyɛlɔn wulosu ndotolo,
mbɔnza nu aloa.
Nrenya ne
2Me kulovolɛ wɔ mbɛlɛra avinli a
ɔle kɛ aloa ndotolo wɔ mbowule nu la.
Raalɛ ne
3Saa me kulovolɛ gyi mgbavolɛ avinli a,
ɔle kɛ ampolo baka gyi ɛbɔ nu mbaka avinli.
Me nye die ye alubo ne anu ɛdɛnlanlɛ,
yɛɛ ye ma ne yɛ me fɛ.
4Ɔvale me ɔhɔle ye ɛkponledolɛ sua ne anu
na ɔvale ye ɛhulolɛ fɛlɛnra ne ɔguale me nwo zo.
5Maa me vanye ma welera maa ɔmaa me anwosesebɛ,
na maa me ampolo maa ɔmaa me anwosesebɛ fofolɛ,
ɔluakɛ ɛhulolɛ ngome ɛmaa me nwo ɛdo me.
6O anrɛɛ yeamaa me ti ala ɔ sa bɛne ne azo,
na yeava ɔ sa fema yeado me nwo zo.
7O Gyɛlusalɛm mraalɛ, mese,
bɛva weɛlɛ nee ahɛtɛboɛ anwondɛne ne mɔ
bɛha ndane kɛ bɛnrɛpele ɛhulolɛ nwo,
kɔkpula kɛ ɛhulolɛ ne mekɛ kpalɛ kɛdwu la.
Edwɛne mɔɔ tɔ zo nwiɔ
Raalɛ ne
8Mete me kulovolɛ ne ane!
Ɔvi awoka ne mɔ azo ɔlɛnriandi,
yeawuluwulu awoka mgbole nee ngyikyi zo yeara.
9Me kulovolɛ ne le kɛ kɛtɛboɛ,
ɔle kɛ weɛlɛ nyinli edonraa.
Yemɔ a gyi yɛ bane ne anzi la,
ɔlɛnea nvɛnzɛlɛ ne anu,
ɔ nye gyi nvɛnzɛlɛ ne anzi neanleɛ ne anu.
Nrenya ne
10Me kulovolɛ ne tendɛ se me kɛ:
“Dwazo, me kulovolɛ,
me kulovolɛ kɛnlɛmaleɛ, maa yɛhɔ.
11Ɔluakɛ ɛyɛlɛ mekɛ ne ɛze;
ezule ne ɛwie tɔ.
12Ndotolo ɛkpakye ɛbɔ biala abo.
Edwɛndolɛ mekɛ ɛdwu;
bɛte abubule ne mɔ ɛzunlɛ
wɔ avule ne mɔ anu.
13Feege mbaka ɛbɔ ɔ bo ɛlɛso,
vanye mbaka ɛbɔ ndotolo,
bɛmaa maanle nu ɛbɔ evuanlɛ.
Dwazo, me kulovolɛ,
me kulovokpa, maa yɛhɔ.
14Ɛle kɛ abubule mɔɔ vea
bodane mɔɔ ɛkpuke la avinli.
Maa menwu ɛ nyunlu kɛnlɛma ne,
na mende ɛ ne fɛlɛko ne,
ɔluakɛ ɛ ne yɛ fɛ,
yɛɛ ɛ nyunlu le kɛnlɛma.
15Bɛhye ɛzonlɛ ne mɔ bɛmaa yɛ,
ɛzonlɛ ngyikyi ne mɔ,
mɔɔ sɛkye vanye egyinli ne mɔ la,
ɔluakɛ yɛ vanye egyinli ne mɔ ɛbɔ ndotolo.”
Raalɛ ne

english_text:
Beautiful Dreams
She Speaks:
1While in bed at night,
I reached for the one I love
with heart and soul.
I looked for him,
but he wasn't there.
2So I searched through the town
for the one I love.
I looked on every street,
but he wasn't there.
3I even asked the guards
patrolling the town,
“Have you seen the one
I love so much?”
4Right after that, I found him.
I held him and would not let go
until I had taken him
to the home of my mother.
5Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles,
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
The Groom and the Wedding Party
Their Friends Speak:
6What do we see approaching
from the desert
like a cloud of smoke?
With it comes the sweet smell
of spices, including myrrh
and frankincense.
7It is King Solomon
carried on a throne,
surrounded by sixty
of Israel's best soldiers.
8Each of them wears a sword.
They are experts at fighting,
even in the dark.
9The throne is made of trees
from Lebanon.
10Its posts are silver,
the back is gold,
and the seat is covered
with purple cloth.
You women of Jerusalem
have taken great care
to furnish the inside.
11Now come and see the crown
given to Solomon by his mother
on his happy wedding day.
translation_text:
1Nɔɔzo mɔɔ mela me ɛkpa ne azo la,
menganle me kulovolɛ ne anwo ɛlalɛ.
