and be cared for
by little children.
7Cows and bears will share
the same pasture;
their young will rest
side by side.
Lions and oxen
will both eat straw.
8Little children will play
near snake holes.
They will stick their hands
into dens of poisonous snakes
and never be hurt.
9 Nothing harmful will take place
on the Lord's holy mountain.
Just as water fills the sea,
the land will be filled
with people who know
and honor the Lord.
God's People Will Come Back Home
10 The time is coming when one of David's descendants will be the signal for the people of all nations to come together. They will follow his advice, and his own nation will become famous.
11When that day comes, the Lord will again reach out his mighty arm and bring home his people who have survived in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Ethiopia, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the land along the coast. 12He will give a signal to the nations, and he will bring together the refugees from Judah and Israel, who have been scattered all over the earth. 13Israel will stop being jealous of Judah, and Judah will no longer be the enemy of Israel. 14Instead, they will get together and attack the Philistines in the west. Then they will defeat the Edomites, the Moabites, and the Ammonites in the east. They will rule those people and take from them whatever they want.
15 The Lord will dry up the arm of the Red Sea near Egypt, and he will send a scorching wind to divide the Euphrates River into seven streams that anyone can step across. 16Then for his people who survive, there will be a good road from Assyria, just as there was a good road for their ancestors when they left Egypt.
translation_text:
Anzonudwolɛ belemgbunli maanle ne
1 Gyɛsi dosinli ne (Belemgbunli Devidi), bakpuke ɛnyelɛ wɔ ye ndinli ne mɔ anu anyi ayɛ Baka Ɛhane.
2Ɛdɛnkɛma Sunsum ne bara ɔ nwo zo,
ɔbanwu nrɛlɛbɛ, yeanyia ndelebɛbo,
ɔbanyia anwosesebɛ, yeayɛ folɛtuvolɛ,
ɔbanyia adwenle na yeazulo Ɛdɛnkɛma.
3Ɔbava anyelielɛ yeayɛ tieyɛ yeamaa Ɛdɛnkɛma,
ɔnrɛbua ndɛne ɛnyelɛzo,
yɛɛ ɔnrɛhyea ɔ nzo ɔnrɛbua ndɛne.
4 Ɔbabua ehyianvolɛma ndɛne pɛlepɛle nu,
na yeabua awienvolɛma ndɛne pɛpɛ;
ɔbava ɔ nloa yeayɛ baka yeadea azɛlɛ ye azo ɛtanema,
yeava ɔ nloa edwɛkɛ yeahu amumuyɛma.
5 Ɔbava pɛlepɛlelilɛ yeayɛ akyeso yeahye ɔ nze zo,
na yeava nɔhalɛlilɛ yeayɛ tabule mɔɔ hye ye avinli.
6 Bedi nee boane ralɛ badɛnla,
yɛɛ boboduma nee abɔnkye ralɛ bala ɛleka ko.
Ɛnlankɛ ralɛ nee awenade babɔ nu adidi,
na kakula yɛɛ banlea bɛ nwo zo a.
7Ɛnlankɛ nee ezizile babɔ nu adidi,
bɛ mra babɔ nu ala ɛleka ko,
na awenade bali ndile kɛ ɛnlankɛ ralɛ la.
8Kakula mɔɔ la nyɛfonlɛ nloa la nee ɛwɔlɛ bali nwɔhoa,
yɛɛ kakula mɔɔ ɛdudu agyakɛ la bava ɔ sa awula bɔna bɔne nu.
9 Bɛnrɛboda anzɛɛ bɛnrɛhu awie
wɔ me boka nwuanzanwuanza ne azo,
ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma anwo adwenle bayi azɛlɛ ye tɛkɛɛ
kɛ nzule mɔɔ wɔ nyevile nu la.
Menli mɔɔ bɛhye bɛ bɛhɔ nlɔnu la bazia ara
10 Mekɛ ne anu Belemgbunli Devidi abo zo sonla ne bagyinla kɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ la yeamaa maanle maanle. Maanle maanle bakpondɛ ye, na ɛleka mɔɔ ɔde la bayɛ anyelielɛ. 11Mekɛ ne anu Awulae badenrɛ ɔ sa bieko yealie Yizilayɛma mɔɔ ɛha la yeavi Aselea, Yigyibiti, Patelɔso, Sudan, Yilam, Babelonia, Heemate, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ ɛnweanloa la asa anu. 12Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa maanle maanle ne mɔ sɛkɛlɛneɛ yeahile kɛ ɔlɛboɔboa Yizilayɛma mɔɔ bɛmbu bɛ bie, nee Dwudama mɔɔ ɛkponde la anloa yeavi azɛlɛ ye muleɛ nna ne mɔ azo yeara. 13Yifelaem anyebolo ne bavi ɛkɛ, bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛgyegye Dwuda la bɛbazɛkye bɛ; Yifelaem anye ɛnrɛbolo Dwuda, yɛɛ Dwuda ɛnrɛgyegye Yifelaem bieko. 14Bɛbabɔ nu bɛara Filisitiama anwo zo wɔ adɔleɛ, yɛɛ bɛbabɔ nu bɛarave menli mɔɔ wɔ aduduleɛ la ninyɛne. Bɛbaho bɛava Yidɔm nee Mowabe, yɛɛ Amɔnoma bayɛ tieyɛ amaa bɛ. 15 Ɛdɛnkɛma bazɛkye Suwɛze Ebolo ne bɔkɔɔ na yeanwɔha ɔ sa wɔ Azule Yufileti ne azo yeamaa anwoma wuluwulu arasesa ye. Ɔbahyɛ nu nsuu yeamaa menli alua azɛlɛ resee zo apɛ. 16Bɛbakpakye ademgbole bɛavi Aselea bɛahɔva Yizilayɛma mɔɔ ɛha la, kɛmɔ ɔyɛle ɔmanle bɛ nlenya mɔ Yizilayɛma wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔyele bɛ ɔvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la.

english_text:
A Song of Praise
1At that time you will say,
“I thank you, Lord!
You were angry with me,
but you stopped being angry
and gave me comfort.
2 I trust you to save me,
Lord God,
and I won't be afraid.
My power and my strength
come from you,
and you have saved me.”
3With great joy, you people
will get water
from the well of victory.
4At that time you will say,
“Our Lord, we are thankful,
and we worship only you.
We will tell the nations
how glorious you are
and what you have done.
5Because of your wonderful deeds
we will sing your praises
everywhere on earth.”
6Sing, people of Zion!
Celebrate the greatness
of the holy Lord of Israel.
God is here to help you.
translation_text:
Moyɛlɛ edwɛne
1Mekɛ ne anu ɛbaha kɛ,
“O Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebayɛ wɔ mo,
ɔluakɛ ɛvale me nwo ɛya bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ,
noko ɛgyakyile ɛmanle ɔhale,
na ɛkyekyele me rɛle.
2 Bɛnlea, Nyamenle le me ngoanedievolɛ;
menrɛzulo, mebava me rɛle meawula ye nu,
ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ne
le me anwosesebɛ nee me edwɛne,
na yeyɛ me ngoanedievolɛ.”
3Ɛbava fɛlɛkolilɛ wɔado nzule
wɔavi ngoanelielɛ bula ne mɔ anu.
4Mekɛ ne anu ɛbaha kɛ,
“Bɛyɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mo,
bɛbɔ ye duma bɛlie moalɛ;
bɛmaa ye nyɛleɛ ne mɔ ɛla ali wɔ maanle maanle avinli,
bɛbɔ ye kpoleyɛlɛ ne nolo bɛhile bɛ.
5Bɛdo ayɛlɛyelɛ edwɛne bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma,
ɔluakɛ yeyɛ ninyɛne mgbole;
bɛmaa awie biala ɛde ɛhye wɔ ewiade amuala anu.
6Bɛdeɛdea nu, bɛva anyelielɛ bɛdo edwɛne, O Zayɔnoma,
ɔluakɛ Yizilayɛ Nwuanzanwuanza Ko ne
mɔɔ de bɛ avinli la le kpole.”

english_text:
Babylon Will Be Punished
1 This is the message that I was given about Babylon:
2From high on a barren hill
give a signal, shout the orders,
and point the way
to enter the gates
of Babylon's proud rulers.
3The Lord has commanded
his very best warriors
and his proud heroes
to show how angry he is.
4Listen to the noisy crowds
on the mountains!
Kingdoms and nations
are joining forces.
The Lord All-Powerful
is bringing together
an army for battle.
5From a distant land
the Lord is coming
fierce and furious—
he brings his weapons
to destroy the whole earth.
6 Cry and weep!
The day is coming
when the mighty Lord
will bring destruction.
* 7All people will be terrified.
Hands will grow limp;
courage will melt away.
8Everyone will tremble with pain
like a woman giving birth;
they will stare at each other
with horror on their faces.
There Will Be No Mercy
9I, the Lord,
will show no mercy or pity
when that time comes.
In my anger I will destroy
the earth and every sinner
who lives on it.
10 Light will disappear
from the stars in the sky;
the dawning sun will turn dark,
and the moon
will lose its brightness.
11I will punish this evil world
and its people
because of their sins.
I will crush the horrible pride
of those who are cruel.
12Survivors will be harder to find
than the purest gold.
13I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am terribly angry—
I will make the sky tremble
and the earth shake loose.
14Everyone will run
to their homelands,
just as hunted deer run,
and sheep scatter
when they have no shepherd.
15Those men who are captured
will be killed by a sword.
16They will see their children
beaten against rocks,
their homes robbed,
and their wives abused.
17The Medes can't be bought off
with silver or gold,
and I'm sending them
to attack Babylonia.
18Their arrows will slaughter
the young men;
no pity will be shown
to babies and children.
The Lord Will Destroy Babylon
19 The city of Babylon
is glorious and powerful,
the pride of the nation.
But it will be like the cities
of Sodom and Gomorrah
after I, the Lord,
destroyed them.
20No one will live in Babylon.
Even nomads won't camp nearby,
and shepherds won't let
their sheep rest there.
21 Only desert creatures,
hoot owls, and ostriches
will live in its ruins,
and goats will leap about.
22Hyenas and wolves will howl
from Babylon's fortresses
and beautiful palaces.
Its time is almost up!
translation_text:
Nyamenle badea Babelɔn
1Nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Babelɔn anwo, mɔɔ Nyamenle luale Emɔzo ara Ayezaya anwo zo vale dole gua la ɛne:
2“Fa sɛkɛlɛneɛ sie boka bie mɔɔ ɛhwee ɛnle zo la azo, na tea nu ka kile bɛ; nwɔha ɛ sa kile bɛ kɛ bɛwolo titilema nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ anu. 3Medame mumua ne yɛɛ meze me menli mɔɔ medu bɛ memaa me nwo, me katakyiema ne kɛ bɛlua me ɛyavalɛ ne azo bɛli gyima a. Bɛle konimlilɛma mɔɔ mefa bɛ metu me nwo a.”
4Bɛdie, alɛra bie wɔ awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ kɛ menli apenle apenle ɛlɛteɛdea nu! Bɛdie, arelemgbunli nee maanle maanle ɛdu ɛfonyia na bɛlɛboɔboa bɛ nloa! Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛboɔboa ye ɛlɔnema anloa ahɔ konle. 5Bɛvi moa moa maanle bie anu wɔ ewiade abo lɔ a bɛlɛba a. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ye ɛya konle ninyɛne ne mɔ ɛlɛba arazɛkye ewiade ye amuala.
6 Bɛzu bɛye awolɛ, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma kenle ne ɛbikye; ɔle kenle mɔɔ Tumivolɛ ne bava azɛkye ninyɛne a. 7Ɛsalɛ biala anu bado, awie biala ahonle badu, 8na bɛ rɛle abɔ. Bɛ nwo bafofo bɛ, bɛ mbowule nu babubu bɛ na bɛade nyane kɛ raalɛ mɔɔ ɛvo awolɛ zo la. Bɛbava ɛzulolɛ bɛanleɛnlea bɛ nyunlu ngoko ngoko; bɛ nyunlu baza. 9Bɛnlea, Ɛdɛnkɛma kenle ne ɛlɛba; ɔle ɛya kenle anu ɛzulolɛ kpole kpalɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bava ahakyi azɛlɛ ye ɛsɛlɛ, na yeazɛkye ɛtanema amuala yeavi zolɛ a. 10 Anwomanyunlu nwɔlɔra nee bɛ sɔsɔkɛ ne amuala, biala ɛnrɛda; sɛnzɛne ne balu wɔ ye ɛdudulɛ nu, yɛɛ siane ne ɛnrɛda.
11Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebadea ewiade amra amuala wɔ bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ ati, yɛɛ mebadea amumuyɛma wɔ bɛ ninyɛndane ne mɔ ati. Mebamaa mɔɔ tu ɔ nloa anu la agyakyi ye adubɛnwo ne, na meamaa mɔɔ ati yɛ se na ɔnze anwunvɔne la agyakyi ɔ nwo zo ɛmemanlɛ. 12Mebamaa nrenya nwo ahyia adɛla ezukoa nvutuke, yɛɛ sonla dasanli nwo bahyia adɛla Ofɛ ezukoa nvutuke. 13Yemɔti mebamaa anwomanyunlu awozo, na azɛlɛ akpusu adudu avi ɛleka mɔɔ ɔgyi la, wɔ medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma me ɛya kenle anu ɛzulolɛ ne anu.
14“Menli kɔsɔɔti bayɛ kɛ ahɛtɛboɛ mɔɔ bɛdoa bɛ bɛlɛkye bɛ, anzɛɛ mboane mɔɔ ɛbɔ asande na awie ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ boɔboa bɛ nloa la. Awie biala banriandi ahɔ ye menli avinli wɔ ɔdaye ye maanle nu. 15Bɛ nuhua biala mɔɔ bɛkɛnwu ye la bɛbawɔ ye atwɛ, yɛɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛhye ye la bawu dadeɛ nloa. 16Bɛbava bɛ mra ne mɔ bɛafifi debie bɛatete bɛ wɔ bɛdabɛ bɛ nye zo, bɛbave bɛ sua nu ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti na bɛamia bɛ ye mɔ bɛ nee bɛ adeda.”
17Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Bɛnlea, melɛmaa Mideama ara Babelɔnoma anwo zo. Bɛmɛ, bɛmbu dwɛtɛ fufule yɛɛ bɛ nye ɛnlie ezukoa nvutuke nwo. 18Bɛbava bɛ ɛda ne mɔ bɛahu mgbavolɛ ne mɔ, bɛnrɛze nlɔma bɔbɔ anwunvɔne na yeayɛ ngakula. 19 Na Nyamenle bazɛkye Babelonia, maanle kɛnlɛma ne mɔɔ tɛla maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti, maanle ne mɔɔ nuhua menli fa ye tu bɛ nwo la, kɛ ɔzɛkyele Sodɔm nee Gomɔla la. 20Awie ɛnrɛdɛnla nuhua ɛlɛ wɔ awolɛndoazo muala anu. Arelabenli biala ɛnrɛzi ye ndanlɛ sua wɔ ɛkɛ ne afoa nu, yɛɛ mboaneneavolɛma ɛnrɛva bɛ mboane ɛnrɛhɔ ɛkɛ ne adidi. 21 Nanemgbole bava ɛkɛ ne ayɛ bɛ alaleɛ, yɛɛ bɛ azua ne mɔ bayɛ nyɛmoa mɔɔ kpo la dabelɛ; soholo bahɔdɛnla ɛkɛ ne bie, yɛɛ ɛkɛ ne a mɛnlamenlakɛ barazi bɛ agole a. 22Ɛrane bakpo ye tawa ne mɔ azo, yɛɛ ɛzonlɛ bava bɛ suakunlu kɛnlɛma ne mɔ. Ye mekɛ ne ɛbikye. Babelɔn mekɛ ɛwie.”

english_text:
The Lord's People Will Come Home
1The Lord will have mercy on Israel and will let them be his chosen people once again. He will bring them back to their own land, and foreigners will join them as part of Israel. 2Other nations will lead them home, and Israel will make slaves of them in the land that belongs to the Lord. Israel will rule over those who once governed and mistreated them.
Death to the King of Babylonia!
3The Lord will set you free from your sorrow, suffering, and slavery. 4Then you will make fun of the King of Babylonia by singing this song:
That cruel monster is done for!
He won't attack us again.
5The Lord has crushed the power
of those evil kings,
6who were furious
and never stopped abusing
the people of other nations.
7Now all the world is at peace;
its people are celebrating
with joyful songs.
8King of Babylonia,
even the cypress trees
and the cedars of Lebanon
celebrate and say,
“Since you were put down,
no one comes along
to chop us down.”
9The world of the dead
eagerly waits for you.
With great excitement,
the spirits of ancient rulers
hear about your coming.
10Each one of them will say,
“Now you are just as weak
as any of us!
11Your pride and your music
have ended here
in the world of the dead.
Worms are your blanket,
maggots are your bed.”
12 You, the bright morning star,
have fallen from the sky!
You brought down other nations;
now you are brought down.
13 You said to yourself,
“I'll climb to heaven
and place my throne
above the highest stars.
I'll sit there with the gods
far away in the north.
14I'll be above the clouds,
just like God Most High.”
15But now you are deep
in the world of the dead.
16Those who see you will stare
and wonder, “Is this the man
who made the world tremble
and shook up kingdoms?
17Did he capture every city
and make earth a desert?
Is he the one who refused
to let prisoners go home?”
18When kings die, they are buried
in glorious tombs.
19But you will be left unburied,
just another dead body
lying underfoot
like a broken branch.
You will be one of many
killed in battle and gone down
to the deep rocky pit.
20You won't be buried with kings;
you ruined your country
and murdered your people.
You evil monster!
We hope that your family
will be forgotten forever.
21We will slaughter your sons
to make them pay for the crimes
of their ancestors.
They won't take over the world
or build cities
anywhere on this earth.
22The Lord All-Powerful has promised to attack Babylonia and destroy everyone there, so that none of them will ever be remembered again. 23The Lord will sweep out the people, and the land will become a swamp for wild animals.
Assyria Will Be Punished
24 The Lord All-Powerful
has made this promise:
Everything I have planned
will happen just as I said.
25I will wipe out every Assyrian
in my country,
and I will crush those
on my mountains.
I will free my people
from slavery
to the Assyrians.
26I have planned this
for the whole world,
and my mighty arm
controls every nation.
27I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have made these plans.
No one can stop me now!
The Philistines Will Be Punished
28 This message came from the Lord in the year King Ahaz died:
29 Philistines, don't be happy
just because the rod
that punished you
is broken.
That rod will become
a poisonous snake, and then
a flying fiery dragon.
30The poor and needy will find
pastures for their sheep
and will live in safety.
But I will starve some of you,
and others will be killed.
31Cry and weep in the gates
of your towns,
you Philistines!
Smoke blows in from the north,
and every soldier is ready.
32If a messenger comes
from a distant nation,
you must say:
“The Lord built Zion.
Even the poorest of his people
will find safety there.”
translation_text:
Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhyele bɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la sia ara sua nu
1Ɛdɛnkɛma banwu Yizilayɛma anwunvɔne na eza yeava bɛ bieko kɛ ye menli. Ɔbamaa bɛadɛnla bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo, nyɛvolɛ baraboka bɛ na bɛava bɛ nwo bɛabeta Yizilayɛma. 2Maanle maanle mɔɔ bɛwɔ nu la anu amra baboa Yizilayɛma bɛamaa bɛazia bɛara. Na Yizilayɛma bava nyɛvolɛ ne mɔ ayɛ bɛ ahanra mraalɛ nee mrenya wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma azɛlɛ ne azo. Bɛbahye menli mɔɔ hyele bɛ hɔle nlɔnu la nuokɛ na bɛazie menli ne mɔɔ sisile bɛ la.
Babelonia belemgbunli ne wɔ mɔwuamra maanle nu
3Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma maa bɛ nyane nee abodelɛ nee gyima ɛsesebɛ mɔɔ bɛmanle bɛyɛle la ka aze a, 4bɛbado edwɛne bɛagolo Babelonia belemgbunli ne anwo bɛaha kɛ,
“Sisiravolɛ ne asa ɛhondo aze, nzisi ɛwie! 5Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛbubu amumuyɛma kpɔma ne anu, yezɛkye arelemgbunli amumuyɛma tumi ne, 6mɔɔ bɛfa ɛya a bɛfa bɛyɛ menli amumuyɛ, na bɛwulowula bɛ ahutuku la. Bɛfa ɛya a bɛsie maanle maanle ne mɔ a na bɛyɛ menli ne kpɔdekpɔde. 7Azɛlɛ ye azo amuala ɛyɛ diinyi, anzonudwolɛ ɛra, na bɛkpakye bɛ ne nu bɛto edwɛne. 8Sepelɛse nee Lɛbanɔn sida mbaka si ɛ ti zo agole bɛka kɛ, ‘Sumunli kɛ bɛbɛlɛle wɔ aze la, awie ɛtɛbale kɛ ɔbabu yɛ yeagua.’
9“Ɛbolɔ ɛboɔboa ɔ nwo kɛ saa ɛba a ɔbarayia wɔ adenle. Azɛlɛ ye azo mgbanyima nwomenle badwazo arayɛ wɔ akoaba, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ anrɛɛ bɛle arelemgbunli wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anu la badwazo bɛ arelemgbunli mbia zo ayia wɔ. 10Bɛ muala bɛbadendɛ na bɛaze wɔ kɛ, ‘Ɛdawɔ noko wɔyɛ bɛtɛɛ kɛ yɛdayɛ la. Ɛ nee yɛ ɛyɛ pɛ! 11Getaa ɛbɔlɛ mgbole mɔɔ bɛvale bɛlile ɛ nzi, nee enililɛ kpole ne ɛrawie Ɛbolɔ; azonlɛ ɛyɛ wɔ ɛkpa ɛla zo, yɛɛ azone a le wɔ kundu mɔɔ gua ɛ nwo a.’
12 “O Alehyenlɛ Ɛwɔlɔra, Aleɛbahye Ralɛ Nrenya, ɛvi anwuma wɔdɔ aze kpole o! Wɔmɔ mɔɔ anrɛɛ ɛka maanle maanle aze fɛɛnye la, nea aze ko mɔɔ bɛvuandi wɔ bɛdo a! 13 Ɛvale ɛlile afua kɛ, ‘Mefo meahɔ anwuma lɔ, meadɛla Nyamenle nwɔlɔra ne mɔ. Mebava me belemgbunli ebia ne meazie anwuma lɔ; mebahɔdɛnla sɔlɔ moa moa nehane ayiama boka ne azo; 14mebavo meahɔ anwuma meadɛla amungu ne mɔ na meayɛ me nwo kɛ Anwuma Anwumanli ne.’ 15Na wɔmɔ a bɛ nee wɔ ɛra ɛbolɔ sua zo ɛke wɔ ewule kuma ye abo la.
16“Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛbanwu wɔ la banlea wɔ kpoonwu na bɛadwenledwenle ɛ nwo bɛabiza kɛ, ‘Asoo nrenya ne mɔɔ manle ewiade kpusule na ɔbutubutule arelemgbunlililɛ nye aze la ɛne? 17Asoo nrenya ne mɔɔ bɔle azuamgbole, na ɔmanle ewiade yɛle kɛ ɛsɛlɛ la ɛne? Asoo nrenya ne mɔɔ angyakyi menli mɔɔ ɔhyele bɛ nuokɛ ɛlɛ la ɛne?’ 18Maanle maanle ne mɔ arelemgbunli deda ye anyunlunyia nu; biala nee ye nla, 19na wɔmɔ, bɛvuandi wɔ bɛdo moa moa bɛvi wɔ belemgbunli bane nu kɛ ralɛ mɔɔ ye mekɛ andwu na bɛkɛwo ye la. Mɔɔ bɛvale bɛguale ɛ nwo la a le ɛlɔnema mɔɔ dɔle dadeɛ nloa la avunli mɔɔ bɛvuandi bɛ bɛgua ewule kuma bo awolɛ nu kɛ asɛɛ ɛle funli mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtietia ɛ nwo zo a. 20Bɛnrɛzie wɔ bɛnrɛboka arelemgbunli nwo, ɔboalekɛ wɔzɛkye wɔ azɛlɛ ne na wɔhu ɛdawɔ wɔ menli mɔɔ wɔ zolɛ la. Awie ɛnrɛbɔ munzule menli ne abo zo amra aluma bieko ɛlɛ. 21Bɛhu ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ: Bɛ ze mɔ ɛtane ne mɔ ati ɔwɔ kɛ bɛwu, anrɛɛ bɛkɛdwazo bɛkɛva ewiade ne na bɛkɛkyekye azuamgbole.”
Nyamenle bazɛkye Babelɔn
22Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebadwazo Babelɔn anwo zo na meazɛkye ye; menrɛvavi awie biala, ngakula nee debie biala, medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a. 23Mebamaa fuke ava azɛlɛ ne; mebamaa nzule apepɛ bula bula agyinlegyinla zolɛ, na meava ɛzɛkyelɛ sane ne meapia ye meahɔgua. Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”
Nyamenle bazɛkye Aseleama
24 Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha ndane kɛ, “Kɛmɔ mehyehyɛ la, zɔhane ala a ɔbayɛ a, yɛɛ kɛmɔ mezuzu la, zɔhane ala a ɔbagyinla a. 25Mebazɛkye Aseleama mɔɔ wɔ me azɛlɛ ne azo, mebaye me menli ne akɔme kpomgbolo na meazokoɛ bɛ adesoa. 26Ngyehyɛlɛ mɔɔ la ɛkɛ maa ewiade amuala la ɛne, yɛɛ tumi mɔɔ mebava meadea maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti la ɛne.” 27Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛhyehyɛ ɛdo ɛkɛ a, nwane a kɛhola kɛzɛkye ye a? Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdenrɛ ɔ sa, nwane a kɛhola kɛkpɔla ɔ sa a?
Nyamenle bazɛkye Filisitiama
28 Ɛvolɛ ne mɔɔ Belemgbunli Ehaze hɔle ayile nu la yɛɛ bɛbɔle nrɛlaleɛ ɛhye nolo a.
29 Nrɛlaleɛ ne se, “O Filisitiama amuala, bɛmmadi fɛlɛko kɛ baka ne mɔɔ bilale bɛ la ɛbubu, ɔluakɛ ɛwɔlɛ wu a, ɛwɔlɛ anwo ɛzulolɛ finde ɔ nzi, yɛɛ ɔto kolonvia a ɔbobɔ ɛwɔlɛ mɔɔ tu la. 30Ehyianli belamunli ralɛ bali aleɛ, yɛɛ mɔɔ ɛhyia la anwo badɔ ye. Na bɛmɛ, mebava ɛhɔne meabɔ bɛ menli mɔɔ hale la abo zo na meahu bɛ muala.
31“O Filisitiama, bɛ muala bɛva ɛzulolɛ bɛzu bɛye awolɛ wɔ bɛ azuamgbole zo nee bɛ nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ anloa. Ɔluakɛ senle vi sɔlɔ ɛlɛba; bɛle ɛlɔnema mɔɔ bɛ nuhua biala ɛnle foanvoanle a.”
32Duzu mualɛ yɛɛ sonla bava amaa maanle ne soanvolɛma a? “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkyekye Zayɔn, na ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ ye menli mɔɔ ɛlɛnwu amaneɛ la anwo badɔ bɛ a.”

english_text:
Moab Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Moab:
The towns of Ar and Kir
were destroyed in a night.
Moab is left in ruins!
2Everyone in Dibon has gone up
to the temple and the shrines
to cry and weep.
All of Moab is crying.
Heads and beards are shaved
because of what happened
at Nebo and Medeba.
3In the towns and at home,
everyone wears sackcloth
and cries loud and long.
4From Heshbon and Elealeh,
weeping is heard in Jahaz;
Moab's warriors scream
while trembling with fear.
Pity Moab
5I pity Moab!
Its people are running to Zoar
and to Eglath-Shelishiyah.
They cry on their way up
to the town of Luhith;
on the road to Horonaim
they tell of disasters.
6The streams of Nimrim
and the grasslands
have dried up.
Every plant is parched.
7The people of Moab are leaving,
crossing over Willow Creek,
taking everything they own
and have worked for.
8In the towns of Eglaim
and of Beerelim
and everywhere else in Moab
mournful cries are heard.
9The streams near Dimon
are flowing with blood.
But the Lord will bring
even worse trouble to Dimon,
because all in Moab who escape
will be attacked by lions.
translation_text:
Nyamenle bazɛkye Mowabe
1 Nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Mowabe anwo la ɛne. Kɛmɔ kenle ko nɔɔzo yɛɛ bɛbɔle suakpole Aale, yɛɛ kenle ko nɔɔzo yɛɛ bɛbɔle suakpole Kɛɛ la, Mowabe maanle ne anu ɛyɛ diinyi. 2Daebɔnoma ɛhɔ ɛleka ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛsonle la kazu. Mowabema ɛlɛsu Niboma nee Midɛbama. Awie biala ɛkpa ɔ ti, ɛkpa ɔ kɛsa. 3Bɛheda ɛrele bɛluolua gua ne mɔ azo, bɛgyinla azua ti zo nee bɛ azuamgbole zo ɛleka wienyi ne mɔ bɛsu bɛtwi monle. 4Hɛhyebɔnoma nee Ɛlɛyalima ɛlɛsu. Bɛte bɛ ne wɔ Gyeehaze, yemɔti akee Mowabe ɛlɔnema ɛlɛsu kpole kpalɛ na bɛ nwo wozo bɛ. 5Medi Mowabema anwo nyane. Maanle ne anu amra nriandi kɔfea Zowaa nee Ɛgelate Hyɛlehyaya. Bie mɔ fo boka ne kɔ Luhete kɔsu; bɛdwu Hɛloneeyem adenle nu a bɛsu toonwo asɛɛ debie yɛ bɛ. 6Nemelem nzule ne mɔ ɛsesa, ndile ne mɔ ɛwe, mɔɔ bɔle nrɛlɛne wɔ ɔ bo la ɛyela, ndile amolɛ ko bɔbɔ ɛnle ɛkɛ. 7Zɔhane ati aleɛ dɔɔnwo mɔɔ bɛnyianle ye, nee bɛ ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛlɛ la, bɛzoale bɛ muala bɛpɛle bɛhɔle Welo Kpɔkɛ Bɔnza ne anzi lɔ. 8Ɛzunlɛ ɛde Mowabe maanle ne anu ɛleka biala. Ɛzunlɛ ne ɛdwu Yigeleeyem nee Biyɛyilem. 9Ɔluakɛ Daebɔn azule ne mɔ ɛhakyi mogya, noko mebamaa mɔɔ tɛla ɛhye la ara Daebɔn anwo zo; mebamaa awenade ahye Mowabema mɔɔ vile ɛsalɛ na bɛnriandi la ali, na meazɛkye bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhale azɛlɛ ne azo la.

english_text:
More Troubles for Moab
1Send lambs as gifts
to the ruler of the land.
Send them across the desert
from Sela to Mount Zion.
2The women of Moab
crossing the Arnon River
are like a flock of birds
scattered from their nests.
3Moab's messengers say
to the people of Judah,
“Be kind and help us!
Shade us from the heat
of the noonday sun.
Hide our refugees!
Don't turn them away.
4Let our people live
in your country
and find safety here.”
Moab, your cruel enemies
will disappear;
they will no longer attack
and destroy your land.
5Then a kingdom of love
will be set up,
and someone from David's family
will rule with fairness.
He will do what is right
and quickly bring justice.
Moab's Pride Is Destroyed
6We have heard of Moab's pride.
Its people strut and boast,
but without reason.
7Tell everyone in Moab
to mourn for their nation.
Tell them to cry and weep
for those fancy raisins
of Kir-Hareseth.
8Vineyards near Heshbon
and Sibmah
have turned brown.
The rulers of nations
used to get drunk
on wine from those vineyards
that spread to Jazer,
then across the desert
and beyond the sea.
9Now I mourn like Jazer
for the vineyards
of Sibmah.
I shed tears for Heshbon
and for Elealeh.
There will be no more
harvest celebrations
10or joyful and happy times,
while bringing in the crops.
Singing and shouting are gone
from the vineyards.
There are no joyful shouts
where grapes were pressed.
God has silenced them all.
11Deep in my heart I hurt
for Moab and Kir-Heres.
12It's useless for Moab's people
to wear themselves out
by going to their altars
to worship and pray.
13The Lord has already said all of this about Moab. 14Now he says, “The contract of a hired worker is good for three years, but Moab's glory and greatness won't last any longer than that. Only a few of its people will survive, and they will be left helpless.”
translation_text:
Mowabe gyinlabelɛ ɛtane ne
1Mowabema ɛzoa menli vi Sila ɛmaa bɛva ɛsɛlɛ zo adenle ne anu bɛva mboane bɛhɔmaa Gyɛlusalɛm belemgbunli ne. 2Bɛdwu Azule Anɔn ne anloa a bɛdi tutɛnla kɛ nloma mɔɔ bɛvoa bɛ wɔ bɛ sane nu la.
3Bɛ edwɛkɛ a le kɛ, “Bɛhile yɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛyɛ la, bɛ nee yɛ ɛli ye pɛlepɛle zo. Bɛheda yɛ nwo zo kɛ nɔɔzo awozinli wɔ ewiazo sɛnzɛngyinla; bɛva menli ne mɔɔ awie ɛmbu bɛ bie la bɛvea, na bɛmmaye menli mɔɔ ɛlɛnriandi konle nu la bɛmaa. 4Bɛmaa yɛdayɛ Mowabema mɔɔ awie ɛmbu yɛ bie la ɛradɛnla bɛ avinli, na bɛlie yɛ kɛ nriandivolɛma wɔ sɛkyevolɛ ne asa anu.”
(Saa nzisi wie na bɛgyakyi azɛlɛ ne ɛzɛkyelɛ, na sɛkyeravolɛ ne vi azɛlɛ ne azo tu a, 5akee bɛbava ɛhulolɛ kpundii bɛazie ebia; ahenle mɔɔ badɛnla zolɛ la vi Belemgbunli Devidi abusua nu. Ɔbava nɔhalɛlilɛ yeazie menli ne, ɔbayɛ sonla mɔɔ kulo tenleneyɛlɛ, yɛɛ ɔbava pɛlepɛlelilɛ yeabua ndɛne.)
6Na Dwudama baha kɛ, “Yɛde Mowabema adubɛnwo ne nee kɛ bɛzile bɛmemanle bɛ nwo zo la; bɛ nloa anu ɛyelɛ, bɛ mgbanyizonle nee bɛ mgbole ɛhehanlɛ ne amuala. Bɛ adubɛnwo ne amuala le mgbane. 7Zɔhane ati bɛmaa Mowabema ɛzu bie. Awie biala ɛzu Mowabe. Bɛnwu amaneɛ yɛɛ nyane ɛha bɛ, ɔluakɛ bɛ Kɛɛ Hɛlɛse vanye ma welera ndɛlamoa ne mɔ ɛbɔ bɛ.”
8Hɛhyebɔn ɛya avule ne mɔ nee Sebema vanye egyinli ne mɔ ɛzɛkye. Ɛbɔ ye Sebema ɛkɛ ne mɔɔ kɔkpula Gyeezɛ, toonwo mɔɔ kɔdwu ɛsɛlɛ ne anloa lɔ, ɔpɛ nu ɛkɛ ɔkɔ toonwo ɔkɔgua ye Nyevile Wulera ne anloa la vanye egyinli ne mɔ mɔɔ manle maanle maanle arelemgbunli zile ngosi la ngane ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti ɛdwɔlɔdwɔlɔ. 9Yemɔti mefa ɛzunlɛ mɔɔ mefa mesu Gyeezɛ la meazu Sebema vanye egyinli ne mɔ. Mesu meagua Hɛhyebɔn nee Ɛlɛyali ati zo, ɔluakɛ bɛ ma nee bɛ bɛyɔba ne mɔ anwo zo a konle nu alɛrayɛlɛ ne ɛragua a. 10Fɛlɛko nee anyelielɛ ɛvi bɛ ma egyinli ne mɔ anu, awie ɛndeɛdea nu wɔ ɛkɛ. Awie ɛndwihwi nwanye ɛnvi vanye ma nu; vanye ma ɛtetelɛ nu anyelielɛ ɛdeɛdeanlɛ ne ɛwie. 11Yemɔti me ɛkɛla kulu ɔ kunlu kɛ getaa kpole la wɔ Mowabe ati, yɛɛ medi Kɛɛ Hɛlɛse anwo nyane. 12Saa Mowabema ye bɛ nyunlu, bɛfa bɛ nyane bɛkɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛsonle la kɛ bɛkaye ɛdɛne a, ɔnrɛyɛ boɛ ɔnrɛmaa bɛ.
13Edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle wɔ Mowabe anwo wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛze ɛhɔ la ɛne. 14Kɛkala Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Ɛvolɛ nsa pɛpɛ, mɔɔ le kɛ ɛkpabɔlɛ mekɛ la pɛpɛ, Mowabe maanle ne anyunlunyia badɔ aze. Menli bebelebe ne mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la, ekyi bie a baha a, yɛɛ eza bɛ nwo ɛnrɛyɛ se.”

english_text:
Damascus Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Damascus:
Damascus is doomed!
It will end up in ruins.
2The villages around Aroer
will be deserted,
with only sheep living there
and no one to bother them.
3Israel will lose its fortresses.
The kingdom of Damascus
will be destroyed;
its survivors will suffer
the same fate as Israel.
The Lord All-Powerful
has promised this.
Sin and Suffering
4When that time comes,
the glorious nation of Israel
will be brought down;
its prosperous people
will be skin and bones.
5Israel will be like wheat fields
in Rephaim Valley
picked clean of grain.
6It will be like an olive tree
beaten with a stick,
leaving two or three olives
or maybe four or five
on the highest
or most fruitful branches.
The Lord God of Israel
has promised this.
7At that time the people will turn and trust their Creator, the holy God of Israel. 8They have built altars and places for burning incense to their goddess Asherah, and they have set up sacred poles for her. But they will stop worshiping at these places.
9Israel captured powerful cities and chased out the people who lived there. But these cities will lie in ruins, covered over with weeds and underbrush.
10Israel, you have forgotten
the God who saves you,
the one who is the mighty rock
where you find protection.
You plant the finest flowers
to honor a foreign god.
11The plants may sprout
and blossom
that very same morning,
but it will do you no good,
because you will suffer
endless agony.
God Defends His People
12The nations are a noisy,
thunderous sea.
13But even if they roar
like a fearsome flood,
God will give the command
to turn them back.
They will be like dust,
or like a tumbleweed
blowing across the hills
in a windstorm.
14In the evening
their attack is fierce,
but by morning
they are destroyed.
This is what happens to those
who raid and rob us.
translation_text:
Nyamenle badea Selea nee Yizilayɛ
1 Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ mɔɔ fane Dɛmasekɛse anwo la ɛne. Ɔse, “Bɛnlea, Dɛmasekɛse ɛnrɛyɛ suakpole bieko; ɔbayɛ ewula edukue. 2Alowɛ azuamgbole ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti badɔ mgbane mɔɔ awie ɛnrɛdɛnla zolɛ bieko ɛlɛ a. Bɛbayɛ nyɛmoa alaleɛ. Bɛbahɔla ɛkɛ na awie ɛnrɛha bɛ ɛzulolɛ. 3Aranemgbole ne mɔ baminliminli Yifelaem, yɛɛ belemgbunlililɛ bavi Dɛmasekɛse; Seleama mɔɔ ɛha la anyunlu bagua aze kɛ Yizilayɛma la. Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.
4“Mekɛ ne anu, Gyekɔbo abo zo amra anyunlu bagua aze na bɛanwa bɛayɛ nrenzenrenze. 5Ɔbayɛ kɛ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛyazonlɛnli ɛlɛbu ye bɛyɔba na ɔlɛtete ye nzoleɛ kɔsɔɔti la; ɔbayɛ kɛ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛyazonlɛnli ɛlɛte ye ma kɔsɔɔti wɔ Relɛfeeyem Bɔnza la. 6Ma ngoko ngoko bie a baha zolɛ a, kɛ ɔlivi baka mɔɔ bɛtete zolɛ ma ne amuala na yeha kɛyɛ nwiɔ anzɛɛ nsa bie wɔ baka ne ati zo nehane, anzɛɛ nna anzɛɛ nnu wɔ baka ne ngane ne mɔɔ so kpalɛ la azo la. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle a mese a.”
7Mekɛ ne anu menli banwu bɛ Bɔvolɛ ne na bɛahakyi bɛ nye Yizilayɛ Nwuanzanwuanza Ko ne anwo. 8Bɛnrɛbu bɛ sa anloa gyima mɔɔ le bɛ azukponle ne mɔ, yɛɛ bɛnrɛnlea mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛva bɛ sa bɛyɛ bɔbɔ la, na yeayɛ bɛ bozonle raalɛ Ahyela ne ananze ne mɔ anzɛɛ bɛ ɛyɛlɛkpunlɛ azukponle ne mɔ.
9Mekɛ ne anu bɛ azuamgbole mɔɔ yɛ se la bayɛ kɛ Haevaema nee Amɔlema azuamgbole ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛyɛ azuadu la. Bɛvile azuamgbole ne mɔ azo bɛnriandile wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Yizilayɛma ɛlɛba la, na azua ne mɔ badɔ mgbane.
10Ɔluakɛ Yizilayɛ arɛle ɛvi ye ngoanelielɛ Nyamenle ne, yɛɛ ɔngakye ye Ɛvealeka Bodane ne, mɔɔ le ye ɛvealeka la. Zɔhane ati bɛdua mbaka ngɛnlɛma na bɛava nyɛvolɛ awozonle bɛaziezie nu bɛazonle bɛ. 11Bɛbanlea bɛamaa bɛanyi kenle ko ne ala mɔɔ bɛkɛlua la, na bɛamaa bɛazo kenle ko ne ala nwonlomɔ ne mɔɔ bɛkɛlua la, noko bɛnrɛnyia bɛyɔba. Nyane nee amaneɛnwunlɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ la a bɛbanwu ye a.
Bɛli kpɔvolɛ maanle maanle ne mɔ anwo zo konim
12Aa, tie maanle maanle dɔɔnwo ane kɛ ɛlɛkulu bie a. Bɛlɛkulu kɛ nyevile mɔɔ ɛha ɔ nwo la. Aa, maanle maanle ne mɔ ɛlɛtea, bɛ ne le kɛ azule kpole bie mɔɔ lua awolɛ zo la. 13Maanle maanle ne mɔ tea, bɛ ne kulu kɛ azule mɔɔ lua awolɛ zo la. Noko ɔbahwi bɛ nyunlu, na bɛbagua ndwɛlɛ aze, bɛanriandi kɛ awoka zo abonle mɔɔ anwoma ɛlɛbɔ ye ahɔ, anzɛɛ munlutu mɔɔ ɛlɛdi akyima wɔ ahumuakyima nu la. 14Aleɛ dwo a, nea, ɛzulolɛ ngome! Mɔɔ aleɛ kahye la ɛnee biala ɛnle ɛkɛ! Menli mɔɔ sɛkye yɛ, wua yɛ nwo ninyɛne la kyɛfoa ɛ.

english_text:
Ethiopia Will Be Punished
1 Downstream from Ethiopia
lies the country of Egypt,
swarming with insects.
2Egypt sends messengers
up the Nile River
on ships made of reeds.
Send them fast to Ethiopia,
whose people are tall
and have smooth skin.
Their land is divided by rivers;
they are strong and brutal,
feared all over the world.
3Everyone on this earth,
listen with care!
A signal will be given
on the mountains,
and you will hear a trumpet.
4The Lord said to me,
“I will calmly look down
from my home above—
as calmly as the sun at noon
or clouds in the heat
of harvest season.”
5Before the blossoms
can turn into grapes,
God will cut off the sprouts
and hack off the branches.
6Ethiopians will be food
for mountain vultures
during the summer
and for wild animals
during the winter.
7Those Ethiopians are tall and their skin is smooth. They are feared all over the world, because they are strong and brutal. But at that time they will come from their land divided by rivers, and they will bring gifts to the Lord All-Powerful, who is worshiped on Mount Zion.
translation_text:
Nyamenle badea Sudan
1 Sudan azule ne mɔ anzi lɔ, azɛlɛ bie wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛbɔ ndɛbalɛ nu, 2na bɛsoa ɛbɔfoɔma wɔ ndɔ ɛlɛne nu bɛmaa bɛkɔ Azule Naele ne nyiakɛ. Bɛmɛ soanvolɛma mɔɔ anwo yɛ ndɛ a, bɛhɔ maanle bie mɔɔ nuhua menli ne le ndendenle, bɛ nwo yɛ fɛ na menli mɔɔ ewiade amra amuala sulo bɛ la anu; ɔle maanle mɔɔ anwo yɛ ɛzulolɛ na ɔdi konim wɔ konle nu a, yɛɛ ye azɛlɛ ne, azule dɔɔnwo ɛgyigya nuhua.
3Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ ewiade la amuala, bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛde azɛlɛ ye azo la, saa bɛmaa sɛkɛlɛneɛ bie zo wɔ awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ a, bɛnlea. Saa bɛbɔ aweɛne tendenle nu a, bɛdie. 4Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, “Ɛleka mɔɔ mede la, mebado me nye meanlea bɛ koonwu kɛ ɛbuhenle nu wuluwulu ɛbɔlɛ mɔɔ tɔ nɔɔzo, meavede me nye meanlea azɛlɛ ye. 5Ɔluakɛ ɔkadwu mekɛ mɔɔ ndotolo kawie kpolo, na ndotolo ne ayɛ ma abolo, na ɛbuhenle ne adwu la, mebava dadeɛ meapepɛ nya ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛlɛfefɛ la anye, na meabubu ngane ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛdɛlɛdɛlɛ la meagua. 6Bɛbagyakyi bɛ bɛamaa awoka zo nloma nee azɛlɛ ye azo nane kɛ bɛli. Bɛbayɛ nloma aleɛ wɔ wawaa nu, na bɛayɛ azɛlɛ ye azo nane kɔsɔɔti aleɛ wɔ fɔsɛlɛ nu.”
7Mekɛ ne anu menli ndendenle anwo fɛlɛko mɔɔ ewiade amra sulo bɛ, na bɛle maanle anwo ɛzulolɛ mɔɔ di konim wɔ konle nu, mɔɔ azule dɔɔnwo ɛgyigya bɛ azɛlɛ ne anu la bava ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne arɛlɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Zayɔn Boka, ɛleka mɔɔ bɛsonle Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma la.

english_text:
Egypt Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Egypt:
The Lord comes to Egypt,
riding swiftly on a cloud.
The people are weak from fear.
Their idols tremble
as he approaches and says,
2“I will punish Egypt
with civil war—
neighbors, cities, and kingdoms
will fight each other.
3“Egypt will be discouraged
when I confuse their plans.
They will try to get advice
from their idols,
from the spirits of the dead,
and from fortunetellers.
4I will put the Egyptians
under the power of a cruel,
heartless king.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have promised this.”
Trouble along the Nile
5The Nile River will dry up
and become parched land.
6Its streams will stink,
Egypt will have no water,
and the reeds and tall grass
will dry up.
7Fields along the Nile
will be completely barren;
every plant will disappear.
8Those who fish in the Nile
will be discouraged
and mourn.
9None of the cloth makers
will know what to do,
and they will turn pale.
10Weavers will be confused;
paid workers will cry and mourn.
Egypt's Helpless Leaders
11The king's officials in Zoan
are foolish themselves
and give stupid advice.
How can they say to him,
“We are very wise,
and our families go back
to kings of long ago?”
12Where are those wise men now?
If they can, let them say
what the Lord All-Powerful
intends for Egypt.
13The royal officials in Zoan
and in Memphis
are foolish and deceived.
The leaders in every state
have given bad advice
to the nation.
14The Lord has confused Egypt;
its leaders have made it stagger
and vomit like a drunkard.
15No one in Egypt can do a thing,
no matter who they are.
16When the Lord All-Powerful punishes Egypt with his mighty arm, the Egyptians will become terribly weak and will tremble with fear. 17They will be so terrified of Judah that they will be frightened by the very mention of its name. This will happen because of what the Lord All-Powerful is planning against Egypt.
The Lord Will Bless Egypt, Assyria, and Israel
18The time is coming when Hebrew will be spoken in five Egyptian cities, and their people will become followers of the Lord. One of these cities will be called City of the Sun.
19In the heart of Egypt an altar will be set up for the Lord; at its border a shrine will be built to honor him. 20These will remind the Egyptians that the Lord All-Powerful is with them. And when they are in trouble and ask for help, he will send someone to rescue them from their enemies. 21The Lord will show the Egyptians who he is, and they will know and worship the Lord. They will bring him sacrifices and offerings, and they will keep their promises to him. 22After the Lord has punished Egypt, the people will turn to him. Then he will answer their prayers, and the Egyptians will be healed.
23At that time a good road will run from Egypt to Assyria. The Egyptians and the Assyrians will travel back and forth from Egypt to Assyria, and they will worship together. 24Israel will join with these two countries. They will be a blessing to everyone on earth, 25then the Lord All-Powerful will bless them by saying,
“The Egyptians are my people.
I created the Assyrians
and chose the Israelites.”
translation_text:
Nyamenle badea Yigyibiti
1 Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Yigyibiti anwo la ɛne.
Bɛnlea, Ɛdɛnkɛma de amungu zo ɛlɛba waa zɛhae, ɔlɛba Yigyibiti. Awozonle mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la nwu ye a bɛ nwo bawozo bɛ, na Yigyibitima ahonle badu. 2Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebamaa Yigyibitima angome adwazo atia bɛ nwo, adiema nee adiema baho, agɔnwolɛ badwazo agɔnwolɛ nwo zo, suakpole nee suakpole baho, na arelemgbunli adwazo arelemgbunli nwo zo. 3Bɛ ɛnwomenle mɔɔ wɔ bɛ nu la bawie, na mebazɛkye bɛ adwenle ngyehyɛleɛ biala. Bɛbahɔ bɛ awozonle ne mɔ, bɛ ngonyiama, menli mɔɔ tendɛ nwomenle nloa azo, yɛɛ bayivolɛma ne mɔ ɛkɛ ne abisa, 4noko mebaye Yigyibitima ne meamaa menlenlɛ bie mɔɔ ati yɛ se la, na belemgbunli anwo ɛzulolɛ bie bazie bɛ. Medame Awulae, Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, kɛ mese la ɛne.”
5Azule Naele ne basesa ayɛ resee, azɛlɛ ne akpakyekpakye; 6ye ngane ne mɔ basesa na ye ɛleka mɔɔ bɛdukue ye bɛva la abɔ nvoanvoa, na nuhua ndɔ nee ndile akpɔlɔ. 7Naele ne anloa azɛlɛ ne mɔ badɔ mgbane; aleɛ mɔɔ bɛlua bɛ ɛkɛ ne la amuala banwoso awu, na anwoma apia bɛ ahɔ. 8Fɛlɛhyelɛma mɔɔ to koba nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛto avonle wɔ Naele ne anu la anwo bavɔ, na bɛbazu bɛaye awolɛ. 9Gyimayɛvoma mɔɔ yɛ dwɛsɛ nwo gyima nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnwo ndanlɛ la arɛle babɔ. 10Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛle mandimase wɔ maanle ne anu la, bɛbaha bɛ senle dwɛɛ, na alɔbɔlɛ bahu gyimayɛvoma mɔɔ di ɛkpa la.
11Zowan mgbanyima le ahoasea kpole kpalɛ, yɛɛ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne folɛtuvoma tu folɛ ɛtane. Duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ bɛka bɛkile Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Mele nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ ra, mele mɔmoane arelemgbunli ne mɔ bie ara nrenya” ɛ? 12Bɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma ne wɔ nienwu? Bɛmaa bɛha na bɛye debie ko mɔɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhyehyɛ mɔɔ ɔbava yeayɛ Yigyibitima la bɛhile bɛ. 13Zowan mgbanyima ɛyɛ ahoasea, yɛɛ bɛbɛlɛbɛla Mɛmefese mgbanyima. Yigyibiti titilema mɔɔ lɛ maanle ne la ɛmaa Yigyibitima anye zo ɛda bɛ. 14Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye anyezota ɛdo Yigyibitima anwo, yemaa bɛbɔ atondo wɔ bɛ debie biala ɛyɛlɛ nu kɛ nzanli mɔɔ ɛbo ɛfefe ɛla nu la. 15Debie biala ɛnle Yigyibiti mɔɔ tile o, dualɛ o, ɛrɛlakɛ anzɛɛ ndɔ kɛhola kɛyɛ a.
Yigyibitima bazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma
16Mekɛ ne anu Yigyibitima bayɛ kɛ mralɛ. Sulosulo bamaa bɛ nwo awozo bɛ wɔ tumi ne mɔɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa yeara bɛ nwo zo la abo. 17Dwuda maanle ne anwo baha Yigyibitima ɛzulolɛ. Mekɛ biala mɔɔ bɛkɛbɔ duma ne bɛkɛhile Yigyibitima la, ɛzulolɛ baha bɛ wɔ mɔɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhyehyɛ kɛ ɔfa yeayɛ bɛ la ati.
18Mekɛ ne anu azuamgbole nnu mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la baha Keena anzɛɛ Hibulu aneɛ ne bie na bɛazonle Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma. Bɛbavɛlɛ azuamgbole ɛhye mɔ anu ko “Sɛnzɛne Suakpole.” 19Mekɛ ne anu bɛbazi Ɛdɛnkɛma azukponle wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo na bɛakpɔnla Ɛdɛnkɛma mpila wɔ maanle ne ɛweɛne zo. 20Ɛhye bayɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma sɛkɛlɛneɛ nee daselɛ wɔ maanle ne anu, amaa mekɛ biala mɔɔ sisiravolɛma kɛdwazo bɛ nwo zo la, saa bɛsu bɛfɛlɛ ye a yearɛlɛ bɛ dievolɛ yeamaa yearaho yealie bɛ. 21Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa Yigyibitima anwu ye, na Yigyibitima banwu Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ mekɛ ne anu na bɛava azubɔlɛ nee ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ bɛazonle ye; bɛbabɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛwɔkɛ na bɛaye. 22Ɛdɛnkɛma badea Yigyibitima na eza yeayɛ bɛ ayile; bɛbazia bɛara Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkɛ, na ɔbadie bɛ modolɛ nzɛlɛlɛ na yeayɛ bɛ ayile.
23Mekɛ ne anu ademgbole bala Yigyibiti nee Aselea avinli. Aseleama bahɔ Yigyibiti, yɛɛ Yigyibitima bahɔ Aselea maanle nu, na Yigyibitima nee Aseleama babɔ nu azonle. 24Mekɛ ne anu Yizilayɛ badɔ Aselea nee Yigyibiti anwo zo bɛayɛ maanle nsa, na bɛayɛ nyilalɛ bɛamaa ewiade amra amuala. 25Bɛmɛ yɛɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha bɛ nwo edwɛkɛ kɛ, “Nyilalɛ ɛha me menli Yigyibitima, Aselea mɔɔ le me sa anloa gyima, yɛɛ Yizilayɛ, me agyadeɛ.”

english_text:
Isaiah Acts Out the Defeat of Egypt and Ethiopia
1King Sargon of Assyria gave orders for his army commander to capture the city of Ashdod. 2About this same time the Lord had told me, “Isaiah, take off everything, including your sandals!” I did this and went around naked and barefoot 3for three years.
Then the Lord said:
What Isaiah has done is a warning to Egypt and Ethiopia. 4Everyone in these two countries will be led away naked and barefoot by the king of Assyria. Young or old, they will be taken prisoner, and Egypt will be disgraced. 5They will be confused and frustrated, because they depended on Ethiopia and bragged about Egypt. 6When this happens, the people who live along the coast will say, “Look what happened to them! We ran to them for safety, hoping they would protect us from the king of Assyria. But now, there is no escape for us.”
translation_text:
Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne mɔɔ lɛ ɔ nwo zɔ la anwo sɛkɛlɛneɛ
1Aselea maanle maanle Belemgbunli Sagɔn zoanle ye Safohyenlema Kpanyinli ne mɔɔ nea ye ɛlɔnema anwo zo la manle ɔvale ɛlɔnema ɔrale Ahyedɔdo ɔrahonle ɔvale suakpole ne. 2Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdendɛ ɛhile Emɔzo ara Ayezaya kɛ, “Kɔzianyi ɛrele ne mɔɔ hye ɛ nze zo la na yeye ɛ gyakɛ mgbɔlaboa ne mɔ,” na yeyɛ ye zɔ, ɔlɛ ɔ nwo zɔ, ɔ gyakɛ gua aze na ɔzo ɔlua. 3Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Me sonvolɛ Ayezaya ɛlɛ ɔ nwo zɔ, ɛgua ɔ gyakɛ aze yeluolua toonwo ɛvolɛ nsa. Ɛhye le sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ kile mɔɔ bazi Yigyibitima nee Sudanema anwo zo la. 4Yemɔti Aselea maanle maanle belemgbunli ne bahye Yigyibitima nuokɛ na yeazoa Sudanema yeahɔ nlɔnu. Ɔbahye ngakula nee mgbanyinli mɔɔ lɛ bɛ nwo zɔ, bɛ gyakɛ gua aze, na bɛ butua gua zo la yeahɔ, yeava yeagua Yigyibitima anyunlu aze. 5Akee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛva bɛ rɛle bɛdo Sudanema anwo zo na bɛfa Yigyibiti bɛtu bɛ nloa anu la arɛle babɔ na bɛ adwenle aha abɔ nu. 6Mekɛ ne anu bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛde ɛnweanloa nehae la baha kɛ, ‘Bɛnlea mɔɔ ɛzi bɛdabɛ mɔɔ yɛvale yɛ rɛle yɛwulale bɛ nu, na yɛnriandile yɛhɔdanenle bɛ kɛ bɛboa yɛ na bɛlie yɛ bɛvi Aselea belemgbunli ne asa anu la anwo zo a! Na yɛmɛ, kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na yɛavi ɛsalɛ ɛ?’ ”

english_text:
The Fall of Babylonia
1This is a message about a desert beside the sea:
Enemies from a hostile nation
attack like a whirlwind
from the Southern Desert.
2What a horrible vision
was shown to me—
a vision of betrayal
and destruction.
Tell Elam and Media
to surround and attack
the Babylonians.
The Lord has sworn to end
the suffering they caused.
3I'm in terrible pain
like a woman giving birth.
I'm shocked and hurt so much
that I can't hear or see.
4My head spins; I'm horrified!
Early evening, my favorite time,
has become a nightmare.
5In Babylon the high officials
were having a feast.
They were eating and drinking,
when someone shouted,
“Officers, take your places!
Grab your shields.”
6The Lord said to me,
“Send guards
to find out
what's going on.
7When they see cavalry troops
and columns of soldiers
on donkeys and camels,
tell them to be ready!”
8Then a guard said,
“I have stood day and night
on this watchtower, Lord.
9 Now I see column after column
of cavalry troops.”
At once someone shouted,
“Babylon has fallen!
Every idol in the city
lies broken on the ground.”
10Then I said, “My people,
you have suffered terribly,
but I have a message for you
from the Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel.”
How Much Longer?
11This is a message about Dumah:
From the country of Seir,
someone shouts to me,
“Guard, how much longer
before daylight?”
12From my guard post, I answered,
“Morning will soon be here,
but night will return.
If you want to know more,
come back later.”
13This is a message for Arabs who live in the barren desert in the region of Dedan:
You must order your caravans
14to bring water for those
who are thirsty.
You people of Tema
must bring food
for the hungry refugees.
15They are worn out and weary
from being chased by enemies
with swords and arrows.
16The Lord said to me:
A year from now the glory of the people of Kedar will all come to an end, just as a worker's contract ends after a year. 17Only a few of their warriors will be left with bows and arrows. This is a promise that I, the Lord God of Israel, have made.
translation_text:
Babelɔn ɛbɔlɛ nwo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ
1Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Babelonia anwo la ɛne:
Ɔle kɛ ahumuakyima mɔɔ vi nyiakɛ ɛlɛtu la, ɔvi ɛsɛlɛ zo a ɔlɛba a, ɔvi maanle anwo ɛzulolɛ bie anu a ɔlɛba a. 2Ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ ɛsesebɛ kpalɛ a menwu ye la; ninyɛnevenlɛma mɔɔ fe ninyɛne nee ninyɛnezɛkyelɛma mɔɔ sɛkye ninyɛne.
Yilam ɛlɔnema, bɛhɔho! Midea ɛlɔnema, bɛhɔbɛnra azuamgbole bɛyia! Nyamenle se, “Mebazi nyanehilelɛ ne mɔɔ Babelɔn ɛhile menli la kɔsɔɔti aze.”
3Yemɔti nyane ɛwolowolo me na me nwo fofo me kɛ raalɛ mɔɔ ɛvo awolɛ zo la. Me ti ɛzi aze, yemɔti mende ɛhwee, yɛɛ me adwenle ɛha ɛbɔ nu, yemɔti mennwu ɛhwee. 4Me ti kpakye me, ɛzulolɛ ɛheda me nwo zo. Akee aledwolɛ ne mɔɔ me nwo lɔle ye la anu ɛyɛ ɛzulolɛ kpole bie ɛmaa me.
5Ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ ne anu, menwunle kɛ bɛdo ɛkponle ne, bɛziezie mbia nwolɛ na bɛlɛdi bɛno. Arɛlevilɛ nu bɛdeanle nu, “Safohyenlema, bɛdwazo bɛvɔ bɛ sa nu enyinlike ne mɔ nwole!”
6Ɔluakɛ Awulae zele me kɛ, “Kɔ, kɔva awie maa ɔgyinla ɔzinza, na mɔɔ ɔkɛnwu ye la yeava yeado gua. 7Saa ɔnwu kɛ menli dede mgbɔnwɔ zo na bɛlua ye nwiɔ nwiɔ, bie mɔ dede asoaso nee afunlumu zo a, maa ɔdie bɛ kpalɛ kpalɛ.”
8Na mɔɔ ɛlɛsinza la nwunle bɛ na ɔdeanle nuhua kɛ, “O Awulae, megyi tawa ye azo mesinza dahuu. Aledwolɛ nu amuala megyi me gyakɛ anu. 9 Na kɛkala nea, bɛmɛ a bɛlɛba la! Menli ne dede mgbɔnwɔ zo na bɛlua ye nwiɔ nwiɔ!”
Na ɔbuale bɛ kɛ, “Yebɔ! Babelɔn ɛbɔ; bɛbubu ye awozonle ananze ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti bɛgua.”
10O me menli mɔɔ bɛtietia bɛ nwo zo bɛwozo bɛ na bɛhegye bɛ kɛ ma a, mɔɔ mede mevi Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne ɛkɛ ne la a mebɔ ye nolo mehile bɛ la.
Nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Yidɔm anwo la
11Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Yidɔm anwo la ɛne:
Awie wɔ Yidɔm (Siyɛ) ɛlɛfɛlɛ me. Ɔse, “Sinzavolɛ, aledwolɛ ne anu ɛ? Sinzavolɛ, aledwolɛ ne anu ɛ?”
12Sinzavolɛ ne bua ye kɛ, “Aleɛ ɛlɛkye, na eza aledwolɛ bara. Saa ɛse ɛbiza a, biza; anrɛɛ sia bɛla bieko.”
Nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Areleebea anwo la
13Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Areleebea anwo la ɛne:
Bɛmɛ Didanema mɔɔ bɛ ehwili a le bɛ azua mɔɔ bɛda nu la, Areleebea kpɔkɛ bo ala a bɛbadɛnla a. 14O bɛmɛ Timama, bɛva nzule bɛrɛlɛ menli mɔɔ nzuhɔne ɛlɛku bɛ la, bɛva aleɛ bɛyia menli mɔɔ ɛlɛnriandi munzule la. 15Ɔluakɛ bɛnriandi bɛvi konle nu, bɛnriandi bɛvi dadeɛ nee ɛda nloa.
16Ɔluakɛ Awulae zele me kɛ, “Ɛvolɛ ko pɛpɛ, kɛmɔ ɛkpabɔlɛ mekɛ ne kile la, Kida anyunlunyia badɔ aze, 17na katakyiema mɔɔ ze ɛda to kpalɛ wɔ Kida la baha ekyi bie, ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne a mese a.”

english_text:
Trouble in Vision Valley
1This is a message about Vision Valley:
Why are you celebrating
on the flat roofs
of your houses?
2Your city is filled
with noisy shouts.
Those who lie drunk
in your streets
were not killed in battle.
3Your leaders ran away,
but they were captured
without a fight.
No matter how far they ran,
they were found and caught.
4Then I said, “Leave me alone!
Let me cry bitter tears.
My people have been destroyed,
so don't try to comfort me.”
5The Lord All-Powerful
had chosen a time
for noisy shouts and confusion
to fill Vision Valley,
and for everyone to beg
the mountains for help.
6The people of Elam and Kir
attacked with chariots
and carried shields.
7Your most beautiful valleys
were covered with chariots;
your cities were surrounded
by cavalry troops.
8Judah was left defenseless.
At that time you trusted in the weapons you had stored in Forest Palace. 9You saw the holes in the outer wall of Jerusalem, and you brought water from the lower pool. 10You counted the houses in Jerusalem and tore down some of them, so you could get stones to repair the city wall. 11Then you built a large tank between the walls to store the water. But you refused to trust the God who planned this long ago and made it happen.
A Time To Weep
12When all of this happened,
the Lord All-Powerful told you
to weep and mourn,
to shave your heads,
and wear sackcloth.
13 But instead, you celebrated
by feasting on beef and lamb
and by drinking wine,
because you said,
“Let's eat and drink today!
Tomorrow we may die.”
14The Lord All-Powerful
has spoken to me
this solemn promise:
“I won't forgive them for this,
not as long as they live.”
Selfish Officials Are Doomed
15The Lord All-Powerful is sending me with this message for Shebna, the prime minister:
16Shebna, what gives you the right to have a tomb carved out of rock in this burial place of royalty? None of your relatives are buried here. 17You may be powerful, but the Lord is about to snatch you up and throw you away. 18He will roll you into a ball and throw you into a wide open country, where you will die and your chariots will be destroyed. You're a disgrace to those you serve.
19The Lord is going to take away your job! 20-21He will give your official robes and your authority to his servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
Eliakim will be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the royal family of Judah. 22 The Lord will put him in charge of the key that belongs to King David's family. No one will be able to unlock what he locks, and no one will be able to lock what he unlocks. 23The Lord will make him as firm in his position as a tent peg hammered in the ground, and Eliakim will bring honor to his family.
24His children and relatives will be supported by him, like pans hanging from a peg on the wall. 25That peg is fastened firmly now, but someday it will be shaken loose and fall down. Then everything that was hanging on it will be destroyed. This is what the Lord All-Powerful has promised.
translation_text:
Nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Gyɛlusalɛm anwo la
1Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ Bɔnza ne anwo la ɛne:
Duzu a bɛlɛyɛ a, mɔɔ bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛvo bɛhɔ bɛ azua ne mɔ ati zo, 2na bɛlɛteɛdea nu, na suakpole ye azo ɛyɛ begyebegye, na bɛ nye ɛlie zɛhae ɛ?
Bɛ menli mɔɔ bɛhu bɛ la andɔ dadeɛ nloa yɛɛ bɛanwu konle nu. 3Bɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ ɛnriandi, noko bɛhye bɛ muala wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ awie ando ɛda ko bɔbɔ la. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnriandile bɛhɔle moa moa bɔbɔ la, bɛnwu bɛ bɛhye bɛ. 4Yemɔti menganle kɛ, “Awie biala mmanea me; bɛmaa menzu mendwi monle kpalɛ; bɛmmapele kɛ bɛkyekye me rɛle wɔ me menli ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛhu bɛ la ati!” 5Ɔluakɛ Tumivolɛ Awulae Nyamenle ne anyezota, ye konle nee ye menli ɛhunlɛ mekɛ wɔ Ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ Bɔnza ɛdwu, na bɛbabubu suakpole ne bane ne mɔ bɛagua, na ɛdeɛdeanlɛ bara awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ.
6Yilam ɛlɔnema lɛ ɛda dede konle ehwili nu nee mgbɔnwɔ zo, yɛɛ Kɛɛ ɛlɔnema ɛye bɛ enyinlike ne mɔ ɛlɛ. 7Bɛ mbɔnza kpalɛ ne mɔ anu ɛyɛ konle ehwili ngome, yɛɛ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ dede mgbɔnwɔ zo la ɛva nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ. 8Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkpa Dwuda anwo ɛdanlɛ.
Mekɛ ne anu bɛvale bɛ adwenle bɛzɔle konle ninyɛne mɔɔ wɔ Kpɔkɛmile Sua ne anu la, 9na bɛnwunle kɛ Devidi suakpole ne bane ne mɔ ɛgyigya dɔɔnwo. Bɛhɔsesale nzule wɔ nyiakɛ azule ne anu, 10bɛdianle Gyɛlusalɛm azua ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ bane ne mɔ anwo la na bɛbubule bie mɔ bɛvale bɛsosɔle bane ne mɔ. 11Bɛzile pike wɔ bane nwiɔ ne avinli bɛmanle azule dɛba ne zenzenle ragyinlanle nu. Noko bɛandwenle ahenle mɔɔ yɛle la anwo, yɛɛ bɛambu ahenle mɔɔ dwenlenle nwolɛ hyehyɛle dole ɛkɛ ne dɛba dɛba la bie.
12Mekɛ ne anu Tumivolɛ Awulae Nyamenle ne zele bɛ kɛ bɛzu na bɛli nyane, bɛkpa bɛ ti na bɛheda ɛrele; 13 na nea, bɛmanle bɛ nye liele, bɛlile fɛlɛko, bɛhunle nlankɛ nee mboane, bɛlile nane na bɛnlonle nwanye, na bɛhanle kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛli na yɛnlo, na ɛhyema ɛnee yɛwu.”
14Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha ɛmaa mede ye me nzo nu kɛ, “Nɔhalɛ, bɛnrɛva ɛtane ɛhye bɛnrɛhyɛ bɛ toonwo bɛkɛwu. Medame Tumivolɛ Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.”
Hyɛbena kɔkɔbɔlɛ
15Tumivolɛ Awulae Nyamenle se, “Bɛla, kɔ Hyɛbena mɔɔ nea belemgbunli awuke ne azo la ɛkɛ na biza ye kɛ, 16‘Duzu debie a ɛyɛ ye ɛke a, yɛɛ ɛ nee nwane a wɔ ɛke, mɔɔ yemɔti wɔbɔ nla wɔmaa ɛ nwo wɔ ɛke a? Wɔmɔ, ɛbɔ nla awoka zo na ɛtu bɔne wɔ bodane nu ɛyɛ wɔ tɛnlabelɛ. 17Nea, Ɛdɛnkɛma bavuandi wɔ ado kpole kpalɛ; ɛdawɔ ɛse ɛ nwo yɛ se! Ɔbazɔ wɔ mrɛlakɛ bo yeabili wɔ, 18na yeavuandi wɔ kɛ bɔlo la yeade azɛlɛ tɛtɛlɛ bie azo; ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ ɛbawu na wɔ konle ehwili kɛnlɛma ne aha a. Anyiemgbanli, ɛ nwo yɛ nyiane wɔ ɛ menle sua nu bɔbɔ. 19Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa bɛaye wɔ gyima nu, na bɛaza wɔ bɛalie wɔ gyinlabelɛ ne.’ ”
20Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Hyɛbena kɛ, “Mekɛ ne anu mebavɛlɛ me sonvolɛ Yilayakem, Helekaya ara nrenya ne, 21na meava wɔ tɛladeɛ ne meawula ye, meava wɔ akyeso ne meahye ye, na meava wɔ tumi ne mɔɔ ɛlɛ la meamaa ye. Na ɔbayɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ Gyɛlusalɛm ɛkɛ nee Dwuda amuala la bɛ ze. 22 Mebava Devidi awuke nu sanvɛ ne meamaa ye; ɔbabuke, na awie biala ɛnrɛhola nuhua to; ɔbado nu, na awie biala ɛnrɛhola ye buke. 23Mebakpɔnla ye kɛ sika wɔ ɛleka kpalɛ, na ɔbayɛ anyunlunyia kpole yeamaa ɔ ze awuke nu amra.
24“Bɛbava debie biala mɔɔ wɔ ɔ ze awuke nu ɛkɛ ne la bɛawula ɔ sa nu: mralɛ nee nlɔnra, ahɔpo mralɛ nee mgbole, nee debie biala bakpolo ɔ kɔme. 25Na mekɛ ne anu medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mese: Sika ne mɔɔ memkpɔnlanle la bakpɔlɔ na yeabu yeadɔ, na kpomgbolo ne mɔɔ kpolo ye la aye, ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”

english_text:
The City of Tyre Will Be Punished
1 This is a message from distant islands about the city of Tyre:
Cry, you seagoing ships!
Tyre and its houses
lie in ruins.
2Mourn in silence,
you shop owners of Sidon,
you people on the coast.
Your sailors crossed oceans,
making your city rich.
3Your merchants sailed the seas,
making you wealthy by trading
with nation after nation.
They brought back grain
that grew along the Nile.
4Sidon, you are a mighty fortress
built along the sea.
But you will be disgraced
like a married woman
who never had children.
5When Egypt hears about Tyre,
it will tremble.
6All of you along the coast
had better cry and sail
far across the ocean.
7Can this be the happy city
that has stood for centuries?
Its people have spread
to distant lands;
8its merchants were kings
honored all over the world.
Who planned to destroy Tyre?
9The Lord All-Powerful planned it
to bring shame and disgrace
to those who are honored
by everyone on earth.
10People of Tyre,
your harbor is destroyed!
You will have to become farmers
just like the Egyptians.
Tyre Will Be Forgotten
11The Lord's hand has reached
across the sea,
upsetting the nations.
He has given a command
to destroy fortresses
in the land of Canaan.
12The Lord has said
to the people of Sidon,
“Your celebrating is over—
you are crushed.
Even if you escape to Cyprus,
you won't find peace.”
13Look what the Assyrians have done to Babylonia! They have attacked, destroying every palace in the land. Now wild animals live among the ruins. 14Not a fortress will be left standing, so tell all the seagoing ships to mourn.
15The city of Tyre will be forgotten for 70 years, which is the lifetime of a king. Then Tyre will be like that evil woman in the song:
16You're gone and forgotten,
you evil woman!
So strut through the town,
singing and playing
your favorite tune
to be remembered again.
17At the end of those 70 years, the Lord will let Tyre get back into business. The city will be like a woman who sells her body to everyone of every nation on earth, 18but none of what is earned will be kept in the city. That money will belong to the Lord, and it will be used to buy more than enough food and good clothes for those who worship the Lord.
translation_text:
Nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Fonehyea anwo la
1 Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Taya anwo la ɛne:
O Sepeen meli nu amra, bɛzu bɛye awolɛ, ɔluakɛ Taya ɛbɔ, sua ɛnle zolɛ na yeayɛ ahonle mɔɔ meli gyinla ɛkɛ a ɔyɛ boɛ a. Nrɛlaleɛ ne vi Saepolɔso a rale a. Luk 10.13-14 2Bɛzie bɛ nwo diinyi, Saedɛn gualilɛma mɔɔ gua ɛnweanloa la, bɛ soanvolɛma ne pɛle nyevile ne 3na bɛdwule tɛtɛlɛ nu lɔ. Bɛvale bɛ ezukoa ne bɛdɔle abɛlɛ wɔ Yigyibiti mɔɔ wɔ Azule Naele ne anloa la, na bɛ nee maanle maanle lile gua.
4O Saedɛn, wɔbɔ anyiemgba! Ɔluakɛ nyevile tandane ne ɛye wɔ. Ɔse, “Me ko ɛtɛkanle me yɛɛ metɛwole ɛlɛ. Metɛtetele ngakula mrenya anzɛɛ ngakula mraalɛ ɛlɛ.”
5Saa edwɛkɛ ne dwu Yigyibiti a, ɛzulolɛ kpole baha bɛ wɔ mɔɔ ɛzi Taya la ati.
6O Fonehyeama mɔɔ de ɛnweanloa, bɛzu bɛye awolɛ! Bɛnriandi bɛhɔ Sepeen! 7Asoo bɛ anyelielɛ suakpole ne mɔɔ bɛkyekyele mɔmoane ne la, yemɔ ɛne? Asoo bɛ suakpole ne mɔɔ zolɛ menli kɔ moa moa kɔbɔ nzeseɛ kyekye maanle la, yemɔ ɛne? 8Nwane yɛɛ ɛhyehyɛ ɛhye ɛtia Taya a, arelemgbunli mgbole sua zo? Anrɛɛ ye gualilɛma le arelemgbunli; yɛɛ azɛlɛ ye azo amra amuala bu ye gualilɛma. 9Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛhyehyɛ a, kɛ ɔfa yeazɛkye adubɛnwoma anyunlunyia, na yeagua bɛdabɛ mɔɔ ewiade amra di bɛ eni la anyunlu aze.
10O Sepeenema, bɛde bɛkponde bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo amuala kɛ Azule Naele bu aze la, na kɛkala awie bieko ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ kola si bɛ aze a. 11Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdende ɔ sa nyevile ne azo, yekpusu maanle maanle ne mɔ, na yeze kɛ bɛzɛkye Keena nee ye aranemgbole ne mɔ. 12Ɔse, “Bɛmɛ Saedɛnema, bɛ anyelielɛ ɛwie. Bɛdwazo, bɛnriandi bɛhɔ Saepolɔso; ɛkɛ ne bɔbɔ, bɛ nzo nu ɛnrɛdwo bɛ.”
13(Bɛnlea Babeloniama! Bɛmɛ ɔ, na tɛ Aseleama ɔ. Babeloniama a ɛmaa ɛbɔ nu nanemgbole ɛrazɛkye Taya a. Bɛbɛnrale bɛyiale ye, bɛbubule ye azua ne mɔ na bɛbɔle sua ne tɔɔ bɛyɛle ye suadu.)
14O Sepeen meli nu amra, bɛzu bɛye awolɛ, ɔluakɛ bɛbubu bɛ aranemgbole ne mɔ bɛgua.
15Mekɛ ne anu menli arɛle bavi Taya ɛvolɛ abulasuu, ɔle belemgbunli ko ngoane mekɛ. Ɛvolɛ abulasuu ne dwu a, mɔɔ bazi Taya anwo zo la le kɛ edwɛne ne mɔɔ tuutuunli ne dole la. 16Ɔse,
“Fa wɔ getaa kpole ne,
duolua suakpole ne azo, O tuutuunli
mɔɔ bɛ rɛle ɛvi wɔ a!
To edwɛne fɛlɛko,
to edwɛne dɔɔnwo,
amaa bɛava bɛahakye wɔ.”
17Saa ɛvolɛ abulasuu ne dwu a, Ɛdɛnkɛma bahɔkpɔla Taya, na Taya bazia ahɔ ye tuutuu gualilɛ gyima ne azo, na ɔ nee maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la ali gua. 18Ye gualilɛ ninyɛne nee mɔɔ ɔkɛnyia bɛ wɔ ɛkpa ɛbɔlɛ nu la, bɛbadu bɛamaa Ɛdɛnkɛma. Bɛnrɛva bɛnrɛzie yɛɛ bɛnrɛva bɛnrɛvea. Ye gualilɛ ninyɛne bamaa yeanyia aleɛ dɔɔnwo nee ndanlɛ ngɛnlɛma yeamaa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛsonle Ɛdɛnkɛma la.

english_text:
The Earth Will Be Punished
1The Lord is going to twist the earth out of shape and turn it into a desert. Everyone will be scattered, 2including ordinary people and priests, slaves and slave owners, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, the rich and the poor. 3The earth will be stripped bare and left that way. This is what the Lord has promised.
4The earth wilts away;
its mighty leaders melt
to nothing.
5The earth is polluted
because its people
disobeyed the laws of God,
breaking their agreement
that was to last forever.
6The earth is under a curse;
its people are dying out
because of their sins.
7Grapevines have dried up:
wine is almost gone—
mournful sounds are heard
instead of joyful shouts.
8No one plays tambourines
or stringed instruments;
all noisy celebrating
has come to an end.
9They no longer sing
as they drink their wine,
and it tastes sour.
10Towns are crushed and in chaos;
houses are locked tight.
11Happy times have disappeared
from the earth,
and people shout in the streets,
“We're out of wine!”
12Cities are destroyed;
their gates are torn down.
13Nations will be stripped bare,
like olive trees or vineyards
after the harvest season.
Praise the God of Justice
14People in the west shout;
they joyfully praise
the majesty of the Lord.
15And so, everyone in the east
and those on the islands
should praise the Lord,
the God of Israel.
16From all over the world
songs of praise are heard
for the God of justice.
But I feel awful,
terribly miserable.
Can anyone be trusted?
So many are treacherous!
There's No Escape
17Terror, traps, and pits
are waiting for everyone.
18If you are terrified and run,
you will fall into a pit;
if you crawl out of the pit,
you will get caught in a trap.
The sky has split apart
like a window thrown open.
The foundations of the earth
have been shaken;
19the earth is shattered,
ripped to pieces.
20It staggers and shakes
like a drunkard
or a hut in a windstorm.
It is burdened down with sin;
the earth will fall,
never again to get up.
21On that day the Lord
will punish the powers
in the heavens
and the kings of the earth.
22He will put them in a pit
and keep them prisoner.
Then later on,
he will punish them.
23Both the moon and sun will
be embarrassed and ashamed.
The Lord All-Powerful will rule
on Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
where he will show its rulers
his wonderful glory.
translation_text:
Nyamenle badea ewiade amra
1Bɛnlea, Ɛdɛnkɛma bazɛkye ewiade amuala yeayɛ ye mgbane yeado ye ɛkɛ. Ɔbadu azɛlɛ ne anye yeafonyia na yeakponde menli mɔɔ de zo la amuala. 2Mɔɔ ɔbava yeayɛ menli ne la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔbava yeayɛ sɛlɛvolɛma ne mɔ a, yɛɛ mɔɔ ɔbava yeayɛ kanranli la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔbava yeayɛ ɔ menle a. Mɔɔ ɔbava yeayɛ sonvolɛ raalɛ la, zɔhane ala a ɔbava yeayɛ ɔ menle raalɛ a. Mɔɔ ɔbava yeayɛ mɔɔ tɔ la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔbava yeayɛ mɔɔ tɔne la a; mɔɔ ɔbava yeayɛ mɔɔ bɔ bosea la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔbava yeayɛ mɔɔ biza bosea la a; yɛɛ mɔɔ ɔbava yeayɛ mɔɔ fa ninyɛne fili la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔbava yeayɛ mɔɔ filivili ninyɛne la a. 3Azɛlɛ ye amuala badɔ mgbane na zolɛ ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti azɛkye, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ ɛha a.
4Azɛlɛ ye ɛwe, ɛhete, ewiade amuala ɛtuto, ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti ɛnwoso, anwuma nee aze amuala ɛdo toboloo. 5Menli mɔɔ wɔ ewiade la ɛzɛkye azɛlɛ ye, ɔluakɛ bɛbulu Nyamenle mɛla ne mɔ azo, bɛzɛkye ye ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ na bɛtulu ye damɛnlangoate ngyekyeleɛ ne. 6Ɛhye ati munzule ɛha azɛlɛ ye yɛɛ zolɛ menli ɛlɛnwu amaneɛ wɔ bɛ ɛtane ne ati. Yemɔti azɛlɛ ye azo amra ɛlɛyela, menli ekyi bie a ɛha a. 7Nwanye nwo ɛhyia, ɔluakɛ vanye mbaka ne mɔ ɛdwɔlɔdwɔlɔ; menli mɔɔ anrɛɛ anye die bɛ nwo la adwenle ɛzɛkye. 8Awie ɛnde getaa mgbole ne mɔ ane, sɔnwosɔnwo nee ahenle ne mɔ ane ɛgua, yɛɛ anyelielɛ alɛra ne ɛzi aze. 9Bɛndɛnla nza bo bɛndo edwɛne bieko yɛɛ nza ɛsesebɛ ɛyɛ ɛnwonle ɛmaa menli mɔɔ no la. 10Suakpole ne azo begyebegye ne akee ɛbo zo, awie biala ɛdo ɔ nwo anlenkɛ nu, amaa awie gyɛne ambanwolo ɛkɛ. 11Awie biala ɛlɛsu kɛ nza ɛwie, anyelielɛ bo ɛdu, yɛɛ fɛlɛkolilɛ ɛnle ewiade ne anu bieko. 12Suakpole ne azo ɛyɛ kɛnlanana, nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ ɛgolo ɛgua. 13Zɛhae yɛɛ maanle maanle ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti anu bayɛ a. Maanle maanle ne mɔ amuala anu bayɛ hilihelee kɛ ɔlivi baka mɔɔ bɛwie zolɛ ma kpolo, anzɛɛ vanye baka mɔɔ bɛwie zolɛ ma tete la.
14Bɛmaa bɛ ne zo bɛto anyelielɛ edwɛne, yɛɛ adɔleɛ amra fa fɛlɛkolilɛ teɛdea nu wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma kpoleyɛlɛ nwo. 15Yemɔti bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ aduduleɛ la, bɛwula Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛde ɛnweanloa la ɛye Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne ayɛlɛ. 16Wɔ ewiade muleɛ kɔsɔɔti azo yɛte kɛ bɛlɛto ayɛlɛyelɛ nee anyunlunyia edwɛne bɛamaa Tenlenenli Ko ne.
Na mame, mese, “Nyane ngome ɛwie me kyekye, nyane ngome ɛwie me kyekye. Abule ɛbu me! Ngunzima tɛyɛ bɛ ngunzi ninyɛne ne mɔ, yɛɛ akee bɛ ngunziyɛlɛ ne ɛyɛ kpole kpalɛ.” 17O ewiade amra, ɛzulolɛ, ɛhane, yɛɛ ewule kuma ɛva bɛ aze. 18Mɔɔ kɛde ɛzulolɛ nganeɛ na ɔkɛnriandi la bahɔdɔ ewule kuma nu, yɛɛ mɔɔ kɛbɔ mɔdenle kɛvo file zo kɛvi ewule kuma nu la badɔ ɛhane nu. Ɔluakɛ bɛbukebuke anwuma nvɛnzɛlɛ ne mɔ, na azɛlɛ ye adiabo ne mɔ ɛlɛkpusu. 19Azɛlɛ ye ɛkpuke kpole bie, nuhua ɛkpakye nwiɔ. Azɛlɛ ye ɛkpusu kpole kpalɛ. 20Azɛlɛ ye ɛyɛ konikoni kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛbo nza la, na yehyea kɛ kpɔda. Ye ɛtane ɛbo ɔ nwo zo, na ɔbagolo yeagua mɔɔ ɔnrɛdwazo bieko ɛlɛ a.
21Mekɛ zɔhane Ɛdɛnkɛma badea anwuma tumivolɛma wɔ anwuma lɔ na yeadea azɛlɛ ye azo arelemgbunli wɔ aze ɛke. 22Bɛbaboɔboa bɛ muala bɛ nloa kɛ pilizama mɔɔ gua kuma nu la; bɛbagua bɛ efiade na mekɛ dɔɔnwo gua nu a bɛadea bɛ. 23Akee siane ne balu kisii na sɛnzɛne ne ɛnrɛda bieko, ɔluakɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bali belemgbunli wɔ Zayɔn Boka nee Gyɛlusalɛm na yeahile ye anyunlunyia ne wɔ ye mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu.

english_text:
A Prayer of Thanks to God
1You, Lord, are my God!
I will praise you
for doing the wonderful things
you had planned and promised
since ancient times.
2You have destroyed the fortress
of our enemies,
leaving their city in ruins.
Nothing in that foreign city
will ever be rebuilt.
3Now strong and cruel nations
will fear and honor you.
4You have been a place of safety
for the poor and needy
in times of trouble.
Brutal enemies pounded us
like a heavy rain
or the heat of the sun at noon,
but you were our shelter.
5Those wild foreigners struck
like scorching desert heat.
But you were like a cloud,
protecting us from the sun.
You kept our enemies from singing
songs of victory.
The Lord Has Saved Us
6On this mountain
the Lord All-Powerful
will prepare for all nations
a feast of the finest foods.
Choice wines and the best meats
will be served.
7Here the Lord will strip away
the burial clothes
that cover the nations.
8 The Lord All-Powerful
will destroy the power of death
and wipe away all tears.
No longer will his people
be insulted everywhere.
The Lord has spoken!
9At that time, people will say,
“The Lord has saved us!
Let's celebrate.
We waited and hoped—
now our God is here.”
10 The powerful arm of the Lord
will protect this mountain.
The Moabites will be put down
and trampled on like straw
in a pit of manure.
11They will struggle to get out,
but God will humiliate them
no matter how hard they try.
12The walls of their fortresses
will be knocked down
and scattered in the dirt.
translation_text:
Ayɛlɛyelɛ edwɛne
1O Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɛle me Nyamenle;
mebali wɔ eni kpole, mebaye wɔ duma ayɛlɛ,
ɔluakɛ wɔyɛ nwanwane ninyɛne,
tete yɛɛ ɛhyehyɛle bɛ a, yɛɛ nɔhalɛ nu wɔyɛ.
2Wɔyɛ suakpole ne ewula edukue,
wɔyɛ suakpole ne mɔɔ bɛhye nwolɛ la suadu;
nyɛvolɛ ne mɔ suakunlu ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛsisile la ɛnle ɛkɛ bieko,
awie ɛnrɛkyekye ye bieko ɛlɛ.
3Yemɔti maanle maanle mɔɔ anwo yɛ se la baye wɔ ayɛlɛ;
bɛbazulo wɔ wɔ maanle maanle mɔɔ ati yɛ se la azuamgbole zo.
4Ɔluakɛ wɔyɛ ɛvealeka kpundii wɔmaa ehyianvolɛma,
ɛvealeka kpundii wɔmaa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhyia la
wɔ bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ mekɛ nu;
wɔyɛ enyinlike wɔwowa bɛ wɔ ahumu nee ewia samɛnlankɛ nu;
ɔluakɛ atisesebɛma ɛtetalɛ ne le kɛ ahumu mɔɔ ɛlɛtia bane la;
5ɔle kɛ anwoma wuluwulu mɔɔ ɛlɛbɔ ɛsɛlɛ zo la.
Ɛmaa nyɛvolɛ ne mɔ alɛrayɛlɛ gua;
kɛ amungu si fa alubo wa ewia samɛnlankɛ nye la,
zɔhane ala yɛɛ wɔmaa atisesebɛma ɛgyakyi edwɛndolɛ a.
Nyamenle to ɛkponle
6Zayɔn Boka ye azo yɛɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bava nane mɔɔ ɛlɔ nee nwanye mɔɔ ɛbe kpalɛ la ado ɛkponle amaa maanle maanle ne mɔ a. 7Ɔbazɛkye debie biala mɔɔ bɛva bɛyɛ aguzo bɛheda maanle maanle ne mɔ azo la wɔ boka ɛhye azo. 8 Ɔbame ewule bɔkɔɔ, na Awulae Nyamenle ne bakyikyi awie biala anye anwo monle, na yeakpa bɛ nwo nyiane kɔsɔɔti yeavi azɛlɛ ye azo. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɔdaye a ɔse a.
9Mekɛ ne anu bɛbaha kɛ, “Bɛnlea, yɛ Nyamenle ne ɛne, yɛhendɛ ye, amaa yealie yɛ ngoane. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛne, yɛhendɛ ye; bɛmaa yɛ nye ɛlie na yɛli fɛlɛko wɔ ye ngoanelielɛ ne ati.”
Nyamenle badea Mowabe
10 Ɛdɛnkɛma tumi ne baheda Boka Zayɔn azo, na bɛbatietia Mowabe anwo zo kɛ bɛtietia ndɔ wulera zo wɔ ewula kuma nu la. 11Ɔbatoto ɔ sa kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛlɛweɛ azule la. Noko Ɛdɛnkɛma babɛlɛ ye mgbanyizonle ne nee ye azuleweɛlɛ kɛnlɛma ne aze. 12Ɔbabubu ye bane ndendenle ne mɔ mɔɔ yelie yebɔ ɔ nwo bane la yeagua aze fɛɛnye.

english_text:
A Song of Victory
1The time is coming when the people of Judah will sing this song:
“Our city is protected.
The Lord is our fortress,
and he gives us victory.
2Open the city gates
for a law-abiding nation
that is faithful to God.
3The Lord gives perfect peace
to those whose faith is firm.
4So always trust the Lord
because he is forever
our mighty rock.
5God has put down our enemies
in their mountain city
and rubbed it in the dirt.
6Now the poor and abused
trample all over that city.”
The Lord Can Be Trusted
7Our Lord, you always do right,
and you make the path smooth
for those who obey you.
8You are the one we trust
to bring about justice;
above all else we want
your name to be honored.
9Throughout the night,
my heart searches for you,
because your decisions
show everyone on this earth
how to live right.
10Even when the wicked
are treated with mercy
in this land of justice,
they do wrong and are blind
to your glory, our Lord.
11 Your hand is raised and ready
to punish them,
but they don't see it.
Put them to shame!
Show how much you care for us
and throw them into the fire
intended for your enemies.
12You will give us peace, Lord,
because everything we have done
was by your power.
13Others have ruled over us
besides you, our Lord God,
but we obey only you.
14Those enemies are now dead
and can never live again.
You have punished them—
they are destroyed,
completely forgotten.
15Our nation has grown
because of you, our Lord.
We have more land than before,
and you are honored.
The Lord Gives Life to the Dead
16When you punished our people,
they turned and prayed
to you, our Lord.
17Because of what you did to us,
we suffered like a woman
about to give birth.
18But instead of having a child,
our terrible pain
produced only wind.
We have won no victories,
and we have no descendants
to take over the earth.
19Your people will rise to life!
Tell them to leave their graves
and celebrate with shouts.
You refresh the earth
like morning dew;
you give life to the dead.
20Go inside and lock the doors,
my people.
Hide there for a little while,
until the Lord
is no longer angry.
The Earth and the Sea Will Be Punished
21The Lord will come out
to punish everyone on earth
for their sins.
And when he does,
those who did violent crimes
will be known and punished.
translation_text:
Nyamenle bamaa ye menli ne ali konim
1Mekɛ ne anu bɛbado edwɛne ɛhye wɔ Dwuda azɛlɛ zo,
Yɛlɛ suakpole bie mɔɔ yɛ se,
ɔmaa ye ngoanelielɛ ne zo
kɛ bane mgbole ndendenle.
2Bɛbukebuke nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ,
amaa maanle tenlene ne mɔɔ di nɔhalɛ la awolo nu.
3Sonla mɔɔ ye adwenle gyi ɛ nwo zo la,
ɛmaa ye anzonudwolɛ mɔɔ di munli,
ɔboalekɛ ɔ rɛle wɔ wɔ nu.
4Fa ɛ rɛle wula Ɛdɛnkɛma anu dahuu,
ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ne
le damɛnlangoate bodane.
5Ɔluakɛ yeha bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛmemaa bɛ nwo zo la aze;
yezɛkye bɛ suakpole kɛnlɛma ne,
yebubu bɛ bane ne mɔ yegua aze fɛɛnye.
6Ehyianvolɛma tietia zolɛ,
menli mɔɔ ɛhyia la tietia zolɛ.
7Tenlenenli adenle la aze fɛɛnye;
ɛyɛ tenlenenli adenle ne tonlotonlo.
8Wɔ wɔ ndɛnebualɛ adenle nu
yɛɛ yɛlɛkendɛ wɔ a, O Ɛdɛnkɛma;
mɔɔ yɛkpondɛ la a le
wɔ duma ne ɛhakyelɛ.
9Nɔɔzo biala me ɛkɛla anwo dɔ wɔ,
me sunsum mɔɔ wɔ me nu la kpondɛ wɔ.
Ɔluakɛ saa wɔ ndeanlɛ ba ewiade a,
ewiade amra sukoa pɛlepɛlelilɛ.
10Saa ɛnwu amumuyɛnli anwunvɔne a,
ɔnzukoa pɛlepɛlelilɛ;
ɔyɛ amumuyɛ wɔ pɛlepɛlema maanle nu,
ɔnnwu kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma si de bedevinli la.
11 O Ɛdɛnkɛma, wɔkpogya ɛ sa zo,
noko bɛnnwu ye.
Maa bɛnwu kɛ ɛsi ɛkulo wɔ menli ne la,
na bɛ nyunlu ɛgua aze.
Maa wɔ senle ne ɛyela wɔ kpɔvolɛma ɛhu bɛ.
12O Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɛbamaa yɛ nzo nu adwo yɛ,
wɔyɛ yɛ gyima ne kɔsɔɔti wɔmaa yɛ.
13O Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle,
menlenlɛ bie mɔ ɛzie yɛ ɛlɛ,
noko wɔmɔ ala yɛɛ yɛdie wɔ yɛto nu a.
14Menlenlɛ zɔhane mɔ ɛwu, bɛnrɛdɛnla ngoane nu bieko;
bɛle kɛ ɛlawolɛ, bɛnrɛdwazo ɛlɛ,
zɔhane ati wɔzɛkye bɛ
na wɔmaa menli arɛle ɛvi bɛ bɔkɔɔ.
15Wɔmaa yɛ maanle ye ɛyɛ kpole, O Ɛdɛnkɛma,
wɔmaa yɛ maanle ye ɛyɛ kpole;
anyunlunyia ɛha wɔ;
wɔmaa yɛ azɛlɛ ye ɛdɛlɛ.
16O Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛkpondɛle wɔ wɔ bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ nu,
bɛvale bɛ nzɛlɛlɛ bɛdole ɛ nyunlu
wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛtea bɛ la.
17O Ɛdɛnkɛma, wɔmɔ ɛ ti,
yɛyɛle kɛ raalɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛnrenzɛ,
mɔɔ ye awolɛ mekɛ ɛdwu,
na ɔ ko ɛha ye, na ɔlɛte nyane la.
18Ɛnee yɛ ko ɛha yɛ na yɛlɛnwu nyane kpalɛ,
na yera kɛ, kɛ ɔsi ɔde la, yɛwo anwoma.
Yɛtɛyɛle ngoanelielɛ nwo gyima yɛtɛmanle azɛlɛ ye,
yemɔti ɛtane ewiade amra ɛtɛtule ɛtɛguale.
19 Mɔwuamra bara ngoane nu, bɛbava bɛ nwonane ne bɛadwazo.
O bɛmɛ mɔwuamra, bɛdunwue na bɛva anyelielɛ bɛdo edwɛne!
Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛbɔlɛ mɔɔ tɔ bɛ nwo zo la le wienyi,
na ɔbada mɔwuamra anwo zo.
Ndeanlɛ nee abozozielɛ
20Me menli, bɛrɛla, bɛwolo bɛ azua ne mɔ anu na bɛtoto bɛ nwo nlenkɛ nu. Bɛvea bɛ nwo ekyii kɔkpula kɛ ɛya ne kɛdwo la. 21Ɔluakɛ bɛnlea, Ɛdɛnkɛma vi ɛleka mɔɔ ɔwɔ la ɔlɛba yearadea azɛlɛ ye azo amra wɔ bɛ ɛtane ne ati. Azɛlɛ ye baye mogya mɔɔ bɛha bɛgua ɔ nwo zo la amaa, yɛɛ ɔnrɛheda bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhu bɛ la anwo zo bieko.

english_text:
1 On that day, Leviathan,
the sea monster,
will squirm and try to escape,
but the Lord will kill him
with a cruel, sharp sword.
Protection and Forgiveness
The Lord said:
2At that time you must sing
about a fruitful vineyard.
3I, the Lord, will protect it
and always keep it watered.
I will guard it day and night
to keep it from harm.
4I am no longer angry.
But if it produces thorns,
I will go to war against it
and burn it to the ground.
5Yet if the vineyard depends
on me for protection,
it will become my friend
and be at peace with me.
6Someday Israel will take root
like a vine.
It will blossom and bear fruit
that covers the earth.
7I, the Lord, didn't punish and kill
the people of Israel
as fiercely as I punished
and killed their enemies.
8I carefully measured out
Israel's punishment
and sent the scorching heat
to chase them far away.
9There's only one way
that Israel's sin and guilt
can be completely forgiven:
They must crush the stones
of every pagan altar
and place of worship.
The Lord Will Bring His People Together
10Fortress cities are left
like a desert
where no one lives.
Cattle walk through the ruins,
stripping the trees bare.
11When broken branches
fall to the ground,
women pick them up
to feed the fire.
But these people are so stupid
that the God who created them
will show them no mercy.
12The time is coming when the Lord will shake the land between the Euphrates River and the border of Egypt, and one by one he will bring all of his people together. 13A loud trumpet will be heard. Then the people of Israel who were dragged away to Assyria and Egypt will return to worship the Lord on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
translation_text:
1 Mekɛ ne anu Ɛdɛnkɛma bava ye dadeɛ ɛsesebɛ, kpole, nlane ne adua ɛwɔlɛ ne mɔɔ ɛlɛnriandi la, Lɛveatan mɔɔ wuluwulu kakyihakyi ɔ nwo la kakɛ. Ɔbahu Lɛveatan na yeahu nane anwo ɛzulolɛ ne mɔɔ le kɛ ɛlɛnrɛne mɔɔ la nyevile ne anu la.
2Mekɛ ne anu Ɛdɛnkɛma baha kɛ, “Bɛdo vanye egyinli kɛnlɛma ne anwo edwɛne! 3Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a menea zolɛ a. Mekɛ biala megugua nzule zolɛ. Amaa awie anzɛkye ye la, mesinza ye nɔɔzo nee ewiazo. 4Menva ɛya. Anrɛɛ ɛnee mbowule nee mbowunzaka wɔ nu mɔɔ me nee bɛ ko a, anrɛɛ menwɔteta bɛ na menwɔbɔ bɛ nu menwɔyela bɛ. 5Anzɛɛ saa bɛto bɛ nloa aze kɛ bɛkpondɛ kɛ mefa bɛ mewula me kunlu a, ɛnee bɛ nee me ɛdɛnla anzonudwolɛ nu. Ɛhɛe, bɛ nee me ɛdɛnla anzonudwolɛ nu.”
6Mekɛ mɔɔ bara la anu Gyekɔbo abo zo amra abo bazɔ ndinli, Yizilayɛma bakpazi na bɛ nwo azo dɔɔnwo, na bɛ bo zo amra ava ewiade amuala.
7Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛtɛteanle Yizilayɛma, kɛmɔ ɔdeanle bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkpɔ bɛ la, yɛɛ ɔtɛkunle bɛ, kɛmɔ bɛhunle bɛ kpɔvolɛma ne la. 8Ngyikyi ngyikyi, ɛ nee bɛ lile na ɛmanle bɛhyele bɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu, ɛvale wɔ aduduleɛ anwoma anloa ɛsesebɛ ne ɛvoanle bɛ. 9Yemɔti debie mɔɔ Yizilayɛma yɛ a bɛkɛva bɛ ɛtane bɛkɛhyɛ bɛ la a le ɛhye: saa bɛbubu awozonle azukponle ne mɔ, bɛti bɛ motomoto kɛ munlutu, bɛbubu bɛ bozonle raalɛ Ahyela ne sɛkɛlɛneɛ anzɛɛ ɛyɛlɛ ɛkpunlɛ azukponle ne mɔ mɔɔ biala ɛnle ɛkɛ ne bieko la a, bɛkɛva bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti bɛkɛhyɛ bɛ.
10Suakpole ne mɔɔ bɛbɔ nwolɛ bane la ɛyɛ suadu; yeyɛ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkpo ye na bɛ rɛle ɛvi ye kɛ ɛsɛlɛ la. Ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ nlankɛ mralɛ didi na bɛda bɛdie bɛ ɛnwomenle a. 11Saa suakpole ne azo mbaka ne bie mɔ ngane wu a bɛbubu bɛ bɛgua; mraalɛ basesa na bɛfa bɛyɛ ɛyɛne. Ɔluakɛ menli ɛhye mɔ ɛnlɛ ndelebɛbo; yemɔti mɔɔ bɔle bɛ la ɛnrɛze bɛ anwunvɔne, yɛɛ ɔnrɛvavi bɛ.
12Mekɛ ne anu Ɛdɛnkɛma bawozo ma ne, ɔvi Azule Yufileti ne anloa yeahɔgua ye wɔ Azudenle ne mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti ɛweɛne zo la anloa. O Yizilayɛma, bɛbadindi bɛ ngoko ngoko na bɛaboa bɛ nloa.
13Mekɛ ne anu bɛbabɔ aweɛne tendenle kpole ne anu, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛminlinle bɛhɔle Aselea azɛlɛ zo, nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvoanle bɛ bɛmanle bɛhɔle Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la bara na bɛarazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Boka Nwuanzanwuanza ne azo wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_text:
Samaria Will Be Punished
1The city of Samaria
above a fertile valley
is in for trouble!
Its leaders are drunkards,
who stuff themselves
with food and wine.
But they will be like flowers
that dry up and wilt.
2Only the Lord is strong
and powerful!
His mighty hand
will strike them down
with the force of a hailstorm
or a mighty whirlwind
or an overwhelming flood.
3Every drunkard in Ephraim
takes pride in Samaria,
but it will be crushed.
4Samaria above a fertile valley
will quickly lose its glory.
It will be gobbled up
like the first ripe fig
at harvest season.
5When this time comes,
the Lord All-Powerful
will be a glorious crown
for his people who survive.
6He will see that justice rules
and that his people are able
to defend their cities.
Corrupt Leaders Will Be Punished
7Priests and prophets stumble
because they are drunk.
Their minds are too confused
to receive God's messages
or give honest decisions.
8Their tables are covered,
completely covered,
with their stinking vomit.
9You drunken leaders
are like babies!
How can you possibly understand
or teach the Lord's message?
10You don't even listen—
all you hear is senseless sound
after senseless sound.
11 So, the Lord will speak
to his people
in strange sounds
and foreign languages.
12He promised you
perfect peace and rest,
but you refused to listen.
13Now his message to you
will be senseless sound
after senseless sound.
Then you will fall backwards,
injured and trapped.
False Security Is Fatal
14You rulers of Jerusalem
do nothing but sneer;
now you must listen
to what the Lord says.
15 Do you think you have
an agreement with death
and the world of the dead?
Why do you trust in your lies
to keep you safe from danger
and the mighty flood?
16 And so the Lord says,
“I'm laying a firm foundation
for the city of Zion.
It's a valuable cornerstone
proven to be trustworthy;
no one who trusts it
will ever be disappointed.
17Justice and fairness
will be the measuring lines
that help me build.”
Hailstones and floods
will destroy and wash away
your shelter of lies.
18Your agreement with death
and the world of the dead
will be broken.
Then angry, roaring waves
will sweep over you.
19Morning, noon, and night
an overwhelming flood
will wash you away.
The terrible things that happen
will teach you this lesson:
20Your bed is too short,
your blanket too skimpy.
21 The Lord will fiercely attack
as he did at Mount Perazim
and in Gibeon Valley.
But this time the Lord
will do something surprising,
not what you expect.
22So you had better stop sneering
or you will be in worse shape
than ever before.
I heard the Lord All-Powerful
threaten the whole country
with destruction.
All Wisdom Comes from the Lord
23Pay close attention
to what I am saying.
24Farmers don't just plow
and break up the ground.
25When a field is ready,
they scatter the seeds
of dill and cumin;
they plant the seeds
of wheat and barley
in the proper places
and sow other grains
around the edges.
26They learn this from their God.
27After dill and cumin
have been harvested,
the stalks are pounded,
not run over with a wagon.
28Wheat and barley are pounded,
but not beaten to pulp;
they are run over with a wagon,
but not ground to dust.
29This wonderful knowledge comes
from the Lord All-Powerful,
who has such great wisdom.
translation_text:
Sɔlɔ Belemgbunli Maanle ne kɔkɔbɔlɛ
1Munzule ɛha Yizilayɛ suakpole kɛnlɛma ne mɔɔ nzabovoma ɛyi ye tɛkɛɛ la! Munzule ɛha ye, ye anyunlunyia ɛlɛkpa kɛ ndotolo abɔtile mɔɔ bobɔ menli mɔɔ nza ɛgya bɛ la ati wɔ anwonyia bɔnza nu la. 2Bɛnlea, Awulae lɛ awie mɔɔ le katakyie na ɔ nwo yɛ se la; ahenle zɔhane le kɛ ahumu mɔɔ ɛlɛtu atete ezuawolɛ agua la, ahumu kpole mɔɔ sɛkye ninyɛne, ahumu anloa ɛsesebɛ mɔɔ maa azule yi bu aze la; ɔbava ɛzɛkyelɛ kpole yeara, yeadudu debie biala yeagua. 3Bɛbali Yizilayɛ suakpole kɛnlɛma ne mɔɔ nzabovoma ɛyi ye tɛkɛɛ la anwo zo konim; 4na ye anyunlunyia ne mɔɔ ɛlɛkpa kɛ ndotolo abɔtile mɔɔ bobɔ menli mɔɔ wɔ anwonyia bɔnza nu la ati la bayɛ kɛ wawaa nloa feege nzoleɛ mɔɔ kɛlumua kɛbolo la. Saa sonla nwu ye a, ɔte ɔdi ndɛndɛ.
5Mekɛ ne anu Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bayɛ kɛ anyunlunyia abɔtile nee zolɛ kpɔba kɛnlɛma yeamaa ye menli ne mɔɔ hale la. 6Ɔbamaa mɔɔ bua ndɛne la pɛlepɛlelilɛ ahonle yeamaa yeabua ndɛne fɔɔnwo, na yeamaa mɔɔ ka konlema gua wɔ anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa la anwosesebɛ.
Ayezaya nee Dwuda nzabovo Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma
7Menli ɛhye mɔ noko no nwanye bo yɛɛ bɛno nza ɛsesebɛ bɛtinda. Sɛlɛvolɛma nee Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma no nza ɛsesebɛ tinda. Nwanye maa bɛ adwenle ka bɔ nu yɛɛ nza ɛsesebɛ maa bɛtinda. Bɛfo wɔ bɛ ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ nu, yɛɛ bɛmbua ndɛne fɔɔnwo. 8Bɛ ɛkponle mɔɔ bɛde nwolɛ la azo le ɛveleɛ ngome, ɛleka ekyi bɔbɔ ɛnle zo mɔɔ le bɔkɔbɔkɔ a.
9Bɛbiza kɛ, “Nwane a ɔkɛhilehile ye ɔkɛbuke ye adwenle nu a, yɛɛ nwane a ɔkɛhile ye nrɛlaleɛ ne anu ɔkɛhile ye a? Asoo bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛva ɛnlankɛ nyɛfonzule bɛli bɛ adane, anzɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɔ zo mɔɔ bɛpɛ bɛ nyɛfonlɛ la? 10Ɔluakɛ ɔkilehile yɛ edwɛkɛ agbɔkɛ, ɛhonlone ɛhonlone, ɛke ekyi, nehane ekyi.”
