The king and his servants listened to what was written on the scroll, but they were not the least bit afraid, and they did not tear their clothes in sorrow.
26The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us.
Jeremiah's Second Scroll
27I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me 28to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one. 29Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim:
Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals. 30So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah. 31You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
32After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_text:
Bɛlɛke kenga nwoma ne wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu
1 Mɔɔ Dwuda Belemgbunli Dwosaya ara nrenya Gyɛhɔyakem lile ɛvolɛ nna wɔ ebia zo la Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle nrɛlaleɛ ɛhye hilele Gyɛlɛmaya. 2Ɔse, “Fa nwoma na bɔ ye Belemgbunli Dwosaya mekɛ zo kɛlɛ edwɛkɛ mɔɔ meha mehile wɔ, mɔɔ tia Yizilayɛ, Dwuda, yɛɛ maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti toonwo mɔɔ badwu ɛnɛ la. 3Ɔkɛyɛ kɛ saa Dwudama te kɛ mebazi meazɛkye bɛ la a, bɛ nuhua ko biala bagyakyi ɛtaneyɛlɛ, na meava bɛ amumuyɛ nee bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ meahyɛ bɛ.”
4Yemɔti Gyɛlɛmaya vɛlɛle Nilaya ara nrenya Bɛlɛke, na ɔhanle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha ɛhile ye la kɔsɔɔti ɔmanle Bɛlɛke hɛlɛle bɛ nwoma zo. 5Akee Gyɛlɛmaya zele Bɛlɛke kɛ, “Bɛdua me kɛ memmakɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu bieko. 6Yemɔti ɔwɔ kɛ ɛkɔ ɛkɛ ne kenle mɔɔ bɛlɛkye ɛhɔne la, ɛkɔkenga Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ meha memaa wɔhɛlɛ la ɛkile menli ne kɔsɔɔti. Eza kenga kile Dwudama mɔɔ vi bɛ azua zo kɛra la amuala. 7Ɔkɛyɛ kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma badie bɛ modolɛ nzɛlɛlɛ ne, na biala ahwe ɔ nwo avi ɛtane nwo, ɔluakɛ ɛya mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva wɔ menli ɛhye mɔ anwo la le kpole.” 8Na Nilaya ara nrenya Bɛlɛke yɛle debie biala, kɛmɔ Nyamenle Kpɔmanvolɛ Gyɛlɛmaya zele ye kɛ ɔgenga Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ wɔ nwoma ne azo, wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu la.
9Dwuda Belemgbunli Dwosaya ara nrenya Gyɛhɔyakem lile ɛvolɛ nnu wɔ ebia zo la, ye siane ngɔnla ne anu, Gyɛlusalɛmma kɔsɔɔti nee menli mɔɔ vi Dwuda azua azua zo la rale Gyɛlusalɛm rahyele ɛhɔne zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma anwunvɔnezelɛ. 10Na Bɛlɛke gengale Gyɛlɛmaya edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ wɔ nwoma ne anu la hilele menli mɔɔ rayiale Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu la amuala. Ɔgengale ye wɔ kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ Hyeefan ara nrenya Gɛmalaya ekpumgbunli ɛdeɛ ne anu a ɔhilele bɛ a. Sua ekpumgbunli zɔhane wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne Anlenkɛ Kpole Fofolɛ ne anwuma.
Bɛgenga nwoma ne bɛhile mgbanyima ne mɔ
11Mɔɔ bɛgengale Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne amuala na Hyeefan anlɔnra Maekaya, Gɛmalaya ara nrenya ne dele la, 12ɔhɔle belemgbunli suakunlu ɛkɛ, kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ ne ekpumgbunli ɛdeɛ ne anu. Ɛnee suakunlu mgbanyima ne mɔ ɛyia ɛkɛ ne. Bɛmɛ a le Yilaehyama, kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ ne; Dɛlaya, ɔ ze a le Hyɛmaya; Ɛleneetan, ɔ ze a le Akebɔ; Gɛmalaya, ɔ ze a le Hyeefan; Zɛdikaya, ɔ ze a le Hananaya; yɛɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala. 13Maekaya hanle edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔdele wɔ nwoma ne mɔɔ Bɛlɛke gengale hilele menli ne la anu la amuala hilele mgbanyima ne mɔ. 14Mgbanyima ne mɔ zoanle Gyɛhudae kɛ ɔhɔze Bɛlɛke kɛ ɔva nwoma ne mɔɔ ɔgengale nuhua edwɛkɛ ɔhilele menli ne la ɔrɛla. Gyɛhudae le Kuhyae angabɛnzo. Kuhyae wole Hyɛlimaya, Hyɛlimaya wole Nɛtanaya mɔɔ wole Gyɛhudae la. Na Bɛlɛke vale nwoma ne rale. 15Mgbanyima ne mɔ hanle hilele ye kɛ, “Tɛnla aze na kenga kile yɛ.” Yemɔti Bɛlɛke dɛnlanle aze na ɔgengale ɔhilele bɛ. 16Mɔɔ mgbanyima ne mɔ dele nwoma ne anu edwɛkɛ ne amuala la, ɛzulolɛ hanle bɛ na bɛnleɛnleanle bɛ nyunlu. Na bɛhanle bɛhilele Bɛlɛke kɛ, “Ɔwɔ kɛ edwɛkɛ ɛhye kɔsɔɔti kɔda belemgbunli anyunlu.” 17Bɛbizale Bɛlɛke kɛ, “Ɛnee kɛ ɛzile ɛ sa hanle edwɛkɛ ɛhye mɔ amuala ɛhɛlɛle ɛ? Ɛnee Gyɛlɛmaya a hanle ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti hilele wɔ manle ɛhɛlɛle a?”
18Bɛlɛke buale bɛ kɛ, “Edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ ko biala mɔɔ mehɛlɛ wɔ nwoma ye anu la vi Gyɛlɛmaya anloa anu.”
19Akee bɛzele ye kɛ, “Bɛlɛke, ɛ nee Gyɛlɛmaya bɛhɔkpondɛ ɛleka bɛvea. Bɛmmamaa awie nwu bɛ nzi adenle.”
Belemgbunli ne yela nwoma ne
20Suakunlu mgbanyima ne mɔ gyakyile nwoma ne wɔ kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ Yilaehyama ekpumgbunli ne anu, na bɛwolole suakunlu ɛkɛ ne na bɛvale edwɛkɛ ne kɔsɔɔti bɛhɔbɔle belemgbunli ne amaneɛ. 21Belemgbunli ne zoanle Gyɛhudae manle ɔhɔvale nwoma ne wɔ kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ Yilaehyama ekpumgbunli ne anu rale, na ɔgengale ɔhilele belemgbunli nee mgbanyima mɔɔ ɛyia ɔ nwo ɛkɛ la amuala. 22Siane ngɔnla ne anu a ɛhye zile a, yɛɛ mekɛ zɔhane le fɔsɛlɛ mekɛ, yemɔti ɛnee belemgbunli ne ɛradɛnla senle nwo wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne, ye ɛyɛlɛ mekɛ sua ne anu. 23Saa Gyɛhudae kenga edwɛkɛ ne ɛhonlone nsa mɔɔ kɔ nna la a, ɛnee belemgbunli ne ɛva dadeɛ ekyi bie ɛpɛ nwoma ne sinli ne mɔɔ edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ bɛgenga la wɔ nu la ɛvuandi ɛdo senle ne mɔɔ ɛlɛsɔ la anu. Ɔyɛle ye zɔhane toonwo ɔyelale nwoma ne amuala. 24Noko belemgbunli ne o, ye sonvolɛma ne mɔ o, biala anli nyane wɔ edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ bɛdele la anwo, yɛɛ bɛanli nyane nretee bɔbɔ. 25Ɛleneetan, Dɛlaya, yɛɛ Gɛmalaya bɔbɔ bodole belemgbunli ne kɛ ɔmmayela nwoma ne, noko belemgbunli ne andie bɛ edwɛkɛ. 26Akee belemgbunli ne manle ɔ ra nrenya Gyɛlamile, Azeleɛle ara nrenya Sɛlaya, yɛɛ Abedili ara nrenya Hyɛlimaya adenle kɛ bɛhye kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ Bɛlɛke nee Nyamenle Kpɔmanvolɛ Gyɛlɛmaya, na Ɛdɛnkɛma vale bɛ veale.
Gyɛlɛmaya kɛlɛ nwoma fofolɛ zo
27Mɔɔ Dwuda Belemgbunli Gyɛhɔyakem yelale nwoma ne mɔɔ Gyɛlɛmaya hanle edwɛkɛ ne manle Bɛlɛke hɛlɛle zolɛ la, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya. 28Ɔse, “Gyɛlɛmaya, fa nwoma fofolɛ kɛlɛ edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ ɛhɛlɛle ye alumua nwoma ɛdeɛ ne mɔɔ belemgbunli ne yelale ye la azo la kɔsɔɔti bieko wɔ zolɛ. 29Ka kile Dwuda Belemgbunli Gyɛhɔyakem kɛ: Ɛdɛnkɛma se, ‘Wɔyela nwoma ɛhye na wɔbiza Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔhɛlɛ ye nuhua kɛ, kɛ ɔkɛyɛ biala la, Babelonia belemgbunli ne barazɛkye azɛlɛ ye na yeahu menli nee nyɛmoa mɔɔ wɔ zolɛ la amuala ɛ?” 30Yemɔti, medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mese: Ɛdawɔ Dwuda Belemgbunli Gyɛhɔyakem, ɛ bo zo sonla ɛnrɛdɛnla Devidi belemgbunli ebia ne azo ɛlɛ, yɛɛ bɛbavuandi wɔ funli ne bɛado ɛleka mɔɔ ewia bɔ ye alehyenlɛ nu na ɛbɔlɛ tɔ gua zolɛ aledwolɛ nu la. 31Mebadea wɔ, ɛ bo zo amra, nee wɔ sonvolɛma amuala wɔ bɛ amumuyɛ ti. Mebamaa munzule mɔɔ meha kɛ mebamaa yeado bɛdabɛ Gyɛlusalɛmma, yɛɛ Dwudama kɔsɔɔti la ado bɛ. Ɔboalekɛ mendendɛle mengilele bɛ, na bɛandie.’ ”
32Akee Gyɛlɛmaya vale nwoma bieko manle Nilaya ara nrenya Bɛlɛke, kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ ne, na ɔhanle alumua edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ wɔ nwoma ne mɔɔ Dwuda Belemgbunli Gyɛhɔyakem yelale ye la anu la amuala ɔhilele ye. Bɛlɛke hɛlɛle ɔ muala; eza ɔhɛlɛle edwɛkɛ ngakyile dɔɔnwo mɔɔ le kɛ ɛhendeɛ ne la ɔbokale nwo.

english_text:
King Zedekiah Asks Jeremiah To Pray
1 King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead. 2But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
3-5Later, the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem, but they left after learning that the Egyptian army was headed in this direction.
One day, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to talk with me. At that time, I was free to go wherever I wanted, because I had not yet been put in prison. Jehucal and Zephaniah said, “Jeremiah, please pray to the Lord our God for us.”
6-7Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message:
Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt. 8Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire. 9Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before. 10Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire.
Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
11The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us. 12So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land. 13I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
14“I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials. 15-16They were angry and ordered the soldiers to beat me. Then I was taken to the house that belonged to Jonathan, one of the king's officials. It had been turned into a prison, and I was kept in a basement room.
After I had spent a long time there, 17King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?”
“Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
18Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation? 19Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem? 20Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
21King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_text:
Zɛdikaya sɛlɛ Gyɛlɛmaya debie
1 Babelonia Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza ziele Gyɛhɔyakem ara nrenya Kɔnaya ahane na ɔvale Dwosaya ara nrenya Zɛdikaya ɔziele belemgbunli wɔ Dwuda. 2Na Zɛdikaya, ye sonvolɛma, yɛɛ Dwudama amuala, biala andie Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ ɔluale Nyamenle Kpɔmanvolɛ Gyɛlɛmaya anwo zo ɔhanle ɔhilele bɛ la.
3Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya zoanle Hyɛlimaya ara nrenya Gyɛhukale nee Meeyasaya ara Sɛlɛvolɛ Zɛfanaya wɔ Gyɛlɛmaya anwo ɛkɛ manle bɛhɔzele ye kɛ, “Sɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne maa yɛ.” 4Mekɛ zɔhane ɛnee Gyɛlɛmaya nee menli ne kɔ ba, ɛnee bɛtɛtole ye efiade. 5Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ɛlɔnema ne yele bɛ nwo Yigyibiti, na mɔɔ Babelonia ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ɛnee ɛbɛnra ɛyia Gyɛlusalɛm kɛ bɛko bɛava la dele bɛ nganeɛ la, bɛhwenle bɛ nzi.
6Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, 7“Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, mese: Ka kile Dwuda Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya mɔɔ manle ɛyɛle nzɛlɛlɛ ne la kɛ, Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ɛlɔnema ne mɔɔ rale baboa bɛ la ɛlɛsia ahɔ Yigyibiti, bɛ maanle nu. 8Babelonia ɛlɔnema ne bazia ara arateta suakpole ye bieko aho ava, na bɛado senle zolɛ bɛayela ye. 9Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mese: Bɛmmabɛlɛbɛla bɛ nwo bɛdwenle kɛ Babeloniama ne mɔ ɛnrɛra; bɛbara. 10Saa kanza bɔbɔ bɛfo Babeloniama anwo zo, bɛbɔ bɛ bo zo, na ɔka menli mɔɔ ɛbodɛboda gua azua nu la a, bɛbadwazo bɛava senle bɛarayela suakpole ye. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”
Bɛhye Gyɛlɛmaya bɛdo efiade
11Mɔɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ɛlɔnema ne ɛlɛba la, Babelonia ɛlɔnema ne vi Gyɛlusalɛm yele bɛ nwo. 12Yemɔti Gyɛlɛmaya dule ɔ bo wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm kɛ ɔkɔ Bɛngyaman maanzinli nu yeahɔlie ye afoa nu agyadeɛ ɛdeɛ ne. 13Mɔɔ ɔdwule Bɛngyaman Anlenkɛ Kpole ne anloa la, Hananaya anlɔnra nrenya Ayelaegya mɔɔ ɔ ze a le Hyɛlimaya la zɔle ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ɛlɛnriandi wɔava ɛ nwo wɔahɔmaa Babeloniama!”
14Gyɛlɛmaya buale ye kɛ, “Ɔnle nɔhalɛ, menriandi menva me nwo mengɔmaa Babeloniama.” Noko Ayelaegya andie mɔɔ ɔhanle ɔhilele ye la. Ɔzɔle ye nu ɔ nee ye hɔle mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu. 15Mgbanyima ne mɔ vale Gyɛlɛmaya anwo ɛya kpole na bɛmanle bɛbole ye na bɛdole ye efiade wɔ kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ Dwɔnatan sua nu mɔɔ bɛva ɛkɛ ne bɛyɛ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛgua menli efiade la. 16Bɛvale Gyɛlɛmaya bɛhɔdole azɛlɛ bo efiade ɛdeɛ ne anu toonwo ɔhyɛle kpalɛ.
17Nzinlii Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya zoanle manle bɛhɔvale ye. Ɔvale ye ɔhɔle ahane na ɔbizale ye saa Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha edwɛkɛ bie a.
Gyɛlɛmaya buale kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, yeha edwɛkɛ. Ɛdɛnkɛma se bɛbaye wɔ bɛamaa Babelonia belemgbunli ne.” 18Eza Gyɛlɛmaya bizale Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya kɛ, “Duzu ɛtane a meyɛ wɔ, wɔ mgbanyima anzɛɛ menli ɛhye mɔ, mɔɔ yemɔti bɛhye me bɛdo efiade a? 19Na wɔ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma mɔɔ hanle Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ hilele wɔ la wɔ nienwu? Bɛmɛ a bɛzele wɔ kɛ Babelonia belemgbunli ne ɛnrɛva konle ɛnrɛradoa wɔ anzɛɛ azɛlɛ ɛhye azo amra a. 20O Nana, mebodo wɔ, tie me. Tie me modolɛ, mmamaa bɛkɔto me efiade bieko wɔ kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ Dwɔnatan sua nu. Bɛto me efiade bieko a mebawu.”
21Yemɔti Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya manle bɛyele Gyɛlɛmaya bɛhɔdole suakunlu sinzavolɛma ne anwo ɛkɛ ne. Kenle ko biala bɛdie kpanwo kunguma ko wɔ menli mɔɔ to kpanwo la ɛkɛ ne bɛbɛlɛ ye. Bɛlɛ ye zɔhane toonwo ɔhɔkpulale mekɛ mɔɔ suakpole ne azo kpanwo kɔsɔɔti wiele la. Yemɔti Gyɛlɛmaya hale suakunlu sinzavolɛma ne mɔ anwo ɛkɛ.

english_text:
Jeremiah Is Held Prisoner in a Dry Well
1One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah 2-3that the Lord had said, “If you stay here in Jerusalem, you will die in battle or from disease or hunger, and the Babylonian army will capture the city anyway. But if you surrender to the Babylonians, they will let you live.”
4So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
5Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
6Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
7-8Ebedmelech from Ethiopia was an official at the palace, and he heard what they had done to me. So he went to speak with King Zedekiah, who was holding court at Benjamin Gate. 9Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
10Zedekiah answered, “Take 30 of my soldiers and pull Jeremiah out before he dies.”
11Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well. 12Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did, 13the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards.
King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
14King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
15“Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
16He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
17Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down. 18But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
19Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
20I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you. 21But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey, 22then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you:
Friends you trusted led you astray.
Now you're trapped in mud,
and those friends you trusted
have all turned away.
23The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
24Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life. 25And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them. 26So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
27The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
28 I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_text:
Gyɛlɛmaya la bula resee bie anu
1Matan ara Hyɛfataya, Pahyɛ ara Gɛdalaya, Hyɛlimaya ara Dwukale, yɛɛ Malekaya ara Pahyɛ dele edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Gyɛlɛmaya ɛnee ɛlɛka ahile menli ne kɔsɔɔti la. 2Gyɛlɛmaya hanle kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma se: Awie biala mɔɔ kɛdɛnla suakpole ye azo la bawu konle nu, ɛhɔne nu anzɛɛ ewulenzane nu; na ɛdawɔ mɔɔ ɛkɛva ɛ nwo ɛkɛhɔmaa Babeloniama la ɛkɛnyia ngoane. Ɔbanyia ngoane kɛ bɛhye ye nuokɛ wɔ konle nu, na bɛnrɛhu ye.” 3Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebaye suakpole ye meamaa Babelonia belemgbunli ne ɛlɔnema ne meamaa bɛali bɛ nwo zo konim.”
4Na mgbanyima ne mɔ hanle hilele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Maa bɛhu nrenya ɛhye, ɔluakɛ ɔlɛka edwɛkɛ yeamaa ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ɛha suakpole ye azo nee menli ne amuala asa anu atuto. Nrenya ɛhye ɛnzuzu maanlema boɛ, ɔsuzu bɛ nee ɛtane.”
5Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya hanle kɛ, “Bɛnlea, ɔwɔ bɛ sa nu, bɛyɛ ye kɛmɔ bɛdabɛ bɛkulo la, ɔluakɛ belemgbunli ne ɛnrɛyɛ ɛhwee ɛnrɛtia bɛ.” 6Yemɔti bɛhyele Gyɛlɛmaya, bɛsosɔle ye nyɛma na bɛdwulale ye Belemgbunli ara nrenya Malekaya bula ne mɔɔ wɔ suakunlu alie ne anwo la anu. Ɛnee nzule ɛnle bula ne anu, ndɛtɛlɛ a wɔ nu a, na Gyɛlɛmaya minle ndɛtɛlɛ ne anu.
7Sudanenli Yibɛdemɛlɛke mɔɔ le sonvolɛ kpanyinli wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la dele kɛ bɛdwula Gyɛlɛmaya bula ne anu. Mekɛ zɔhane ɛnee belemgbunli ne de Bɛngyaman Anlenkɛ Kpole ne anloa. 8Yibɛdemɛlɛke vi suakunlu ɛkɛ ne hɔhanle hilele belemgbunli ne kɛ, 9“Nana, nea ɛtane kokye mɔɔ menli ɛhye mɔ ɛyɛ la. Bɛdwula Nyamenle Kpɔmanvolɛ Gyɛlɛmaya bula ne anu. Ɛhɔne bamaa yeawu ɛkɛ, ɔluakɛ aleɛ fee ɛnle suakpole ye azo.” 10Belemgbunli ne hanle hilele Sudanenli Yibɛdemɛlɛke kɛ, “Fa menli nsa ɛke boka ɛ nwo na bɛhɔye Nyamenle Kpɔmanvolɛ Gyɛlɛmaya bɛvi bula ne anu kolaa na yeawu.” 11Yemɔti Yibɛdemɛlɛke vale menli nsa bokale ɔ nwo na ɔ nee bɛ rale suakunlu ɛkɛ. Bɛhɔvale adɛladeɛ ndeteleka wɔ ɛlamoa bie mɔɔ wɔ sua ne mɔɔ bɛsie ninyɛne nu la anu, bɛvale nyɛma bɛzɔle bɛ na bɛdwulale bɛ bula ne anu bɛmanle Gyɛlɛmaya. 12Akee sonvolɛ Yibɛdemɛlɛke hanle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, “Fa adɛladeɛ ndeteleka ne mɔ wulowula ɛ nvonlɔma anu, na fa nyɛma ne sosɔ wɔ awane bo.” Na Gyɛlɛmaya yɛle ye zɔhane. 13Akee bɛhwenle Gyɛlɛmaya wɔ bula ne anu bɛvindele. Na ɔdɛnlanle sinzavolɛma ne sua nu ɛkɛ.
Zɛdikaya biza Gyɛlɛmaya adwenle
14Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya manle bɛvɛlɛle Gyɛlɛmaya, na ɔyiale ye wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anlenkɛ kpole ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa la anloa. Ɔhanle ɔhilele Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, “Mebiza wɔ edwɛkɛ, na mmafa ɛhwee ɛfea me.”
15Gyɛlɛmaya buale kɛ, “Saa meka nɔhalɛ ne mekile wɔ a, ɛnrɛmaa bɛnrɛhu me ɔ? Yɛɛ saa metu wɔ folɛ bɔbɔ a, ɛnrɛva.”
16Na Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya hanle ndane fealera nu hilele Gyɛlɛmaya. Ɔse, “Meka tease Ɛdɛnkɛma ne mɔɔ bɔle yɛ la kɛ, menrɛmaa bɛnrɛhu wɔ anzɛɛ menrɛye wɔ menrɛmaa menli ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ kpondɛ wɔ ahu wɔ la.”
17Na Gyɛlɛmaya hanle hilele Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma, Tumivolɛ Nyamenle, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se: Saa ɛto ɛ nloa aze ɛmaa Babelonia belemgbunli ne mgbanyima ne mɔ a, bɛnrɛhu wɔ, yɛɛ bɛnrɛdo senle suakpole ye azo bɛnrɛyela ye. Ɛdawɔ nee wɔ sua nu amra banyia ngoane. 18Na saa wɔando ɛ nloa aze wɔammaa Babelonia belemgbunli ne mgbanyima ne mɔ a, bɛbava suakpole ɛhye bɛamaa Babeloniama; bɛbado senle zolɛ bɛayela ye, na wɔmɔ, ɛnrɛvi ɛsalɛ.”
19Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya hanle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, “Mesulo Dwuuma mɔɔ ɛva bɛ nwo ɛmaa, na bɛpɛ bɛhɔli Babeloniama ɛkɛ la, kɛ bɛkɛye me bɛkɛmaa bɛ na bɛkɛbɔ me aholoba.”
20Gyɛlɛmaya hanle kɛ, “Bɛnrɛye wɔ bɛnrɛmaa bɛ. Wɔmɔ tie edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛzoa me, mɔɔ melɛka meahile wɔ la na ɔbayɛ boɛ yeamaa wɔ, bɛnrɛhu wɔ. 21Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ ɛhile me, yehile debie mɔɔ saa wɔando ɛ nloa aze wɔammaa bɛ a ɔbara ɛ nwo zo la. 22Ɛnee ɔle kɛ bɛlɛfa mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛha Dwuda belemgbunli ne suakunlu ɛkɛ la amuala bɛahɔ Babelonia mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu, na bɛlɛka kɛ,
‘Agɔnwolɛma mɔɔ ɛdie bɛ ɛdi la ɛbɛlɛbɛla wɔ,
ɛdo wɔ senle nu;
kɛkala mɔɔ wɔmi ndɛtɛlɛ nu la,
akee bɛhakyi bɛ nzi bɛzi wɔ.’
23“Bɛbava ɛ ye mɔ nee ɛ mra mrenya kɔsɔɔti bɛamaa Babeloniama, na ɛdawɔ mumua ne, ɛnrɛva ɛ nwo dwɔɔ. Babelonia belemgbunli ne bahye wɔ nuokɛ, na yeado senle suakpole ye azo, yeayela ye.”
24Zɛdikaya buale Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, “Mmabɔ edwɛkɛ ɛhye azo ɛkile awie biala na bɛnrɛhu wɔ. 25Saa mgbanyima ne mɔ te kɛ me nee wɔ ɛrali adwelie na bɛbaka kɛ, ‘Ka edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛhanle ɛhilele belemgbunli ne nee mɔɔ belemgbunli hanle hilele wɔ la kile yɛ, mmafa debie biala ɛfea yɛ na yɛnrɛhu wɔ’ a, 26ka kile bɛ kɛ, ‘Membodole belemgbunli ne kɛ ɔmmamaa bɛkɔto me efiade bieko wɔ Dwɔnatan sua nu lɔ na anrɛɛ menwɔwu ɛkɛ ne.’ ” 27Mgbanyima ne mɔ rabizale Gyɛlɛmaya, na ɔhanle edwɛkɛ ne, kɛmɔ belemgbunli hanle hilele ye ala la. Yemɔti bɛgyakyile ye bɛhɔle, ɔboalekɛ awie ande adwelielilɛ ne ɔ nzo nu. 28 Na Gyɛlɛmaya dɛnlanle suakunlu sinzavolɛma ne ɛkɛ toonwo ɔhɔdwule mekɛ mɔɔ bɛhonle bɛvale Gyɛlusalɛm la.

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Captured by the Babylonians
(Jeremiah 52.4-16; 2 Kings 25.1-12)
1-3In the tenth month of the ninth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian army began their attack on Jerusalem. They kept the city surrounded for a year and a half. Then, on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year that Zedekiah was king, they broke through the city walls.
After Jerusalem was captured, Nebuchadnezzar's highest officials, including Nebo Sarsechim and Nergal Sharezer from Simmagir, took their places at Middle Gate to show they were in control of the city.
4When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley. 5But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty, 6and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families. 7Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
8Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls. 9Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar. 10Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
11Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan: 12“Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
13Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar 14sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah.
The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
15While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say 16to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen. 17-18But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Gyɛlusalɛm ɛbɔlɛ
1Mekɛ mɔɔ Dwuda Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya lile ɛvolɛ ngɔnla wɔ ebia ne azo la, ye siane bulu ne anu, Babelonia Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza nee ye ɛlɔnema amuala ratetale Gyɛlusalɛm na bɛbɛnrale bɛyiale suakpole ne. 2Zɛdikaya nyianle ɛvolɛ bulu nee ko la, ye siane nna ne na ye kenle ngɔnla ne azo, bɛhanle suakpole ne bane ne mɔ bɛguale aze.
3Mɔɔ bɛvale Gyɛlusalɛm la, Babelonia belemgbunli ne mgbanyima ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti radɛnlanle Avinli Anlenkɛ Kpole ne anloa. Bɛmɛ a le Nɛgale Salizɛ, Samegaa Nibo, Relabesa Saasɛkem, yɛɛ Nɛgale Salizɛ.
4Dwuda Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya nee ye ɛlɔnema ne nwunle bɛ la, bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛnriandile bɛguale ɛbɔ nu. Bɛdule bɛ bo nɔe ne bɛluale belemgbunli tola ne anu. Bɛzenle anlenkɛ kpole ne mɔɔ dua bane nwiɔ ne la anu, bɛluale bane ne avinli bɛvale bɛ ti bɛbɔle Dwɔdan Bɔnza ne anu lɔ. 5Na Babelonia ɛlɔnema ne voanle bɛ na bɛhɔhyele Zɛdikaya wɔ azɛlɛ sɛsɛ ne mɔɔ zua Gyɛleko la azo. Bɛvale ye bɛrɛlɛle Babelonia Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza wɔ suakpole Relebela mɔɔ wɔ Heemate azɛlɛ zo la azo. Nɛbukadenɛza buale Zɛdikaya ndɛne ɛkɛ ne. 6Ɔhunle Zɛdikaya amra mrenya ne mɔ wɔ ɔdaye Zɛdikaya ɔ nyunlu ɛkɛ ne; eza ɔhunle Dwuda menli titile ne mɔ amuala. 7Akee ɔdudule Zɛdikaya anye, ɔguale ye anga kɛ bɛva ye bɛhɔ Babelonia. 8Babeloniama ne yelale belemgbunli ne awuke ne, bɛyelale ezuavolɛ ne mɔ azua ne mɔ na bɛbubule Gyɛlusalɛm bane ne mɔ. 9Na Babelonia ɛlɔnema kpanyinli Nɛbuzaladan vale menli mɔɔ hale suakpole ne azo, nee menli mɔɔ ɛva bɛ nwo ɛmaa ye dɛba la hɔle nlɔnu wɔ Babelonia. 10Ɔgyakyile Dwudama mɔɔ le ehyianvolɛma kpalɛ kpalɛ la bie mɔ wɔ maanle ne anu na ɔmanle bɛ vanye egyinli nee azɛlɛ.
Bɛdwula Gyɛlɛmaya
11Na Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza zele sinzavolɛma Safohyenle Nɛbuzaladan kɛ, 12“Kpondɛ Gyɛlɛmaya abo zo, nea ye boɛ gyɛlɛɛnye, mmafa ɛ sa ɛka ye, na yɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɔkɛbiza wɔ la maa ye.” 13Yemɔti sinzavolɛma Safohyenle Nɛbuzaladan, Nɛbu Hyazeban, Nɛgale Salizɛ, yɛɛ Babelonia mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala 14zoanle manle bɛhɔvale Gyɛlɛmaya wɔ Nɛbuzaladan, sinzavolɛma sua nu ɛkɛ bɛhɔmanle bɛ. Bɛvale ye bɛwulale Hyeefan anlɔnra Gɛdalaya, Ahaekam ara nrenya ne asa anu kɛ ɔva ye ɔhɔ sua nu, na ɔnlea ye. Yemɔti ɔ nee menli ne mɔ dɛnlanle.
Yibɛdemɛlɛke anyelazo
15Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔla efiade wɔ suakunlu sinzavolɛma ne ɛkɛ la. Ɔse, 16“Kɔ, kɔha kile Yibɛdemɛlɛke mɔɔ vi Sudan la kɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se: Kɛmɔ menzele ala la, mebamaa suakpole ɛhye abɔ, menrɛmaa ɔnrɛyɛ boɛ; kenle zɔhane, debie biala bawie ɛ nyunlu. 17Na medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebalie wɔ, bɛnrɛye wɔ bɛnrɛmaa menli mɔɔ ɛsulo bɛ la, 18ɔluakɛ, nɔhalɛ, mebalie wɔ, bɛnrɛhu wɔ. Ɛbavi ɛsalɛ wɔ konle ne anu, ɔboalekɛ wɔva ɛ rɛle wɔwula me nu. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Is Set Free
1I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free. 2Nebuzaradan said:
Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land. 3But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
4Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish. 5King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose.
Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave. 6I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah.
The Harvest Is Brought In
7-8 Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, together with Johanan and Jonathan, the two sons of Kareah, had been officers in Judah's army. And so had Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah from Maacah. They and their troops had been stationed outside Jerusalem and had not been captured. They heard that Gedaliah had been chosen to rule Judah, and that the poorest men, women, and children had not been taken away to Babylonia. So they went to Mizpah and met with their new ruler.
9Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar. 10I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
11-12Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year.
Gedaliah Is Murdered
13One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah. 14They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!”
Gedaliah refused to believe them, 15so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
16Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_text:
Gyɛlɛmaya nee Gɛdalaya tɛnla
1Mɔɔ Safohyenle Nɛbuzaladan dwulale Gyɛlɛmaya wɔ Releema la, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele ye. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Gyɛlɛmaya boka Gyɛlusalɛmma nee Dwudama mɔɔ bɛgua bɛ anga bɛ nee bɛ ɛlɛkɔ nlɔnu wɔ Babelonia la anwo.
2Sinzavolɛma safohyenle ne vale Gyɛlɛmaya hɔle ahane na ɔhanle ɔhilele ye kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma, wɔ Nyamenle ne hanle kɛ ɔmaa munzule ɛhye ara azɛlɛ ye azo, 3amgba yemaa yeyɛ zɔhane na yeyɛ mɔɔ ɔzele la. Kɛmɔ bɛyɛle ɛtane bɛtiale Ɛdɛnkɛma na bɛandie ɔ ne la yɛɛ yemaa ɛhye ɛzi bɛ nwo zo a. 4Nea, melɛye anga ne mɔɔ gua ɛ sa la ɛnɛ kenle ye. Saa ɛnea na ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛ nee me kɛhɔ Babelonia a, ɛnee maa yɛhɔ na mebanlea wɔ gyɛlɛɛnye. Saa ɛnea noko na ɔnle kpalɛ kɛ ɛ nee me kɛhɔ Babelonia a, ɛnee mmaba. Nea, azɛlɛ ne amuala a la ɛkɛ ne tɛtɛtɛlɛlɛ la, tɛnla ɛleka biala mɔɔ ɛnea a ɔle kpalɛ na ɔfɛta kɛ ɛtɛnla la.”
5Nɛbuzaladan hanle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, “Saa ɛkulo kɛ ɛtɛnla ɛke a ɛnee sia na ɛ nee Hyeefan anlɔnra Gɛdalaya, Ahaekam ara nrenya ne ɛhɔdɛnla. Gɛdalaya a Babelonia belemgbunli ne ɛyɛ ye amɛnlado kɛ ɔnlea Dwuda azuamgbole ne mɔ azo a. Ɛ nee ye nee menli ne ɛhɔdɛnla, anzɛɛ ɛleka biala mɔɔ ɛkulo kɛ ɛkɔtɛnla la, kɔdɛnla.” Akee ɔmanle Gyɛlɛmaya aleɛ nee ahyɛlɛdeɛ na ɔmanle ɔhɔle.
6Yemɔti Gyɛlɛmaya hɔle Ahaekam ara nrenya Gɛdalaya anwo ɛkɛ wɔ Mezepa, na ɔ nee ye nee menli mɔɔ bɛgyakyi bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo la hɔdɛnlanle.
Dwuda Amɛnlado Gɛdalaya
(2 Arl 25.22-24)
7 Dwuda ɛlɔnema safohyenlema mɔɔ wɔ azua azua ne mɔ azo la nee menli ne dele kɛ Babelonia belemgbunli ne ɛva Ahaekam ara nrenya Gɛdalaya ɛyɛ amɛnlado wɔ maanle ne anu kɛ ɔnlea mrenya, mraalɛ nee ngakula, ehyianvolɛma kpalɛ kpalɛ mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu mɔɔ bɛanva bɛ bɛangɔ nlɔnu wɔ Babelonia la anwo zo. 8Yemɔti bɛ muala bɛrale Gɛdalaya ɛkɛ wɔ Mezepa. Safohyenlema ne mɔ ɛne: Nɛtanaya ara nrenya Yehyemeeyɛle, Kalia amra mrenya Dwoheenan nee Dwɔnatan, Tanehumɛte ara nrenya Sɛlaya, Yifae mɔɔ vi Nɛtɔfa la amra mrenya ne mɔ, yɛɛ Gyɛzanaya mɔɔ vi Meeyaka la. 9Hyeefan anlɔnra Gɛdalaya, Ahaekam ara nrenya ne hakyele bɛ nee bɛ menli ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛmmasulo kɛ bɛkɛzonle Babeloniama. Bɛdɛnla maanle ye anu, bɛzonle Babelonia belemgbunli ne na ɔkɛyɛ boɛ ɔkɛmaa bɛ. 10Na mame, mebadɛnla Mezepa na meagyinla bɛ ti wɔ yɛ nee Babeloniama mɔɔ kɛra yɛ ɛkɛ la avinli. Bɛdɛnla bɛ azua mɔɔ bɛwɔ zo la azo, bɛboɔboa nwanye, vanye ma, yɛɛ ɔlivi nwole nloa bɛzie ɛkɛ.” 11Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ Mowabe, Amɔn, Yidɔm, yɛɛ maanle gyɛne gyɛne nu la dele kɛ Babelonia belemgbunli ne ɛmaa Dwuuma bie mɔ ɛha Dwuda maanle ne anu na yeyɛ Gɛdalaya amɛnlado kɛ ɔnlea bɛ nwo zo. 12Yemɔti Dwuuma mɔɔ ɛnee bɛvoa bɛ bɛhɔgua maanle gyɛne gyɛne zo la amuala ziale rale Dwuda azɛlɛ zo, wɔ Gɛdalaya anwo ɛkɛ wɔ Mezepa. Bɛraboɔboale nwanye nee vanye ma dɔɔnwo anloa.
Bɛhu Gɛdalaya
(2 Arl 25.25-26)
13Akee Kalia ara nrenya Dwoheenan nee safohyenle mgbanyinli mɔɔ wɔ azua azua ne mɔ azo la 14rale Gɛdalaya anwo ɛkɛ wɔ Mezepa. Bɛbizale ye kɛ, “Asoo ɛze kɛ Amɔle Belemgbunli Beeyalese ɛzoa Nɛtanaya ara nrenya Yehyemeeyɛle kɛ ɔrahu wɔ?” Noko Gɛdalaya anlie bɛ edwɛkɛ ne anli. 15Akee Kalia ara nrenya Dwoheenan dule Gɛdalaya azukue wɔ Mezepa kɛ, “Maa me adenle maa mengɔngu Yehyemeeyɛle na awie ɛnrɛnwu ye. Duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ Yehyemeeyɛle ku wɔ, na Dwuuma mɔɔ ɛ nee bɛ de la kɔsɔɔti kɛbɔ asande, na bɛ bo zo kɛminli bɔkɔɔ ɛ?” 16Na Gɛdalaya buale Dwoheenan kɛ, “Mmakɔyɛ deɛ ɛhye, ɔluakɛ edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ ɛlɛka ye wɔ Yehyemeeyɛle anwo la ɛnle nɔhalɛ.”

english_text:
1 But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah. 2During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia. 3Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
4The next day, the murders had still not been discovered, 5when 80 men came down the road toward Mizpah from the towns of Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They were on their way to the temple to offer gifts of grain and incense to the Lord. They had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes, and cut themselves, because they were mourning.
6Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah. 7But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well. 8He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field. 9The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
10Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
11Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done. 12So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon. 13When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy 14and turned around and ran toward Johanan. 15But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon.
Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
16Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon 17-18toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar.
The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them
On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_text:
1 Ɛvolɛ ne ala anu, siane nsuu ne anu, Nɛtanaya ara nrenya Yehyemeeyɛle nee menli bulu bie rale Gɛdalaya anwo ɛkɛ wɔ Mezepa. Yehyemeeyɛle ɔ nlenya a le Yilaehyama mɔɔ vi belemgbunli ne abusua nu, na ɔle belemgbunli mgbanyima ne mɔ bie la. Ɔrale ye kɛ, mɔɔ bɛ muala bɛlɛdi debie la, 2Yehyemeeyɛle nee menli bulu ne dwazole Gɛdalaya anwo zo, bɛhwenle bɛ dadeɛ ne mɔ bɛhunle ye. Gɛdalaya a Babelonia belemgbunli ne ɛyɛ ye amɛnlado wɔ Dwuu maanle ne anu a. 3Eza Yehyemeeyɛle hunle Dwuuma mɔɔ nee Gɛdalaya de Mezepa la, nee Babelonia ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ɛnee wɔ ɛkɛ la amuala.
4Kɔdiawu edwɛkɛ ɛhye zile la, ye alehyenlɛ nu mɔɔ ɛnee awie ɛtɛtele kɛ bɛhu Gɛdalaya la, 5menli abulatwɛ vi Hyikɛm, Hyaelo, yɛɛ Samɛlea rale kɛ bɛlɛ ma azubɔdeɛ nee ɛyɛlɛ bɛba Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu. Ɛnee menli zɔhane mɔ ɛkpa bɛ kɛsa, ɛsuosua bɛ adɛladeɛ nu, na bɛbodɛboda bɛ nwo. 6Yehyemeeyɛle vale ɛzunlɛ vi Mezepa rayiale bɛ adenle. Ɔradole bɛ la ɔhanle ɔhilele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛrɛla bɛranlea Ahaekam ara nrenya Gɛdalaya.” 7Bɛrale suakpole ne azo la, Nɛtanaya ara nrenya ne nee menli bulu ne mɔɔ boka ɔ nwo la zɔle bɛ hunle bɛ na bɛvuandinle bɛ bɛguale bula nu.
8Na menli bulu mɔɔ boka abulatwɛ ne anwo la hanle hilele Yehyemeeyɛle kɛ, “Mmaku yɛ na yɛlɛ hwiiti, baale, ɔlivi nwole, yɛɛ wolɛ wɔ yɛ ɛya ne mɔ anu.” Yemɔti Yehyemeeyɛle angu bɛ amboka ɛhendeɛ ne mɔ anwo. 9Yehyemeeyɛle zoale menli mɔɔ ɔhunle bɛ la avunli ne mɔ amuala guale Belemgbunli Esa bula kpole ne mɔɔ ɔbɔle la anu ɔmanle ɔyile. Belemgbunli Esa bɔle bula ɛhye kɛ ɔfa yeabɔ ɔ nwo bane wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Beeyahya dwazole ɔ nwo zo kɛ ɔ nee ye ko la. 10Akee Yehyemeeyɛle hyele menli mɔɔ ɛnee ɛha Mezepa la amuala nee belemgbunli ne amra mraalɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ Babelonia sinzavolɛma Safohyenle Nɛbuzaladan vale bɛ wulale Ahaekam ara nrenya Gɛdalaya asa anu kɛ ɔzie bɛ la nuokɛ na ɔvale bɛ ɔzile nu kɛ ɔ nee bɛ kɔ Amɔn azɛlɛ zo.
11Kalia ara nrenya Dwoheenan nee ɛlɔnema mgbanyinli ne mɔ dele ɛtane mɔɔ Yehyemeeyɛle ɛli kɔsɔɔti la. 12Yemɔti bɛvale bɛ ɛlɔnema ne amuala bɛdoale ye kɛ bɛ nee ye kaho, na bɛhɔdole ye wɔ Gebɛyɔn azule kpole ne anloa. 13Mɔɔ menli mɔɔ nee Yehyemeeyɛle lua la nwunle Dwoheenan nee ɛlɔnema mgbanyinli ne mɔ kɛ bɛlɛba la, bɛlile fɛlɛko. 14Yemɔti menli mɔɔ Yehyemeeyɛle ɛhye bɛ nuokɛ ɔ nee bɛ ɛlɛkɔ Amɔn la amuala ziale bɛ nzi doale Dwoheenan. 15Na Yehyemeeyɛle wolole Dwoheenan asa abo na ɔ nee ye ɛlɔnema ne mɔ anu mɔtwɛ pɛle lile Amɔn azɛlɛ zo.
16Akee Dwoheenan nee ɛlɔnema mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala vale menli mɔɔ Yehyemeeyɛle hunle Gɛdalaya wɔ Mezepa la ɔhyele bɛ nuokɛ la vi Gebɛyɔn ziale. Bɛle sogyama, mraalɛ, ngakula yɛɛ sonvolɛma. 17Na bɛhɔle bɛhɔdɛnlanle Kyemeham mɔɔ zua Bɛtelɛhɛm la. Bɛnyianle adwenle kɛ Babeloniama ati bɛkɔ Yigyibiti, 18ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛzulo bɛ, ɔboalekɛ Yehyemeeyɛle ɛhu Gɛdalaya mɔɔ Babelonia belemgbunli yɛle ye amɛnlado kɛ ɔnlea maanle ne azo la.

english_text:
1Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me 2and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left. 3Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
4“All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
5They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says, 6even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
7Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for 8Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together 9and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said:
You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do. 10I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you. 11Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him, 12and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
13But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God. 14We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
15People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen. 16-17You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
18I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word.
Jeremiah Gives a Warning
19I told the people:
You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt. 20You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake, 21because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him. 22And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_text:
Menli ne se Gyɛlɛmaya ɛzɛlɛ ɛmaa bɛ
1Akee Dwuda ɛlɔnema mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala, Kalia ara nrenya Dwoheenan, Hɛhyaya ara nrenya Azalaya, yɛɛ menli ne amuala, mɔɔ lɛ bie nee mɔɔ ɛnlɛ bie la 2rahanle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, “Gyɛlɛmaya, yɛbodo wɔ, yɛ mɔɔ yɛlɛbiza la maa yɛ. Sɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne maa yɛdayɛ mɔɔ yɛha la, ɔluakɛ kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ ɛkola ɛnwu ye la, yɛdayɛ menli ɛwolaa ne, akee yɛwie, yɛha ekyi bie. 3Yemɔti sɛlɛ maa Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne ɛhile yɛ adenle mɔɔ yɛva zo, nee debie mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛyɛ la.”
4Na Gyɛlɛmaya buale bɛ kɛ, “Mede, bɛnlea, mebazɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne meamaa bɛ, kɛmɔ bɛbiza la, na edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ ɔkɛze kɛ menga mengile bɛ la, mebamaa bɛade; menrɛvea bɛ edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔkɛha la biala anu.”
5Na bɛhanle bɛhilele Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, “Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne dua ɛ nwo zo ka edwɛkɛ kile yɛ na yɛanva a, Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne ɛli nɔhalɛ daselɛ fɔɔnwo ɛtia yɛ. 6Saa ɔle kpalɛ o, ɔle ɛtane o, yɛbadie Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne mɔɔ yɛlɛsoa wɔ ɔ nwo ɛkɛ la ane, amaa saa yɛtie ɔ ne a yeayɛ boɛ yeamaa yɛ.”
Ɛdɛnkɛma bua Gyɛlɛmaya nzɛlɛlɛ ne anwo
7Ye kenle bulu ne azo Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya. 8Na ɔvɛlɛle Kalia ara nrenya Dwoheenan, ɛlɔnema mgbanyima mɔɔ boka ɔ nwo la amuala, yɛɛ menli mɔɔ lɛ bie nee mɔɔ ɛnlɛ bie, mɔɔ ɔ nee bɛ lua la amuala na ɔhanle ɔhilele bɛ. 9Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, mɔɔ bɛzoanle me kɛ menva bɛ modolɛ mengɔndo ɔ nyunlu la se la ɛne: 10Saa bɛkɛdɛnla azɛlɛ ɛhye azo a, anrɛɛ mebalua bɛ na menrɛdu bɛ; mebamaa bɛ bo adila, na menrɛzɛkye bɛ, ɔluakɛ menlu me nwo kɛ medea bɛ memaa munzule ɛdo bɛ a. 11Bɛmmasulo Babelonia belemgbunli ne mɔɔ bɛsulo ye la bieko. Bɛmmasulo ye, ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, me nee bɛ lua yɛɛ mebalie bɛ meavi ɔ sa nu. 12Mebaze bɛ anwunvɔne, amaa ɔdaye noko yeaze bɛ anwunvɔne na yeamaa bɛadɛnla bɛdabɛ bɛ azɛlɛ ye azo. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.
13“Na saa bɛka kɛ, ‘Yɛnrɛdɛnla azɛlɛ ɛhye azo,’ na bɛtu Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne anloa bɛto, bɛka kɛ, 14‘Kyɛkyɛ, yɛkɔ Yigyibiti; ɛkɛ ne, yɛnrɛnwu konle, yɛnrɛde aweɛne ndendenle ne, yɛnrɛhyia aleɛ nwo, na ɛkɛ ne ala a yɛkadɛnla’ a, 15ɛnee bɛmɛ Dwudama mɔɔ ɛha la, bɛdie mɔɔ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma melɛka la. Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, mese: Saa bɛtu bɛ gyakɛ bɛtia Yigyibiti kɛ bɛkadɛnla ɛkɛ ne a, 16konle ne mɔɔ bɛsulo ye la bado bɛ wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo; ɛhɔne ne mɔɔ bɛsulo ye la bazi bɛ nwo zo wɔ Yigyibiti, na ɛkɛ ne a bɛbawu a. 17Menli mɔɔ kɛye bɛ nyunlu kɛ bɛkɔ Yigyibiti bɛahɔdɛnla lɔ la kɔsɔɔti badɔ dadeɛ nloa anzɛɛ ɛhɔne nu anzɛɛ ewulenzane nu. Munzule mɔɔ mebamaa yeado bɛ la, bɛ nuhua ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛha.
18“Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, mese: Saa bɛkɔ Yigyibiti a mebakpokpo me ɛya ne meagua bɛ nwo zo kɛ mɔɔ memkpokpole menguale Gyɛlusalɛmma anwo zo la. Bɛbazɔho ewula wɔ menli nye zo, bɛ nwo baha ɛzulolɛ, yɛɛ bɛ duma bayɛ ɛfenle nee amowa ala menli nloa. Bɛnrɛnwu ɛke bieko.”
19Gyɛlɛmaya zele bɛ kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛze bɛdabɛ Dwudama mɔɔ bɛha la kɛ: ‘Bɛmmakɔ Yigyibiti.’ Bɛnwu ye wienyi kɛ mebɔ bɛ kɔkɔ wɔ ɛnɛ kenle ye. 20Bɛva bɛ ngoane bɛdo nzeleba na bɛminli, ɔluakɛ bɛzoanle me wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne ɛkɛ kɛ menzɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne memaa bɛ, na edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ ɔkɛze bɛ la bɛkɛli zolɛ. 21Na ɛnɛ, edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle zoanle me kɛ menga mengile bɛ la meha mehile bɛ, noko bɛtɛtiele ɔ ne. 22Ɔlua ɛhye ati bɛnwu ye kɛ bɛbawu dadeɛ nloa, ɛhɔne nu anzɛɛ ewulenzane nu wɔ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛkulo kɛ bɛkɔtɛnla zolɛ la azo.”

english_text:
The People Go to Egypt
1I told the people everything the Lord had told me. 2But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt. 3Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
4Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command. 5 So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah. 6Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
7The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes, 8when the Lord told me:
9Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
10Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury. 11He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners. 12-13I will let him set Egypt's temples on fire, and he will either burn or carry off their idols. He will destroy the sacred monuments at the temple of the sun-god. Then Nebuchadnezzar will pick the land clean, just like a shepherd picking the lice off his clothes. And he will return safely home.
translation_text:
Bɛva Gyɛlɛmaya bɛhɔ Yigyibiti
1Mɔɔ Gyɛlɛmaya wiele edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne vale zoanle ye kɛ ɔhɔha ɔhile menli ne kɔsɔɔti la amuala ka la, 2Hohyaya ara nrenya Azalaya, Kalia ara nrenya Dwoheenan yɛɛ mgbanyizonlema bie mɔɔ wɔ nu la amuala hanle hilele ye kɛ, “Gyɛlɛmaya, ɛlɛbɔ adalɛ. Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne anzoa wɔ kɛ ɛraze yɛ kɛ yɛmmakɔ Yigyibiti yɛkɔtɛnla ɛkɛ. 3Nilaya ara nrenya Bɛlɛke ala a ɛli ɛwula wɔ a, amaa wɔaye yɛ wɔamaa Babeloniama wɔamaa bɛahu yɛ anzɛɛ bɛavula yɛ bɛahɔ nlɔnu wɔ Babelonia.” 4Yemɔti Dwoheenan, ɛlɔnema mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala, yɛɛ menli ne kɔsɔɔti andie Ɛdɛnkɛma ane kɛ bɛkɛdɛnla Dwuda maanle nu. 5 Dwoheenan nee ɛlɔnema mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala vale Dwudama mɔɔ ɛha, na bɛvi maanle maanle mɔɔ bɛnriandile bɛhɔguale nu la anu bɛzia bɛra la amuala hɔle Yigyibiti. 6Menli ne mɔ ɛne: Mrenya, mraalɛ, ngakula, arelemgbunli amra mraalɛ, menli mɔɔ ɛlɔnema Kpanyinli Nɛbuzaladan vale bɛ gyakyile Ahaekam ara nrenya Gɛdalaya, Hyeefan anlɔnra ne kɛ ɔzie bɛ la, medame Gyɛlɛmaya, yɛɛ Nilaya ara nrenya Bɛlɛke. 7Bɛkpole kɛ bɛnrɛdie Ɛdɛnkɛma ane, na bɛradɛnlanle Yigyibiti wɔ suakpole Tapanehizi azo.
8Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Gyɛlɛmaya wɔ Tapanehizi kɛ, 9“Sesa awolɛ mgbole wulowula belekese bama ne mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli suakunlu ne mɔɔ wɔ Tapanehizi la anuhɔlɛ ne la anu wɔ Dwudama anye zo. 10Se bɛ kɛ, Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se: Bɛnlea, mebazoa meamaa bɛahɔvɛlɛ Babelonia belemgbunli, me sonvolɛ Nɛbukadenɛza bɛara. Ɔbava ye belemgbunli ebia ne yearazie awolɛ ɛhye mɔ azo na yeazi ye belemgbunli ndanlɛ sua zolɛ. 11Ɔbaradua Yigyibitima kakɛ. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛfɛta ewulenzane la, bɛbawu ewulenzane nu; bɛdabɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛkye bɛ nuokɛ la, bɛbahye bɛ nuokɛ, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛwu dadeɛ nloa la, bɛbawu dadeɛ nloa. 12Ɔbasesa Yigyibiti mmonle ne mɔ na yeatoto senle bɛ awozonle ɛzonlenlɛ azua ne mɔ anu, yeayela bɛ na yeava mmonle ne mɔ yeahɔ. Ɔbakpoa Yigyibiti evinli ne kɛ mboaneneavolɛ tudu ye tɛladeɛ nu ɛzozoa la, na ɔbazia yeahɔ anzonudwolɛ nu. 13Ɔbazɛkye awolɛ mpila ngakyedeɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Hɛleɔpɔlese mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la. Eza ɔbayela Yigyibiti awozonle ɛzonlenlɛ azua ne mɔ.”

english_text:
The Lord Will Destroy the People of Judah
1The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
2I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today, 3because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
4Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning, 5but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods. 6Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
7Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies. 8You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word. 9When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens. 10Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
11I, the Lord All-Powerful, have decided to wipe you out with disasters. 12There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word. 13I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you. 14None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back.
The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
15A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
16Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen! 17We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us. 18But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
19Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
20Then I told the crowd:
21Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah? 22And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today. 23This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
24-25Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven. 26Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name. 27Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death. 28Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
29And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt. 30 I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ ɔhɛlale Yizilayɛma mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la
1Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔhanle ɔhilele Gyɛlɛmaya, mɔɔ fane Dwuuma kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ de Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo wɔ Megedɔlo, Tapanehizi, Mɛmefese, yɛɛ Yigyibiti nyiakɛ la ɛne. 2Ɔse, “Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, mese: Bɛnwu munzule kpole mɔɔ memaa yedo Gyɛlusalɛmma nee Dwuda azuamgbole ne mɔ la. Bɛnlea, ɛnɛ bɛyɛ azuadu, yɛɛ awie ɛnde biala azo, 3ɔboalekɛ bɛyɛle amumuyɛ na bɛhanle me ɛya. Bɛkpunle ɛyɛlɛ bɛmanle nyamenle gyɛne gyɛne mɔɔ bɛmɛ o, bɛdabɛ o, bɛ ze mɔ o, biala ɛnze bɛ la na bɛzonlenle bɛ. 4Menzoanle me sonvolɛma, Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma amuala bɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne dahuu kɛ, ‘O, bɛmmayɛ bɛkyi ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ na mekyi!’ 5Noko bɛandie yɛɛ bɛangyakyi bɛ amumuyɛ ne mɔ ɛyɛlɛ; bɛhɔle zolɛ bɛkpunle ɛyɛlɛ bɛmanle nyamenle gyɛne gyɛne. 6Zɔhane ati memkpokpole me ɛya ne amuala menguale Dwuda azuamgbole ne mɔ azo yɛɛ Gyɛlusalɛm guabile ne mɔ azo, na bɛdɔ mgbane, bɛyɛ azuadu toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ a.
7“Na kɛkala, medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, mebiza bɛ kɛ: Duzu ati a bɛbɔ munzule bɛva na bɛkulo kɛ bɛminli mrenya nee mraalɛ, bɛ nlɔma nee bɛ ngakula mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda na bɛnrɛnyia bɛ bo zo amra ɛ? 8Duzu ati a bɛfa bɛ sa anloa gyima bɛka me ɛya, bɛkpu ɛyɛlɛ bɛmaa Yigyibiti ɛke mɔɔ bɛradɛnla la nyamenle ne mɔ na bɛsonle bɛ, amaa meazɛkye bɛ na bɛayɛ amowa nee agolobɛnwo menli wɔ maanle maanle mɔɔ wɔ ewiade la avinli ɛ? 9Bɛ rɛle ɛvi bɛ ze mɔ amumuyɛ ne, Dwuda arelemgbunli nee bɛ ye mɔ amumuyɛ ne yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mumua ne nee bɛ ye mɔ amumuyɛ ne mɔɔ bɛyɛle wɔ Dwuda azɛlɛ zo nee Gyɛlusalɛm guabile ne mɔ azo la ɔ? 10Bɛtɛbɛlɛle bɛ nwo aze bɛtɛmanle me toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ kenle ye a, yɛɛ bɛtɛsulole me, bɛtɛdile me mɛla nee me ngyehyɛlɛ mɔɔ menvale memanle bɛ nee bɛ ze mɔ la azo.
11“Yemɔti, medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, mese: Bɛ ɛtane ne ati mebava me nye meawula bɛ nyunlu na meabɔ Dwuda bɔkɔɔ. 12Mebamaa bɛazɛkye Dwudama mɔɔ ɛha, mɔɔ ɛva ɛzie bɛ nyunlu kɛ bɛkɔ bɛahɔdɛnla Yigyibiti la amuala. Bɛ muala bɛbawu bɛagua Yigyibiti. Bɛ muala bɛbawu konle nee ɛhɔne nu. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛ bie nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnlɛ bie la amuala bawu dadeɛ nloa nee ɛhɔne nu. Bɛbayɛ mgbane wɔ menli nye zo, bɛayɛ amowa wɔ menli nloa. 13Mebadea bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛde Yigyibiti la kɛmɔ medea Gyɛlusalɛm la. Mebava konle, ɛhɔne anzɛɛ ewulenzane a meadea bɛ a, 14amaa Dwudama mɔɔ ɛha la anu bie mɔɔ de Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la anvi ɛsalɛ. Bɛ nye ɛnrɛnwu Dwuda ɛlɛ, kɛmɔ bɛkpondɛ kɛ akee bɛsia bɛkɔ lɔ la, kyesɛ menli ekyi mɔɔ nriandile radanenle Dwuda la ala.”
15Na mrenya mɔɔ ze kɛ bɛ ye mɔ ɛkpu ɛyɛlɛ ɛmaa nyamenle gyɛne gyɛne, nee mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛnee gyigyi ɛkɛ ne la amuala, menli dɔɔnwo kpalɛ, boka Yizilayɛma mɔɔ de Yigyibiti nyiakɛ la hanle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya kɛ, 16“Gyɛlɛmaya, edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ wɔlua Ɛdɛnkɛma duma nu wɔha wɔhile yɛ la, yɛnrɛdie. 17Yɛbayɛ debie biala mɔɔ yɛvua kɛ yɛyɛ la. Yɛbakpu ɛyɛlɛ yɛamaa Anwomanyunlu Belemgbunli Raalɛ ne, na yɛagua nza yɛaye ɛdɛne yɛamaa ye, kɛmɔ yɛ nee yɛ ze mɔ, yɛ arelemgbunli nee maanle mgbanyima yɛyɛle ye wɔ Dwuda azuamgbole zo nee Gyɛlusalɛm guabile ne mɔ azo la. Ɔluakɛ mekɛ zɔhane yɛnyianle aleɛ dɔɔnwo, yɛkpazile, yɛɛ munzule biala ando yɛ. 18Noko sumunli kɛ yɛduale kɛ yɛnrɛkpu ɛyɛlɛ yɛnrɛmaa Anwomanyunlu Belemgbunli Raalɛ ne yɛɛ yɛnrɛgua nza yɛnrɛye ɛdɛne yɛnrɛmaa ye la, yɛhyia debie biala anwo yɛɛ yɛ menli ne ɛwie wu wɔ konle nee ɛhɔne nu.”
19Mraalɛ ne mɔ hanle kɛ, “Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee yɛkpu ɛyɛlɛ, yɛgua nza yɛye ɛdɛne yɛmaa Anwomanyunlu Belemgbunli Raalɛ ne, na yɛto keeki mɔɔ yɛyɛ yɛmaa ɔsɔho ye yɛmaa ye la, yɛ hu mɔ anye liele yɛ nyɛleɛ ne anwo.”
20Gyɛlɛmaya hanle hilele mrenya nee mraalɛ mɔɔ buale ye edwɛkɛ ne anwo zɛhae la kɛ, 21“Bɛdwenle kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma arɛle ɛvi ɛyɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛkpunle ye wɔ Dwuda azuamgbole ne mɔ azo nee Gyɛlusalɛm guabile ne mɔ azo la ɔ? Bɛ nee bɛ ze mɔ, bɛ arelemgbunli, bɛ mgbanyima, yɛɛ maanle ne anu amra a bɔle zɔhane ɛbɛla ne a. Ɛdɛnkɛma tɛkakye ye kɔsɔɔti. 22Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnrɛdɛnla ɛnrɛnlea bɛ ninyɛndane ɛyɛlɛ nee bɛ bɛkyi ninyɛne ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛyɛle la bieko. Yemɔti a bɛ azɛlɛ ne ɛdɔ mgbane, ɛyɛ ewula, ɛyɛ amowa, mɔɔ awie ɛnde zolɛ, kɛmɔ kɛkala ɔde la. 23Bɛyɛle ɛtane kɛ bɛkpunle ɛyɛlɛ na bɛandie Ɛdɛnkɛma ane, bɛanli ye mɛla nee ye ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ azo yɛɛ bɛambu ye daselɛlilɛ ne mɔ la, yemɔti a munzule ɛhye ɛdo bɛ toonwo yeradwu ɛnɛ la.”
24Gyɛlɛmaya zele menli ne nee mraalɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti kɛ, “Dwudama mɔɔ de Yigyibiti la, bɛdie mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛka ahile bɛ la. 25Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se: Bɛ nee bɛ ye mɔ bɛha kɛ bɛsonle Anwomanyunlu Belemgbunli Raalɛ ne. Bɛbɔ kpɔkɛ kɛ bɛbakpu ɛyɛlɛ bɛamaa ye, bɛagua nza bɛaye ɛdɛne bɛamaa ye. Bɛ mo. Bɛhɔ zolɛ bɛli bɛ ɛwɔkɛbɔlɛ ne mɔ azo. 26Akee bɛdabɛ Dwudama mɔɔ bɛde Yigyibiti la amuala, bɛdie. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, meka medame me ngome me duma kpole ne kɛ Dwudanli biala mɔɔ de Yigyibiti la ɛnrɛbɔ me duma ɛnrɛze kɛ, ‘Mekɛ ala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle de aze la’, ɛlɛ. 27Bɛnlea, bɛnrɛkpazi ɛlɛ, munzule ala a bado bɛ a. Bɛdabɛ Dwudama mɔɔ bɛpɛ bɛli Yigyibiti la amuala bawu konle nee ɛhɔne nu kɔkpula kɛ bɛ bo zo kɛbɔ bɔkɔɔ la. 28Bɛdabɛ ekyi bie a bɛbavi ɛsalɛ wɔ konle nu na bɛvi Yigyibiti bɛazia bɛara Dwuda a. Na akee Dwudama mɔɔ ɛha, mɔɔ rale kɛ bɛbadɛnla Yigyibiti na bɛanyia ngoane la anwu bɛmɛ nee mame, nuhua ko mɔɔ ye edwɛkɛ le nɔhalɛ la. 29Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebamaa ɛhye ayɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ amaa bɛ, mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛke ala meamaa bɛanwu kɛ me edwɛkɛ gyi kpundii kɛ munzule ala a bado bɛ a. 30 Mebaye Yigyibiti Belemgbunli Hɔfela meamaa ye kpɔvolɛma mɔɔ kpondɛ ye ahu ye la. Mebayɛ ye kɛ menyɛle Dwuda Belemgbunli Zɛdikaya mɔɔ menyele ye memanle ye kpɔvolɛ Babelonia Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza mɔɔ ɛnee ɛlɛkpondɛ ye ahu ye la.”

english_text:
The Lord Will Not Let Baruch Be Killed
1 In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him. 2Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
3You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest. 4But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted. 5I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Nyamenle bɔ Bɛlɛke ɛwɔkɛ
1 Dwuda Belemgbunli Gyɛhɔyakem, Dwosaya ara nrenya ne lile ɛvolɛ nna wɔ ebia ne azo la, Gyɛlɛmaya hanle edwɛkɛ manle Nilaya ara nrenya Bɛlɛke hɛlɛle wɔ buluku nu. 2Ɔse, “O Bɛlɛke, Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se: 3Ɛhanle kɛ, ‘Medame Bɛlɛke, abule ɛbu me! Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma akee ɛmaa me nyanelilɛ ɛyɛ kpole. Mekponle dedee akee mevɛ, mennwu ɛleka mɔɔ mesie me nwo a.’
4“Ɛdɛnkɛma se menga mengile wɔ kɛ, ‘Nea, melɛbubu mɔɔ mezi la meagua, yɛɛ mɔɔ melua la, melɛtudu meagua. Mebayɛ ɛhye wɔ aleɛabo ɛleka biala. 5Na wɔmɔ, ɛkpondɛ ninyɛne mgbole ɔ? Mmakpondɛ bɛ bo zo, ɔluakɛ nea, melɛmaa munzule ado menli kɔsɔɔti, na wɔmɔ, ɛleka biala mɔɔ ɛkɛhɔ la ɛlɛ ngoane. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Speaks to Jeremiah about the Nations
1The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world.
What the Lord Says about Egypt
2 In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
3It's time to go into battle!
So grab your shields,
4saddle your horses,
and polish your spears.
Put on your helmets and armor,
then take your positions.
5I can see the battle now—
you are defeated
and running away,
never once looking back.
Terror is all around.
6You are strong and run fast,
but you can't escape.
You fall in battle
near the Euphrates River.
7What nation is this,
that rises like the Nile River
overflowing its banks?
8It is Egypt, rising with a roar
like a raging river
and saying,
“I'll flood the earth,
destroying cities, and killing
everyone in them.”
9Go ahead, Egypt.
Tell your chariots and cavalry
to attack and fight hard.
Order your troops to march out,
with Ethiopians and Libyans
carrying shields,
and the Lydians armed with bows
and arrows.
10But the Lord All-Powerful
will win this battle
and take revenge
on his enemies.
His sword will eat them
and drink their blood
until it is full.
They will be killed in the north
near the Euphrates River,
as a sacrifice to the Lord.
11Egypt, no medicine can heal you,
not even the soothing lotion
from Gilead.
12All nations have heard you weep;
you are disgraced,
and they know it.
Your troops fall to the ground,
stumbling over each other.
A Warning for Egypt
13-14 When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them:
Prepare to defend yourselves!
Everywhere in your nation,
people are dying in war.
15I have struck down
your mighty god Apis
and chased him away.
16Your soldiers stumble
over each other
and say, “Get up!
The enemy will kill us,
unless we can escape
to our own land.”
17Give the king of Egypt
this new name,
“Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
18Egypt, I am the true king,
the Lord All-Powerful,
and as surely as I live,
those enemies who attack
will tower over you
like Mount Tabor among the hills
or Mount Carmel by the sea.
19You will be led away captive,
so pack a few things
to bring with you.
Your capital, Memphis,
will lie empty and in ruins.
20An enemy from the north
will attack you, beautiful Egypt,
like a fly biting a cow.
21The foreign soldiers you hired
will turn and run.
But they are doomed,
like well-fed calves
being led to the butcher.
* 22The enemy army will go forward
like a swarm of locusts.
Your troops will feel helpless,
like a snake in a forest
23when men with axes
start chopping down trees.
It can only hiss
and try to escape.
24Your people will be disgraced
and captured by the enemy
from the north.
25I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power. 26I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Bring Israel Home
The Lord said:
27 Israel, don't be afraid.
Someday I will bring you home
from foreign lands.
You and your descendants
will live in peace and safety,
with nothing to fear.
28So don't be afraid,
even though now
you deserve to be punished
and have been scattered
among other nations.
But when I destroy them,
I will protect you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Bɛli Yigyibiti anwo zo konim wɔ Kaakimehye
1Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle maanle maanle ne mɔ anwo edwɛkɛ hilele Gyɛlɛmaya. 2Ɔbɔle ɔ bo wɔ Yigyibiti anwo zo, ɔhanle Belemgbunli Niko ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ɛnee gua Azule Yufileti ne anloa wɔ Kaakimehye, na Babelonia Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza ɛli bɛ nwo zo konim wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ Dwosaya ara nrenya Gyɛhɔyakem ɛli ɛvolɛ nna wɔ Dwuda belemgbunli ebia ne azo la anwo edwɛkɛ.
3“Bɛsesa bɛ enyinlike ne mɔ
na bɛhɔ konle nloa!
4Bɛziezie mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ,
O mgbɔnwɔkavoma, bɛvo bɛ mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ azo!
Bɛva bɛ mbulalɛ ahyɛlɛ na bɛrasolo!
Bɛzi bɛ atwɛ ne mɔ, bɛva bɛ mbulahɛba ne mɔ bɛgyela!
5“Ɛdɛnkɛma se:
Duzu a menwu ye a?
Ɛzulolɛ ɛha bɛ, ɛmaa bɛzia bɛ nzi.
Bɛ ɛlɔnema ne ɛli akoatɔ, bɛgua ndwɛlɛ aze,
bɛndo bɛ nye bɛ nzi, ɛzulolɛ wɔ ɛleka biala.
6Mɔɔ anwo yɛ ndɛ la ɛngola nriandi;
ɛlɔne nu katakyiema ɛnvi ɛsalɛ.
Bɛdu koti na bɛdu bɛgua
Azule Yufileti ne anloa wɔ sɔlɔ lɔ.
7Nwane a ɛlɛmaa ɔ nwo zo kɛ Azule Naele ne,
kɛ azule mɔɔ ɛyi ɛbu aze la?
8Yigyibiti dwazo kɛ azule Naele,
ɔle kɛ azule mɔɔ ɛyi ɛbu aze la.
Ɔhanle kɛ, ‘Mebayi meava ewiade;
mebazɛkye azuamgbole nee zolɛ ezuavolɛ.’
9O mgbɔnwɔ, bɛluo,
O konle ehwili, bɛbili!
Bɛva ɛlɔnema ne bɛhɔ:
Sudan nee Lebea mrenya mɔɔ dedɛ enyinlike,
Ledea mrenya mɔɔ ze ɛda to la.”
10Kenle ne le medame Tumivolɛ Awulae Nyamenle me kenle,
ɔle nzenralɛlilɛ kenle;
mebali me kpɔvolɛma nzenralɛ.
Dadeɛ bali bɛ antɛnlɛma;
bɛ mogya bavɔ ye soonwu,
ɔluakɛ Tumivolɛ Awulae Nyamenle bɔ azu
wɔ sɔlɔ maanle nu, wɔ Azule Yufileti ne anloa.
11O Yigyibitima,
bɛhɔ Geleade bɛhɔkpondɛ ayile!
Bɛyɛ ayile dɔɔnwo,
noko bɛtɛtele kpɔkɛ.
12Maanle maanle ɛde wɔ anyiemgbabɔlɛ,
awie biala ɛde wɔ ɛzunlɛ,
ɔluakɛ ɛlɔnenli katakyie ɛfofo ɔ gɔnwo anwo zo;
bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛdu bɛgua.
Nɛbukadenɛza ɛralɛ
13 Babelonia Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza ɛzɛkyelɛ mɔɔ ɔba yearazɛkye Yigyibiti la anwo edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle hilele Gyɛlɛmaya la ɛne:
14“Bɛha ye wɔ Yigyibiti, na bɛbɔ ye nolo wɔ Megedɔlo;
bɛbɔ ye nolo wɔ Mɛmefese yɛɛ Tapanehizi,
bɛha kɛ, ‘Bɛdwazo bɛboɔboa bɛ nwo,
ɔluakɛ bɛ muala bɛbawu konle nu.’
15Duzu ati a bɛ amonle kpole Epese ɛnriandi ɛ?
Duzu ati a bɛ ɛnlankɛ nyinli ananze ne angola gyinla ɛ?
ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma dele ye aze.
16Wɔ ɛlɔnema dɔɔnwo ne ɛdu koti, ɛdu ɛgua;
bɛka bɛkile bɛ nwo ngoko kɛ,
‘Bɛdwazo, bɛmaa yɛzia yɛdoa yɛ menli ne,
yehɔ maanle mɔɔ bɛwole yɛ nu la anu,
yɛnriandi mɔɔ sisi yɛ la dadeɛ ne.’
17“Bɛvɛlɛ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne
‘Belemgbunli anwo alɛra
mɔɔ maa ye mekɛ kpalɛ kpa ɔ ti a.’
18Medame mɔɔ me duma a le Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma la,
mele Belemgbunli, na mese:
Meka, meka kɛ, awie mɔɔ kɛzua wɔ la
le kɛ yezua Boka Teebɔ wɔ awoka avinli
anzɛɛ Boka Kamɛle wɔ nyevile nloa.
19O Yigyibitima,
bɛboɔboa bɛ nwo na bɛ nee bɛ kɔ nlɔnu!
Mɛmefese badɔ mgbane,
ɔbabɔ, awie ɛnrɛdɛnla zo.
20Yigyibiti le ɛnlankɛ belɛ kɛnlɛma,
na tunli vi sɔlɔ ɛra banlo ye.
21Ɛlɔnema bɔbɔ mɔɔ yebɔ bɛ ɛkpa la
le kɛ nlankɛ mralɛ dɔlera.
Ɛhɛe, bɛ muala bɛnriandi bɛzia bɛ nzi;
bɛangyinla bɛ gyakɛ anu,
ɔluakɛ bɛ awieleɛ mekɛ ɛdwu, bɛ ndeanlɛ mekɛ ɛdwu.
22Yigyibiti twolo kɛ ɛwɔlɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛtwenle ɔ nwo ahɔ la,
ɔluakɛ ye kpɔvolɛma tia kilikili ba ɔ nwo zo;
bɛfa akuma bɛba ɔ nwo zo
kɛ menli mɔɔ bu mbaka la.
23Bɛbazɛkye ye kpɔkɛmile ne
mɔɔ bɛwolo nu a ɔnwolo la,
ɔboalekɛ bɛzonle bɛtɛla abɛbɛ,
bɛtia bɛ a bɛnnwu bɛ nloa.
24Yigyibitima anyunlu bagua aze,
bɛbaye bɛ bɛamaa menli bie mɔɔ vi sɔlɔ la.
Medame, Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”
25Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne zele kɛ, “Mebadea Tibise bozonle Amɔn ne, Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne, Yigyibitima yɛɛ bɛ awozonle ne mɔ. Mebadea Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne nee menli mɔɔ ɛva bɛ rɛle ɛwula ye nu la. 26Mebaye bɛ meamaa menli mɔɔ kpondɛ bɛ ahu bɛ la. Mebava bɛ meamaa Babelonia Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza nee ye safohyenlema ne. Nzinlii, menli badɛnla Yigyibiti bieko kɛ anrɛɛ mɔmoane ɔde la. Medame, Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”
Ɛdɛnkɛma balie ye menli ne ngoane
27 “O me akɛlɛ Gyekɔbo, mmasulo.
O Yizilayɛ, mmamaa wɔ ahonle tu.
Mebalie wɔ meavi moa moa lɔ meara.
Mebalie ɛ bo zo amra meavi ɛleka mɔɔ bɛhyele bɛ nuokɛ
bɛhɔle la meara.
Gyekɔbo bazia ara na ɔ nzo nu adwo ye,
ɔ nwo badɔ ye, awie ɛnrɛha ye ɛzulolɛ.
28O me akɛlɛ Gyekɔbo, mmasulo, me nee wɔ lua.
Mebazɛkye maanle maanle mɔɔ menvoanle wɔ
memanle ɛhɔle nu la kɔsɔɔti,
na wɔmɔ, menrɛzɛkye wɔ.
Mebazuzu meadea wɔ,
ɛnrɛva ɛ nwo dwɔɔ.
Medame, Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”

english_text:
What the Lord Says about the Philistines
1 Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
2I, the Lord, tell you
that your land will be flooded
with an army from the north.
It will destroy your towns
and sweep you away,
moaning and screaming.
3When you hear the thunder
of horses and chariots,
your courage will vanish,
and parents will even abandon
their own children.
4You refugees from Crete,
your time has now come,
and I will destroy you.
None of you will be left
to help the cities
of Tyre and Sidon.
5The Anakim who survive
in Gaza and Ashkelon
will mourn for you
by shaving their heads
and sitting in silence.
6You ask how long will I continue
to attack you with my sword,
then you tell me to put it away
and leave you alone.
7But how can my sword rest,
when I have commanded it
to attack Ashkelon
and the seacoast?
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Filisitiama anwo la
1 Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ mɔɔ hanle ye wɔ Filisitiama anwo hilele Gyɛlɛmaya kolaa na Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne abɔ Gaza la ɛne. 2Ɔse:
“Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mese:
Bɛnlea! Azule ɛlɛmaa ɔ nwo zo wɔ sɔlɔ lɔ,
na ɔbayɛ azule mɔɔ ye ɛzenlɛ yɛ ɛzulolɛ a.
Ɔbayi yeabu azɛlɛ ye azo yeava debie biala,
azuamgbole nee menli baha azule bo.
Menli badea nu abiza moalɛ;
aleɛabo sonla biala baye awolɛ.
3Saa bɛte mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ agyakɛ abo,
bɛte konle ehwili ne mɔ anwo alɛra ne nee bɛ gyakɛ ne
mɔ ɛbililɛ ne ane a,
selɛma ɛnrɛdo bɛ nye bɛ nzi ɛnrɛnlea bɛ mra,
ɔboalekɛ bɛ sa nu ɛtuto bɔkɔɔ.
4Filisitia ɛzɛkyelɛ mekɛ ɛdwu,
bɛbade boavolɛ biala mɔɔ ɛha la bɛavi Taya nee Saedɛn
anwo,
ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, melɛsɛkye Filisitiama
mɔɔ vi Kiliti ɛnweanloa rale la amuala.
5Gazama ɛkpa bɛ ti, Ahyekɛlɔn abo zo ɛminli.
O Anakema mɔɔ ɛha,
bɛsu bɛabodɛboda bɛ nwo yeahɔdwu kenlenzu?
6Aa, Ɛdɛnkɛma konle dadeɛ!
Kenlenzu a ɛkɛgyakyi ɛbililɛ a?
Kɔvea wɔ boa ne anu,
die wɔ ɛnwomenle na yɛ koonwu.
7Na kɛ ɔkɛzi ɔkɛla koonwu
wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzie ye gyima nwo la ɛ?
Gyima ne tia Ahyekɛlɔn
nee menli mɔɔ de ɛnweanloa la.”

english_text:
What the Lord Says about Moab
1 The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab:
The town of Nebo is doomed;
Kiriathaim will be captured
and disgraced,
and even its fortress
will be left in ruins.
2No one honors you, Moab.
In Heshbon, enemies make plans
to end your life.
My sword will leave only silence
in your town named “Quiet.”
3The people of Horonaim
will cry for help,
as their town is attacked
and destroyed.
4Moab will be shattered!
Your children will sob
5and cry on their way up
to the town of Luhith;
on the road to Horonaim
they will tell of disasters.
6Run for your lives!
Head into the desert
like a wild donkey.
7You thought you could be saved
by your power and wealth,
but you will be captured
along with your god Chemosh,
his priests, and officials.
8Not one of your towns
will escape destruction.
I have told your enemies,
“Wipe out the valley
and the flatlands of Moab.
9Spread salt on the ground
to kill the crops.
Leave its towns in ruins,
with no one living there.
10I want you to kill the Moabites,
and if you let them escape,
I will put a curse on you.”
11Moab, you are like wine
left to settle undisturbed,
never poured from jar to jar.
And so, your nation continues
to prosper and improve.
12But now, I will send enemies
to pour out the wine
and smash the jars!
13Then you will be ashamed,
because your god Chemosh
cannot save you,
just as Bethel could not help
the Israelites.
14You claim that your soldiers
are strong and brave.
15But I am the Lord,
the all-powerful King,
and I promise that enemies
will overpower your towns.
Even your best warriors
will die in the battle.
16It won't be long now—
disaster will hit Moab!
17I will order the nearby nations
to mourn for you and say,
“Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others,
but now its glorious power
has been shattered.”
18People in the town of Dibon,
you will be honored no more,
so have a seat in the dust.
Your walls will be torn down
when the enemies attack.
19You people of Aroer,
go wait beside the road,
and when refugees run by,
ask them, “What happened?”
20They will answer,
“Moab has been defeated!
Weep with us in shame.
Tell everyone at the Arnon River
that Moab is destroyed.”
21I will punish every town
that belongs to Moab,
but especially Holon,
Jahzah, Mephaath,
22Dibon, Nebo,
Beth-Diblathaim, 23Kiriathaim,
Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
24Kerioth, and Bozrah.
25My decision is final—
your army will be crushed,
and your power broken.
26People of Moab, you claim
to be stronger than I am.
Now I will tell other nations
to make you drunk
and to laugh while you collapse
in your own vomit.
27You made fun of my people
and treated them like criminals
caught in the act.
28Now you must leave your towns
and live like doves
in the shelter of cliffs
and canyons.
29I know about your pride,
and how you strut and boast.
30But I also know bragging
will never save you.
31So I will cry and mourn
for Moab
and its town of Kir-Heres.
32People of Sibmah,
you were like a vineyard
heavy with grapes,
and with branches reaching
north to the town of Jazer
and west to the Dead Sea.
But you have been destroyed,
and so I will weep for you,
as the people of Jazer weep
for the vineyards.
33Harvest celebrations are gone
from the orchards and farms
of Moab.
I have silenced the shouts
of people making wine.
34Weeping from Heshbon
can be heard as far
as Elealeh and Jahaz;
cries from Zoar are heard
in Horonaim
and Eglath-Shelishiyah.
And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
35I will get rid of anyone
who burns incense
to the gods of Moab
or offers sacrifices
at their shrines.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
36In my heart I moan for Moab,
like a funeral song
played on a flute.
I mourn for the people
of the town of Kir-Heres,
because their wealth is gone.
* 37-38The people of Moab
mourn on the rooftops
and in the streets.
Men cut off their beards,
people shave their heads;
they make cuts on their hands
and wear sackcloth.
And it's all because I, the Lord,
have shattered Moab like a jar
that no one wants.
39Moab lies broken!
Listen to its people cry
as they turn away in shame.
Other nations are horrified
at what happened,
but still they mock her.
40Moab, an enemy swoops down
like an eagle spreading its wings
over your land.
41Your cities and fortresses
will be captured,
and your warriors as fearful
as women giving birth.
42You are finished as a nation,
because you dared oppose me,
the Lord.
43Terror, pits, and traps
are waiting for you.
44If you are terrified and run,
you will fall into a pit;
and if you crawl out of the pit,
you'll get caught in a trap.
The time has come
for you to be punished.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
45Near the city of Heshbon,
where Sihon once ruled,
tired refugees stand in shadows
cast by the flames
of their burning city.
Soon, the towns on other hilltops,
where those warlike people live,
will also go up in smoke.
46People of Moab, you worshiped
Chemosh, your god,
but now you are done for,
and your children are prisoners
in a foreign country.
47Yet someday, I will bring
your people back home.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Mowabe ɛbɔlɛ
1 Edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle ye wɔ Mowabe anwo la ɛne:
“Bɛzu Niboma, ɔluakɛ bɛ sua ne ɛdɔ mgbane!
Bɛho bɛva Keleateeyem, yebɔ anyiemgba,
bɛgolo ye aranemgbole ne bɛgua ɔ nyunlu aze;
2Mowabe anyunlunyia ɛdɔ aze ɛbɔ.
Bɛvale ɔ nwo adwenle ɛtane ne wɔ Hɛhyebɔn.
Bɛse, ‘Bɛrɛla bɛmaa yɛbɔ ye bɔkɔɔ
mɔɔ ɔnle maanle bieko a.’
O Mademɛn, ɛdawɔ noko, bɛbaha wɔ aze,
bɛbava konle bɛadoa wɔ.
3Bɛdie! Bɛlɛtea Hɔloneeyem nehane
kɛ, ‘Bɛlɛto maanle ye mgbane, bɛlɛsɛkye ninyɛne.’
4“Mowabe maanle ne ɛbɔ bɔkɔɔ;
yɛte ngakula ne kɛ bɛlɛsu,
5ɔluakɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛfo boka ne bɛahɔ Luhete la
ɛnee bɛlɛ ɛzunlɛ,
ɔboalekɛ Hɔloneeyem ndololeɛ nu
yɛɛ bɛde ɛzɛkyelɛ ɛzunlɛ ne a.
6Bɛnriandi bɛlie bɛ nwo!
Bɛnriandi kɛ ɛsɛlɛ zo asoaso.
7“Bɛvale bɛ rɛle bɛwulale bɛ anwosesebɛ nee bɛ anwonyia
nu,
yemɔti bɛbavo bɛ nwo zo;
bɛbava bɛ bozonle Kimɔhye,
ye ahɔmenle yɛɛ bɛ mgbanyima bɛahɔ nlɔnu.
8Sɛkyevolɛ ne bavo suakpole biala azo,
suakpole ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛvi ɛsalɛ;
ɔbazɛkye bɔnza ne, ɔbazɛkye azɛlɛ sɛsɛ ne,
kɛmɔ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma meha la.
9Bɛmaa Mowabe ndɛbalɛ, ɔluakɛ ɔbadu yeahɔ;
ye azuamgbole badɔ mgbane, awie ɛnrɛdɛnla zolɛ.”
10(Munzule ɛha sonla mɔɔ ɛnyeye ɔ ti anu ɛnyɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma gyima la! Munzule ɛha sonla mɔɔ ɛnva ye dadeɛ ne ɛnga mogya ɛngua la!)
Bɛbɔ Mowabe azuamgbole ne mɔ
11Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Sumunli Mowabe ngakula nu, awie ɛtɛgyegyele ye, yɛɛ ɔle kɛ nza mɔɔ ɛdɔne ɔ bo la; bɛngakyi ye bɛngua dwora gyɛne gyɛne nu. Ɔtɛkɔle nlɔnu ɛlɛ, yemɔti ɔtɛyɛ fɛ, yɛɛ ɔtɛbɔ evuanlɛ.
12“Yemɔti, mekɛ bie badwu mɔɔ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mebazoa menli meamaa bɛahɔhakyi Mowabe kɛ bɛkakyi nza bɛagua dwora gyɛne nu la. Bɛbawola nza ne na bɛabobɔ dwora ne mɔ. 13Na Mowabe anyunlu bagua aze, ɔlua ye bozonle Kimɔhye ati, kɛmɔ Yizilayɛma anyunlu guale aze wɔ Bɛtɛle mɔɔ ɛnee bɛ rɛle wɔ ye nu la.
14Mowabema, duzu ati a bɛka kɛ,
‘Yɛmɛ ɛne, yɛle katakyiema wɔ konle nu’ ɛ?
15Mɔɔ babɔ Mowabe nee ye azuamgbole la ɛra;
bɛhu bɛ mgbavolɛ ngɛnlɛma ne mɔ.
Medame Belemgbunli, mɔɔ me duma a le
Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma la a mese a.
16Munzule ɛlɛba arava Mowabe,
ye nyanenwunlɛ ɛbikye.
17“Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee Mowabe zua la, bɛzu ye,
bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛze duma mɔɔ yelie la, bɛzu ye.
Bɛha kɛ, ‘Bɛlie Mowabe belemgbunlililɛ tumi kpole ne,
ye anyunlunyia tumi ne ɛbɔ aze.’
18Daebɔnoma, bɛvi bɛ anyunlunyia ɛleka ne bɛtolo
bɛrakpofo azɛlɛ ketekete ye azo,
ɔluakɛ sɛkyevolɛ ne mɔɔ ɛzɛkye Mowabe la ɛra bɛ nwo zo;
yebubu bɛ aranemgbole ne mɔ.
19O Alowɛma!
Bɛgyinla adehane ne na bɛnlea!
Bɛbiza nrenya anzɛɛ raalɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛnriandi la
kɛ, ‘Duzu edwɛkɛ ɔ?’
20Bɛbabua kɛ, ‘Mowabe ɛbɔ, ye anyunlunyia ɛdɔ aze;
bɛzu ye, bɛye ye awolɛ.
Bɛbɔ ye nolo wɔ Azule Anɔn ne anloa
kɛ Mowabe ɛdɔ mgbane!’
21“Ndeanlɛ ɛra azɛlɛ sɛsɛ ne azo na yeha azuamgbole ɛhye mɔ: Hɔlɔn, Gyaza, Mɛfeeyate, 22Daebɔn, Nibo, Bɛte Debelateeyem, 23Keleateeyem, Bɛtegamɛle, Bɛtemiyɔn, 24Kɛleyo, Bɔzela, yɛɛ azuamgbole mɔɔ wɔ Mowabe azɛlɛ zo, mɔɔ wɔ moa moa nee mɔɔ zuozua ye la kɔsɔɔti. 25Bɛha Mowabe anwosesebɛ ne aze, yɛɛ bɛzɛkye ye tumi ne, medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”
Bɛbabɛlɛ Mowabe aze
26Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Bɛmaa Mowabe ɛbo ɛyɛ tindaanwu, ɔboalekɛ yede me nwo atua. Mowabe bave ala nu, na menli agolo ɔ nwo. 27Mowabema, asoo tɛ bɛmɛ a bɛzelele Yizilayɛma la? Asoo Yizilayɛma wuale debie la ati a mekɛ biala mɔɔ bɛkɛbɔ Yizilayɛma duma la bɛkɔsɔ bɛ ti a?
28“O Mowabema, bɛdu bɛvi azuamgbole ne mɔ azo! Bɛhɔdɛnla bodane ne mɔ azo! Bɛyɛ kɛ abubule mɔɔ nwo ye sane wɔ bodane tokule nloa la. 29Yɛde Mowabe adubɛnwo ne nganeɛ, ɔmemaa ɔ nwo zo kpole, ɔbu ɔ nwo, ɔle mgbanyizonle yɛɛ ɔtu ɔ nloa anu. 30Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mese: Meze ye mgbanyizonle mɔɔ wɔ ɔ nwo, ɔ nloa anu ɛdulɛ ne le mgbane, yɛɛ ye nyɛleɛ le gyɛne. 31Yemɔti meye Mowabe awolɛ; mesu Mowabe maanle ne amuala; mesu Kɛɛ Hilɛzema. 32O Sebema vanye! Mesu wɔ metɛla Gyeezɛ. Wɔ vanye mbaka ngane ndendenle pɛle Nyevile Wulera ne dwule Gyeezɛ. Sɛkyevolɛ ne ɛzɛkye wɔ wawaa mbaka ma nee wɔ vanye ma mɔɔ ɛbolo la. 33Fɛlɛko nee anyelielɛ ɛvi Mowabe azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ kye aleɛ la azo. Memaa nwanye ne mɔɔ vi nwanye melahyinli ne mɔ anu twi la ɛgyakyi ɛhwinlɛ. Awie biala ɛnva anyelielɛ ɛndeɛdea nu ɛndwihwi vanye ma; ɛdeɛdeanlɛ ne ɛnle anyelielɛ ɛdeɛdeanlɛ.
34“Hɛhyebɔnoma nee Ɛlɛyalima tea nu su; bɛsu bɛmaa bɛte bɛ ne moa moa wɔ Gyeehaze. Bɛ ne kɔ toonwo bɛte ye wɔ Zowaa, Hɔloneeyem, yɛɛ Ɛgelate Hyɛlehyaya lɔ.
