28I, the Lord God, am ready to hand you over to those hateful enemies that you find so disgusting. 29They will cruelly take away everything you have worked for and strip you naked. Then everyone will see you for the prostitute you really are. Your own vulgar sins 30have led to this. You were the one determined to have sex with men from other nations and to worship their idols. 31You have turned out no better than your older sister, and now you must drink from the cup filled with my anger.
32I, the Lord God, gave your sister a large, deep cup filled with my anger. And when you drink from that cup, you will be mocked and insulted. 33You will end up drunk and devastated, because that cup is filled with horror and ruin. 34But you must drink every drop! Then smash the cup and chew on its broken pieces. Use them to cut your breasts in sorrow. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
35You have completely rejected me, and so I promise that you will be punished for the disgusting things you did as a prostitute.
The Two Sisters Are Condemned
36The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, it's time for you to tell Oholah and Oholibah that they are guilty. Remind them of their evil ways! 37They have been unfaithful by worshiping idols, and they have committed murder by sacrificing my own children as offerings to idols. 38-39They came into my temple that same day, and that made it unfit as a place to worship me. They have even stopped respecting the Sabbath.
40They sent messengers to attract men from far away. When those men arrived, the two sisters bathed themselves and put on eye shadow and jewelry. 41They sat on a fancy couch, and in front of them was a table for the olive oil and incense that had belonged to me. 42Their room was always filled with a noisy crowd of drunkards brought in from the desert. These men gave the women bracelets and beautiful crowns, 43and I noticed that the men were eager to have sex with these women, though they were exhausted from being prostitutes. 44In fact, the men had sex over and over with Oholah and Oholibah, the two sinful sisters. 45But honest judges will someday accuse those two of murder and of being unfaithful, because they are certainly guilty.
46So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters:
I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you. 47They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses. 48I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have. 49You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_text:
Mediema mraalɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ yɛle ɛtane la
1Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2Ɔse, “Sonla ra, mraalɛ nwiɔ wɔ ɛkɛ, bɛ nli ko. 3Bɛbɔle tuutuu ɛbɛla wɔ Yigyibiti. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee bɛle mbɛlɛra, na bɛmanle bɛmiemianle bɛ nyɛfo na bɛminlinle bɛ belamunliyɛlɛ ne. 4Bɛfɛlɛ kpanyinli ne Ɔhola, yɛɛ bɛfɛlɛ ekyi ne Ɔhɔleba. (Ɔhola gyi ɛkɛ ne maa Samɛlea, yɛɛ Ɔhɔleba gyi ɛkɛ ne maa Gyɛlusalɛm). Bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛyɛle me ɛdeɛ, na bɛwole mralɛ mrenya nee mralɛ mraalɛ. 5Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Ɔhola le me ɛdeɛ la, ɔbɔle tuutuu ɛbɛla na nla atiakunluwɔzo ti ɔdule ɔdoale ye kulovolɛma mɔɔ vi Aselea la. 6Bɛle sogyama mɔɔ wula adɛladeɛ kɔkɔlɛ, amɛnladoma nee safohyenlema mgbanyinli. Bɛ muala bɛle mgbavolɛ mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ, yɛɛ bɛka mgbɔnwɔ. 7Ɔvale ye tuutuulilɛ ne ɔbɛkabɛkale Aseleama ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ la, na ɔzonlenle awie ko biala mɔɔ vale ye la bozonle mɔɔ ɔlɛ la. 8Yeangyakyi ye tuutuulilɛ ne mɔɔ ɔlile wɔ Yigyibiti la anzi ɛlilɛ, ɔluakɛ ɔvi ye mbɛlɛra nu, mrenya nee ye lale na bɛsosɔle ɔ nyɛfo, na bɛyɛle ye kɛmɔ bɛkɛyɛ tuutuunli ala la. 9Yemɔti menyele ye menwulale ye kulovolɛma, Aseleama asa anu. 10Menli ɛhye mɔ kpale ɔ nwo, bɛhyele ɔ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ ne mɔ na bɛhunle ɔdaye mumua ne. Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛduale ye kakɛ mɔɔ le zɛhae la, mraalɛ kɔsɔɔti vale ye edwɛkɛ lile adwelie.
11“ Ɔ diema Ɔhɔleba nwunle ɛhye, noko yemɔ bɔbɔ akee ɔzɛkyele ɔdɛlale ɔ diema ne. Ɔbɔle tuutuu ɛbɛla ɔdɛlale ɔ diema ne. 12Ɔtetele ɔdɔle Aseleama, amɛnladoma, safohyenlema mgbanyinli, sogyama mɔɔ wulowula adɛladeɛ kɔkɔlɛ, yɛɛ sogyama mɔɔ tɛnla mgbɔnwɔ zo la akɔme nu; bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛle mgbavolɛ mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ a. 13Na menwunle kɛ yezɛkye, na bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛlua edinli ko azo.
14“Ɔhɔleba ati minle tuutuulilɛ ne anu kpalɛ. Ɔnwunle kɛ bɛdolɔdolɔ mrenya bie wɔ bane nwo, mrenya mɔ vi Babelonia la nvoninli ɔ; bɛpenti bɛ ngɛnlɛma, 15bɛva bɛlɛte bɛhyehye bɛ avinli, bɛbɔ bɛ abɔtile na ko biala zɔho sogya kpanyinli mɔɔ vi Babelonia la. 16Ɔnwunle bɛ ala la ye nla atiakunluwɔzo ne rale bɛ nwo zo, na ɔzoanle menli bɛ nwo lɔ wɔ Babelonia. 17Babeloniama rale na bɛ nee ye ralale, bɛhulole bɛ nwo; bɛvale bɛ atiakunluwɔzo ne bɛguale ɔ nwo zo. Na mɔɔ akee bɛzɛkyele ye bɛwiele la, bɛ nwo vonlonle ye na ɔgyakyile bɛ. 18Mɔɔ akee ɔyele ɔ nyunlu ɔbɔle tuutuu ɛbɛla, ɔkpale ɔ nwo ɔhilele la, ɔmanle mengyile ye na mengakyile me nzi menzile ye, kɛmɔ menyɛle ɔ diema raalɛ ne la. 19Noko ɔ ti minle tuutuulilɛ nu kpalɛ kpalɛ; ɔhakyele mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee ɔle bɛlɛra, mɔɔ ɔbɔ ye tuutuu ɛbɛla ne wɔ Yigyibiti la. 20Ɔvale nwuvolɛ mrenya mɔɔ bɛ mrenyanu mgbole le kɛ asoaso ɛdeɛ ne, na bɛ nlanzule zonle kɛ ɛkpɔnwɔ ɛdeɛ ne la. 21(Ɔhɔleba, zɛhae yɛɛ ɛyɛle ɛvale ɛhakyele wɔ mbɛlɛra nu adwɔmane ne mɔɔ ɛbɔle wɔ Yigyibiti, ɛmanle bɛmiemianle ɛ nyɛfo mgbokua ne na bɛzɛkyele wɔ la.)”
Nyamenle ndeanlɛ mɔɔ wɔ adiema raalɛ ekyi ne anwo zo la
22Zɔhane ati, Ɔhɔleba, Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Nea, mebamaa wɔ kulovolɛma mɔɔ anwo vonlonle wɔ na ɛhakyile ɛ nzi ɛzile bɛ la adwazo ɛ nwo zo. Mebava bɛ meavi ɛleka kɔsɔɔti meara ɛ nwo zo: 23Babeloniama nee Kaledeama amuala, Pikɔdo, Hyowa, Kowa, yɛɛ Aselea mgbavolɛ mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ, amɛnladoma nee safohyenle mgbanyinli, sogya mgbanyinli nee sogyama mɔɔ tɛnla mgbɔnwɔ zo la amuala. 24Bɛvi sɔlɔ, bɛlɛ konle ehwili nee aleɛ ehwili nee menli dɔɔnwo kpalɛ mɔɔ dedɛ ahoholombaka nee bɛ sa nu enyinlike, na bɛzozo mbulalɛ ahyɛlɛ la bɛbara ɛ nwo zo, na mebagyakyi bɛ meamaa bɛadea wɔ, kɛmɔ ɔfɛta la. 25Mebava ɛ nwo ɛya kpole, amaa bɛ nee wɔ ali ye ɛsesebɛ kpalɛ. Bɛbapɛ ɛ bonyi nee ɛ nzo. Menli mɔɔ baha ɛ nzi la badɔ dadeɛ nloa. Bɛbahye ɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ, na bɛava senle bɛayela bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛha la. 26Bɛbakpa ɛ nwo ndanlɛ kɔsɔɔti na bɛava wɔ anwoneɛ ne mɔ bɛahɔ. 27Mebayɛ ɛhye meava meadua wɔ tuutuulilɛ nee wɔ adwɔmanebɔlɛ atiakunluwɔzo ne mɔɔ ɛ nee ye vi Yigyibiti rale la. Ɛnrɛhola ɛ nye zo maa nea Yigyibitima, yɛɛ ɛnrɛhakye bɛ bieko.”
28Ɔluakɛ Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Nea, mebaye wɔ meawula bɛdabɛ mɔɔ ɛkyi bɛ la asa anu. 29Bɛ nee wɔ bali ye ɛkpɔlɛ nu, na bɛava ɛ nwo ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti, bɛagyakyi wɔ kpoholokpo bɛado ɛkɛ, na wɔ tuutuulilɛ ne ala ali. Wɔ tuutuulilɛ nee wɔ adwɔmanebɔlɛ a ɛva ɛhye ɛra ɛ nwo zo a, 30ɔboalekɛ ɛbɔle tuutuu ɛbɛla wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anu na ɛguale ɛ nwo evinli, ɛzonlenle bɛ mmonle ne mɔ. 31Wɔva ɛ diema raalɛ ne agyakɛ, yemɔti mebava ye nyane kɔpo ne meawula ɛ sa nu.”
32Awulae Nyamenle ne se.
“Ɛbanlo ɛ diema ralɛ ne nyane kɔpo ne anu;
ɔle kpole yɛɛ ɔ kunlu kɔ.
Bɛbazele wɔ, bɛagolo ɛ nwo,
ɔluakɛ edwɛkɛ dɔɔnwo wɔ nu.
33Nyane ngome babo wɔ nza.
Ɛ diema raalɛ Samɛlea nyane kɔpo ne,
nuhua yɛ ɛzulolɛ, ɔle ɛzɛkyelɛ ngome.
34Ɛbanlo wɔatafe nuhua,
na wɔazɔ ɛ ti enrinli wɔadudu ye,
wɔarelerele ɛ kɛnra azo;
ɔluakɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.”
35Yemɔti Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Kɛmɔ wɔmaa ɛ rɛle ɛvi me na wɔye me wɔdo ɛ nzi la ati, ɛdawɔ soa wɔ tuutuulilɛ nee wɔ adwɔmanebɔlɛ ne mɔ anwo ndeanlɛ ne.”
Nyamenle ndeanlɛ mɔɔ wɔ mediema mraalɛ nwiɔ ne anwo zo la
36Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, “Sonla ra, tea Ɔhola nee Ɔhɔleba. Fa bɛ bɛkyi ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛyɛ la si bɛ nyunlu. 37Ɔluakɛ bɛdo awuvolɛvalɛ mɛla ne, yɛɛ mogya wɔ bɛ sa anwo. Bɛva bɛ awozonle ɛzonlenlɛ bɛzɛkye agyalɛ, na bɛva mralɛ mrenya mɔɔ me nee bɛ wole la bɛbɔ azu bɛmaa awozonle bɛmaa bɛdo bɛli. 38Eza bɛyɛ ɛhye noko bɛtia me: bɛva kenle ko ne bɛgua me Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anwo evinli, bɛbulu me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle mɛla ne azo. 39Ɔluakɛ kenle ko ne ala mɔɔ bɛhunle bɛ mra ne mɔ bɛmanle bɛ awozonle ne mɔ la, bɛrale me Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu bɛraguale ɛkɛ ne evinli. Na nea, debie mɔɔ bɛyɛle la ɛne.
40“Bɛzoanle menli bɛmanle bɛhɔle moa moa bɛhɔvale mrenya. Mrenya zɔhane mɔ ati, bɛbiale bɛ nwo, bɛdole bɛ nye anzi, bɛvale bɛ anwoneɛ bɛzieziele bɛ nwo; 41bɛdɛnlanle ehwili kɛnlɛma mɔɔ bɛzie ɛkponle nu na bɛva me ɛyɛlɛ evuanlɛ ne nee me nwole ne bɛzie zolɛ la anu. 42Menli mɔɔ ɛhwee ɛnvane bɛ nwo la nee ye a lua a, yɛɛ eza menli mgbane bie, nzabovoma mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ vi kpɔkɛ bie anu a rale la doale ye. Bɛvale ngɛba bɛguguale mraalɛ ne mɔ asa na bɛvale arelemgbunli ahyɛlɛ ngɛnlɛma bɛzoɔzoale bɛ. 43Na menganle kɛ: Asoo kɛkala, mrenya ne mɔ mɔɔ nee ye bɔ tuutuu ɛbɛla ne la ɛnnwu kɛ bɛlɛto awuvolɛvalɛ mɛla ne? 44Ɔluakɛ bɛ nee ye hɔlale na bɛvale ye kɛ mrenya fa tuutuu raalɛ la. Zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛ nee Ɔhola nee ɔ diema Ɔhɔleba yɛle bɔle bɛ ɛbɛla mgbane mgbane ne a. 45Na menli mɔɔ di pɛlepɛle la babua bɛ ndɛne na bɛabua bɛ awuvolɛvalɛ nwo fɔlɛ. Eza bɛdi mraalɛ mɔɔ ku menli la anwo fɔlɛ, ɔboalekɛ bɛzɛkye agyalɛ yɛɛ mogya wɔ bɛ sa anwo.”
46Kɛ Awulae Nyamenle ne se la ɛne, “Bɛva menli dɔɔnwo bɛhɔ bɛ nwo zo, bɛnwunlonwunla bɛ na bɛve bɛ nwo ninyɛne. 47Bɛzi bɛ awolɛ, na bɛva dadeɛ bɛvoa bɛ. Bɛhu bɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ na bɛyela bɛ azua. 48Zɛhae a mebayɛ meadua adwɔmanebɔlɛ wɔ maanle ne anu a, amaa yeayɛ kɔkɔbɔlɛ yeamaa mraalɛ kɔsɔɔti na bɛambɔ adwɔmane ɛbɛla, kɛmɔ bɛmɛ bɛbɔ la. 49Bɛ adwɔmanebɔlɛ ne babɔ bɛ ti na bɛdabɛ bɛali bɛ awozonle ɛzonlenlɛ nwo ɛtane ne mɔ anwo ɛzonle, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Awulae Nyamenle ne a.”

english_text:
A Cooking Pot
1Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem. 3Then tell my rebellious people:
“Pour water in a cooking pot
and set it over a fire.
* 4Throw in the legs and shoulders
of your finest sheep
and put in the juicy bones.
5Pile wood underneath the pot,
and let the meat and bones
boil until they are done.”
6These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it. 7The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground. 8But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
9I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood, 10so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch. 11Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust. 12I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
13Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it. 14That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Ezekiel's Wife Dies
15The Lord said, 16“Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry. 17Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
18One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me, 19and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
20I answered:
The Lord God says 21he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed. 22Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat. 23You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
24I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
25The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well. 26On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened. 27Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Danesɛne ne mɔɔ ɛlɔ nrɛnlana la
1Bɛ nee yɛ hɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ ngɔnla ne anu, siane bulu ne kenle bulu ne azo, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2 Ɔse, “Sonla ra, kɛlɛ ɛnɛ kenle ye duma. Ɛnɛ kenle ye Babelonia belemgbunli ɛva ɛlɔnema ɛbɛnra ɛyia Gyɛlusalɛm. 3Bu atuadelɛma ɛhye mɔ ɛrɛlɛ na ka kile bɛ kɛ, medame Awulae Nyamenle, mese:
Bɛva danesɛne ne bɛzie senle zo,
bɛva nzule bɛgua nu.
4Bɛva nane azinli ne mɔ bɛgua nu,
ye ɛleka biala mɔɔ le kpalɛ, ye ɛzɔlɛ nee ye
abɛsa ne mɔ;
bɛva mbowule kpalɛ ne mɔ noko bɛgua nu.
5Bɛnlea nu bɛye nyɛmoa ne mɔ anu kpalɛ ne,
bɛhua senle ɔ bo;
bɛdo nane ahunguma ahunguma ne mɔ;
bɛdo ye mbowule ne mɔ noko.”
6Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Munzule ɛha ahɔdiawu suakpole ne, munzule ɛha zolɛ danesɛne ne mɔɔ ɛlɔ nrɛnlana na nuhua nrɛnlana ne ɛtɛtule la. Bɛyeye nuhua nane azinli ne mɔ ngoko, bɛmmakpa nu. 7Mogya ne mɔɔ yeha yegua la tɛbɔ zolɛ. Yeandwi yeangua anwea nu na anwea aheda zolɛ; ɔhwinle ɔguale bolɛ tandane zo. 8Memaa mogya ne mɔɔ yeha yegua la ɛla bolɛ ne azo, amaa yeaha me ɛya na meali nzenralɛ.”
9Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Munzule ɛha ahɔdiawu suakpole ne. Medame noko mebahua ɛyɛne meamaa ɔ nwo zo ahɔ anwuma kpalɛ. 10Bɛhuohua ɛyɛzinli ne mɔ anloa, bɛva senle bɛgua nu, bɛmaa nane ne ɛbe kpalɛ, na akee bɛwola subue ne mɔɔ wɔ nwolɛ la, na bɛhakyi mbowule ne mɔ bɛgua senle ne anu bɛyela bɛ. 11Akee bɛva danesɛne mgbane ne bɛzie senle ne azo, bɛmaa ɔlɔ kpalɛ, ɔdɔlɔ woonwu na kɔbele ne ɛholo ɛheda evinli nee nrɛnlana biala azo. 12Medame, mevɛ mgbane. Senle ne angola kɔbele ne kolo yeammaa yeangeda nrɛnlana ne azo. 13Wɔ adwɔmane ɛbɛla mgbane mgbane ne a le nrɛnlana ne mɔɔ andu la. Kɛmɔ anrɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ metu ɛ nwo evinli ne amuala, noko ɛ nwo anvie, na ɛ nwo evinli ne bie tɛbɔ ɛkɛ ne la, ɛ nwo ɛnrɛvie ɛlɛ, kyesɛ mewola me ɛya kpole ne megua ɛ nwo zo na me kunlu adwo. 14Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a, mebayɛ mɔɔ meha la. Menrɛzia me nzi, menrɛze anwunvɔne yɛɛ menrɛvu me nwo. Mebadea bɛ, kɛmɔ bɛ nyɛleɛ nee bɛ ndenle ne mɔ si de la. Medame, Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.”
Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne aye ne ewule
15Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, 16“Sonla ra, nea, mefa kɛlɛ kokye meaye ɛ ye ne mɔɔ ɛkulo ye kɛ debie la meavi ɛ nye zo, noko ɔnle kɛ ɛsu ye anzɛɛ ɛdi nyane, yɛɛ ɔnle kɛ ɛsuosua wɔ adɛladeɛ nu. 17Ɛbagu ɛnwomenle, noko ɔnle kɛ awie te, yɛɛ mmakile kɛ ɛlɛdi nyane. Fa wɔ abɔtile ne bɔ ɛ ti na fa wɔ mgbɔlaboa ne wula, mmakeda ɛ nyunlu yɛɛ mmadi aleɛ mɔɔ kile kɛ ɛlɛdi nyane la.”
18Yemɔti nwonlomɔ ne menganle mengilele menli ne, na ye nɔsolɛ nu me ye wule. Aleɛ hyenle bieko na ye nwonlomɔ ne menyɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me la. 19Na menli ne bizale me kɛ, “Ɛnrɛhile ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ ɛlɛyɛ la abo ɛnrɛhile yɛ ɔ?”
20Na menganle mengilele bɛ kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛze me kɛ, menga mengile Yizilayɛma kɛ, 21Awulae Nyamenle ne se: Bɛnlea, mebagua me Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anwo evinli. Ɔle debie mɔɔ bɛfa bɛtu bɛ nwo a, bɛ nye ɛralɛ mɔɔ bɛ nye kuku nwolɛ a. Bɛ mra mrenya nee bɛ mra mraalɛ mɔɔ bɛgyakyile bɛ bɛ nzi la badɔ dadeɛ nloa. 22Na bɛbayɛ mɔɔ meyɛ la bie: bɛnrɛheda bɛ nyunlu yɛɛ bɛnrɛli aleɛ mɔɔ kile kɛ bɛlɛdi nyane la. 23Bɛbabɔ bɛ abɔtile ne mɔ, bɛawula mgbɔlaboa; bɛnrɛzu yɛɛ bɛnrɛli nyane. Bɛ ninyɛndane ne mɔ bamaa bɛanwa na bɛazu bɛ kunlu bɛakponle bɛahile bɛ nwo ngoko. 24Yizikeɛle bayɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ amaa bɛ, na mɔɔ yeyɛ la, bie yɛɛ bɛdabɛ noko bɛbayɛ a. Na saa ɛhye mɔ sisi a, yɛɛ bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Awulae Nyamenle ne a.”
25Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Na wɔmɔ, Sonla ra, kenle ne mɔɔ mebaza bɛ mealie bɛ aranemgbole ne, bɛ anyelielɛ nee bɛ anyunlunyia, bɛ nye ɛralɛ ne, nee mɔɔ bɛ nye kuku nwolɛ, bɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ la, 26kenle ko zɔhane mɔɔ mebayɛ ɛhye la, awie mɔɔ vile ɛsalɛ la yɛɛ baraha ahile wɔ a. 27Kenle ko ne ɛ nloa bade na wɔadendɛ wɔahile ahenle ne mɔɔ vile ɛsalɛ la. Ɛbadendɛ, ɛnrɛdɔ mumule bieko. Yemɔti ɛbayɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ wɔamaa bɛ, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_text:
Judgment on Ammon
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon 3and tell them:
You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners. 4Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk. 5Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
6You hated Israel so much that you clapped and shouted and celebrated. 7And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
Judgment on Moab
8 The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation. 9So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim. 10The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever, 11Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.”
Judgment on Edom
12 The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah. 13So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan. 14I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.”
Judgment on Philistia
15 The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them. 16Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast. 17In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Amɔn la
1 Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, 2“Sonla ra, kakyi ɛ nye wɔ Amɔnoma anwo zo, na ka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ tia bɛ la. 3Ka kile Amɔnoma kɛ bɛdie Awulae Nyamenle edwɛkɛ ne. Awulae Nyamenle ne se, ‘Kɛmɔ bɛdeanle nu “Mɔɔ kɛza bɛ la ɛne!” wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛvale evinli bɛhanle me ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne na bɛzɛkyele Yizilayɛ azɛlɛ ne bɛdole ye mgbane, bɛzɛkyele Dwuda maanle ne wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛhyele bɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la, 4melɛye bɛ meamaa menli ne mɔɔ wɔ Aduduleɛ la meamaa bɛava bɛ bɛayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ bɔkɔɔ. Bɛbadɛnla bɛ avinli na bɛasisi bɛ azua wɔ bɛ avinli. Bɛbali bɛ mbaka ma ne mɔ na bɛanlo bɛ nlankɛ nyɛfonzule. 5Mebamaa Relaba ayɛ adidileka amaa afunlumu, na Amɔnoma sua ne ayɛ nyɛmoa tunli, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.’
6“Kɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle ne mese la ɛne: Kɛmɔ bɛbɔle bɛ sa nu, bɛzile agole na bɛ ngunzi ti bɛ nye liele bɛ nwo dɔɔnwo bɛtiale Yizilayɛma la ati, 7bɛnlea, meva bɛ nwo ɛya kpole, na mebaye bɛ meamaa maanle maanle ne mɔ, na bɛava bɛ kɛ konle nu afedeɛ. Mebaye bɛ meavi menli avinli na meaminli bɛ bo zo wɔ maanle maanle avinli. Mebazɛkye bɛ bɔkɔɔ, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”
Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Mowabe la
8 Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Kɛmɔ Mowabe hanle kɛ, Dwudama ɛyɛ kɛ maanle maanle gyɛne ne mɔ la ati, 9mebamaa bɛaho bɛava azuamgbole mɔɔ wɔ Mowabe maanle ne ɛweɛne zo, mɔɔ bɔ maanle ne anwo bane la amuala, Bɛte Gyɛhyemo, Beeyale Mɛyɔn, yɛɛ Keleateeyem boka nwolɛ. 10Mebaye Mowabe maanle ne meaboka Amɔnoma maanle ne meamaa maanle maanle mɔɔ wɔ aduduleɛ la ayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ, amaa bɛangakye ye bieko wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ avinli. 11Mebadea Mowabema, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”
Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Yidɔm la
12 Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Kɛmɔ Yidɔm vale atisesebɛ lile Dwudama nzenralɛ, na bɛvonle wɔ nzenralɛlilɛ ne anu la ati, Mal 1.2-5 13kɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle ne mese la ɛne: Mebadea Yidɔmma, na meahu menli nee nyɛmoa mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la amuala, na meamaa maanle ne adɔ mgbane. Menli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la amuala, ɔvi Timan mɔɔ kɔdwu Didan la badɔ dadeɛ nloa. 14Mebamaa Yizilayɛma aha Yidɔm senle meava meali nzenralɛ. Bɛbayɛ Yidɔmma, kɛmɔ me ɛya ne kpole si de la, na bɛanwu me nzenralɛlilɛ ne deɛ holɛ, medame, Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.”
Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Filisitia la
15 Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Filisitiama le abolɛ yɛɛ bɛvale ɛkpɔlɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ la a bɛlile bɛ nzenralɛ ne a. 16Yemɔti medame Awulae Nyamenle mese, mebadea Filisitiama nee Kɛlɛtema, meabɔ bɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ, na meazɛkye bɛ menli mɔɔ ɛha mɔɔ wɔ ɛnweanloa la. 17Mebava ɛya ndeanlɛ kpole kpalɛ a meali nzenralɛ ne a, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_text:
Judgment on the City of Tyre
1 Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing,
“Jerusalem has fallen!
It used to be powerful,
a center of trade.
Now the city is shattered,
and we will take its place.”
3Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore. 4They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock, 5where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed 6and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
7King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops. 8First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you. 9He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers. 10He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city. 11His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground. 12The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea. 13 You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps, 14because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
15The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death. 16 The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear 17and sing this funeral song:
“The great city beside the sea
is destroyed!
Its people once ruled the coast
and terrified everyone there.
18But now Tyre is in ruins,
and the people on the coast
stare at it in horror
and tremble in fear.”
19I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you 20and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people. 21 You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Taya la
1Bɛhyele yɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ bulu nee ko ne anu, siane ko ne kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la azo, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2Ɔse, “Sonla ra, Taya ɛha Gyɛlusalɛm anwo edwɛkɛ kɛ, ‘Ɛhɛe, bɛbubu menli ne anlenkɛ kpole ne; akee yela nwolɛ wanaanwo yemaa me. Kɛkala mɔɔ yedɔ mgbane la, me sa baha mɔɔ meminlinle ye la amuala.’
3“Yemɔti medame Awulae Nyamenle mese, ɛdawɔ Taya, meyɛ wɔ kpɔvolɛ, na mebamaa maanle maanle dɔɔnwo ara ɛ nwo zo, kɛmɔ nyevile azɛlɛkye bu la. 4Bɛbazɛkye Taya bane ne mɔ, na bɛabubu ye tawa ne mɔ bɛagua aze. Mebadu ye ɛnwea ne kɔsɔɔti meagua, meamaa yeaha ye bolɛ tandane ne mɔɔ la azɛlɛ ne abo la. 5Ɔbayɛ ɛleka mɔɔ fɛlɛhyelɛma rɛlɛ bɛ avonle a, wɔ nyevile ne avinli. Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a. Ɔbayɛ afedeɛ yeamaa maanle maanle dɔɔnwo. 6Bɛbahu menli mɔɔ wɔ azuamgbole ne mɔ azo la, na bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”
7Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Mebava belemgbunli kpole mɔɔ bo bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛ nwo zo, Babelonia belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza meavi sɔlɔ nehane, meamaa yeava mgbɔnwɔ, konle ehwili, ɛlɔnema mɔɔ tɛnla mgbɔnwɔ zo nee ɛlɔnema dɔɔnwo kpalɛ yeara Taya anwo zo. 8Ɔbahu bɛ mra mraalɛ wɔ bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo; ɔbamaa ye ɛlɔnema abɛnra ayia bɛ, bɛbavunvu ahuma, bɛahuohua ɛnwea edukue edukue, na bɛava enyinlike bɛalie bɛ nwo bane bɛaho bɛatia bɛ. 9Ɔbamaa bɛava mbaka mgbole bɛasisi bɛ azuamgbole bane ne mɔ kɛ bɛbubu bɛ bɛagua, na yeamaa bɛava akuma bɛagologolo bɛ tawa ne mɔ bɛagua. 10Ye mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ bazo dɔɔnwo kpalɛ mɔɔ bɛ nzi munlutu bɔbɔ baheda bɛ nwo zo a. Ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ nee konle ehwili ne mɔ la agyakɛ abo nee bɛ ne bakpusu bɛ azuamgbole bane ne mɔ, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔkɛze kɛ akee ɔfo azua ne mɔ azo kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛli konim la. 11Ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ la barava bɛ azuamgbole gua ne mɔ, bɛbahu bɛ menli ne mɔ, na bɛ mpila mgbole ne mɔ babubu agua. 12Ɛlɔnema ne bave bɛ nwo ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti, bɛ anwonyia nee bɛ ninyɛne adɔne, bɛbabubu bɛ azuamgbole bane ne mɔ nee bɛ azua ngɛnlɛma ne mɔ bɛagua. Bɛbavuandi bɛ awolɛ, dubinli nee ɛnwea bɛagua azule ne mɔ anu. 13 Mebamaa bɛagyakyi bɛ edwɛne mɔɔ bɛto la, na awie ɛnrɛde bɛ getaa ne mɔ ane bieko. 14Mebayɛ bɛ kɛ bodane mɔɔ ɛhwee ɛnle zolɛ la, na bɛayɛ kɛ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛrɛlɛ avonle la. Bɛnrɛkyekye bɛ azua ne mɔ bieko, ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ meha a.”
15Awulae Nyamenle hanle ɛhye hilele Taya amra. Ɔse, “Saa bɛba kɛ bɛbahu bɛ a, bɛ menli mɔɔ ɛbodɛboda la ɛkponlenlɛ nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛho bɛgua la azedɔlɛ bakpusu bɛ ɛnweanloa azua ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti. 16 Akee arelemgbunli mɔɔ wɔ ɛnweanloa maanle maanle ne mɔ anu la vi bɛ ebia ne mɔ anu badwazo; bɛbayeye bɛ arelemgbunli adɛladeɛ ne mɔ, na bɛayeye bɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ nee bɛ adɛladeɛ mɔɔ bɛnwo bɛ nloa la. Bɛ nwo bawozo bɛ; bɛbakpofokpofo aze na bɛ nwo awozo mekɛ biala, na bɛ rɛle abɔ bɛmɛ bɛ nwo. 17Na bɛbado edwɛne bɛaye awolɛ wɔ bɛmɛ bɛ ti, na bɛaha kɛ:
O suakpole mɔɔ lɛ duma,
ɛ bo zo ɛbɔ bɔkɔɔ.
Ɛnee ɛle suakpole mɔɔ yɛ se, mɔɔ sie nyevile a,
ɛdawɔ nee menli mɔɔ wɔ zo la,
anwo ka ɛzulolɛ
maa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛde azɛlɛ ne azo la.
18Kenle mɔɔ bɛhonle bɛdɔle la,
mbɔra ne mɔ wozole.
Ɛhɛe, mbɔra mɔɔ wɔ nyevile nu la
arɛle bɔle wɔ bɛ ɛzɛkyelɛ nwo.”
19Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Saa meyɛ bɛ suakpole ne suadu kɛ azuamgbole mɔɔ awie ɛnde zolɛ la, memaa nyevile ne bu fa bɛ nwo zo, na azɛlɛkye ne mɔ keda bɛ nwo zo a, 20akee meavuandi bɛ meamaa bɛahɔboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɔ ewule kuma nu la anwo, mebaye bɛ meamaa bɛahɔboka mɔmoane amra anwo, meamaa bɛahɔboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ ɛbolɔ maanle nu na bɛde alɔbɔlɛ nu la anwo, amaa bɛannyia ɛleka bɛandɛnla anzɛɛ bɛannyia ɛleka wɔ teasema azɛlɛ zo. 21 Mebamaa bɛ awieleɛ ayɛ ɛzulolɛ na bɛ bo zo aminli bɔkɔɔ. Bɛbakpondɛ bɛ bo zo, na bɛnrɛnwu bɛ.” Awulae Nyamenle ne a se a.

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Tyre
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre, 3the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me:
Tyre, you brag about
your perfect beauty,
4and your control of the sea.
You are a ship
built to perfection.
5Builders used cypress trees
from Mount Hermon
to make your planks
and a cedar tree from Lebanon
for your tall mast.
6Oak trees from Bashan
were shaped into oars;
pine trees from Cyprus
were cut for your deck,
which was then decorated
with strips of ivory.
7The builders used fancy linen
from Egypt for your sails,
so everyone could see you.
Blue and purple cloth
from Cyprus was used
to shade your deck.
8Men from Sidon and Arvad
did the rowing,
and your own skilled workers
were the captains.
9Experienced men from Byblos
repaired any damages.
Sailors from all over
shopped at the stores
in your port.
10Brave soldiers from Persia,
Lydia, and Libya
served in your navy,
protecting you with shields
and helmets,
and making you famous.
11Your guards came from
Arvad and Cilicia,
and men from Gamad
stood watch in your towers.
With their weapons
hung on your walls,
your beauty was complete.
12Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products. 13The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze, 14and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules. 15You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods. 16Edom traded emeralds, purple cloth, embroidery, fine linen, coral, and rubies. 17Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise. 18The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar. 19Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices. 20The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets, 21while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats. 22Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products. 23You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad, 24and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope. 25 Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go.
You were like a ship
loaded with heavy cargo
26and sailing across the sea,
but you were wrecked
by strong eastern winds.
27Everything on board was lost—
your valuable cargo,
your sailors and carpenters,
merchants and soldiers.
28The shouts of your drowning crew
were heard on the shore.
29Every ship is deserted;
rowers and sailors and captains
all stand on shore,
30mourning for you.
They show their sorrow
by putting dust on their heads
and rolling in ashes;
31they shave their heads
and dress in sackcloth
as they cry in despair.
32In their grief they sing
a funeral song for you:
“Tyre, you were greater
than all other cities.
But now you lie in silence
at the bottom of the sea.
33“Nations that received
your merchandise
were always pleased;
kings everywhere got rich
from your costly goods.
34But now you are wrecked
in the deep sea,
with your cargo and crew
scattered everywhere.
35People living along the coast
are shocked at the news.
Their rulers are horrified,
and terror is written
across their faces.
36The merchants of the world
can't believe what happened.
Your death was gruesome,
and you are gone forever.”
translation_text:
Taya ɛzɛneyɛlɛ nwo edwɛne
1Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, 2“Akee wɔmɔ, sonla ra, ye Taya awolɛ, na ka kile ye kɛ, 3Wɔmɔ mɔɔ bɛkyekye wɔ nyevile nloa, menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛnwea ɛnwea gualilɛ ɛleka, kɛ Awulae Nyamenle se la ɛne:
O Taya, wɔmɔ wɔha kɛ,
wɔ anwofɛlɛko di munli.
4Wɔ ɛweɛne ne mɔ wɔ nyevile kunlu lɔ;
menli mɔɔ kyekyele wɔ la kyekyele wɔ kɛnlɛma.
5Bɛvale Hɛmɔn Boka mbaka ɛsesebɛ bɛyɛle mgbunla,
bɛvale Lɛbanɔn sida mbaka
bɛyɛle wɔ meli avela mbaka.
6Beehyan mbaka ɛsesebɛ a
bɛvale bɛzele bɛ ndahoma a;
bɛvale Saepelɛse ɛnweanloa mbaka
bɛzɛle wɔ meli ne mɔ anu,
na bɛvale ɛzɛlɛ bɛduoduale nu.
7Bɛvale Yigyibiti lenen ɛdanlɛ kɛnlɛma mɔɔ bɛnwo
ɔ nloa la
bɛyɛle bɛ meli ne mɔ avela,
bɛhilele kɛ ɔle bɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ.
Bɛvale Saepelɛse ndanlɛ kɔkɔlɛ nee buluwu
bɛbole kpɔda bɛdɛnlanle ɔ bo;
bɛbole belandane bɛ meli ne mɔ anu.
8Saedɛnema nee Avadema a hanle meli ne mɔ a;
ɛdawɔ wɔ menli mɔɔ ze nyevile nye zo la
lile bɛ ɛlɛne bo hanle meli ne mɔ.
9Bebolɔsoma mɔɔ ze adwinli kpalɛ,
duoduale bɛ meli ayiazo ne mɔ,
Nyevile nye meli nee nuhua menli kɔsɔɔti
nee bɛ ralile gua.
10“Sogyama vi Pɛhyea, Ledea, yɛɛ Lebeya rayɛle gyima wɔ wɔ ɛlɔnema anu. Bɛ nee bɛ dɛnlanle, bɛvale bɛ ahyɛlɛ nee bɛ enyinlike bɛhendɛhendanle bɛ azua nu; bɛlile konim bɛmanle bɛ, bɛmanle bɛ nyunlu rale anyia. 11Ɛlɔnema mɔɔ vi Avade nee Hilɛke la zinzale bɛ bane ne mɔ, yɛɛ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ vi Gamade la zinzale bɛ tawa ne mɔ. Bɛhendɛhendanle bɛ enyinlike ne mɔ wɔ bɛ bane ne mɔ anwo na bɛmanle bɛ anwofɛlɛko ne lile munli.
12“Wɔ ninyɛne ngɛnlɛma dɔɔnwo ne ati, Sepeenema nee wɔ lile gua na bɛvale bɛ dwɛtɛ fufule, bulalɛ, kyɛnze, yɛɛ sumi bɛmanle wɔ bɛliele ninyɛne. 13Gilikima, Tubalema, yɛɛ Mihyɛkema nee wɔ lile gua na bɛdɔnenle menli nee kɔbele ninyɛne bɛmanle wɔ bɛliele ninyɛne bɛvile wɔ ɛkɛ. 14Bɛte Togama amra dɔnenle bɛ mgbɔnwɔ, konle mgbɔnwɔ, yɛɛ mgbɔnwɔndua manle wɔ liele ninyɛne. 15Menli mɔɔ wɔ Didan la nee wɔ lile gua; menli mɔɔ de ɛnweanloa la rɛlɛle wɔ ɛzɛlɛ nee mbaka ɛsesebɛ bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye ɛbɔni la liele ninyɛne. 16Wɔ ninyɛne ngakyile dɔɔnwo ne mɔ ati, Yidɔmma nee wɔ lile gua na bɛdɔnenle ezukoa bolɛ anye asuomenle, ndanlɛ kɔkɔlɛ, ndanlɛ mɔɔ bɛnwo ɔ nloa nee nuhua, lenen ndanlɛ ngɛnlɛma, yɛɛ ezukoa awolɛ dɔɔnwo bɛmanle wɔ bɛliele ninyɛne. 17Dwudama nee Yizilayɛma nee wɔ lile gua. Bɛrɛlɛle wɔ hwiiti, ɔlivi, feege, wolɛ, nwole, yɛɛ ɛnlomedazia na bɛliele wɔ ninyɛne ne mɔ bie. 18Wɔ ninyɛne ngakyile dɔɔnwo ne mɔ ati, Dɛmasekɛsema nee wɔ lile gua na bɛdɔnenle Hɛlebɔn nwanye, mboane enrinli fufule, 19yɛɛ Sahɛɛ nwanye bɛmanle wɔ bɛliele wɔ ninyɛne ne mɔ bie. Bɛdɔnenle mbulalɛ mɔɔ bɛva bɛli adwinli yɛɛ aleɛdonlɛ ninyɛne evuanlɛ bɛmanle wɔ. 20Didan nee wɔ lile gua dɔnenle ɛkpɔnwɔ zo ndanlɛ manle wɔ. 21Arelebiama nee Kida arelemgbunli a le menli mɔɔ ɛ nye liele bɛ nwo kpalɛ wɔ mboane mralɛ, mboane nyinli, yɛɛ mbɔnkye gualilɛ nu a. Ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛvale bɛ nee wɔ lile gua la ɛne. 22Hyibama nee Releemama nee wɔ lile gua; bɛdɔnenle bɛ aleɛdonlɛ ninyɛne evuanlɛ kpalɛ, ezukoa awolɛ kpalɛ kpalɛ, yɛɛ ezukoa nvutuke bɛmanle wɔ bɛliele wɔ ninyɛne kpalɛ kpalɛ ne mɔ bie. 23Hɛlan, Kani, Yidɛn, Ahyɔɔ, yɛɛ Kelemade nee wɔ lile gua. 24Bɛ nee wɔ lile ndakpa gua, yɛɛ akee ndanlɛ buluwu, ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛnwo, kapɛte futufutu mɔɔ bɛva nyɛma bɛkyekye bɛmia nu la amuala. 25 Meli vi Tahyehye yɛɛ batwe wɔ ninyɛne kɔ a.
“Yemɔti ɛnee ɛle kɛ meli mɔɔ la nyevile nye,
mɔɔ ninyɛne ɛyi ye tɛkɛɛ la.
26Menli mɔɔ ka wɔ la ɛva wɔ ɛdo nyevile nye.
Aduduleɛ anwoma ɛnloma wɔ nyevile buma nu.
27Wɔ anwonyia, wɔ ninyɛne adɔne,
wɔ menli mɔɔ ka meli nee zolɛ neavolɛma,
wɔ kapentama nee adenduvoma,
ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ɛlɛ bɛ la amuala
nee menli mɔɔ ɛlɛ bɛ la amuala
banloma gbodogbodo wɔ nyevile kunlu lɔ,
wɔ kenle ne mɔɔ ɛbanwu ɛ nyunlu la.
28Wɔ menli mɔɔ nea wɔ meli ne mɔ azo la
ɛzunlɛ dielie maanle ne anu amuala.
29“Menli mɔɔ ka meli ne la fo gua ndahoma zo
weɛ azule ba ɛnweazo.
Bɛ muala bɛbagyinla ɛnwea ne anloa,
30bɛsu alɔbɔlɛ ɛzunlɛ, bɛye awolɛ.
Bɛfula anwea bɛgua bɛ ti zo,
bɛweweɛ bɛ nwo nzonle nu.
31Wɔmɔ ati, bɛkpa bɛ ti, bɛkeda ɛrele,
na bɛfa nyane bɛsu alɔbɔlɛ ɛzunlɛ.
32Bɛye awolɛ wɔ bɛ ɛzunlɛ nu,
na bɛye awolɛ kɛ:
‘Suakpole boni a wɔ nyevile avinli
mɔɔ bɛzɛkye ye bɛdɛla Taya a?
33Mekɛ mɔɔ wɔ ninyɛne adɔne vi nyevile nzi ba la,
ɛmanle menli dɔɔnwo anye liele;
wɔ anwonyia nee wɔ ninyɛne adɔne
manle azɛlɛ ye azo arelemgbunli nyianle bɛ nwo.
34Wɔmɔ a nyevile ne ɛbɔ ɛ bo zo
wɔ azule buma ne anu lɔ la;
wɔ ninyɛne adɔne nee menli mɔɔ ka meli ne la,
nee wɔ ɛnloma gbodogbodo.’
35“Wɔ anwubɛnyunlu ne ɛmaa awie biala mɔɔ de ɛnweanloa la ahonle ɛdu; na ɛzulolɛ ɛmaa bɛ arelemgbunli nyunlu ɛdo. 36Gualilɛma mɔɔ wɔ menli ne anu la ahonle dule kɛ wɔ awieleɛ ɛwie ɛzulolɛ zɛhae, na ɛnrɛkpazi bieko ɛlɛ na aloa abɔ a.”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Tyre
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying:
You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human. 3You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
4Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver. 5You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
6You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God, 7will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get. 8Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
9When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human. 10Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
11The Lord said:
12Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying:
At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking. 13You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born. 14I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
15You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things. 16You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
17It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you. 18You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood, 19and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever.
Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
20 The Lord said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon 22and tell its people:
I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy. 23I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
24When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
A Blessing for Israel
25The Lord God said:
Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob. 26They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_text:
Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Taya belemgbunli ne la
1Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ka kile Taya belemgbunli ne kɛ, medame Awulae Nyamenle mese: Kɛmɔ ɛtu ɛ nwo la ati, wɔha mgbole kɛ, ‘Medame, mele nyamenle, mede nyamenle ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti ebia nu, wɔ nyevile kunlu nehane,’ noko ɛle sonla, ɛnle nyamenle. Ɛyɛ ɛ nwo kɛ ɛze nrɛlɛbɛ kɛ nyamenle bie, 3na ɛze nrɛlɛbɛ bɔbɔ ɛtɛla Daneɛle, yemɔti debie biala ɛnvea wɔ. 4Wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ nee wɔ ndelebɛbo ti wɔnyia ɛ nwo, na wɔboɔboa ezukoa nvutuke nee dwɛtɛ fufule dɔɔnwo anloa wɔ wɔ gya ne mɔ anu. 5Wɔ gualilɛ nu nrɛlɛbɛ kpole ne mɔɔ ɛlɛ la ati, wɔ anwonyia ɛzo dɔɔnwo, na ɔmaa ɛmemaa ɛ nwo zo.
6“Yemɔti kɛ medame, Awulae Nyamenle mese la ɛne: Kɛmɔ wɔyɛ ɛ nwo kɛ ɛze nrɛlɛbɛ kɛ nyamenle bie la ati, 7nea, mebamaa nyɛvolɛ maanle anwo ɛzulolɛ bie ara ɛ nwo zo. Bɛbahwe dadeɛ bɛazɛkye wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ ninyɛne ngɛnlɛma ne mɔ, bɛamaa ɛ nyunlu adɔ aze abɔ. 8Bɛbavuandi wɔ bɛado ewule kuma ne anu, na wɔawu dadeɛ nloa wɔ nyevile kunlu nehane. 9Asoo ɛbaha kɛ, ‘Mele nyamenle,’ wɔ menli mɔɔ ɛlɛku wɔ la anyunlu? Ɛle sonla, ɛnle nyamenle wɔ menli mɔɔ ɛlɛbodɛboda wɔ la asa anu. 10Ɛbawu anyiemgba ewule wɔ nyɛvolɛ asa anu; ɔluakɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle yɛɛ mese a.”
Taya belemgbunli ne azedɔlɛ
11Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me bieko. 12Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ye awolɛ gua Taya belemgbunli ne ati zo, na se ye kɛ, medame, Awulae Nyamenle, mese: Ɛnee ɛle sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ di munli, ɛze nrɛlɛbɛ na wɔ anwofɛlɛko di munli. 13Ɛnee ɛwɔ Yidɛn, Nyamenle tola ne anu; ezukoa bolɛ biala mɔɔ anwo hyia la, menvale mengedale wɔ. Ezukoa awolɛ, kanɛlia, topaze, gyasepa, kelesɔlaete, bɛlele, ɔnekese, safaya, kɛbɛnkele, yɛɛ ɛmelade yɛɛ bɛvale bɛduoduale wɔ adɛladeɛ nu a. Kenle ko ne ala mɔɔ bɛbɔle wɔ la yɛɛ bɛboɔboale bɛ nloa bɛmanle wɔ a. 14Wɔmɔ, menyɛle wɔ tease abɔdeɛ mɔɔ mekpokpa wɔ nwole la menziele wɔ Nyamenle boka nwuanzanwuanza ne azo, na ɛluoluale awolɛ guaanye zo. 15Ɔvi kenle ko ne mɔɔ bɛbɔle wɔ la, ɛ nwo annyia nvonleɛ biala, hɔdwule kɛ ɛtane rale wɔ nu la. 16Wɔ gualilɛ ne yɛle kpole la ati, ɛbɔle kɔdiawu ɛbɛla na ɛyɛle ɛtane. Yemɔti ɛyɛle bɛkyi debie wɔ me sa nu, na menvuandinle wɔ wɔ Nyamenle boka nwuanzanwuanza ne azo mendele aze, na tease abɔdeɛ ne mɔɔ sinza wɔ la voanle wɔ vile awolɛ guaanye ne mɔ avinli. 17Ɛlile wɔ kɛnlɛma nzi ɛdule ɛ nwo, ɛlile wɔ kpoleyɛlɛ nzi ɛzɛkyele wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ. Menvuandinle wɔ mendole aze, menyele ɛ nwo zo ɛdanlɛ mengilele arelemgbunli kɛ bɛnlea wɔ. 18Wɔ ɛtane dɔɔnwo ne mɔ ati, ɛlile gua ɛtane ɛvale ɛzɛkyele wɔ ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ. Yemɔti memanle senle zɔle bɛ avinli na ɔyelale wɔ ɔhunle wɔ. Awie biala mɔɔ anye babɔ ɛ nwo zo la banwu kɛ wɔdɔ nzonle wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo. 19Bɛdabɛ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ bɛze wɔ wɔ maanle maanle avinli la arɛle babɔ ɛ nwo, kɛ wɔ awieleɛ ɛwie ɛzulolɛ zɛhae, na ɛnrɛkpazi bieko ɛlɛ na aloa abɔ a.”
Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ tia Saedɛn la
20 Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, 21“Sonla ra, kakyi ɛ nye Saedɛn na ka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne tia ye kɛ, 22Awulae Nyamenle ne se, ‘Saedɛn, meyɛ wɔ kpɔvolɛ, na mebamaa menli aye me ayɛlɛ wɔ wɔmɔ ɛ ti. Bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ me nee wɔ kɛli, kɛmɔ ɔfɛta na menwɔlua ɛ nwo zo menwɔye me nwuanzanwuanzayɛlɛ ne menwɔhile la. 23Ɔluakɛ mebaye ewulenzane ɛzulolɛ bie meado ɛ nwo na mogya ava wɔ guabile ne mɔ azo. Bɛbava konle bɛadoa wɔ wɔ adenle biala azo, na bɛahu wɔ menli ne mɔ. Na bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a!’ ”
Bɛbayila Yizilayɛ
24Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Na Yizilayɛma ɛdeɛ, agbɔvolɛ maanle maanle mɔɔ ɛbɔ ɛyia bɛ la anu biala ɛnrɛhakyi ɔ nwo mbowunzaka anzɛɛ mbowule ɛnrɛwowɔ anzɛɛ ɛnrɛbodɛboda bɛ. Na bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Awulae Nyamenle ne a.”
25Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Saa meboɔboa Yizilayɛma anloa mefi maanle maanle mɔɔ mebɔ bɛ asande mehɔgua nuhua la anu, na meye me nwuanzanwuanzayɛlɛ ne mekile, wɔ maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti anye zo a, bɛbadɛnla bɛdabɛ bɛ maanle ne mɔɔ menvale memanle me sonvolɛ Gyekɔbo la anu. 26Bɛ nwo badɔ bɛ na bɛasisi azua, bɛayɛ bɛ vanye egyinli. Saa me nee maanle maanle mɔɔ zuozua bɛ, mɔɔ ɛmbu bɛ la di, kɛmɔ ɔfɛta la a, bɛbadɛnla, bɛ nwo adɔ bɛ. Na akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a.”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Egypt
1 Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people 3that I am saying:
King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy! 4I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body. 5I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh. 6 Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord.
You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick. 7When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
8So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock, 9until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things.
You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it. 10Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia. 11No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for 40 years. 12It will be the most barren place on earth. Every city in Egypt will lie in ruins during those 40 years, and I will scatter your people throughout the nations of the world.
13Then after those 40 years have passed, I will bring your people back from the places where I scattered them. 14They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom 15and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past. 16My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
17Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
18King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city. 19So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops. 20Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
21Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Yigyibiti la
1Bɛ nee yɛ hɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ bulu, siane bulu ne, kenle bulu nee nwiɔ ne azo, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2Ɔse, “Sonla ra, kakyi ɛ nye wɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne anwo, na ka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ tia ye nee Yigyibitima amuala la kile ye. Tendɛ se ye kɛ, 3Awulae Nyamenle ne se: Bɛnlea, mekpo Yigyibitima belemgbunli ne. Yeyɛ ɔ nwo nane kpole anwo ɛzulolɛ bie mɔɔ le kɛ ɛlɛnrɛne la yela azule Naele ne anu, na ɔka kɛ, ‘Medame a melɛ azule Naele ne a; medame a menyɛle a.’ 4Mebabɔ koba wɔ wɔ awudwɔlɛ nu, na meamaa fɛlɛ mɔɔ wɔ wɔ azule ne mɔ anu la abetɛbeta ɛ nwo abonle ne mɔ anu. Mebaye wɔ nee fɛlɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ betɛbeta wɔ abonle ne mɔ anu la meavi azule ne mɔ anu, 5na meavuandi bɛ meagua ɛsɛlɛ ne azo lɔ, na ɛdawɔ nee fɛlɛ mɔɔ wɔ wɔ azule ne mɔ anu la baha ɛsɛlɛ ne azo, na awie ɛnrɛsesa bɛ ɛnrɛzie bɛ. Mebava bɛ meamaa azɛlɛ ye azo nanemgbole nee nloma mɔɔ wɔ anwomanyunlu la kɛ bɛli. 6 Na Yigyibitima kɔsɔɔti banwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a!”
Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Yigyibitima yɛle bɛ nwo ndɔ baka wulera.” 7Yemɔti mekɛ mɔɔ Yizilayɛma zɔle nu dudule hisale bɛ la, bɛbubule, bɛbodɛbodale bɛ bati, bɛmanle bɛ nzi kpolokpolole na bɛ adwongu wozole. 8Yemɔti Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Mebava konle meara bɛ nwo zo, na bɛahu menli nee nane kɔsɔɔti, 9Yigyibiti maanle ne badɔ mgbane; awie biala ɛnrɛdɛnla nuhua. Na akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.
“Kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ɛhanle kɛ Azule Naele ne le wɔ ɛdeɛ, na ɛdawɔ yɛɛ ɛyɛle la ti, 10nea, mehakyi me nzi mezi wɔ nee wɔ azule ne mɔ amuala. Mebamaa Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne adɔ mgbane, ɔvi suakpole Megedɔlo mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne sɔlɔ lɔ la, yearadwu Asewan, toonwo yearadwu Sudanema ɛweɛne zo, wɔ maanle ne nyiakɛ. 11Sonla anzɛɛ nane biala agyakɛ ba ɛnrɛtia zolɛ. Awie ɛnrɛdɛnla zolɛ toonwo ɛvolɛ abulanla. 12Mebayɛ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne mgbane meado maanle maanle mɔɔ ɛdɔ mgbane la avinli. Awie ɛnrɛdɛnla ye azuamgbole ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛdɔ mgbane anzɛɛ ɛyɛ azuadu la azo toonwo ɛvolɛ abulanla wɔ azuamgbole mɔɔ ɛyɛ azuadu la avinli. Mebabɔ Yigyibitima asande meahɔgua maanle maanle zo, na meazande bɛ wɔ aneɛ ngakyile avinli.”
13Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Saa ɛvolɛ abulanla ne dwu a, mebaboɔboa Yigyibitima anloa meavi maanle maanle mɔɔ memkpondenle bɛ nu la anu. 14Mebamaa bɛazia bɛanyia bɛ anwonyia ne mɔ bieko, na meava bɛ meara bɛdabɛ bɛ maanle nu, wɔ Patolɔso azɛlɛ zo, na akee bɛayɛ maanle bɛlɛvo. 15Ɔbayɛ maanle bɛlɛvo kpalɛ kpalɛ, na ɔnrɛdu ɔ nwo bieko wɔ maanle maanle avinli. Mebaha bɛ aze fɛɛnye mɔɔ bɛnrɛzie maanle biala ɛlɛ a. 16Yizilayɛma ɛnrɛva bɛ rɛle ɛnrɛwula bɛ nu bieko. Bɛbahakye amumuyɛ mɔɔ bɛvale bɛyɛle bɛ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛhɔbizale bɛ moalɛ la. Na akee Yigyibitima banwu kɛ medame a mele Awulae Nyamenle ne a.”
Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza bali Yigyibiti anwo zo konim
17Bɛ nee yɛ hɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ nee nsuu ne, siane ne mɔɔ lumua la, kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la azo, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 18Ɔse, “Sonla ra, Babelonia Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza manle ye ɛlɔnema yɛle ketekete kpalɛ tiale Taya. Ɔmanle bɛzoale awolɛ toonwo bɛ ti zo dule, bɛ bati kpolokpolole, noko ɔdaye o, ye ɛlɔnema o, biala annyia ɛhwee anvi Taya wɔ ɛvɛlɛ totohyia ne mɔɔ bɛvɛle la anwo. 19Zɔhane ati kɛ medame, Awulae Nyamenle ne mese la ɛne: Bɛnlea, mebava Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne meamaa Babelonia belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza. Ɔbazoa zolɛ anwonyia muala yeahɔ, na ye ɛlɔnema ave zolɛ ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti bɛava bɛadua bɛ nwo kakɛ. 20Meva azɛlɛ ne memaa ye kɛ ye ɛvɛlɛ nwo ahatualɛ ɔ, ɔboalekɛ ɔyɛle gyima ne ɔmanle me. Kɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle mese la ɛne.
21“Mekɛ ne anu, mebamaa katakyiema adwazo Yizilayɛma avinli, na mebade ɛ nloa wɔ bɛ avinli. Na akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_text:
Egypt Will Be a Barren Desert
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying:
Cry out in despair,
3because you will soon
be punished!
That will be a time
of darkness and doom
for all nations.
4Your own nation of Egypt
will be attacked,
and Ethiopia will suffer.
You will be killed in battle,
and your land will be robbed
and left in ruins.
5Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle. 6All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
7Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin. 8I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
9On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
10Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army. 11He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
12I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken.
Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins
The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
13All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land. 14The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed! 15The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
16I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear. 17The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner. 18You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity. 19When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord.
Egypt's King Is Powerless
20Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword. 22So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever, 23and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
24-25I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord. 26I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma badea Yigyibitima
1Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne, ka kɛ, Awulae Nyamenle ne kɛ se la ɛne:
Bɛzu kenle ne!
3Ɔluakɛ kenle ne ɛbikye,
Ɛdɛnkɛma kenle ne ɛbikye.
Amungu ngome bava kenle ne,
ɔle munzule mekɛ ɔmaa maanle maanle ne mɔ.
4Konle bava Yigyibiti aze,
na abodelɛ kpole ado Sudanema,
mekɛ mɔɔ Yigyibitima kɛho kɛdɔ,
bɛkɛzoa ye anwonyia muala bɛkɛhɔ
na bɛkɛgyakyi ye bɛkɛdo ye ɛkɛ ne kpoholokpo la.
5“Sudanema, Lebeyama, Ledeama, Arelebiama amuala, yɛɛ Kɛɛbema mɔɔ bɛbɔle bɛ ɛkpa wɔ konle ne anu la amuala baho adɔ. Me menli ne bie mɔ noko baho adɔ.”
6Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛboa Yigyibiti la amuala baho adɔ, yɛɛ ye anwosesebɛ kpole ne baha aze, ɔvi Megedɔlo yeahɔdwu Asewan mɔɔ wɔ nyiakɛ la, bɛ muala bɛbawu dadeɛ nloa, medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a. 7Azɛlɛ ne badɔ mgbane adɛla azɛlɛ biala, yɛɛ ye azuamgbole bayɛ azuadu wɔ azuadu avinli. 8Na akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ menwɔdo senle wɔ Yigyibiti, na ye boavolɛma amuala kɛwie wu la. 9Mekɛ zɔhane anu, mebazoa menli meamaa bɛava meli bɛahɔnwunlonwunla Sudanema wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛ nye ɛnla la, na nyane mɔɔ bɛbade nee abodelɛ mɔɔ bɛbanwu ye la bayɛ kɛ mekɛ mɔɔ Yigyibiti bɔle la, ɔluakɛ nea, mekɛ ne asɛɛ ɛdwu!”
10Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Mebamaa Babelonia belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza adua Yigyibiti anwonyia adenle. 11Bɛbava yemɔ yɛɛ ye menli mɔɔ li ɔ nzi, mɔɔ le maanle anwo ɛzulolɛ tɛla maanle kɔsɔɔti la bɛara, bɛamaa bɛazɛkye azɛlɛ ne, na bɛ nee Yigyibitima aho, bɛahu menli ne bɛagua azɛlɛ ne azo. 12Mebamaa azule Naele ne asesa, na meadɔne azɛlɛ ne meamaa amumuyɛma. Mebamaa nyɛvolɛ azɛkye azɛlɛ ne nee debie biala mɔɔ wɔ zolɛ la. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”
13Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Mebazɛkye mmonle ne mɔ nee ananze ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Mɛmefese la. Belemgbunli ɛnrɛdwazo Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo bieko, yemɔti mebava sulosulo meado Yigyibitima anwo. 14Mebamaa Yigyibiti nyiakɛ (Patolɔso) adɔ mgbane, na meado senle wɔ Zowan. Mebadea suakpole Tibɛse. 15Mebadea Yigyibiti aranemgbole Pɛluseyɔm, na meahu menli mɔɔ wɔ Tibɛse la amuala. 16Mebado senle wɔ Yigyibiti; Pɛluseyɔmma banwu nyane nee abodelɛ kpole. Bane mɔɔ bɛhye ye wɔ suakpole Tɛɛbe anwo la bagologolo agua, na nyane ayɛ kɛ azuyilɛ ava suakpole ne. 17Mgbavolɛ mɔɔ wɔ azuamgbole Hɛleɔpɔlese nee Bubatese azo la badɔ dadeɛ nloa, yɛɛ bɛbahye mraalɛ ne mɔ nuokɛ. 18Awozinli bava Tapanehizi wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ menwɔzɛkye Yigyibiti nee ye anwosesebɛ ne mɔɔ ɔfa ɔtu ɔ nloa anu la. Amungu bava ye na bɛahye ye mralɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ nuokɛ. 19Kɛ mebazi meadea Yigyibiti la ɛne. Na akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”
Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne tumi ne mɔɔ ɛbɔ aze la
20Bɛhyele yɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ bulu nee ko ne, siane ne mɔɔ lumua la, kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsuu la azo, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 21Ɔse, “Sonla ra, mebu Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne asa. Bɛtɛbɔle ye bɔlɛ kɛ bɛyɛ ye ayile na nuhua ayɛ se, na yeahola yeava konle dadeɛ yeaho. 22Yemɔti medame, Awulae Nyamenle, mese: Mekpo Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne. Mebabubu ɔ sa, ɔ sa kpalɛ ne nee mɔɔ ɛbu dɛba la amuala, na meamaa konle dadeɛ ne avi ɔ sa nu adɔ aze. 23Mebabɔ Yigyibitima asande meagua maanle maanle ne mɔ avinli na meakponde bɛ wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo amuala. 24Mebamaa Babelonia belemgbunli ne asa anu ayɛ se na meava me konle dadeɛ ne meawula ɔ sa nu. Mebakpanekpane Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne asa, na yeakponle Babelonia belemgbunli ne anyunlu ɛkɛ ne kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛboda kpole bie la. 25Mebamaa Babelonia belemgbunli ne asa anu ayɛ se, na Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne asa anu ado, na bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a. Saa mefa me konle dadeɛ ne mewula Babelonia belemgbunli ne asa anu a, ɔbava yeahɔ Yigyibitima anwo zo, 26na mebazande Yigyibitima wɔ maanle maanle avinli, na meakponde bɛ wɔ maanle zɔhane mɔ anu. Na akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_text:
Egypt's King Will Be Chopped Down like a Cedar Tree
1Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying:
You are more powerful
than anyone on earth.
Now listen to this.
3There was once a cedar tree
in Lebanon
with large, strong branches
reaching to the sky.
4This tree had plenty of water
to help it grow tall,
and nearby streams watered
the other trees
in the forest.
5But this tree towered over
those other trees,
and its branches
grew long and thick.
6Birds built nests
in its branches,
and animals were born
beneath it.
People from all nations
lived in the shade
of this strong tree.
7It had beautiful,
long branches,
and its roots found water
deep in the soil.
8 None of the cedar trees
in my garden of Eden
were as beautiful
as this tree;
no tree of any kind
had such long branches.
9I, the Lord, gave this tree
its beauty,
and I helped the branches
grow strong.
All other trees in Eden
wanted to be just like it.
10King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree:
The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant. 11So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness. 12Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else. 13Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
14Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
15On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither. 16This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble.
The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls. 17Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
18King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Bɛva Yigyibiti bɛdo sida baka nwo
1Bɛhyele yɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ bulu nee ko, siane nsa ne, kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ka kile Yigyibiti belemgbunli nee ye menli ne amuala kɛ:
Nwane a ɛzɔho ye wɔ wɔ kpoleyɛlɛ nu a?
3Nea, mefa wɔ meado Lɛbanɔn sida baka nwo,
ɔlɛ ngane ngɛnlɛma mɔɔ maa alubo,
yɛɛ ɔwale, ɔ ti dwu amungu ne mɔ anu.
4Ɔnyia nzule ɔnyi ɔyɛ kpole;
azɛlɛ bo nzule maa ɔnyi tendenle.
Azule se dua ɛleka mɔɔ bɛlua bɛ la,
na ɔdoɔloa kpɔkɛ ne anu mbaka bo.
5Yemɔti ɔwa ɔyɛ tendenle
ɔtɛla kpɔkɛ nu mbaka kɔsɔɔti.
Ye ngane kye yɛ mgbole,
na ɔtoto ɔ sa ndendenle.
Ɔluakɛ ye ndinli nyia nzule dɔɔnwo.
6Anwomanyunlu nloma kɔsɔɔti
yɛ bɛ sane wɔ ye ngane ne mɔ anu;
kpɔkɛ nu nane kɔsɔɔti
wo bɛ mra wɔ ye ngane ne mɔ abo;
maanle maanle tɛnla bɛ alubo nu.
7Baka ne kpole le kɛnlɛma,
ɔwale, ye ngane le ndendenle;
ye ndinli dwu kɔ aze kpalɛ,
ɔto azɛlɛ bo nzule.
8 Sida mbaka mɔɔ wɔ Nyamenle tola ne anu la
nee ye ɛnzu kɛnlɛma,
yɛɛ bolonyia baka nee ye ngane mgbole ɛnzɛ.
Baka biala ngane nee ye ɛdeɛ ne ɛnzɛ,
yɛɛ baka biala ɛnle Nyamenle tola ne anu
mɔɔ nee ye sɛ kɛnlɛma a.
9Menyɛle ye kɛnlɛma
memanle ɔdɛlɛdɛlɛle ye ngane,
mbaka mɔɔ wɔ Nyamenle Yidɛn tola ne anu la
anye bolole ye.
10“Yemɔti, medame Awulae Nyamenle, mese: Kɛmɔ ɔnyinle ɔyɛle tendenle na ɔ ti dwule amungu ne mɔ anu, na ɔmemanle ɔ nwo zo wɔ ye tendenle ne ati la, 11mebava ye meawula maanle ne mɔ anu katakyie ne asa anu, ɔ nee ye ali, kɛmɔ ye amumuyɛ ne mɔ fɛta la. Mevuandi ye medo ala ɛne. 12Nyɛvolɛ maanle maanle mɔɔ anwo yɛ ɛzulolɛ la bapɛ ye ado na bɛagyakyi ye ɛkɛ. Ye ngane ne mɔ babubu agua mbɔnza nu nee awoka ne mɔ azo, na ye baka mumua ne abubu agua azɛlɛ ne azo azudenle ne mɔ anu. Menli mɔɔ wɔ ewiade la amuala banriandi avi ye alubo ne anu. 13Anwomanyunlu nloma baradɛnlɛdɛnla baka wulera ne azo na ɛbɔ nu nanemgbole araluolua ye ngoloka ne mɔ anu. 14Meyɛ ɛhye mɔ amuala, amaa baka biala mɔɔ gyi azule nloa la annyi angɔ anwuma somaa, anzɛɛ ɔ ti annyi andwu amungu ne mɔ anu, na mbaka mɔɔ no nzule la annyi ndendenle zɔhane, ɔluakɛ bɛye bɛ muala bɛmaa ewule, kɛmɔ menli wu la, bɛboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɔ ewule kuma nu la anwo.”
15Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Saa baka ne wu kɔ ɛbolɔ a, mebamaa azɛlɛ bo nzule azu ye, na yeasisi ye azule ne mɔ, yeamaa azule dɔɔnwo azi. Mebamaa awozinli ava Lɛbanɔn, na ɔdaye ti kpɔkɛ nu mbaka kɔsɔɔti agyengye. 16Saa mefuandi ye meto ɛbolɔ meboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɔ ewule kuma nu la anwo a, ye azedɔlɛ ne bamaa maanle maanle ne mɔ anwo awozo bɛ. Mbaka kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ wɔ Yidɛn tola nu, Lɛbanɔn mbaka kpalɛ ne mɔ, mɔɔ nyia nzule la, arɛle bakyekye wɔ ɛbolɔ lɔ. 17Bɛ nee ye bɛ muala bɛbahɔ ɛbolɔ sua zo, ɛleka mɔɔ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛdɔ dadeɛ nloa la wɔ la; ɛhɛe, bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛdɛnlanle ye alubo nu wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anu la abo zo baminli.
18“Ɛnee akee mbaka mɔɔ wɔ Yidɛn tola nu la, boni yɛɛ wɔ anyunlunyia nee ye sɛ a? Bɛbapɛ wɔ bɛado bɛaboka Yidɛn tola nu mbaka ne mɔ anwo bɛagua bɛ ɛbolɔ lɔ wɔahɔboka menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle, mɔɔ ɛdɔ dadeɛ nloa la anwo.
“Ɛhye fane Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne nee ye menli ne amuala anwo.” Kɛ Awulae Nyamenle ne se la ɛne.

english_text:
A Funeral Song for the King of Egypt
1Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying:
You act like a lion
roaming the earth;
but you are nothing more than
a crocodile in a river,
churning up muddy water
with your feet.
3King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore. 4I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh. 5I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys, 6and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams. 7 I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining. 8The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
9Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you. 10They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
11The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt! 12Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed. 13I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water. 14The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
15Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
16This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
A Sad Ending for Egypt
17On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations. 19Say to them:
You may be more beautiful
than the people
of other nations,
but you will also die
and join the godless
in the world below.
20You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you. 21Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
22-23The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
24-25The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
26The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle. 27They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
28You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
29The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
30The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
31The Lord God says:
When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering. 32I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Bɛva Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne bɛdo ɛlɛnrɛne nwo
1Bɛhyele yɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ bulu nee nwiɔ, siane bulu nee nwiɔ ne, kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ye awolɛ gua Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ati zo na se ye kɛ: Ɛdwenle kɛ ɛle awenade wɔ maanle maanle avinli, noko ɛle kɛ nane bie mɔɔ le kɛ ɛlɛnrɛne mɔɔ la azukpole nu la. Ɛkpakye azule ne waa waa, ɛfa ɛ gyakɛ ɛbɔ azule ne anu na ɛkpoto ye.”
3Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Mebava maanle maanle meahakyi avonle meado wɔ, na meahwe wɔ meara file zo. 4Mebavuandi wɔ meade ɛnweakpanye ne azo wɔ wienyi ne anu, na meamaa anwomanyunlu nloma nee ewiade nane kɔsɔɔti arali wɔ nane. 5Mebapepɛ wɔ nwonane ne azinli azinli meakponde awoka ne mɔ azo na meamaa mbɔnza ne mɔ anu ayɛ wɔ nwonane azinli kpɔlɔlera ngome. 6Mebahwi wɔ mogya meagua azɛlɛ ne azo toonwo yeahɔdwu awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ, nee azule ne mɔ anu. 7 Saa meminli ɛ bo zo a, mebaheda anwomanyunlu, na meamaa nwɔlɔra anlu. Mebava amungu meaheda sɛnzɛne ne anyunlu, yɛɛ siane ɛnrɛda. 8Mebamaa anwomanyunlu ngɛnlaneɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti anlu, na meava awozinli meaheda azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɛwɔ zolɛ la azo. Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.
9“Mebamaa maanle maanle dɔɔnwo mɔɔ kɛde kɛ mehye wɔ nuokɛ mehɔ maanle bie mɔɔ ɛtɛtele ye nganeɛ ɛlɛ la azo la ahonle adu. 10Wɔmɔ ati, mebamaa maanle maanle dɔɔnwo adwenle azɛkye, na saa menwɔha me konle dadeɛ ne bɛ nyunlu a, debie badɔ bɛ arelemgbunli ne mɔ anwo zo. Kenle ne mɔɔ ɛbadɔ aze la, awie biala anwo bawozo ye na yeazu ɔdaye ɔ ngome ye ngoane.”
11Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Babelonia belemgbunli ne dadeɛ ne bara ɛ nwo zo. 12Wɔ menli ne dɔɔnwo badɔ katakyiema mɔɔ anwo yɛ ɛzulolɛ wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ avinli la dadeɛ nloa. Bɛbazɛkye Yigyibiti debie biala mɔɔ hyia na ɔsonle bolɛ la, na bɛahu ye menli ne amuala. 13Mebazɛkye bɛ nane mɔɔ wɔ bɛ azule ne mɔ anloa la amuala. Awie biala ɛnrɛhola ɛnrɛgyegye bɛ bieko, yɛɛ nane biala ɛnrɛhola ye mɛne fa gyegye bɛ bieko. 14Akee mebade bɛ azule ne mɔ anye na meamaa bɛ azule ne mɔ aze bɛtɛɛ kɛ nwole la. Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a. 15Saa memaa Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne tɔ mgbane na mesɛkye debie biala mɔɔ wɔ zolɛ la, na meku menli mɔɔ de zolɛ la amuala a, akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a. 16Ɛhye le awolɛyelɛ mɔɔ bɛbaye a; mraalɛ mɔɔ wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anu la baye zɛhae awolɛ ne agua Yigyibiti nee menli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la ati zo, medame, Awulae Nyamenle yɛɛ mese a.”
Mɔwuamra maanle nu
17Bɛhyele yɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ bulu nee nwiɔ ne, siane ne mɔɔ lumua la, ye kenle bulu nee nnu ne azo, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 18Ɔse, “Sonla ra, su gua Yigyibitima amuala ati zo, na pia bɛ kɔsɔɔti, ɔdaye nee menli mɔɔ lɛ tumi wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anu la amuala kɔgua mɔwuamra ewiade ne anu, maa bɛhɔboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhɔ ɛbolɔ la anwo. 19Se bɛ kɛ,
‘Nwane a bɛnea a bɛtɛla ye kɛnlɛma a?
Bɛdwu bɛhɔ mɔwuamra anu,
na bɛzie bɛ bɛboka menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la anwo.’
20“Bɛbawu bɛagua menli mɔɔ ɛdɔ dadeɛ nloa la avinli, na menli mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la amuala bahɔ ewule kuma nu. 21Arelemgbunli katakyiema baha bɛ nwo edwɛkɛ. Bɛ nee bɛ boavolɛma mɔɔ bɛ muala bɛwɔ ɛbolɔ la baha kɛ, ‘Menli ne mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle, mɔɔ bɛhunle bɛ konle ne anu la ɛra, na bɛmɛ a bɛgua ɛkɛ ne la?’
22“Aselea wɔ ɛkɛ, ye ɛlɔnema nla ne mɔ gua ɛkɛ. Bɛ muala bɛdɔle dadeɛ nloa wɔ konle nu. 23Bɛ nla ne mɔ wɔ azie ne abo lɔ, yɛɛ ye ɛlɔnema nla ɛdeɛ ne mɔ ɛbɔ ɛyia ye ɛdeɛ ne. Bɛhunle bɛ muala, bɛ muala bɛdɔle dadeɛ nloa. Bɛde aze la ɛnee bɛ nwo ka ɛzulolɛ kpalɛ.
24“Yilam wɔ ɛkɛ, ye ɛlɔnema ɛwolaa ne nla ne mɔ ɛbɔ ɛyia ye nla ɛdeɛ ne. Bɛ muala bɛdɔle dadeɛ nloa wɔ konle nu, na bɛ nee menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la hɔle mɔwuamra anu. Bɛde aze la ɛnee bɛ nwo ka ɛzulolɛ; bɛva bɛ anyiemgba ne bɛhɔ ɛbolɔ. 25Yilam boka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhunle bɛ la anwo, ye ɛlɔnema ne sɛka ɛbɔ ɛyia ye. Bɛ muala bɛnze Nyamenle, yɛɛ bɛhunle bɛ muala wɔ konle nu. Bɛde aze la ɛnee bɛ nwo ka ɛzulolɛ, na kɛkala, bɛva anyiemgba bɛwu bɛhɔ ɛbolɔ bɛhɔboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhunle bɛ konle nu la anwo.
26“Mihyɛke nee Tubale wɔ ɛkɛ, bɛ ɛlɔnema ɛwolaa ne nla ne mɔ ɛbɔ ɛyia bɛ. Bɛ muala bɛle menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle a, yɛɛ bɛhunle bɛ wɔ konle nu, ɔluakɛ bɛde aze la bɛ nwo hanle ɛzulolɛ. 27Bɛanzie bɛ kɛ bɛziele mɔmoane katakyiema mɔɔ vale bɛ konle ninyɛne hɔle ɛbolɔ la. Bɛvale bɛ konle dadeɛ ne mɔ nee bɛ sa nu enyinlike ne mɔ a bɛziele bɛ a, ɔluakɛ bɛ nwo ɛzulolɛ ne tɛbɔ anyewɔzoamra anu.
28“Zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛbahu bɛmɛ Yigyibitima na bɛ nee menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle na bɛhu bɛ wɔ konle nu la ahɔla a.
29“Yidɔm wɔ ɛkɛ, ye arelemgbunli nee ye maanle mgbanyima, bɛ anwosesebɛ kpole ne anzi, bɛ nee menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle na bɛhunle bɛ konle nu la a wɔ ɛbolɔ maanle nu a.
30“Arelemgbunli mɔɔ wɔ Sɔlɔ la wɔ ɛkɛ; bɛmɛ yɛɛ Saedɛnema amuala, bɛhunle bɛ anyiemgba nu wɔ konle nu. Bɛ nwo ɛzulolɛ ne mɔɔ bɛvale bɛ anwosesebɛ kpole ne bɛhanle la anzi, bɛwu kɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnze Nyamenle la bɛboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhu bɛ konle nu la anwo; bɛ anyiemgba doa bɛ kɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ ɛbolɔ la.
31“Saa Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne nwu bɛ a, ɔdaye nee ye ɛlɔnema ɛwolaa ne mɔɔ ɛwu konle nu la arɛle bakyekye,” Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.
32 “Ɔluakɛ, kɛmɔ Yigyibiti hanle anyewɔzoamra ɛzulolɛ la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛbahu ye belemgbunli ne nee ye ɛlɔnema amuala konle nu bɛaboka menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la anwo a.” Awulae Nyamenle a se a.

english_text:
The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch
(Ezekiel 3.16-21)
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying:
Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch 3and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming. 4-5If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
6But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
7Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me. 8When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death. 9If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
The Lord Is Always Fair
(Ezekiel 18.21-30)
10The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me. 11Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
12Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
13Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
14Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right. 15For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live. 16Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
17Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair. 18If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned. 19And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 20But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done.
The News of Jerusalem's Fall
21 Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
22The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak.
What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
23Then the Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
25So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying:
How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder 26and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
27As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases. 28I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them. 29I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The People Listen, but Don't Change
The Lord said:
30Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.” 31So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money. 32They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
33Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_text:
Nyamenle ye Yizikeɛle kɛ ɔle sinzavolɛ
(Yiz 3.16-21)
1Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me: 2Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ka kile wɔ menli ne na se bɛ kɛ: Saa mefa konle meto maanle anzɛɛ azɛlɛ bie azo, na menli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la ye bɛ sonla ko kɛ bɛ sinzavolɛ, 3na ɔnwu kɛ konle asɛɛ ɛva maanle ne aze, na ɔwu aweɛne tendenle ne anu ɔkakye bɛ 4na saa awie te aweɛne ne ane na yeanla ɔ nwo zo, na ɛlɔne ne fa ye aze a, ye mogya gua ɔdaye ɔ ngome ɔ ti zo. 5Ɔdele aweɛne tendenle ne ane yɛɛ yeanla ɔ nwo zo a; ye mogya gua ɔ ti zo. Saa ɔlale ɔ nwo zo a, anrɛɛ ɔvile ɛsalɛ. 6Na saa sinzavolɛ ne nwu kɛ ɛlɔne ɛlɛba arava bɛ aze na yeanwu aweɛne tendenle ne anu, yeammaa menli ne anla bɛ nwo zo, na ɛlɔne ne ba na bɛku bɛ nuhua bie a, ɛnee sonla zɔhane, ye ɛtane ti yɛɛ bɛhu ye a, na mebalie ye mogya ne meavi sinzavolɛ ne ɛkɛ.
7“Yemɔti wɔmɔ, sonla ra, meyɛ wɔ Yizilayɛma sinzavolɛ.
