10 Bɛbolo bɛ azɛlɛvudulɛ mbulalɛ ne mɔ ati bɛyɛ konle dadeɛ,
na bɛbolo bɛ ɛdedadeɛ ndendenle ne mɔ bɛyɛ atwɛ.
Bɛmaa sonla mɔɔ ɛwie tuto la ɛha ye kɛ, ‘Mele ɛlɔnenli.’
11Bɛha bɛ nwo bɛrɛla,
bɛmɛ maanle maanle mɔɔ ɛbɔ ɛyia,
na bɛboɔboa bɛ nloa wɔ bɔnza ne anu.”
O Ɛdɛnkɛma, maa wɔ ɛlɔnema ɛrateta bɛ.
12“Bɛmaa maanle maanle ne mɔ ɛboɔboa bɛ nwo,
na bɛrɛla Ndɛnebualɛ Bɔnza ne anu.
Ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ medame, Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebadɛnla
meabua maanle maanle mɔɔ ɛbɔ ɛyia bɛ la ndɛne a.
13 Bɛkpogya ɛdedadeɛ ne zo,
ɔluakɛ bɛyɔba ne ɛbolo.
Bɛhɔ, bɛhwihwi nwanye ne,
ɔluakɛ nwanye melahyinli ne ɛyi.
Angola ne mɔ ɛyiyi ɛbulu zo,
bɛ amumuyɛ le kpole.”
14Apenle apenle, apenle apenle
wɔ Ndɛnebualɛ Bɔnza ne anu.
Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mekɛ ne ɛbikye,
ɔbazi Ndɛnebualɛ Bɔnza ne anu.
15Sɛnzɛne ne nee siane ne balu ayɛ awozinli,
yɛɛ nwɔlɔra bagyakyi ɛdalɛ.
Nyamenle bayila ye menli ne
16 Ɛdɛnkɛma kulu wɔ Zayɔn Boka;
ɔ ne kpusu wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm,
na anwuma nee azɛlɛ kpusu.
Ɛdɛnkɛma le ye menli ne ɛvealeka,
ɔle aranemgbole ɔmaa Yizilayɛma.
17“Yemɔti bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne,
mɔɔ mede Zayɔn, me boka nwuanzanwuanza ne azo la.
Gyɛlusalɛm bayɛ nwuanzanwuanza,
na nyɛvolɛ ɛnrɛze zolɛ bieko ɛlɛ.
18“Kenle zɔhane nwanye fɛlɛko
vi awoka ne mɔ anu bazonyi,
meleke baze awoka ngyikyi ne mɔ azo,
nzule bayi Dwuda azule kɔsɔɔti;
nzufeanvea vi Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu bazenze
aze kɛ azule wɔ Akasea Bɔnza.
19“Yigyibiti bahakyi ɛsɛlɛ,
na Yidɔm adɔ mgbane,
ɔboalekɛ bɛvale konle bɛdoale Dwuda maanle ne
na bɛhunle menli mɔɔ ɛnze nwolɛ bie la.
20Na Dwuda bayɛ menli gbudugbudu dahuu,
Gyɛlusalɛm bayɛ zɔhane yeahɔdwu awolɛndoazo
kɔsɔɔti anwo zo.
21Mebali me menli ne mogya nwo nzenralɛ,
menrɛva menli mɔɔ di fɔlɛ la ɛtane menrɛhyɛ bɛ,
ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mede Zayɔn Boka.”

english_text:
1 I am Amos. And I raised sheep near the town of Tekoa when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.
Two years before the earthquake, the Lord gave me several messages about Israel, 2 and I said:
When the Lord roars
from Jerusalem,
pasturelands and Mount Carmel
dry up and turn brown.
Judgment on Syria
3 The Lord said:
I will punish Syria
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They dragged logs with spikes
over the people of Gilead.
4Now I will burn down the palaces
and fortresses of King Hazael
and of King Benhadad.
5I will break through
the gates of Damascus.
I will destroy the people
of Wicked Valley
and the ruler of Beth-Eden.
Then the Syrians will be dragged
as prisoners to Kir.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Philistia
6 The Lord said:
I will punish Philistia
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They dragged off my people
from town after town
to sell them as slaves
to the Edomites.
7That's why I will burn down
the walls and fortresses
of the city of Gaza.
8I will destroy the king of Ashdod
and the ruler of Ashkelon.
I will strike down Ekron,
and that will be the end
of the Philistines.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Phoenicia
9 The Lord said:
I will punish Phoenicia
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They broke their treaty
and dragged off my people
from town after town
to sell them as slaves
to the Edomites.
10That's why I will send flames
to burn down the city of Tyre
along with its fortresses.
Judgment on Edom
11 The Lord said:
I will punish Edom
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They killed their own relatives
and were so terribly furious
that they showed no mercy.
12Now I will send fire to wipe out
the fortresses of Teman
and Bozrah.
Judgment on Ammon
13 The Lord said:
I will punish Ammon
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
In Gilead they ripped open
pregnant women,
just to take the land.
14Now I will send fire to destroy
the walls and fortresses
of Rabbah.
Enemies will shout and attack
like a whirlwind.
15Ammon's king and leaders
will be dragged away.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
1Edwɛkɛ mɔɔ mboaneneavolɛ Emɔso mɔɔ vi Tɛkowa la hanle la ɛne. Mɔɔ ɔhale ɛvolɛ nwiɔ na azɛlɛ ne akpusu, mɔɔ ɛnee Ɛzaya a le belemgbunli wɔ Dwuda na Gyɛhowahye ara nrenya Gyɛlɔbowam a le belemgbunli wɔ Yizilayɛ la, Nyamenle yele ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ fane Yizilayɛ maanle ne anwo la hilele Emɔso.
2 Emɔso hanle kɛ,
“Ɛdɛnkɛma kulu wɔ Zayɔn Boka;
ɔ ne kpusu Gyɛlusalɛm.
Mboaneneavolɛma adidileka ne mɔ ɛwe,
Kamɛle Boka ne azo ndile ne mɔ ɛwu.”
Maanle maanle mɔɔ zuozua Yizilayɛ la ndeanlɛ
Selea
3 Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Dɛmasekɛsema yɛ ɛtane la ɛnee bɛyɛ, na mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛhye anwo, ɔboalekɛ bɛva atisesebɛ amaamuo bɛbu Geleadema. 4Yemɔti mebado senle Belemgbunli Hazeeyɛle suakunlu ɛkɛ na senle ne bayela Belemgbunli Bɛneheedade aranemgbole ne mɔ. 5Mebagologolo suakpole Dɛmasekɛse nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ na meaye Evɛn Bɔnza ne anu amra nee Bɛteyidɛn meavi me nye zo. Bɛbahye Seleama bɛahɔ nlɔnu wɔ Kɛɛ.”
Filisitia
6 Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Gazama yɛ ɛtane la ɛnee bɛyɛ, na mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛhye anwo, ɔboalekɛ bɛhyele maanle mumua ko anu amra bɛhɔle nlɔnu na bɛdɔnenle bɛ bɛmanle Yidɔmma. 7Yemɔti mebado senle Gaza bane ne mɔ anu, na senle ne bayela ye aranemgbole ne mɔ. 8Mebahu Ahyedɔdoma nee Ahyekɛlɔn belemgbunli ne. Mebadea suakpole Ɛkelɔn, na Filisitiama mɔɔ ɛha la amuala bawu.”
Taya
9 Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Tayama yɛ ɛtane la ɛnee bɛyɛ, na mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛhye anwo, ɔboalekɛ bɛyele maanle mumua ko anu amra amuala bɛmanle Yidɔmma. Bɛangakye mediemayɛlɛ ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ yɛle la. Luk 10.13-14 10Yemɔti mebado senle suakpole Taya bane ne mɔ anu, na senle ne bayela ye aranemgbole ne mɔ.”
Yidɔm
11 Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Yidɔmma yɛ ɛtane la ɛnee bɛyɛ, na mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛhye anwo, ɔboalekɛ bɛvale konle bɛyɛle bɛ mediema Yizilayɛma kpɔdekpɔde, bɛanze bɛ anwunvɔne. Bɛ ɛya ne andwo ɛlɛ. Oba 1-14; Mal 1.2-5 12Yemɔti mebado senle suakpole Timan azo na ɔbayela Bɔzela aranemgbole ne mɔ.”
Amɔn
13 Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Amɔnoma yɛ ɛtane la ɛnee bɛyɛ, na mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛhye anwo, ɔboalekɛ bɛko bɛakpondɛ azɛlɛ bɛaboka bɛ maanle ne anwo la, bɛhunle Geleade nrenzɛvolɛma. 14Yemɔti mebado senle suakpole Relaba bane ne mɔ anu, na senle ne bayela ye aranemgbole ne mɔ. Akee bɛbadeɛdea nu wɔ konle kenle ne, na konle ne anu bayɛ se kɛ ahumuakyima la. 15Bɛbahye bɛ belemgbunli ne nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ bɛahɔ nlɔnu.”

english_text:
Judgment on Moab
1 The Lord said:
I will punish Moab
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They made lime from the bones
of the king of Edom.
2Now I will send fire to destroy
the fortresses of Kerioth.
Battle shouts and trumpet blasts
will be heard as I destroy Moab
3with its king and leaders.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Judah
4The Lord said:
I will punish Judah
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They have rejected my teachings
and refused to obey me.
They were led astray
by the same false gods
their ancestors worshiped.
5Now I will send fire on Judah
and destroy the fortresses
of Jerusalem.
Judgment on Israel
6The Lord said:
I will punish Israel
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They sell honest people for money,
and the needy are sold
for the price of sandals.
7They smear the poor in the dirt
and push aside
those who are helpless.
My holy name is dishonored,
because fathers and sons sleep
with the same young women.
8They lie down beside altars
on clothes taken
as security for loans.
And they drink wine in my temple,
wine bought with the money
they received from fines.
9 Israel, the Amorites were there
when you entered Canaan.
They were tall as cedars
and strong as oaks.
But I wiped them out—
I destroyed their branches
and their roots.
10I had rescued you from Egypt,
and for forty years I had led you
through the desert.
Then I gave you the land
of the Amorites.
11 I chose some of you
to be prophets
and others to be Nazirites.
People of Israel,
you know this is true.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
12But you commanded the prophets
not to speak their message,
and you pressured the Nazirites
into drinking wine.
13And so I will crush you,
just as a wagon full of grain
crushes the ground.
14No matter how fast you run,
you won't escape.
No matter how strong you are,
you will lose your strength
and your life.
15Even if you are an expert
with a bow and arrow,
you will retreat.
And you won't get away alive,
not even if you run fast
or ride a horse.
16You may be brave and strong,
but you will run away,
stripped naked.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Mowabe
1 Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mowabema yɛ ɛtane la ɛnee bɛyɛ, na mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛhye anwo, ɔboalekɛ bɛyelale Yidɔm belemgbunli ne mbowule bɛmanle bɛdɔle nzonle. 2Yemɔti mebado senle Mowabe azɛlɛ zo na ɔbazɔ yeayela Kɛleɔto aranemgbole ne mɔ. Mowabema bawu konle nu wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛlɔnema ne ɛlɛteɛdea nu na bɛlɛwu aweɛne ndendenle nu la. 3Mebahu Mowabe belemgbunli ne nee ye mgbanyima mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo la amuala.”
Dwuda
4Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Dwudama yɛ ɛtane la ɛnee bɛyɛ, na mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛhye anwo, ɔboalekɛ bɛkpo Ɛdɛnkɛma mɛla ne, yɛɛ bɛanli ye ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ azo. Bɛli nyamenle adalɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛ mgbanyima zonlenle bɛ la anzi toonwo bɛminli. 5Yemɔti mebado senle Dwuda azɛlɛ zo na ɔbazɔ yeayela Gyɛlusalɛm aranemgbole ne mɔ.”
Nyamenle ndeanlɛ wɔ Yizilayɛma anwo zo
6Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Yizilayɛma yɛ ɛtane la ɛnee bɛyɛ, na mebadea bɛ wɔ ɛhye anwo, ɔboalekɛ bɛtɔne tenlenema bɛdie dwɛtɛ fufule, yɛɛ bɛtɔne ehyianvolɛma bɛdie mgbɔlaboa. 7Bɛtietia menli mɔɔ bɛ anwosesebɛ ɛwie nee menli mɔɔ ɛnlɛ boavolɛ la anwo zo, na bɛsuhu menli mɔɔ ɛlɛdi nyane la bɛsie ahane. Ralɛ nrenya nee ɔ ze fa raalɛ ko na bɛgua me duma nwuanzanwuanza ne anwo evinli. 8Bɛkundohundo bɛ nwo aze wɔ azukponle biala anyunlu, wɔ adɛladeɛ mɔɔ bɛva bɛwula bɛ lɔ awoba la azo, na bɛno nwanye mɔɔ bɛbɔ menli kakɛ bɛlie la wɔ bɛ Nyamenle ne ɛzonlenlɛ sua ne anu.
9 “Noko bɛmɛ bɛ ti, menzɛkyele Amɔlema, mɔɔ bɛ ndendenle le kɛ sida mbaka na bɛ anwosesebɛ le kɛ oku mbaka la bɔkɔɔ membɔle bɛ bo zo. 10Eza menyele bɛ menvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo, na menlile bɛ nyunlu wɔ fienemgbole ne anu toonwo ɛvolɛ abulanla, na menvale Amɔlema azɛlɛ ne memanle bɛ, memanle bɛvale bɛyɛle bɛ ti anwo ɛdeɛ. 11 Menyele bɛ mra mrenya ne bie mɔ menyɛle bɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma, na memanle bɛ mgbavolɛ ne bie mɔ dule bɛ nwo ziele ahane manle Nyamenle na bɛbɔle ɛwɔkɛ kɛ bɛnrɛnlo nwanye, bɛnrɛpepɛ bɛ ti, yɛɛ bɛnrɛva bɛ sa bɛnrɛha funli. O Yizilayɛma, asoo ɛhye ɛnle nɔhalɛ? Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mebiza bɛ a.
12“Noko bɛmanle menli mɔɔ dule bɛ nwo manle Nyamenle la nlonle nwanye, na bɛduale Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma kɛ bɛmmaka me nrɛlaleɛ ne. 13Na bɛnlea, mebahomo bɛ nwo zo azɛlɛ ne anwo kɛ ehwili mɔɔ abɛlɛ ngyekyeleɛ ɛyi ye tɛkɛɛ na yemi la. 14Menli mɔɔ anwo yɛ ndɛ la ɛnrɛhola nriandi; anwosesebɛma agbɔkɛ nu batuto, yɛɛ katakyiema ɛnrɛhola bɛ nwo ngoane die. 15Menli mɔɔ to ɛda la ɛnrɛnyia gyinlagyakɛ, menli mɔɔ agyakɛ anzi kola bɛ kpalɛ kpalɛ la ɛnrɛvi ɛsalɛ, yɛɛ menli mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ la ɛnrɛva bɛ nwo dwɔɔ. 16Kenle zɔhane menli mɔɔ akɛnra yɛ se wɔ katakyiema avinli bɔbɔ la bagua bɛ adu aze alɛ bɛ sa mgbane agua ndwɛlɛ aze.” Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne.

english_text:
1People of Israel,
I rescued you from Egypt.
Now listen to my judgment
against you.
2Of all nations on earth,
you are the only one
I have chosen.
That's why I will punish you
because of your sins.
The Work of a Prophet
3Can two people walk together
without agreeing to meet?
4Does a lion roar in the forest
unless it has caught
a victim?
Does it growl in its den
unless it is eating?
5How can anyone catch a bird
without using a net?
Does a trap spring shut
unless something is caught?
6Isn't the whole city frightened
when the trumpet
signals an attack?
Isn't the Lord the one who brings
disaster on a city?
7Whatever the Lord God
plans to do,
he tells his servants,
the prophets.
8Everyone is terrified
when a lion roars—
and ordinary people
become prophets
when the Lord God speaks.
Samaria Is Doomed
9Here is a message
for the leaders
of Philistia and Egypt—
tell everyone to come together
on the hills of Samaria.
Let them see the injustice
and the lawlessness
in that city.
10The Lord has said
that they don't even know how
to do right.
They have become rich
from violence and robbery.
11And so the Lord God has sworn
that they will be surrounded.
Enemies will break through
their defenses
and steal their treasures.
12The Lord has promised
that only a few from Samaria
will escape with their lives
and with some broken pieces
of their beds and couches.
It will be like when a shepherd
rescues two leg bones
and part of a sheep's ear
from the jaws of a lion.
The Altars at Bethel
13The Lord God All-Powerful
told me to speak this message
against Jacob's descendants:
14 When I, the Lord, punish Israel
for their sins,
I will destroy the altars
at Bethel.
Even the corners of the altar
will be left in the dirt.
15I will tear down winter homes
and summer homes.
Houses decorated with ivory
and all other mansions
will be gone forever.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
1O Yizilayɛma, bɛdie edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha ɛtia bɛmɛ maanle mumua ko mɔɔ ɔyele bɛ ɔvile Yigyibiti la. 2Ɔse, “Maanle maanle mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo la kɔsɔɔti, ɛdawɔ ɛ ngomekye ala yɛɛ meze wɔ na menlea wɔ gyɛlɛɛnye a, yemɔti mebadea wɔ, wɔ wɔ amumuyɛ ne mɔ ati.”
Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne gyima
3Menli nwiɔ ɛngola ɛmbɔ nu ɛndu adenle, kyesɛ bɛka bɛsie.
4Awenade ɛmkpo kpɔkɛ nu, kyesɛ yenwu nane mɔɔ ɔkye ye yeali la.
Awenade ralɛ ɛnzu mgbane wɔ ye tunli ne anu, kyesɛ yenyia debie mɔɔ ɔdi la.
5Asoo anloma to ɛhane wɔ azɛlɛ nwo, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛsuale ye ɛhane la?
Asoo ɛhane fuandi, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ debie ɛtɛkanle ye la? 6Asoo bɛwu aweɛne tendenle ne anu wɔ suakpole ne azo a menli ahonle ɛndu?
Asoo munzule to suakpole, kyesɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ ɛyɛ a?
7Nɔhalɛ, Awulae Nyamenle ɛnyɛ debie wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔtɛyele ɔtɛkilele ye sonvolɛma, Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma la.
8Awenade ne ɛkpo, nwane a ɛzulolɛ ɛnga ye a?
Awulae Nyamenle ne ɛdendɛ, nwane a kɛkpo kɛ ɔnrɛha ye nrɛlaleɛ ne a?
Samɛlea ɛbɔlɛ
9Bɛbɔ ye nolo bɛhile bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ Yigyibiti nee Ahyedɔdo aranemgbole ne mɔ anu la kɛ, “Bɛboɔboa bɛ nloa wɔ Samɛlea awoka ne mɔ azo, na bɛnlea ninyɛmunli mɔɔ bɛlɛyɛ, nee nzisi mɔɔ bɛlɛdi wɔ zolɛ la.”
10Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Menli ɛhye mɔ ɛnze boɛlilɛ deɛ holɛ yɛɛ bɛva konle nee awule ninyɛne bɛyiyi bɛ aranemgbole ne mɔ. 11Yemɔti medame Awulae Nyamenle mese: Kpɔvolɛma babɔ ayia bɛ azɛlɛ ne, abubu bɛ nwo banebɔlɛ ne na bɛave bɛ aranemgbole ne mɔ anu ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti.”
12Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Kɛmɔ awenade kye boane na mboaneneavolɛ ne kɔ ye ɛlielɛ a debie mɔɔ ɔnwu ye ala la a le ye ndwɛlɛ nwiɔ anzɛɛ ɔ nzo ko la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ Yizilayɛma mɔɔ de Samɛlea la ɛlielɛ bayɛ a; bɛbanwu ebia mɔɔ bɛda nu la ebule na bɛanwu ɛkpa sinli. 13Bɛdie, na bɛbɔ Gyekɔbo abo zo amra ne kɔkɔ kɛ, kɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle, Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mese la ɛne: 14 Kenle mɔɔ menwɔdea Yizilayɛma wɔ bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ ati la, mebazɛkye Bɛtɛle azukponle ne mɔ, na azukponle biala mgbɛne zo nna ne azo kpokpɔkoo ne mɔ babubu agua aze. 15Mebabubu bɛ fɔsɛlɛ nee wawaa mekɛ azua ne mɔ. Azua mɔɔ bɛva ɛzɛlɛ bɛziezie nuhua la bagologolo agua; azua mgbole ne mɔ abo zo baminli. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”

english_text:
The Women of Samaria
The Lord said:
1You women of Samaria
are fat cows!
You mistreat and abuse
the poor and needy,
then you say to your husbands,
“Bring us more drinks!”
2I, the Lord God, have sworn
by my own name
that your time is coming.
Not one of you will be left—
you will be taken away
by sharp hooks.
3You will be dragged through holes
in your city walls,
and you will be thrown
toward Harmon.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Israel Refuses To Obey
The Lord said:
4Come to Bethel and Gilgal.
Sin all you want!
Offer sacrifices the next morning
and bring a tenth of your crops
on the third day.
5Bring offerings to show me
how thankful you are.
Gladly bring more offerings
than I have demanded.
You really love to do this.
I, the Lord God, have spoken!
How the Lord Warned Israel
6 I, the Lord, took away the food
from every town and village,
but still you rejected me.
7Three months before harvest,
I kept back the rain.
Sometimes I would let it fall
on one town or field
but not on another,
and pastures dried up.
8People from two or three towns
would go to a town
that still had water,
but it wasn't enough.
Even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
9I dried up your grain fields;
your gardens and vineyards
turned brown.
Locusts ate your fig trees
and olive orchards,
but even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
10I did terrible things to you,
just as I did to Egypt—
I killed your young men in war;
I let your horses be stolen,
and I made your camp stink
with dead bodies.
Even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
11 I destroyed many of you,
just as I did the cities
of Sodom and Gomorrah.
You were a burning stick
I rescued from the fire.
But even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
12Now, Israel, I myself
will deal with you.
Get ready to face your God!
13I created the mountains
and the wind.
I let humans know
what I am thinking.
I bring darkness at dawn
and step over hills.
I am the Lord God All-Powerful!
translation_text:
1Bɛdie edwɛkɛ ɛhye, bɛmɛ Beehyan nlankɛ mbelɛ mɔɔ wɔ Samɛlea boka zo, mɔɔ sisi ehyianvolɛma, mɔɔ fa atisesebɛ amaamuo bu menli mɔɔ ehyia na bɛka bɛkile bɛ hu mɔ kɛ bɛva bɛrɛla bɛmaa bɛnlo la. 2Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha ye nwuanzanwuanzayɛlɛ ne kɛ, “Bɛnlea na mekɛ ne mɔɔ bɛbabobɔ bɛ koba bɛahwe bɛ bɛahɔ la ɛlɛba. Ko biala bayɛ kɛ fɛlɛ mɔɔ ɛva koba la. 3Na bɛbalua bane adokule nu bɛavinde, awie biala bahɔ ɔ nyunlu fɔɔnwo na bɛavuandi bɛ bɛagua Hɛmɔn.” Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne.
Yizilayɛma anzukoa anyɛ
4Awulae Nyamenle se, “Yizilayɛma, bɛhɔ Bɛtɛle ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne na bɛhɔdo mɛla ne mɔ. Bɛhɔ Gelegale bɛhɔtietia mɛla ne azo! Bɛhɔ zolɛ bɛbɔ azu nwonlomɔ biala, na bɛva bɛ ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ko ne bɛrɛla kenle nsa nsa. 5Bɛva kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle wɔ nu la bɛbɔ moyɛlɛ azu, na bɛbɔ ahonle fufule nu azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ nolo, ɔluakɛ bɛmɛ Yizilayɛma, ɛhye a le nyɛleɛ mɔɔ bɛkulo kɛ bɛyɛ a.”
6Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Medame a memanle ɛhɔne zile bɛ azuamgbole ne mɔ azo na aleɛ wiele bɛ azua nu a, noko bɛanzia bɛamba me ɛkɛ. 7Eza memanle ezule gyakyile ɛdɔlɛ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ yeha siane nsa na ɛbuhenle ne adwu la. Memaa suakpole ko nyia ezule, na suakpole ko ɛnnyia bie. Memaa ɛya avule ko nyia ezule a, avule ko ɛnnyia bie, yɛɛ ɛya mɔɔ ezule andɔ nu la anu ninyɛne sɛkye. 8Yemɔti azuamgbole nwiɔ anzɛɛ nsa dule hɔle suakpole ko mɔɔ bɛ nye la kɛ bɛkɛnyia nzule bɛkɛnlua bɛ ahonle la azo, na bɛannyia nzule mɔɔ sa bɛ no la, noko bɛanzia bɛamba me ɛkɛ.
9“Memanle ewia katekate rayelale bɛ bɛyɔba ne mɔ. Memanle abɛbɛ ralile bɛ tola nee bɛ vanye avule ne mɔ anu ninyɛne, bɛ feege mbaka nee bɛ ɔlivi mbaka ne mɔ; noko bɛanzia bɛamba me ɛkɛ.
10“Memanle ewulenzane ne mɔɔ rale Yigyibiti la bie rale bɛ nwo zo. Mengunle bɛ mgbavolɛ wɔ konle nu na mengyele bɛ mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ nuokɛ. Memanle bɛ avunli kpɔlɔlera ne mɔ nvoanle bɔnlebɔnlenle bɛ bonyi nu wɔ bɛ azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ ne, noko bɛanzia bɛamba me nwo ɛkɛ.
11 “Menzɛkyele bɛ bie mɔ, kɛmɔ menzɛkyele azuamgbole Sodɔm nee Gomɔla la. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvile ɛsalɛ la le kɛ ɛyɛne mɔɔ bɛdu bɛvi senle nu la. Noko bɛanzia bɛamba me ɛkɛ. 12Yemɔti O Yizilayɛma, mɔɔ mebava meayɛ bɛ la ɛne. Kɛmɔ mebayɛ ɛhye la ati, bɛboɔboa bɛ nwo bɛrayia medame, bɛ Nyamenle ne!”
13Ɔluakɛ bɛnlea, Nyamenle ne mɔɔ bɔle awoka ne mɔ,
na ɔbɔle anwoma,
ɔda ye adwenle ali ɔkile sonla;
ɔkakyi alehyenlɛ ɔmaa ɔyɛ aledwolɛ,
na ɔtietia azɛlɛ ye azo awoka zo la,
ye duma ɛne, bɛfɛlɛ ye “Ɛdɛnkɛma, Tumivolɛ Nyamenle!”

english_text:
Turn Back to the Lord
1Listen, nation of Israel,
to my mournful message:
2You, dearest Israel, have fallen,
never to rise again—
you lie deserted in your own land,
with no one to help you up.
3The Lord God has warned,
“From every ten soldiers
only one will be left;
from a thousand troops,
only a hundred will survive.”
4The Lord keeps saying,
“Israel, turn back to me
and you will live!
5Don't go to Gilgal or Bethel
or even to Beersheba.
Gilgal will be dragged away,
and Bethel will end up
as nothing.”
6Turn back to the Lord,
you descendants of Joseph,
and you will live.
If you don't, the Lord
will attack like fire.
Bethel will burn to the ground,
and no one can save it.
7You people are doomed!
You twist the truth
and trample on justice.
8 But the Lord created the stars
and put them in place.
He turns darkness to dawn
and daylight to darkness;
he scoops up the ocean
and empties it on the earth.
9God destroys mighty soldiers
and strong fortresses.
Choose Good Instead of Evil!
The Lord said:
10You people hate judges
and honest witnesses;
11you abuse the poor and demand
heavy taxes from them.
You have built expensive homes,
but you won't enjoy them;
you have planted vineyards,
but you will get no wine.
12I am the Lord, and I know
your terrible sins.
You cheat honest people
and take bribes;
you rob the poor of justice.
13Times are so evil
that anyone with good sense
will keep quiet.
14If you really want to live,
you must stop doing wrong
and start doing right.
I, the Lord God All-Powerful,
will then be on your side,
just as you claim I am.
15Choose good instead of evil!
See that justice is done.
Maybe I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will be kind to what's left
of your people.
Judgment Is Coming
16This is what the Lord has sworn:
Noisy crying will be heard
in every town and street.
Even farmers will be told
to mourn for the dead,
together with those
who are paid to mourn.
17Your vineyards will be filled
with crying and weeping,
because I will punish you.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
When the Lord Judges
18You look forward to the day
when the Lord comes to judge.
But you are in for trouble!
It won't be a time of sunshine;
all will be darkness.
19You will run from a lion,
only to meet a bear.
You will escape to your house,
rest your hand on the wall,
and be bitten by a snake.
20The day when the Lord judges
will be dark, very dark,
without a ray of light.
What the Lord Demands
21 I, the Lord, hate and despise
your religious celebrations
and your times of worship.
22I won't accept your offerings
or animal sacrifices—
not even your very best.
23No more of your noisy songs!
I won't listen
when you play your harps.
24But let justice and fairness
flow like a river
that never runs dry.
25 Israel, for forty years
you wandered in the desert,
without bringing offerings
or sacrifices to me.
26Now you will have to carry
the two idols you made—
Sakkuth, the one you call king,
and Kaiwan, the one you built
in the shape of a star.
27I will force you to march
as captives beyond Damascus.
I, the Lord God All-Powerful,
have spoken!
translation_text:
Bɛnlu bɛ nwo
1O Yizilayɛma, bɛdie awolɛyelɛ edwɛne ɛhye mɔɔ meto meagua bɛ ti zo la:
2“Belamunli Yizilayɛ ɛdɔ aze,
Ɔnrɛdwazo bieko ɛlɛ!
Bɛkpo ye, wɔ ɔdaye ye azɛlɛ zo,
Awie biala ɛnrɛkpogya ye zo.”
3Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Suakpole mɔɔ vale ɛlɔnema apenle ko hɔle la bava ɛya ko ala a azia ara a; yɛɛ suakpole mɔɔ vale ɛya ko hɔle la, bulu ala a bazia ara Yizilayɛ a.”
4Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛse Yizilayɛma kɛ, “Bɛkpondɛ me bo zo na bɛkɛnyia ngoane. 5Bɛmmakɔ Biyɛhyiba bɛkɔsonle. Bɛmmakpondɛ me wɔ Bɛtɛle, Bɛtɛle bayɛ mgbane. Bɛmmakɔ Gelegale noko, ɔluakɛ bɛbahye ye menli ne kɔsɔɔti bɛahɔ nlɔnu.”
6Bɛkpondɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma abo zo, na bɛnyia ngoane. Saa bɛamkpondɛ ɔ bo zo a, ɔbayɛ senle yeazɔ Dwosefi sua nu, yeayela Bɛtɛle, na awie ɛnrɛhola ye nua ɛlɛ. 7Bɛmɛ, bɛmaa pɛlepɛlelilɛ yɛ ɛnwonle, na bɛtietia tenleneyɛlɛ zo.
8 Mɔɔ bɔle nwɔlɔra Nsuu nee Apea Nsa,
na ɔmaa awozinli kakyi alehyenlɛ,
ɔmaa alehyenlɛ du yɛ aledwolɛ;
yemɔ mɔɔ ɔtwe nyevile nu nzule ɔkɔ
na ɔmaa ɔkakyi ezule ɔtɔ azɛlɛ ye azo la,
ye duma a le Ɛdɛnkɛma.
9Yemɔ yɛɛ ɔsɛkye anwosesebɛma
na ɔbubu bɛ aranemgbole ɔgua a.
10Bɛkyi awie biala mɔɔ twi sonla mɔɔ ɛnli pɛlepɛle la anyunlu, yɛɛ bɛngulo awie biala mɔɔ ka nɔhalɛ la edwɛkɛ. 11Yemɔti, kɛmɔ bɛsisi ehyianvolɛma na bɛwua bɛ hwiiti ne mɔ la ati bɛva awolɛ bɛsisi azua ngɛnlɛma, noko bɛnrɛla nuhua, yɛɛ bɛyɛ vanye egyinli ngɛnlɛma, noko bɛnrɛnlo bɛ ma ne mɔ anu nwanye. 12Ɔluakɛ meze bɛ mɛladonlɛ mgbole ne mɔ nee kɛ bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ mgbole si de la. Bɛkile tenlenema nyane, bɛdie ndoloboa, na bɛdi bɛtia ehyianvolɛma. 13Yemɔti mɔɔ ze nrɛlɛbɛ la bayɛ koonwu wɔ mekɛ zɛhae anu, ɔluakɛ ɔle munzule mekɛ.
14Yɛ mɔɔ le kpalɛ la, mmayɛ mɔɔ le ɛtane la, amaa wɔadɛnla ngoane nu, na Ɛdɛnkɛma, Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne nee wɔ alua, kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ wɔha la. 15Kyi mɔɔ le ɛtane la, na kulo mɔɔ le kpalɛ la, na nea maa nɔhalɛlilɛ ɛrɛla edwɛkɛlilɛ ɛleka ne mɔ; wɔannea a Ɛdɛnkɛma, Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne kɛnwu Dwosefi abo zo amra ne mɔɔ ɛha la anwunvɔne.
16Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma, Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne, Awulae se, “Menli bazu, aye awolɛ wɔ suakpole ne ɛleka kpatawienyi ne nee guabile ne mɔ azo. Bɛbavɛlɛ ɛyazonlɛma kɛ bɛboka menli mɔɔ ze awolɛ ye kpalɛ kpalɛ la anwo bɛmaa bɛzu mɔwuamra. 17Ɛzunlɛ bade vanye egyinli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti anu, ɔboalekɛ melɛba mearadea bɛ.” Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛdendɛ la.
18Munzule ɛha bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛ kunlu a anrɛɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma kenle ne ɛdwu la! Duzu nvasoɛ a kenle zɔhane bayɛ amaa bɛ a? Ɔluakɛ ɔle awozinli kenle, ɔnle kenle mɔɔ anu te a. 19Ɔbayɛ kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛnriandi awenade na yehɔyia bedi la! Anzɛɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛhɔ ye sua nu, ɔhisa bane ne na yeva ɔ sa yedo bane ne azo na ɛwɔlɛ ɛha ye la! 20Ɛdɛnkɛma kenle ne le awozinli, ɔnle wienyi; ɔle kabii, nuhua ɛnde.
21Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mekyi yɛɛ mekpo bɛ nyamenlezonlenlɛ ɛvoyia ne mɔ; yɛɛ me nye ɛnlie bɛ ɛzonlenlɛ ne mɔ anwo. 22Bɛfa bɛ ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ nee bɛ ma azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ bɛba bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko menrɛlie, yɛɛ menrɛnlea bɛ nane dɔlera anzonudwolɛ azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ bɔbɔ. 23Bɛva bɛ alɛra edwɛne ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛlɛto la bɛhɔ nehane; mengulo kɛ mete bɛ getaa ne mɔ ane bɔbɔ. 24Kɛ bɛkɛyɛ ɛhye mɔ la, bɛmaa pɛlepɛlelilɛ ɛze kɛ azudenle, na tenleneyɛlɛ ɛze kɛ azule mɔɔ ɛnsesa ɛlɛ la.
25“Yizilayɛma, ɛvolɛ abulanla ne mɔɔ menlile bɛ ti wɔ fienemgbole ne anu la, bɛbɔle azu bɛmanle me anzɛɛ bɛvale azubɔdeɛ bɛrɛlɛle me ɔ? 26Na kɛkala, kɛmɔ bɛsonle bɛ Bozonle Belemgbunli Sakɛte, nee bɛ Ɛwɔlɔra Bozonle Kaewan ne mɔ ananze ne mɔ, mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛyɛ la, 27mebava bɛ meahɔ nlɔnu wɔ Dɛmasekɛse anzi lɔ,” kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, mɔɔ ye duma a le Tumivolɛ Nyamenle la se la ɛne.

english_text:
Israel Will Be Punished
1Do you rulers in Jerusalem
and in the city of Samaria
feel safe and at ease?
Everyone bows down to you,
and you think you are better
than any other nation.
But you are in for trouble!
2Look what happened
to the cities of Calneh,
powerful Hamath,
and Gath in Philistia.
Are you greater than any
of those kingdoms?
3You are cruel, and you forget
the coming day of judgment.
4You rich people lounge around
on beds with ivory posts,
while dining on the meat
of your lambs and calves.
5You sing foolish songs
to the music of harps,
and you make up new tunes,
just as David used to do.
6You drink all the wine you want
and wear expensive perfume,
but you don't care about
the ruin of your nation.
7So you will be the first
to be dragged off as captives;
your good times will end.
8The Lord God All-Powerful
has sworn by his own name:
“You descendants of Jacob
make me angry by your pride,
and I hate your fortresses.
And so I will surrender your city
and possessions
to your enemies.”
9If only ten of you survive
by hiding in a house
you will still die.
10As you carry out a corpse
to prepare it for burial,
your relative in the house
will ask, “Are there others?”
You will answer, “No!”
Then your relative will reply,
“Be quiet! Don't dare mention
the name of the Lord.”
11At the Lord's command,
houses great and small
will be smashed to pieces.
12Horses can't gallop on rocks;
oceans can't be plowed.
But you have turned justice
and fairness
into bitter poison.
13You celebrate the defeat
of Lo-Debar and Karnaim,
and you boast by saying,
“We did it on our own.”
14But the Lord God All-Powerful
will send a nation to attack
you people of Israel.
They will capture Lebo-Hamath
in the north,
Arabah Creek in the south,
and everything in between.
translation_text:
Yizilayɛ Ɛzɛkyelɛ
1Munzule ɛha bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛ nwo ɛdɔ bɛ wɔ Zayɔn, nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛdwenle kɛ bɛ nwo le kɔlɔnwo wɔ Samɛlea la, bɛmɛ mgbolema mɔɔ bɛwɔ Yizilayɛ, mɔɔ menli ba bɛ ɛkɛ babiza moalɛ la! 2Bɛhɔnlea suakpole Kaleni. Akee bɛhɔ suakpole Heemate maanzinli ne anu na bɛtele zolɛ bɛhɔ Filisitia suakpole Gate azo. Ɛnee bɛle kpalɛ bɛtɛla Dwuda nee Yizilayɛ arelemgbunli maanle ne mɔ ɔ? Ɛnee bɛ maanzinli ne le kpalɛ tɛla bɛ maanzinli ɛdeɛ ne ɔ? 3Bɛnlie bɛndo nu kɛ munzule kenle ne ɛbikye, na konle ala a bɛtwe bɛba ɔ? 4Munzule ɛha bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛda ɛzɛlɛ ɛkpa zo na bɛtenrɛdenrɛ bɛ nwo wɔ mbia ndendenle nu bɛdi mboane nee nlankɛ la. 5Bɛkulo kɛ bɛyɛ edwɛne, kɛmɔ Devidi yɛle la, na bɛbɔ wɔ bɛ getaa ne mɔ azo. 6Bɛno nwanye wɔ ahyɛnze bonkuma nu na bɛgua anatele evuanlɛ, na bɛnzu Yizilayɛ nee ye ɛzɛkyelɛ. 7Yemɔti bɛdabɛ a bɛbalumua bɛahye bɛ bɛahɔ nlɔnu a. Bɛ ɛvoyialilɛ nee bɛ ɛkponledolɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti bara awieleɛ.
8Ɛdɛnkɛma, Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne se, “Medame Awulae Nyamenle, meka me ngome me nwo kɛ: Mekyi Yizilayɛma mgbanyizonleyɛlɛ ne, mekpo bɛ azua mgbole ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛbɔ nwolɛ bane la. Mebava bɛ suakpole ne nee zolɛ debie biala meamaa kpɔvolɛma!”
9Saa menli bulu ka awuke ko anu a bɛbawu. 10Awie mɔɔ kɛwu la anwo sonla, ahenle ne mɔɔ ɛlɛnea yeamaa bɛayela funli ne la baye funli ne wɔ sua ne anu avinde, na yeadea nu yeavɛlɛ awie mɔɔ wɔ sua ne anu la kɛ, “Awie bieko tɛbɔ ɛkɛ ɔ?”
Ahenle babua kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ!”
Akee funli ne anwo sonla ne baha kɛ, “Yɛ koonwu! Ɔnle kɛ yɛbɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma duma bɔbɔ.”
11Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma ka ye tumi edwɛkɛ ne a, azua mgbole nee ngyikyi kɔsɔɔti badwulu agua. 12Asoo mgbɔnwɔ kola wuluwulu bodane zo? Asoo menli kola fa nlankɛ nyinli so ɛya wɔ nyevile nye? Noko bɛmɛ, bɛmaa pɛlepɛlelilɛ ɛhakyi pɔezen, yɛɛ bɛmaa tenleneyɛlɛ ɛyɛ ɛnwonle.
13Bɛfa bɛtu bɛ nwo kɛ bɛva sua Lodɛbaa aze. Bɛfa bɛtu bɛ nwo kɛ, “Yɛlua yɛdayɛ yɛ anwosesebɛ zo yɛva Kaaneeyem yɛyɛ yɛ ɛdeɛ.”
14Ɛdɛnkɛma, Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne se, “Yizilayɛma, bɛnlea, mebamaa maanle gyɛne arava bɛ aze. Bɛbasisi bɛ, ɔvi Heemate Ademgbolezo mɔɔ wɔ sɔlɔ la toonwo yeahɔdwu Alaba Bɔnza wɔ nyiakɛ.”

english_text:
A Vision of Locusts
1The Lord God showed me that he is going to send locusts to attack your crops. It will happen after the king has already been given his share of the grain and before the rest of the grain has been harvested. 2In my vision the locusts ate every crop in the land, and I said to the Lord, “Please forgive your nation. It's so weak. How can it survive?”
3Then the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.”
A Vision of Fire
4The Lord showed me that he is going to send a ball of fire to burn up everything on earth, including the ocean. 5Then I said, “Won't you please stop? How can our weak nation survive?”
6Again the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.”
A Vision of a Measuring Line
7The Lord showed me a vision of himself standing beside a wall and holding a string with a weight tied to the end of it. The string and weight had been used to measure the straightness of the wall. 8Then he asked, “Amos, what do you see?”
“A measuring line,” I answered.
The Lord said, “I'm using this measuring line to show that my people Israel don't measure up, and I won't forgive them any more. 9Their sacred places will be destroyed, and I will send war against the nation of King Jeroboam.”
Amos and Amaziah
10Amaziah the priest at Bethel sent this message to King Jeroboam of Israel, “Amos is plotting against you in the very heart of Israel. Our nation cannot put up with his message for very long. 11Here is what he is saying:
‘Jeroboam will be put to death,
and the people will be taken
to a foreign country.’ ”
12Then Amaziah told me, “Amos, take your visions and get out! Go back to Judah and earn your living there as a prophet. 13Don't do any more preaching at Bethel. The king worships here at our national temple.”
14I answered:
I'm not a prophet! And I wasn't trained to be a prophet. I am a shepherd, and I take care of fig trees. 15But the Lord told me to leave my herds and preach to the people of Israel. 16And here you are, telling me not to preach! 17Now, listen to what the Lord says about you:
Your wife will become
a prostitute in the city,
your sons and daughters
will be killed in war,
and your land will be divided
among others.
You will die in a country
of foreigners,
and the people of Israel
will be dragged
from their homeland.
translation_text:
Abɛbɛ nwo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ
1Awulae Nyamenle ne yele ninyɛne hilele me wɔ ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ nu. Wɔ ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ ne anu, menwunle kɛ mɔɔ bɛpɛle belemgbunli ne ndile ne mɔɔ nyɛmoa di la bɛwiele la, Ɛdɛnkɛma yele abɛbɛ tɔka wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɔ zo mɔɔ ndile ne ɛbɔ ɔ bo kɛ ɔfifi bieko la. 2Wɔ me ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ ne anu, menwunle kɛ abɛbɛ ne mɔ ɛli nya nee ndile amolɛ biala mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo la, na menganle kɛ, “O Awulae Nyamenle, mebodo wɔ, fa wɔ menli ne mɔ ɛtane kyɛ bɛ! Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na Yizilayɛma adɛnla ngoane nu ɛ? Bɛ nwo anzo!”
3Ɛdɛnkɛma hakyile ye adwenle na ɔhanle kɛ, “Mɔɔ ɛnwunle ye la ɛnrɛyɛ zɔhane.”
Senle nwo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ
4Eza Awulae Nyamenle ne yele ɛhye hilele me. Menwunle kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛboɔboa ɔ nwo ava senle adea ye menli ne. Senle ne yelale nyevile ne na ɔbɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔyela azɛlɛ ne. 5Na menganle kɛ, “O Awulae Nyamenle, mebodo wɔ, gyakyi! Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na Yizilayɛma adɛnla ngoane nu ɛ? Bɛ nwo anzo!”
6Ɛdɛnkɛma hakyile ye adwenle na ɔhanle kɛ, “Ɛhye noko ɛnrɛyɛ zɔhane.”
Ɛzuzunyɛma nwo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ
7Awulae yele debie bieko hilele me. Menwunle kɛ Awulae gyi bane bie mɔɔ bɛvale ɛzuzunyɛma bɛdole nwo a bɛdole la anwo, na ɔlɛ ɛzuzunyɛma ne ɔ sa nu. 8Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, “Emɔso, duzu a ɛnwu ye a?”
Membuale ye kɛ, “Menwu ɛzuzunyɛma”
Na ɔzele me kɛ, “Melɛfa ɛhye meahile kɛ me menli ne le kɛ bane mɔɔ ɛndenrɛ la. Me adwenle mɔɔ meva kɛ metea bɛ la, menrɛhakyi ye bieko. 9Ɛleka ne mɔ mɔɔ Ayezeke zonlenle la, mebazɛkye bɛ. Mebazɛkye Yizilayɛ ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ. Mebamaa belemgbunli Gyɛlɔbowam abo zo amra amuala awu dadeɛ nloa.”
Emɔso nee Amazaya
10Amazaya, Bɛtɛle sɛlɛvolɛ ne hɔdoanle Emɔso hilele Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Gyɛlɔbowam kɛ, “Emɔso ɛlɛmaa menli ne ɛ nwo adwenle ɛtane. Ye ngehanleɛ ne mɔ ɛbo maanle ne anwo zo. 11Ye edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔka la ɛne: ‘Gyɛlɔbowam bawu dadeɛ nloa, yɛɛ bɛbahye Yizilayɛma bɛavi bɛ maanle nu bɛ nee bɛ ahɔ nlɔnu.’ ”
12Akee Amazaya hanle hilele Emɔso kɛ, “Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ, wɔha bie a yeyɛ boɛ! Sia kɔ Dwuda, kɔbɔ wɔ Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne nolo wɔ nehane na di nwolɛ aleɛ. 13Mmaka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ bieko wɔ Bɛtɛle ɛke. Ɛke a le belemgbunli ne ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne a, yɛɛ ɔle maanle ne ɛzonlenlɛ sua.”
14Na Emɔso buale Amazaya kɛ, “Menle Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ, yɛɛ menle Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ra. Meka mboane, yɛɛ feege mbaka ɛnleanlɛ gyima a meyɛ a. 15Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle mengyakyile mboaneneavolɛ gyima ne, na ɔzoanle me kɛ mengɔnga mɔɔ kenle bie bazi la anwo edwɛkɛ mengile ye menli Yizilayɛma. 16Yemɔti bɛdie mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛka la. Bɛdua me kɛ memmaka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ tia Yizilayɛma la, yɛɛ memmabɔ Nyamenle edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ tia Ayezeke abo zo amra la nolo mekile bɛ. 17Yemɔti, Amazaya, Ɛdɛnkɛma se menga mengile wɔ kɛ, ‘Ɛ ye bayɛ tuutuu ala suakpole ye azo, yɛɛ ɛ mra mrenya nee ɛ mra mraalɛ badɔ dadeɛ nloa. Bɛbahyɛ wɔ azɛlɛ ne bɛamaa awie mɔ, yɛɛ ɛdawɔ mumua ne ɛbawu menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la maanle nu. Na Yizilayɛma ɛdeɛ, bɛbahye bɛ bɛ nee bɛ avi bɛ maanle ye anu ahɔ nlɔnu.’ ”

english_text:
A Basket of Fruit
1The Lord God showed me a basket of ripe fruit 2and asked, “Amos, what do you see?”
“A basket of ripe fruit,” I replied.
Then he said,
“This is the end
for my people Israel.
I won't forgive them again.
3Instead of singing
in the temple,
they will cry and weep.
Dead bodies will be everywhere.
So keep silent!
I, the Lord, have spoken!”
Israel Is Doomed
The Lord said:
4You people crush those in need
and wipe out the poor.
5You say to yourselves,
“How much longer before the end
of the New Moon Festival?
When will the Sabbath be over?
Our wheat is ready,
and we want to sell it now.
We can't wait to cheat
and charge high prices
for the grain we sell.
We will use dishonest scales
6and mix dust in the grain.
Those who are needy and poor
don't have any money.
We will make them our slaves
for the price
of a pair of sandals.”
7I, the Lord, won't forget
any of this,
though you take great pride
in your ancestor Jacob.
8Your country will tremble,
and you will mourn.
It will be like the Nile River
that rises and overflows,
then sinks back down.
9On that day, I, the Lord God,
will make the sun
go down at noon,
and I will turn daylight
into darkness.
10Your festivals and joyful singing
will turn into sorrow.
You will wear sackcloth
and shave your heads,
as you would at the death
of your only son.
It will be a horrible day.
11I, the Lord, also promise you
a terrible shortage,
but not of food and water.
You will hunger and thirst
to hear my message.
12You will search everywhere—
from north to south,
from east to west.
You will go all over the earth,
seeking a message
from me, the Lord.
But you won't find one.
13Your beautiful young women
and your young men
will faint from thirst.
14You made promises
to the goddess Ashimah
at Samaria;
you made vows to other gods
at the shrines
of Dan and Beersheba.
So now you will fall
and never get up.
translation_text:
Mbakama kɛndɛne ko nwo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ
1Eza Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma yele ɛhye hilele me. Menwunle kɛndɛne mɔɔ mbakama wɔ nu la. 2Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale me kɛ, “Emɔso, duzu a ɛnwu ye la?”
Membuale ye kɛ, “Menwu mbakama kɛndɛne ko.”
Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, “Me menli Yizilayɛma awieleɛ kenle ne ɛdwu. Menrɛhakyi me adwenle, ɛdeanlɛ ne ala a metea bɛ a. 3Kenle zɔhane edwɛne mɔɔ bɛto wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la amuala bahakyi awolɛyelɛ. Ɛleka biala bayɛ avunli ngome, bɛbayɛ koonwu bɛavuandi bɛ bɛagua.”
Yizilayɛ ɛbɔlɛ
4Bɛdie, bɛmɛ mɔɔ bɛmbu menli mɔɔ ɛhyia, na bɛmaa ehyianvolɛma mɔɔ wɔ maanle ye anu la anwo ɛwie bɛ kyele, 5na bɛka kɛ, “Kenlenzu a siane fofolɛ ɛvoyialilɛ ne kɛwie na yɛanyia adenle yɛadɔne yɛ abɛlɛ a? Kenlenzu yɛɛ Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne kɛze na yɛanyia adenle yɛadɔne yɛ hwiiti, yɛanyia adenle yɛazi yɛ ‘yifa’ ɛzuzudeɛ ne abo na yɛawodo yɛ ‘hyikɛle’ ɛzuzudeɛ ne anu, na yɛawua mɔɔ yɛfa tone yɛazuzu la anu, 6amaa yɛava dwɛtɛ fufule yɛadɔ ehyianvolɛma, yɛava mgbɔlaboa yɛadɔ menli mɔɔ anwo ɛhyele bɛ, na yɛadɔne yɛ hwiiti mɔɔ ɛnle kpalɛ la a?”
7Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne ɛha ndane kɛ, “Me rɛle ɛnrɛvi bɛ nyɛleɛ ne mɔ. 8Yemɔti azɛlɛ ne bakpusu, na awie biala mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la banwu nyane. Maanle ne anu bapi na yeabɔ kɛ Yigyibiti Azule Naele ne di yitwe la. 9Kenle zɔhane mebamaa sɛnzɛne ne adɔ ewiazo ketekete, na aleɛ adwo na awozinli ava ewia henlema ne. Medame, Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a. 10Mebamaa bɛ ɛvoyialilɛ ne mɔ ahakyi ɛzɛneyɛlɛ na meamaa bɛ edwɛne fɛlɛko ne mɔ ahakyi awolɛyelɛ. Mebamaa bɛakpa bɛ ti, bɛaheda ɛrele, na bɛayɛ kɛ awovolɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛsu bɛ ra nrenya kokye mɔɔ ɛwu la. Kenle zɔhane bayɛ ɛnwonle ɛnwonle toonwo ahɔ ye awieleɛ.
11“Bɛnlea, mekɛ ne ɛlɛba mɔɔ mebamaa ɛhɔne azi azɛlɛ ne azo a. Tɛ aleɛ ɛhɔne anzɛɛ nzule ɛhɔne ɔ. Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne anwo ɛhɔne nee nzuhɔne a bahu bɛ a. Medame, Awulae Nyamenle a mese a. 12Menli bakpɔsa ɛnwea ɛnwea, bɛvi sɔlɔ bɛahɔ nyiakɛ na bɛvi aduduleɛ bɛahɔ adɔleɛ. Bɛbanriandi bɛahɔ bɛara ɛleka biala kɛ bɛkakpondɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne, na bɛnrɛnyia ye. 13Kenle zɔhane nzuhɔne bamaa mgbavolɛ yɛɛ mbɛlɛra mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ na bɛnze nrenya fee la anye zo abulu bɛ. 14Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛfa Samɛlea awozonle ananze ne mɔ bɛka ndane kɛ, ‘Meka Dan bozonle ne’, anzɛɛ ‘Meka Biyɛhyiba bozonle ne’ la amuala bagua aze, yɛɛ bɛnrɛdwazo bieko.”

english_text:
Judgment on Israel
1I saw a vision of the Lord
standing by the temple altar,
and he said,
“Shake the columns
until the tops fall loose,
and the doorposts crumble.
Then make the pieces fall
on the people below.
I will take a sword and kill
anyone who escapes.
2“If they dig deep into the earth
or climb to the sky,
I'll reach out and get them.
3If they escape to the peaks
of Mount Carmel,
I'll search and find them.
And if they hide from me
at the bottom of the ocean,
I'll command a sea monster
to bite them.
4I'll send a sword to kill them,
wherever their enemies
drag them off as captives.
I'm determined to hurt them,
not to help them.”
His Name Is the Lord
5When the Lord God All-Powerful
touches the earth, it melts,
and its people mourn.
God makes the earth rise
and then fall,
just like the Nile River.
6He built his palace in the heavens
and let its foundations
rest on the earth.
He scoops up the ocean
and empties it on the earth.
His name is the Lord.
The Lord Is God
7Israel, I am the Lord God,
and the Ethiopians
are no less important to me
than you are.
I brought you out of Egypt,
but I also brought
the Philistines from Crete
and the Arameans from Kir.
8My eyes have seen
what a sinful nation you are,
and I'll wipe you out.
But I will leave a few
of Jacob's descendants.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
9At my command, all of you
will be sifted like grain.
Israelites who remain faithful
will be scattered
among the nations.
And the others will be trapped
like trash in a sifter.
10Some of you are evil,
and you deny
that you will ever get caught.
But you will be killed.
The Lord's Promise to Israel
11 In the future, I will rebuild
David's fallen kingdom.
I will build it from its ruins
and set it up again,
just as it used to be.
12Then you will capture Edom
and the other nations
that are mine.
I, the Lord, have spoken,
and my words will come true.
13You will have such a harvest
that you won't be able
to bring in all of your wheat
before plowing time.
You will have grapes left over
from season to season;
your fruitful vineyards
will cover the mountains.
14I'll make Israel prosper again.
You will rebuild your towns
and live in them.
You will drink wine
from your own vineyards
and eat the fruit you grow.
15I'll plant your roots deep
in the land I have given you,
and you won't ever
be uprooted again.
I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_text:
Awulae ndeanlɛ ne mɔ
1Menwunle kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma gyi azukponle ne anwo, na ɔzele me kɛ: “Si Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne mpila ndendenle ne mɔ ati ne mɔ ɛsesebɛ maa nwolodo ne mɔ ɛkpusu. Bubu bɛ maa bɛha bɛgua menli ne amuala ati zo. Mebava dadeɛ meahu menli mɔɔ kɛha la; ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛhola nriandi; kokye bɔbɔ ɛnrɛvi ɛsalɛ. 2Saa bɛnriandi bɛkɔfea Ɛbolɔ a, mebahwe bɛ meara. Saa bɛfo bɛkɔ anwuma a, mebadwula bɛ aze. 3Saa bɛnriandi bɛkɔfea Kamɛle Boka ne azo a, mebakpondɛ bɛ meahye bɛ. Saa bɛnriandi bɛkɔfea nyevile ne abo lɔ a, mebamaa ɛwɔlɛ akeka bɛ. 4Saa bɛ kpɔvolɛma kye bɛ nuokɛ a, mebamaa bɛahu bɛ. Mezi pi kɛ mesɛkye bɛ, tɛ kɛ meboa bɛ ɔ.”
5Awulae, Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne
mɔɔ fa ɔ sa ka azɛlɛ ye a ɔkpusu,
na menli kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ de zolɛ la di nyane,
na maanle ne anu pi na ɔbɔ,
kɛ Yigyibiti Azule Naele ne di yitwe la;
6yemɔ mɔɔ ɔsi ye azua wɔ anwuma,
na ɔsi ye ninyɛnezielɛ ɛleka wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo;
yemɔ mɔɔ ɔtwe nyevile nu nzule,
na ɔmaa ɔtɔ ezule ɔgua azɛlɛ ye azo la,
ye duma a le Ɛdɛnkɛma.
7Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Yizilayɛma, kɛ mesi medwenle Sudanema anwo la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ medwenle bɛdabɛ noko bɛ nwo a. Menyele Filisitiama menvile Kiliti na menyele Seleama menvile Kɛɛ, kɛmɔ menyele bɛdabɛ noko menvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la. 8Medame, Awulae Nyamenle, melɛnea ɛtane belemgbunli maanle Yizilayɛ, na mebazɛkye ye, meaye ye meavi azɛlɛ ye azo. Noko menrɛzɛkye Gyekɔbo abo zo amra ne amuala.
9“Mebaha tumi edwɛkɛ ne na meahegye Yizilayɛma kɛ bɛkɛgye ma la. Mebahegye bɛ meavi maanle maanle avinli na meaye mɔɔ ɛnle kpalɛ la meavi nuhua. 10Bɛdabɛ ɛtanevolɛma mɔɔ bɛwɔ me menli ne avinli mɔɔ bɛka kɛ, ‘Nyamenle ɛnrɛmaa munzule biala ɛnrɛdo yɛ’ la badɔ dadeɛ nloa.”
Kenlebie Yizilayɛ banyia ye gyinlabelɛ dɛba ne
11 Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mekɛ ɛlɛba mɔɔ mebava Devidi belemgbunli maanle ne mɔɔ ɛtete kɛ sua mɔɔ ɛyɛ kpasakpasa la gyinlabelɛ ne meamaa ye bieko. Mebalie ye bane ne mɔ fofolɛ meazie bɛ bo zo ne mɔ, na meakyekye maanle ne fofolɛ meayɛ ye kɛ ye dɛba ne ala la. 12Yemɔti Yizilayɛma bava Yidɔm azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɛha, nee maanle maanle mɔɔ le me ɛdeɛ la kɔsɔɔti ayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ.” Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ bamaa ɛhye azi la se la ɛne.
13“Bɛnlea, mekɛ ne ɛlɛba, ” Ɛdɛnkɛma a se a,
“abɛlɛ bavievia mralɛ dɔɔnwo abo menli mɔɔ bu la anwo zo,
yɛɛ vanye ma bazo abo nwanyeyɛlɛ zo.
Nwanye fɛlɛko bazonyi avi awoka ne mɔ azo,
na yeaze awoka ngyikyi ne mɔ azo.
14Mebamaa me menli Yizilayɛma eza akpazi,
bɛbakyekye bɛ azuadu ne mɔ na bɛadɛnla zolɛ;
bɛbayɛ vanye egyinli na bɛanlo nuhua nwanye ne;
bɛbayɛ tola na bɛali nuhua ninyɛne.
15Mebava me menli ne meazie bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo,
na bɛnrɛdu bɛ bieko ɛlɛ;
bɛnrɛvi azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ meva memaa bɛ la azo.”
Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a se a.

english_text:
Edom's Pride and Punishment
1 The Lord God gave Obadiah
a message about Edom,
and this is what we heard:
“I, the Lord, have sent
a messenger
with orders for the nations
to attack Edom.”
2The Lord said to Edom:
I will make you the weakest
and most despised nation.
3You live in a mountain fortress,
because your pride
makes you feel safe from attack,
but you are mistaken.
4I will still bring you down,
even if you fly higher
than an eagle
or nest among the stars.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
5If thieves break in at night,
they steal
only what they want.
And people who harvest grapes
always leave some unpicked.
But, Edom, you are doomed!
6Everything you treasure most
will be taken from you.
7Your allies can't be trusted.
They will force you out
of your own country.
And your best friends
will trick and trap you,
even before you know it.
8Edom, when this happens,
I, the Lord, will destroy
all your marvelous wisdom.
9Warriors from the city of Teman
will be terrified,
and you descendants of Esau
will be wiped out.
The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
10You were cruel to your relatives,
the descendants of Jacob.
Now you will be destroyed,
disgraced forever.
11You stood there and watched
as foreigners entered Jerusalem
and took what they wanted.
In fact, you were no better
than those foreigners.
12Why did you celebrate
when such a dreadful disaster
struck your relatives?
Why were you so pleased
when everyone in Judah
was suffering?
13They are my people,
and you were cruel to them.
You went through their towns,
sneering and stealing
whatever was left.
14In their time of torment,
you ambushed refugees
and handed them over
to their attackers.
The Lord Will Judge the Nations
15The day is coming
when I, the Lord,
will judge the nations.
And, Edom, you will pay in full
for what you have done.
16I forced the people of Judah
to drink the wine of my anger
on my sacred mountain.
Soon the neighboring nations
must drink their fill—
then vanish without a trace.
Victory for Israel
17The Lord's people who escape
will go to Mount Zion,
and it will be holy.
Then Jacob's descendants
will capture the land of those
who took their land.
18Israel will be a fire,
and Edom will be straw
going up in flames.
The Lord has spoken!
19The people of Israel
who live in the Southern Desert
will take the land of Edom.
Those who live in the hills
will capture Philistia,
Ephraim, and Samaria.
And the tribe of Benjamin
will conquer Gilead.
20Those who return from captivity
will control Phoenicia
as far as Zarephath.
Captives from Jerusalem
who were taken to Sepharad
will capture the towns
of the Southern Desert.
21Those the Lord has saved
will live on Mount Zion
and rule over Edom.
Then the kingdom will belong
to the Lord.
translation_text:
1 Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ Obadaya vale dole gua la ɛne. Ɔfane edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Awulae Nyamenle ne hanle wɔ Yidɔm maanle ne anwo la anwo. Mal 1.2-5
Awulae badea Yidɔmma
Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzoa sonla wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anu.
na yɛde ye nrɛlaleɛ ne. Ɔse:
“Bɛdwazo! Bɛmaa yɛ nee Yidɔmma ɛhɔho!”
2Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛze Yidɔmma kɛ,
“Nea, mebabɛlɛ bɛ aze
wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anyunlu,
awie biala bakpo bɛ bɔkɔɔ.
3Bɛ adubɛnwo ne ɛbɛlɛbɛla bɛ.
Bɛ mgbole ne mɔɔ bɛlua a bɛka kɛ,
kɛmɔ bɛkyekye bɛ suakpole ne bodane zo,
na bɛwɔ awoka zo la ati,
‘Awie ɛnrɛhola yɛ ɛhwee yɛ’ la,
4nea, saa bɛtu bɛkɔ anwuma kɛ kɔleɛ,
na bɛyɛ bɛ sane wɔ nwɔlɔra ne mɔ azo bɔbɔ a,
mebadwula bɛ aze.
5“Saa nwule ba bɛ nwo zo nɔɔzo a,
bɛfa ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛkulo la.
Saa menli tete vanye ma a,
dahuu bɛgyakyi ekyi.
Na bɛmɛ, bɛ kpɔvolɛma ɛkpokpo bɛ bɔkɔɔ.
6Bɛwie Yisɔ abo zo amra wua bɔkɔɔ,
bɛve bɛ anwonyia ne amuala.
7Bɛ ɛlɔne nu agɔnwolɛma ɛbɛlɛbɛla bɛ,
ɛdu bɛ ɛvi bɛdabɛ bɛ maanle nu.
Menli mɔɔ anrɛɛ nee bɛ le ko la
ɛdwazo ɛtia bɛ ɛli bɛ nwo zo konim.
Bɛdabɛ bɛ gɔnwo mɔ kpalɛ kpalɛ ɛvua bɛ ti,
na bɛnrɛde ɔ bo ɛlɛ.”
8Ɛdɛnkɛma se,
“Kenle mɔɔ metea Yidɔmma la,
mebazɛkye nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma mɔɔ wɔ Yidɔm la
na meaminliminli ndelebɛbo bo zo wɔ Yisɔ Boka.
9Katakyiema mɔɔ wɔ Timan la ahonle badu,
na bɛbahu awie biala mɔɔ wɔ Yidɔm la.
Deɛ mɔɔ yemɔti bɛtea Yidɔmma la
10“Mɔɔ bɛvale bɛyɛle bɛ mediema Gyekɔbo abo zo amra la ati,
bɛbagua bɛdabɛ bɛ nyunlu aze na bɛabɔ bɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ.
11Suzuamgba ala mɔɔ kenle ko ne bɛgyinlanle ɛkɛ ne
bɛmanle nyɛvolɛ vole Gyɛlusalɛm
sesale zolɛ anwonyia hɔle,
na bɛguale nwolɛ nzeleba bɛhyɛle la,
ɛnee bɛdabɛ bɛboka menli ne anwo ala ɛne.
12Saa bɛ mediema ɛnwu bɛ nyunlu a,
ɛnee ɔnle kɛ bɛsi bɛ amgbu.
Saa bɛlɛsɛkye Dwudama bɛbɔ bɛ bo zo a,
ɔnle kɛ bɛgyinla ahane bɛsele bɛ,
anzɛɛ bɛtu bɛ nloa anu wɔ bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ nwo.
13Saa me menli ne ɛnwu bɛ nyunlu bɔbɔ a,
anrɛɛ ɔnle kɛ bɛfa ɛlɔnema bɛfo suakpole ne azo,
bɛsele bɛ na bɛgolo bɛ nwo,
na bɛwua bɛ ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti.
14Anrɛɛ ɔnle kɛ bɛsia bɛ adenle nu,
bɛtua menli mɔɔ nriandi la adenle.
Anrɛɛ ɔnle kɛ bɛye bɛ bɛmaa
na bɛmaa bɛnwu amaneɛ.
Nyamenle badea maanle maanle ne mɔ
15“Mekɛ ne asɛɛ ɛdwu mɔɔ medame, Ɛdɛnkɛma,
mebadea maanle omaanle ne mɔ a.
Mɔɔ bɛdabɛ Yidɔmma bɛyɛle la, bɛbayɛ bɛ bie bɛadua,
bɛ munzule babɔ bɛ ti.
16Bɛhilele me menli ne mɔ nyane
wɔ me boka nwuanzanwuanza ne azo
Zɔhane ati bɛbahile maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti nyane ne bie;
bɛbanwu amaneɛ kpalɛ na bɛ bo zo aminli.
Yizilayɛma bali konim
17“Noko Zayɔn Boka azo menli ne bie mɔ bavi ɛsalɛ
na ɛkɛ ne bayɛ ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza.
Na Gyekɔbo abo zo amra bazia arava bɛ agyadeɛ.
18“Gyekɔbo abo zo amra badɔlɔ kɛ samɛnlakɛ,
na Dwosefi abo zo amra azɔ kɛ senle tafinlima.
Bɛbayela Yisɔ abo zo amra kɛ mbaka alosinli.
Awie ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛha Yisɔ sua nu.
Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.
19“Dwuda nyiakɛ amra barava Yisɔ Boka,
na menli mɔɔ wɔ adɔleɛ la arava Filisitia maanle ne.
Bɛbava Yifelaem nee Samɛlea azɛlɛ ne,
na Bɛngyaman abo zo amra ava Geleade.
20Yizilayɛma mɔɔ bɛhyele bɛ nuokɛ
wɔ maanle ye sɔlɔ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la
bazia arava azɛlɛ ye,
ɔvi Fonehyea ahɔkpula Zalɛfate.
Nlɔnuma mɔɔ vi Gyɛlusalɛm na bɛwɔ Sadese la
baraho ava azua mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda nyiakɛ la.
21Katakyiema bahɔyia Zayɔn Boka,
na bɛaho bɛava Yisɔ Boka.
Na medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebali bɛ nwo zo belemgbunli.”

english_text:
Jonah Runs from the Lord
1 One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai, 2to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
3Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
4But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces. 5The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter.
All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep. 6The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
7Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
8They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
9Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
10When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
11The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
12Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
13The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute. 14So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.” 15Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down. 16The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
17 The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
translation_text:
Dwona tu Nyamenle anloa ado
1 Kenle ko Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Ametayi ara Dwona kɛ, 2“Dwona, kɔ suakpole Nenɛvɛ mɔɔ ɛlie duma kpole la azo na kɔbɔ nolo, bɔ bɛ ɛrele zo kɛ menwu bɛ amumuyɛ mɔɔ bɛyɛ la amuala.” 3Noko Dwona dwazole la ɔyɛle ye adwenle kɛ ɔnriandi Nyamenle yeahɔ Sepeen. Yemɔti ɔhɔle Dwɔpa na ɔnyianle meli bie mɔɔ ɛlɛkɔ Sepeen la. Ɔduale ye ɛlɛne kakɛ ne na ɔhɔvole meli ne anu kɛ ɔ nee menli mɔɔ wɔ meli ne anu la kɔ Sepeen, yeaye ɔ nwo wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye zo. 4Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle anwoma kpole bie dwazole nyevile ne anye. Ahumu ne dule kpole kpalɛ mɔɔ ɛnee asɛɛ azudulɛ ne ɛbubu meli ne ɛwie a. 5Menli mɔɔ ka meli ne la ahonle dule kpalɛ na awie biala bɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔtea yeavɛlɛ ye nyamenle ne kɛ ɔlie ye. Bɛvuandinle meli ne anu ninyɛne ne mɔ bɛguale azule nu, amaa meli ne ayɛ felafela. Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛhye mɔ ɛlɛkɔ zolɛ la, ɛnee Dwona ɛwolo ɛhɔ meli ne abo lɔ na yelafe.
6Yemɔti kpanyinli ne mɔɔ nea meli ne azo la hɔdunwuele ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔmɔ wɔlafe a? Dwazo na fɛlɛ wɔ nyamenle ne mɔɔ ɛsonle ye la. Wɔannea a ɔkɛyɛ kɛ wɔmɔ wɔ nyamenle ɛdeɛ ne se anwunvɔne. Fɛlɛ ye maa ɔlie yɛ na yɛwie wu!”
7Na bɛhanle bɛhilele bɛ nwo ngoko ngoko kɛ, “Bɛrɛla bɛmaa yɛgua nzeleba yɛkpondɛ sonla holɛ ko ne mɔɔ ɔlua ɔ ti munzule kpole ɛhye ɛdo yɛ la.” Bɛguale nzeleba ne la, ɔbɔle Dwona. 8Na bɛbizale Dwona kɛ, “Yemɔti, wɔmɔ ɛ ti yɛɛ munzule kpole ɛhye ɛdo yɛ a? Ka maa yɛdie! Duzu gyima a ɛyɛ a? Ɛvi nienwu? Ɛvi maanle boni anu? Menli boni a ɛvi bɛ nuhua a?”
9Dwona buale kɛ, “Mele Hibulunli. Mesonle Ɛdɛnkɛma, Nyamenle ne mɔɔ wɔ anwuma la. Yemɔ a ɔbɔle nyevile nee azɛlɛ a.” 10Na Dwona vale zɔle zolɛ kɛ ɔlɛnriandi Ɛdɛnkɛma.
Ɛzulolɛ kpole hanle bɛ na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Duzu debie a wɔyɛ la?” 11Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee akee ahumu ne ɛlɛtu kpole kpalɛ. Na bɛbizale Dwona kɛ, “Duzu debie a yɛva yɛyɛ wɔ na ahumu ye agua amaa yɛ a?”
12Dwona zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛmaa me zo, bɛvuandi me bɛdo nyevile nu na nyevile ne bagua amaa bɛ, ɔluakɛ meze kɛ medame me ti yɛɛ ahumu kpole ɛhye ɛdwazo a.”
13Na menli ne bɔle mɔdenle kɛ bɛka meli ne bɛahɔ aze, noko yeanyɛ boɛ, ɔluakɛ ɛnee akee ahumu ne anu ɛza na ɔtia bɛ. 14Zɔhane ati bɛvɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛzele kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, yɛsɛlɛ wɔ kpalɛ kpalɛ, mmamaa yɛwu kɛ nrenya ɛhye kɛwu a, yɛɛ mmamaa ye mogya gua yɛ ti zo. Ɔluakɛ, wɔmɔ, O Ɛdɛnkɛma, yɛɛ wɔhyehyɛ wɔyɛ mɔɔ ɛdawɔ ɛkulo la a.”
15Na bɛmanle Dwona zo bɛvuandinle ye bɛdole nyevile ne anu, na ɛkɛ ne ala nyevile ne guale diinyi. 16Menli ne mɔ zulole Ɛdɛnkɛma kpole na bɛbɔle azu bɛmanle ye. Na bɛhanle ndane kɛ bɛkɛzonle Ɛdɛnkɛma.
17 Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle fɛlɛ kpole bie ramenle Dwona. Dwona lile kenle kɔkɔlɛ nsa wɔ fɛlɛ ne akunlu.

english_text:
Jonah's Prayer
1From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
2When I was in trouble, Lord,
I prayed to you,
and you listened to me.
From deep in the world
of the dead,
I begged for your help,
and you answered my prayer.
3You threw me down
to the bottom of the sea.
The water was churning
all around;
I was completely covered
by your mighty waves.
4I thought I was swept away
from your sight,
never again to see
your holy temple.
5I was almost drowned
by the swirling waters
that surrounded me.
Seaweed had wrapped
around my head.
6I had sunk down deep
below the mountains
beneath the sea.
I knew that forever,
I would be a prisoner there.
But, you, Lord God,
rescued me from that pit.
7When my life was slipping away,
I remembered you—
and in your holy temple
you heard my prayer.
8All who worship worthless idols
turn from the God
who offers them mercy.
9But with shouts of praise,
I will offer a sacrifice
to you, my Lord.
I will keep my promise,
because you are the one
with power to save.
10 The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
translation_text:
Dwona nzɛlɛlɛ ne
1Mekɛ mɔɔ Dwona wɔ fɛlɛ ne akunlu la, ɔzunle ɔvɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma ye Nyamenle ne; ɔzele kɛ,
2“Munzule kpole dole me,
na menzunle menvɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma,
na ɔdiele me.
Mela ewule kuma nu la,
menzunle menvɛlɛle wɔ
na ɛdele me ne.
3Ɔluakɛ ɛdawɔ yɛɛ ɛvuandinle me ɛdole buma ne anu,
wɔ nyevile kunlu nehane a;
mengɔle azule bo na elonra
nee azelɛkye mgbole bule vale me ti zo.
4Na menganle kɛ,
‘Akee meminli ɛ nye zo ala ɛne,
na menrɛnwu wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua Nwuanzanwuanza ne bieko!’
5Azule ne monlanle me,
meminlinle buma ne anu bɔkɔɔ,
na nyevile bo ndile bɛkɛbɛkale me.
6Menomanle azule kuma ne abo kpalɛ,
wɔ awoka ne mɔ abo lɔ,
ɛleka mɔɔ bɛto sonla anlenkɛ nu a
bɛndukue ye ɛlɛ la.
Noko wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma, me Nyamenle,
ɛyele me ɛvile Kuma ne anu ɛrale ngoane nu.
7Mɔɔ ɛnee me nye zo ɛbulu la,
mengakyele, na menzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma;
me nzɛlɛlɛ dwule ɛ nyunlu wɔ
wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua Nwuanzanwuanza ne anu.
8Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ amonle ala a bɛsɔ la,
bɛmbu wɔ yɛɛ bɛnzonle wɔ.
9Na mame, mebado edwɛne meaye wɔ ayɛlɛ,
mebabɔ azu meamaa wɔ
na meali me ɛwɔkɛ mɔɔ mebɔ la azo.
Wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ala a ɛdie ngoane a.”
10Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle fɛlɛ ne hɔkpule Dwona dole file zo.

english_text:
Jonah Goes to Nineveh
1Once again the Lord told Jonah 2to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
3Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it. 4 After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
5They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
6When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust. 7-9Then he and his officials sent out an order for everyone in the city to obey. It said:
None of you or your animals may eat or drink a thing. Each of you must wear sackcloth, and you must even put sackcloth on your animals.
You must also pray to the Lord God with all your heart and stop being sinful and cruel. Maybe God will change his mind and have mercy on us, so we won't be destroyed.
10When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_text:
Dwona yɛ tieyɛ amaa Ɛdɛnkɛma
1Eza Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne dwule Dwona anwo zo bieko 2na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Dwona, dwazo kɔ Nenɛvɛ, suakpole ne mɔɔ ɛlie duma kpole la azo, na kɔbɔ me edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ meva mewula ɛ nloa la nolo.” 3Na Dwona hɔle Nenɛvɛ, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle hilele ye la. Nenɛvɛ le suakpole kpalɛ mɔɔ sonla fa kenle nsa a fi ɔ ti kɔ ɔ bo a. 4 Na Dwona bɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔkɔ sua bɔdenle ne azo. Ɔdiale kenle ko ala na ɔbɔle nolo kɛ, “Yeha kenle abulanla na bɛazɛkye Nenɛvɛ!”
5Menli mɔɔ wɔ Nenɛvɛ la liele Nyamenle lile. Bɛ muala bɛliele bɛdole nuhua kɛ bɛkeda ɛrele, bɛahye ɛhɔne, mgbolema nee ahoahweabane, bɛ muala bɛhyele ɛhɔne bɛvale bɛhilele kɛ bɛnlu bɛ nwo.
6Nenɛvɛ belemgbunli ne dele edwɛkɛ ne la, ɔvi ye belemgbunli ebia ne azo ɔdwazole, ɔkpale ye belemgbunli tɛladeɛ ne ɔguale, ɔvale ɛrele ɔhedale, na ɔvale nzonle ɔbɔle ɔ nwo. 7Akee ɔmanle bɛbɔle nolo wɔ suakpole ne azo kɛ, “Kɛ Nenɛvɛ belemgbunli nee ye mgbanyima se la ɛne: awie biala mɔɔ wɔ suakpole ye azo la mmadi debie yɛɛ ɔmmano nzule. Akee bɛmmamaa nlankɛ yɛɛ mboane anzɛɛ nyɛmoa biala fa bɛ nloa ka debie biala. 8Awie biala ɛva ɛrele ɛheda, ɔva bie ɔhedɛheda ye nyɛmoa, na akee awie biala ɛyeye ye ahonle nu ɛzɛlɛ Nyamenle. Awie biala ɛgyakyi amumuyɛ nee ɛtane ɛyɛlɛ. 9Awie ɛnze; bie a ɛnee Nyamenle ɛnwu yɛ anwunvɔne, yehakyi ye adwenle na yegyakyi ye ɛya kpole ne, amaa yɛanwu.”
10Nyamenle nwunle mɔɔ bɛyɛle la. Ɔnwunle kɛ bɛnlu bɛ nwo na bɛgyakyi bɛ nyɛleɛ ɛtane ne nee bɛ amumuyɛ ne mɔ ɛyɛlɛ. Yemɔti ɔhakyile ye adwenle, na yeammaa munzule kpole ne mɔɔ anrɛɛ ɔmaa yeara bɛ nwo zo la amba.

english_text:
Jonah Gets Angry with the Lord
1Jonah was really upset and angry. 2 So he prayed:
Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
3 Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
4The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
5Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
6The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine, 7but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up. 8During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
9But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?”
“Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
10But the Lord said:
You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next. 11In that city of Nineveh there are more than 120,000 people who cannot tell right from wrong, and many cattle are also there. Don't you think I should be concerned about that big city?
translation_text:
Dwona ɛyavalɛ nee Nyamenle anwunvɔnezelɛ
1Ɔrale ye zɛhae la, yeanyɛ Dwona fɛ fee na ɔvale ɛya. 2 Na ɔzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma, mesɛlɛ wɔ, edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ mewɔ me sua zo lɔ mɔɔ menganle la, yemɔ a ɛyɛ zɔhane la. Na ɛhye ati noko yɛɛ anrɛɛ menriandi meahɔ Sepeen la. Ɔluakɛ meze kɛ wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɛle ɛlolɛ Nyamenle mɔɔ se anwunvɔne a. Ɛlɛ abotane, ɛlɛ ɛhulolɛ kpole, yɛɛ ɛ nye ɛnlie munzule nwo. 3Zɔhane ati, O Ɛdɛnkɛma, mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa menwu, ɔluakɛ ɔle kpalɛ kɛ menwɔwu tɛla kɛ menwɔdɛnla aze a.”
4Na Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale ye kɛ, “Dwona, asoo ɛya kpalɛ a wɔva la?”
5Dwona hɔle suakpole ne kandiba mɔɔ di kɔ aduduleɛ la. Ɔyɛle kpato ɔdɛnlanle ɔ bo na ɔyɛle kɛ ɔnea mɔɔ bazi suakpole ne azo la. 6Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle manle baka fifile hedale Dwona anwo zo, ɔmanle ye alubo, amaa ɔ nwo adɔ ye. Na Dwona anye liele baka ne anwo kpalɛ. 7Na aleɛbahye ne, Nyamenle manle nvuba ralile baka ne, na baka ne nwosonle na ɔwule. 8Sɛnzɛne ne kpogyale ɔ nwo zo la, Nyamenle manle aduduleɛ anwoma wuluwulu bie bɔle. Na ewia katekate bie vile bɔle Dwona ati mgbandanlama ne azo manle ɔ nwo yɛle ye bɛtɛɛ. Ɛnee akee Dwona akunlu a anrɛɛ yewu. Na ɔhanle kɛ, “Saa menwule bɔbɔ a anrɛɛ ɔle kpalɛ.”
9Nyamenle bizale Dwona kɛ, “Asoo ɛya kpalɛ a baka ye mɔɔ ɛwu la ati wɔva la?”
Dwona buale kɛ, “Saa menwule bɔbɔ a anrɛɛ mewu.”
10Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Dwona kɛ, “Baka ye, mɔɔ wɔmɔ wɔanyɛ nwolɛ ɛhwee biala, tɛ wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛluale a; ɔfifile kenle ko nɔɔzo, na ye alehyenlɛ nu yewu la, yemɔ ɔyɛ wɔ nyane. 11Duzu ati yɛɛ mame, suakpole mɔɔ le kɛ Nenɛvɛ, mɔɔ ɛlie duma na menli mɔɔ bo apenle ngoko ɛya ko abulanwiɔ mɔɔ bɛnze bɛ bɛne a bɛnze bɛ fema, nee nyɛmoa wɔ zolɛ la, menrɛze bɛ anwunvɔne a?”

english_text:
1 I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah.
Judgment on Samaria
2Listen, all of you!
Earth and everything on it,
pay close attention.
The Lord God accuses you
from his holy temple.
3And he will come down
to crush underfoot
every pagan altar.
4Mountains will melt
beneath his feet
like wax beside a fire.
Valleys will vanish like water
rushing down a ravine.
5This will happen because of
the terrible sins of Israel,
the descendants of Jacob.
Samaria has led Israel to sin,
and pagan altars at Jerusalem
have made Judah sin.
6So the Lord will leave Samaria
in ruins—
merely an empty field
where vineyards are planted.
He will scatter its stones
and destroy its foundations.
7Samaria's idols will be smashed,
and the wages
of temple prostitutes
will be destroyed by fire.
Silver and gold from those idols
will then be used by foreigners
as payment for prostitutes.
Judah Is Doomed
8Because of this tragedy,
I go barefoot and naked.
My crying and weeping
sound like howling wolves
or ostriches.
9The nation is fatally wounded.
Judah is doomed.
Jerusalem will fall.
10Don't tell it in Gath!
Don't even cry.
Instead, roll in the dust
at Beth-Leaphrah.
11Depart naked and ashamed,
you people of Shaphir.
The town of Bethezel mourns
because no one from Zaanan
went out to help.
12Everyone in Maroth
hoped for the best,
but the Lord sent disaster
down on Jerusalem.
13Get the war chariots ready,
you people of Lachish.
You led Jerusalem into sin,
just as Israel did.
14Now you will have to give
a going-away gift
to Moresheth.
Israel's kings will discover
that they cannot trust
the town of Achzib.
15People of Mareshah,
the Lord will send someone
to capture your town.
Then Israel's glorious king
will be forced to hide
in Adullam Cave.
16Judah, shave your head
as bald as a vulture
and start mourning.
Your precious children
will be dragged off
to a foreign country.
translation_text:
1Wɔ Dwuda arelemgbunli Dwɔtam, Ehaze, yɛɛ Hɛzikaya mekɛ zo, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele Maeka mɔɔ vi Molɛhyɛte la. Edwɛkɛ ne fane Samɛlea nee Gyɛlusalɛm anwo.
Samɛlea nee Gyɛlusalɛm anwo ɛzunlɛ nee awolɛyelɛ
2Maanle maanle, bɛ muala bɛdie;
bɛdie, O azɛlɛ ye nee zolɛ ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti;
Awulae Nyamenle badendɛ atia bɛ,
Awulae badendɛ avi ye anwuma lɔ sua nwuanzanwuanza ne anu.
3Ɔluakɛ bɛnlea, Ɛdɛnkɛma vi ɛleka mɔɔ ɔde la ɔlɛba,
ɔbara yearaluolua ewiade awoka mgbole ne mɔ azo.
4Awoka ne mɔ baholo ɔ gyakɛ abo,
mbɔnza ne mɔ anu badudu ahuma mgbole;
bɛbaholo kɛ ɛyɛlɛ mɔɔ ɛha senle la,
na bɛaze kɛ azule mɔɔ vi boka kyengye zo ɛlɛwola la.
5Yizilayɛma mɛladonlɛ nee bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ ati yɛɛ ɛhye mɔ bazi a. Yizilayɛma mɛladonlɛ ne a le boni? Asoo tɛ Samɛlea ɔ? Dwudama ɛtane ne mɔ a le boni? Asoo tɛ Gyɛlusalɛm ɔ? 6Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebazɛkye Samɛlea maanle ne amuala, meahakyi ye ɛleka mɔɔ bɛyɛ vanye egyinli la. Mebapiepia sua ne azo azua ne awolɛ ne mɔ meahɔgua bɔnza ne anu, na meaza bɛ adiabo ne mɔ meagua zolɛ. 7Bɛbabubu ye mmonle ananze ne mɔ dwɔkɔdwɔkɔ, bɛayela mɔɔ ɔnyianle bɛ wɔ ɛkpabɔlɛ nu la amuala, na meazɛkye bɛ awozonle ananze ne mɔ meayɛ bɛ ewula edukue, ɔluakɛ ɔluale tuutuulilɛ zo a ɔnyianle ɛhye mɔ a, na bɛbava bɛazia bɛahɔmaa menli mɔɔ bɔ tuutuu ɛbɛla la.”
8Na Maeka hanle kɛ, “Ɔlua ɛhye ati mebazu meaye awolɛ, mebakpa me nwo, mealɛ me nwo zɔ, meaye awolɛ kɛ ɛsɛlɛ zo ɛzonlɛ, na meali nyane kɛ anloma soholo, 9ɔluakɛ Samɛlea nganlɛ ne mɔ ɛyɛ kukulabi. Nganlɛdudulɛ ne ɛva Dwuda na yera toonwo yeradwu me menli ne anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm.”
Kpɔvolɛ ne bikye Gyɛlusalɛm
10Bɛmmaka ye wɔ Gate, bɛmmasu fee; bɛva nzonle bɛbɔ bɛ nwo wɔ Bɛte Lɛyafela. 11Bɛmɛ Hyeefɛma, bɛva nyiane bɛlɛ bɛ nwo zɔ bɛpɛ nuhua bɛhɔ. Zeeyanema mmaba fee; anrɛɛ Bɛte Yizɛlema ɛzunlɛ kpole ne kɛheda bɛ nwo zo na bɛkɛlie ye gyinlabelɛ ne bɛkɛvi ye ɛkɛ ne. 12Menli mɔɔ wɔ Mɛlo la ɛlɛkendɛ anyebololɛ nu akpondɛ kpalɛ, ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa munzule ɛdo Gyɛlusalɛm. 13Bɛmɛ Leekehyema, bɛhendɛhenda bɛ konle ehwili ne mɔ. Bɛmɛ a bɛlumuale bɛyɛle ɛtane, bɛmanle mɛladonlɛ zanenle Yizilayɛ kɔsɔɔti na Gyɛlusalɛmma yɛle ɛtane a. 14Zɔhane ati bɛbava ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne bɛamaa Molɛhyɛte Gatema bɛ nee bɛ ali nrɛlaleɛ. Akezebe azua ne mɔ bayɛ mɛlɛbɛla debie amaa Yizilayɛ arelemgbunli.
15Bɛmɛ Malihyaama, Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebamaa awie arali bɛ nwo zo konim. Yizilayɛ titilema banriandi ahɔvea Adɛlam. 16Yizilayɛma, bakpa bɛ ti, bɛbapepɛ bɛ nwo enrinli kɔsɔɔti wɔ bɛ mra ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛ nye die bɛ nwo la ati. Bɛkpa bɛ ti koabekoabe kɛ ɛkpɔtɛ, ɔluakɛ bɛbahye bɛ mra ne mɔ bɛahɔ nlɔnu.”

english_text:
Punishment for Those Who Abuse Their Power
1Doomed! You're doomed!
At night you lie in bed,
making evil plans.
And when morning comes,
you do what you've planned
because you have the power.
2You grab any field or house
that you want;
you cheat families
out of homes and land.
3But here is what the Lord says:
“I am planning trouble for you.
Your necks will be caught
in a noose,
and you will be disgraced
in this time of disaster.”
4When that happens,
this sorrowful song
will be sung about you:
“Ruined! Completely ruined!
The Lord has taken our land
and given it to traitors.”
5And so you will never again
own property
among the Lord's people.
6“Enough of your preaching!”
That's what you tell me.
“We won't be disgraced,
so stop preaching!”
7Descendants of Jacob,
is it right for you to claim
that the Lord did what he did
because he was angry?
Doesn't he always bless
those who do right?
8My people, you have turned against
one another!
You have even stolen
clothes right off the backs
of innocent neighbors
who pass by in peace.
9You take over lovely homes
that belong to the women
of my nation.
Then you cheat their children
out of the inheritance
that comes from the Lord.
10Get out of here, you crooks!
You'll find no rest here.
You're not fit to belong
to the Lord's people,
and you will be destroyed.
11The only prophet you want
is a liar who will say,
“Drink and get drunk!”
A Promise of Hope
12I, the Lord, promise
to bring together
the people of Israel
who have survived.
I will gather them,
just as a shepherd
brings sheep together,
and there will be many.
13I will break down the gate
and lead them out—
then I will be their king.
translation_text:
Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛsisi ehyianvolɛma la awieleɛ
1Munzule ɛha bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛdwenle amumuyɛ ɛyɛlɛ nwo na bɛda bɛ ɛkpa zo bɛbɔ ɛtaneyɛlɛ nwo adwenle la. Bɛlɛ tumi la ati, aleɛ kye a bɛyɛ awukade. 2Bɛ nye bolo awie mɔ ɛya avule na bɛsa bɛ bɛdie; bɛ nye bolo awie mɔ azua na bɛdie bɛfi bɛ sa nu; bɛsisi awie mɔ bɛdie bɛ agyadeɛ nee bɛ sua nu amra.
3Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebamaa munzule ado menli ne mɔɔ ɛyɛ kpomgbolo ɛkpolo bɛ kɔme na bɛngola ye ye la. Menli zɔhane ɛnrɛhola tia memaa bɛ bati zo, ɔluakɛ mekɛ ne bayɛ munzule mekɛ amaa bɛ. 4Mekɛ ne anu menli bado edwɛne agolo bɛ nwo, na bɛbazu bɛaye awolɛ nyane nyane kɛ,
Munzule ɛdo yɛ!
Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlie yɛ agyadeɛ muala;
yemaa yɛ azɛlɛ ne amuala ɛvi yɛ sa,
yehyɛ yemaa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛhye yɛ nuokɛ la.”
5Yemɔti saa mekɛ ne dwu na Ɛdɛnkɛma menli ne sia bayia a, menli zɔhane mɔ abo zo amra ɛnrɛnyia awie ɛnrɛgua bɛ ti nzeleba ɛnrɛmaa bɛ.
6Menli ne mɔ tendɛ me na bɛse me kɛ, “Mmabɔ zɔhane nolo ne! Ɔnle kɛ awie biala bɔ nolo mɔɔ le zɛhae la. Nyamenle ɛnrɛmaa yɛ nyunlu ɛnrɛgua aze.” 7O Yizilayɛma, asoo edwɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛka la ɛne? Asoo Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnlɛ abotane? Asoo ɔdaye a yeyɛ ɛhye mɔ a? Asoo ye edwɛkɛ ne ɛnle kpalɛ ɛmmaa mɔɔ di boɛ la?
8Noko bɛmɛ bɛyɛ me menli ne kpɔvolɛma; bɛdwazo bɛtia me menli ne; bɛkpolo mɔɔ ɛngulo kpolera la adɛladeɛ, na bɛdie menli mɔɔ se bɛ adenle zo, mɔɔ ɛnlɛ konle adwenle biala la anwo ninyɛne. 9Bɛtu me menli ne mɔ mraalɛ wɔ bɛ azua ngɛnlɛma ne mɔ anu, bɛmaa bɛ mra nyilalɛ mɔɔ anrɛɛ kenle bie menwɔmaa bɛ la bɔ bɛ bɔkɔɔ. 10Bɛdwazo bɛhɔ, ɛke ɛnle ɛleka mɔɔ bɛdie bɛ ɛnwomenle a, ɔboalekɛ bɛva bɛ nwo evinli bɛzɛkye ɛke bɔkɔɔ.
11Saa awie duolua nuhua aheha mgbane mgbane, abɔ adalɛ kɛ, “Mebabɔ nwanye nee nza ɛsesebɛ nwo nolo meahile bɛ” a, anrɛɛ yemɔ a ɔkɛyɛ nolobɔvo kpalɛ ɔkɛmaa menli ɛhye mɔ a.
12Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebaboɔboa bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛ nloa, O Yizilayɛma. Mebaboɔboa Yizilayɛma mɔɔ ɛha la anloa. Mebayɛ bɛ menli ekpunli ko kɛ mboane mɔɔ wɔ tunli nu la. Mebamaa menli ayɛ bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo gbudugbudu kɛ nyɛmoa mɔɔ ɛhɔ adidileka la.”
13Nyamenle, mɔɔ yemɔ a ɔbabuke adenle ne yeamaa bɛ la, bali bɛ nyunlu. Bɛbalua suakpole ne mɔɔ bɛhyele bɛ nuokɛ bɛhɔle zolɛ la anlenkɛ kpole ne anu bɛavinde; Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛ belemgbunli ne bali bɛ ti.

english_text:
Evil Rulers and Lying Prophets
1Listen to me,
you rulers of Israel!
You know right from wrong,
2but you prefer to do evil
instead of what is right.
You skin my people alive.
You strip off their flesh,
3break their bones,
cook it all in a pot,
and gulp it down.
4Someday you will beg the Lord
to help you,
but he will turn away
because of your sins.
5You lying prophets promise
security for anyone
who gives you food,
but disaster for anyone
who refuses to feed you.
Here is what the Lord says
to you prophets:
6“You will live in the dark,
far from the sight of the sun,
with no message from me.
7You prophets and fortunetellers
will all be disgraced,
with no message from me.”
8But the Lord has filled me
with power and his Spirit.
I have been given the courage
to speak about justice
and to tell you people of Israel
that you have sinned.
9So listen to my message,
you rulers of Israel!
You hate justice
and twist the truth.
10You make cruelty and murder
a way of life in Jerusalem.
11You leaders accept bribes
for dishonest decisions.
You priests and prophets
teach and preach,
but only for money.
Then you say,
“The Lord is on our side.
No harm will come to us.”
12 And so, because of you,
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple now stands.
translation_text:
Maeka tendɛ atia Yizilayɛ mgbanyima
1Na Maeka hanle kɛ, “Bɛmɛ Yizilayɛ mbusua mgbanyinli nee mgbanyima mɔɔ sie Yizilayɛma la, bɛdie! Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdwenle pɛlepɛlelilɛ nwo. 2Noko bɛmɛ, bɛkyi kpalɛ na bɛkulo ɛtane; bɛye me menli ne nwoma na bɛye bɛ nwonane bɛfi bɛ mbowule nwo. 3Bɛdi me menli ne nwonane; bɛye bɛ nwo nwoma; bɛbubu bɛ mbowule nu dwɔkɔdwɔkɔ, na bɛpepɛ bɛ azinli kɛ nane mɔɔ bɛgua bɛ danesɛne nu bɛado la. 4Mekɛ badwu mɔɔ bɛbadea bɛavɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a, na ɔnrɛdɛne bɛ zo. Ɔbava ɔ nye yeavea bɛ, ɔboalekɛ bɛbɔ ɛbɛla ɛtane.”
5Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma bɛlɛbɛla Nyamenle menli ne minli bɛ. Saa bɛnyia ye bɛdi a ɛnee bɛse, “Anzonudwolɛ!” Awie mɔɔ annyia bie ammaa bɛ la ɛnee bɛzo konle bɛdoa ye. Yemɔti kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne, 6“Bɛmɛ kpɔmanvolɛma, aleɛ badwo bɛ, bɛnrɛnwu ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ; awozinli bava bɛ, na bɛnrɛde ɛbizalɛ edwɛkɛ biala. Sɛnzɛne ne badɔ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma ati zo, yɛɛ alehyenlɛ ne bayɛ awozinli ava bɛ.” 7Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛka mɔɔ kenle bie bazi la anyunlu bagua aze, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛka ɛbizalɛ edwɛkɛ la babɔ anyiemgba. Bɛ muala bɛbamua bɛ nloa, ɔluakɛ Nyamenle ɛnrɛbua bɛ.
8Na mame, Ɛdɛnkɛma Sunsum ne ɛva tumi ɛyi me tɛkɛɛ, yemaa me pɛlepɛlelilɛ nee anwosesebɛ kɛ membɔ Gyɛkɔbo abo zo amra mɛladonlɛ ne nee Yizilayɛma ɛtane mɔɔ bɛyɛ la nolo mengile bɛ. 9Bɛmɛ Yizilayɛ mbusua mgbanyinli nee Yizilayɛ mgbanyima mɔɔ bɛkyi pɛlepɛlelilɛ na bɛdi mɔguazo la, bɛdie ɛhye. 10Bɛlɛfa menli ɛhunlɛ nee nzisi a bɛakyekye Nyamenle suakpole Gyɛlusalɛm a. 11Zolɛ mgbanyima die ndoloboa na bɛabua ndɛne, zolɛ sɛlɛvolɛma maa bɛbɔ bɛ ɛkpa na bɛahilehile Nyamenle edwɛkɛ ne, yɛɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma pɛ bolɛ na bɛaha ɛbizalɛ edwɛkɛ ne. Noko bɛfa bɛ adwenle bɛto kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma nee bɛ lua na bɛka kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma de yɛ avinli. Munzule biala ɛnrɛra yɛ nwo zo.”
12 Yemɔti bɛmɛ ti, bɛbagologolo Gyɛlusalɛm kɛ bɛgolo ɛya la bɛamaa yeayɛ suadu na boka ne mɔɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne gyi zo la ahakyi kpɔkɛ.

english_text:
Peace and Prosperity
1In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills,
and every nation
will rush to it.
2People of many nations
will come and say,
“Let's go up to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
3 He will settle arguments
between distant
and powerful nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never again make war
or attack one another.
4 Everyone will find rest
beneath their own fig trees
or grape vines,
and they will live in peace.
This is a solemn promise
of the Lord All-Powerful.
5Others may follow their gods,
but we will always follow
the Lord our God.
The Lord Will Lead His People Home
6The Lord said:
At that time
I will gather my people—
the lame and the outcasts,
and all others into whose lives
I have brought sorrow.
7Then the lame and the outcasts
will belong to my people
and become a strong nation.
I, the Lord, will rule them
from Mount Zion forever.
8Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
guardian of my people,
you will rule again.
9Jerusalem, why are you crying?
Don't you have a king?
Have your advisors gone?
Are you suffering
like a woman in childbirth?
10Keep on groaning with pain,
you people of Jerusalem!
If you escape from your city
to the countryside,
you will still be taken
as prisoners to Babylonia.
But later I will rescue you
from your enemies.
11Zion, because of your sins
you are surrounded
by many nations who say,
“We can hardly wait
to see you disgraced.”
12But they don't know
that I, the Lord,
have gathered them here
to grind them like grain.
13Smash them to pieces, Zion!
I'll let you be like a bull
with iron horns
and bronze hoofs.
Crush those nations
and bring their wealth to me,
the Lord of the earth.
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma bali ewiade kɔsɔɔti belemgbunli
(Aye 2.1-4)
1Ɔbara ye kɛ, mekɛ ne mɔɔ li amozi la anu,
boka ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne gyi zolɛ la
bayɛ boka tendenle adɛla ewiade boka biala.
Maanle maanle bapia ara nwolɛ,
2na menli dɔɔnwo baraha kɛ,
“Bɛrɛla bɛmaa yɛhɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Boka ne azo,
yɛhɔ Gyekɔbo Nyamenle ne sua nu,
amaa yeahilehile yɛ ye ndenle ne mɔ,
na yɛalua ye ndenle ne mɔ anu.
Ɔluakɛ Zayɔn yɛɛ mɛla ne vi bara a,
Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne vi Gyɛlusalɛm a bara a.”
3 Ɔbabua maanle maanle ne mɔ ndɛne,
ɔbabua maanle mgbole mɔɔ wɔ moa la ndɛne.
Bɛbabolo bɛ konle dadeɛ ne mɔ bɛava bɛazo ɛya,
bɛbabolo bɛ atwɛ ne mɔ bɛayɛ ɛdedadeɛ.
Maanle biala ɛnrɛva konle ɛnrɛdoa maanle,
yɛɛ bɛnrɛzukoa konle ɛhonlɛ bieko.
4 Awie biala badɛnla ye vanye egyinli nu,
yɛɛ ye feege mbaka bo anzonudwolɛ nu;
awie ɛnrɛha bɛ ɛzulolɛ,
ɔluakɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛdendɛ a.
5Maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti di bɛ nyamenle ne mɔ mɛla zo na bɛsonle bɛ, na yɛmɛ, yɛbazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne na yɛali ye mɛla zo dahuu.
Yizilayɛma mɔɔ bɛhye bɛ bɛhɔ nlɔnu la bazia ara
6Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mekɛ ne anu, mebaboɔboa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ medea bɛ la amuala anloa, abuburama nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvoa bɛ bɛmaa bɛhɔ nlɔnu la. 7Abuburama ne bayɛ Yizilayɛ abo zo amra mɔɔ ɛha la, na menli ne mɔɔ bɛambu bɛ bie la bayɛ maanle kpole, na Ɛdɛnkɛma badɛnla Boka Zayɔn na yeazie bɛ, ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ nee mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ.”
8Na wɔmɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, boka mɔɔ ɛle tawa, mɔɔ Nyamenle gyinla zolɛ sinza ye menli kɛ mboaneneavolɛ sinza ye nyɛmoa la, wɔ ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ mɔmoane fanwodi ne bazia ara a, na ɛbayɛ maanle ne suakpole. 9Na duzu ati a ɛsu kpole zɛhae a? Ɛnlɛ belemgbunli ɔ? Asoo wɔ folɛdulɛma ɛwie wu la ati a ɛlɛte nyane kɛ raalɛ mɔɔ ɛvo awolɛ zo la ɔ? 10Gyɛlusalɛmma, bɛgyengye bɛ nwo bɛkponle kɛ raalɛ mɔɔ ɛvo awolɛ zo la. Ɔluakɛ ɔvi ɛnɛ, bɛvi suakpole ye azo bɛbadu bɛahɔdɛnla namule nu wɔ kpɔkɛ nu. Bɛbahye bɛ bɛahɔ Babelɔn, na ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma baralie bɛ, yeakpɔne bɛ yeavi bɛ kpɔvolɛma asa anu a. 11Maanle maanle dɔɔnwo ɛli bɛ nloa ɛvua Gyɛlusalɛm ati; bɛse, “Bɛmaa yɛva yɛ nye yɛzie Gyɛlusalɛm anwo na yɛhɔzɛkye ye.” 12Noko bɛnze Ɛdɛnkɛma adwenle, bɛnde ye ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ abo. Bɛnze kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛboɔboa bɛ nloa kɛ ma mɔɔ bɛkyekye bɛ avile avile mɔɔ bɛfa bɛahɔ ma ɛwozolɛ ɛleka la.
13Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Gyɛlusalɛmma, bɛdwazo bɛwozo ma ne na mebamaa bɛ mɛne ne mɔ ayɛ mbulalɛ na bɛ ndwɛlɛ ndaboa ayɛ kɔbele. Bɛbatietia maanle maanle dɔɔnwo anwo zo bɛazɛkye bɛ, na bɛadu anwonyia mɔɔ bɛkɛnyia ye la bɛamaa medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, ewiade amuala Awulae.”

english_text:
A Promised Ruler
1Jerusalem, enemy troops
have surrounded you;
they have struck Israel's ruler
in the face with a stick.
2 Bethlehem Ephrath,
you are one of the smallest towns
in the nation of Judah.
But the Lord will choose
one of your people
to rule the nation—
someone whose family
goes back to ancient times.
3The Lord will abandon Israel
only until this ruler is born,
and the rest of his family
returns to Israel.
4Like a shepherd
taking care of his sheep,
this ruler will lead
and care for his people
by the power and glorious name
of the Lord his God.
His people will live securely,
and the whole earth will know
his true greatness,
5because he will bring peace.
