11 Then I asked the angel, “What about the olive trees on each side of the lampstand? What do they represent? 12And what is the meaning of the two branches from which golden olive oil flows through the two gold pipes?”
13“Don't you know?” he asked.
“No sir, I don't,” was my answer.
14Then he told me, “These branches are the two chosen leaders who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
translation_text:
Kɛnlaneɛbaka ne anwo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ
1Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne mɔɔ nee me dendɛle la rale bieko, na ɔradunwuele me kɛ asɛɛ sonla bie mɔɔ wɔ nafelɛ nu la. 2Na ɔbizale me kɛ, “Duzu a ɛnwu ye a?”
Membuale ye kɛ, “Menwu ezukoa nvutuke kɛnlaneɛbaka, dwora gyi zolɛ, na ahɛnlaneɛ nsuu gyigyi zolɛ. Kɛnlaneɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ gyigyi kɛnlaneɛbaka ne azo la, ko biala anloa nsuu. 3 Ɔlivi mbaka nwiɔ noko gyigyi nwolɛ. Ko wɔ dwora ne fema zo yɛɛ ko wɔ ye bɛne zo.” 4Akee membizale Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne mɔɔ nee me dendɛle la kɛ, “Me menle, ɛhye mɔ abo a le duzu?”
5Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne mɔɔ nee me dendɛle la buale me kɛ, “Ɛnde ɛhye mɔ abo ɔ?”
Menganle kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, me menle, mende ɔ bo.”
Nyamenle ɛwɔkɛ mɔɔ ɔbɔle Zɛlubabɛle la
6 Na ɔzele me kɛ, “Edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛka ahile Zɛlubabɛle la ɛne: Tɛ anwosesebɛ anzɛɛ tumi, na me Sunsum ne yɛɛ ɛbava wɔali konim a, medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a. 7O awoka mgbole, bɛle duzu? Zɛlubabɛle badwulu bɛ yeamaa bɛayɛ kɛ azɛlɛ sɛsɛ; akee mɔɔ ɔkɛze kɛ ɔfa bolɛ ne mɔɔ la zolɛ anwuma la yeara la ɛnee bɛlɛtea nu kɛ, ‘Kɛnlɛmaleɛ! Ɔle kɛnlɛma somaa!’ ”
8Eza Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me, 9ɔse, “Zɛlubabɛle ɛwula sua ɛhye adiabo ne aze; ɔbazi yeawie. Na ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ bɛbanwu kɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛzoa wɔ bɛ nwo ɛke a. 10Awie biala mɔɔ ɛkpo mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛlɛyɛ ninyɛne ngyikyi ngyikyi la bali fɛlɛko, na ɔbanwu kɛ Zɛlubabɛle gua zolɛ ɛlɛsi sua ne.
“Ahɛnlaneɛ nsuu ɛhye mɔ a le Ɛdɛnkɛma anye ne mɔɔ ɔfa ɔnea ewiade amuala la.”
11 Membizale ye kɛ, “Na ɔlivi mbaka nwiɔ ɛhye mɔɔ ko gyi kɛnlaneɛbaka ne fema zo, ko gyi ye bɛne zo la abo a le duzu?” 12Eza membizale ye kɛ, “Na ɔlivi mbaka ngane ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ gua ezukoa nvutuke paepe nwiɔ ne mɔɔ nwole dua nu finde gua la anwo la noko abo a le duzu.”
13Na ɔbizale me kɛ, “Ɛnde ɛhye abo ɔ?”
Membuale ye kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, me menle, mende ɔ bo.”
14Ɔzele me kɛ, “Ɛhye mɔ a le menli nwiɔ ne mɔɔ bɛkpokpa bɛ nwole na bɛgyi ewiade amra amuala Awulae anwo ɛkɛ ne la.”

english_text:
Sixth Vision: A Flying Scroll
1When I looked the next time, I saw a flying scroll, 2and the angel asked, “What do you see?”
“A flying scroll,” I answered. “About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide.”
3Then he told me:
This scroll puts a curse on everyone in the land who steals or tells lies. The writing on one side tells about the destruction of those who steal, while the writing on the other side tells about the destruction of those who lie.
4The Lord All-Powerful has said, “I am sending this scroll into the house of everyone who is a robber or tells lies in my name, and it will remain there until every piece of wood and stone in that house crumbles.”
Seventh Vision: A Woman in a Basket
5Now the angel who was there to explain the visions came over and said, “Look up and tell me what you see coming.”
6“I don't know what it is,” was my reply.
“It's a big basket,” he said. “And it shows what everyone in the land has in mind.”
7The lead cover of the basket was opened, and in the basket was a woman. 8“This woman represents evil,” the angel explained. Then he threw her back into the basket and slammed the heavy cover down tight.
9Right after this I saw two women coming through the sky with wings outstretched like a stork in the wind. Suddenly they lifted the basket into the air, 10and I asked the angel, “Where are they taking the basket?”
11“To Babylonia,” he answered, “where they will build a house for the basket and set it down inside.”
translation_text:
Nwoma ne mɔɔ tu la anwo ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ
1Eza memanle me nye zo, na menwunle nwoma mɔɔ ɛdu faa la. 2Na Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne bizale me kɛ, “Duzu a ɛnwu ye a?”
Membuale ye kɛ, “Menwu nwoma mɔɔ ɛdu faa la; ye tendenle le mita ngɔnla yɛɛ ye tɛtɛlɛ le mita nna nee foa ko.”
3Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne zele me kɛ, “Munzule mɔɔ bahɔ ewiade amuala la wɔ nwoma ɛhye azo. Bɛhɛlɛ zolɛ kɛ awie biala mɔɔ kɛyɛ awule la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtu ye bɛfi azɛlɛ ne azo, yɛɛ awie biala mɔɔ kɛha ndane adalɛ la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtu ye bɛfi azɛlɛ ne azo. 4Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se ɔbazoa ye yeamaa yeawolo awule awuke biala nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛfa ye duma bɛka ndane adalɛ la biala awuke nu, na ɔbadɛnla ɛkɛ ne toonwo kɔkpula kɛ sua zɔhane kɛyɛ suadu, na nuhua mbaka nee awolɛ kɛgologolo kɛgua la.”
Raalɛ ne mɔɔ de kɛndɛne ne anu la
5Akee Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne mɔɔ nee me dendɛle la razele me kɛ, “Maa ɛ nye zo na nea debie mɔɔ ɛlɛse ahɔ la.”
6Membizale ye kɛ, “Duzu debie ɔ?”
Ɔbuale me kɛ, “Kɛndɛne ne a ɛlɛse la.” Ɔvale ɔzɔle zolɛ kɛ, “Ɔgyi ɛkɛ ne ɔmaa ewiade amra amuala ɛtane ne.”
7Kɛndɛne ne lɛ sumi nduazo; bɛdukuele zolɛ, na ɛnee raalɛ bie de nuhua.
8Na Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne hanle kɛ, “Raalɛ ɛhye gyi ɛkɛ ne maa amumuyɛ.” Akee ɔzuhunle ye ɔdole kɛndɛne ne anu na ɔhanle sumi nduazo ne ɔdole zolɛ. 9Memanle me nye zo bieko la menwunle kɛ mraalɛ nwiɔ mɔɔ lɛ ndɛbalɛ kɛ anloma akoso ɛdeɛ ne la ɛdu faa ɛlɛba, na anwoma ne ɛlɛbɔ bɛ bo. Bɛramanle kɛndɛne ne zo bɛhɔle anwuma.
10Membizale Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne kɛ, “Na bɛfa kɛndɛne ne bɛahɔ nienwu?”
11Ɔbuale me kɛ, “Bɛfa bɛahɔ Babelonia. Bɛbazi sua ɛkɛ bɛamaa ye. Bɛbava kɛndɛne ne bɛazie sua ne anu na bɛazonle ye.”

english_text:
Eighth Vision: Four Chariots
1Finally, I looked up and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains. 2 The first chariot was pulled by red horses, and the second by black horses; 3 the third chariot was pulled by white horses, and the fourth by spotted gray horses.
4“Sir,” I asked the angel. “What do these stand for?”
5 Then he explained, “These are the four winds of heaven, and now they are going out, after presenting themselves to the Lord of all the earth. 6The chariot with black horses goes toward the north, the chariot with white horses goes toward the west, and the one with spotted horses goes toward the south.”
7The horses came out eager to patrol the earth, and the angel told them, “Start patrolling the earth.”
When they had gone on their way, 8he shouted to me, “Those that have gone to the country in the north will do what the Lord's Spirit wants them to do there.”
The Chosen Leader
9The Lord said to me:
10-11Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah have returned from Babylonia. Collect enough silver and gold from them to make a crown. Then go with them to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah and put the crown on the head of the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak. 12-13 Tell him that I, the Lord All-Powerful, say, “Someone will reach out from here like a branch and build a temple for me. I will name him ‘Branch,’ and he will rule with royal honors. A priest will stand beside his throne, and the two of them will be good friends. 14This crown will be kept in my temple as a reminder and will be taken care of by Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah.”
15When people from distant lands come and help build the temple of the Lord All-Powerful, you will know that the Lord is the one who sent me. And this will happen, if you truly obey the Lord your God.
translation_text:
Konle ehwili nna ne
1Eza memanle me nye zo na menwunle kɛ konle ehwili nna vi awoka nwiɔ avinli ɛlɛba. Awoka ne mɔ le kɔbele awoka. 2 Konle ehwili ne mɔɔ lumua la, mgbɔnwɔ kɔkɔlɛ a ɛlɛtwe ye a. Mɔɔ tɔ zo nwiɔ la mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ le bile, 3 mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa la mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ le fufule, yɛɛ mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ le nzonle anwo ndetandeta. 4Na membizale Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne mɔɔ nee me dendɛle la kɛ, “Me menle, na ɛhye mɔ noko ɛ?”
5 Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne buale kɛ, “Ɛhye mɔ hɔvale bɛ nwo hilele Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ bɔle azɛlɛ ye la, na kɛkala bɛlɛkɔ anwuma anwoma nna ne anu. 6Konle ehwili ne mɔɔ mgbɔnwɔ bile ne mɔ ɛlɛtwe ye la kɔ ɛbɔ nu afoa nu maanle ne anu, wɔ Babelonia, mɔɔ mgbɔnwɔ fufule ne mɔ ɛlɛtwe ye la kɔ adɔleɛ afoa nu maanle ne anu, yɛɛ mɔɔ mgbɔnwɔ nzonle anwo ndetandeta ne mɔ ɛlɛtwe ye la kɔ nyiakɛ afoa nu maanle ne anu.” 7Mgbɔnwɔ nzonle anwo ndetandeta ne mɔ vindele rale la, ɛnee bɛngola gyinla fee; ɛhɔlɛ ala yɛɛ bɛkulo kɛ bɛkɔ na bɛkɔkpɔla azɛlɛ ye a. Na Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔ ɛ, bɛhɔkpɔla azɛlɛ ye.” Yemɔti bɛhɔle kɛ bɛkakpɔla azɛlɛ ye. 8Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne deanle nu zele me kɛ, “Nea, mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛlɛkɔ ɛbɔ nu afoa nu la ɛmaa me Sunsum ne akunlu ɛdwo ɛbɔ nu afoa nu maanle ne anwo.”
Nyamenle se bɛzoa Dwɔhyua belemgbunli kyɛlɛ
9Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 10-11Ɔse, “Die dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke fi Hɛledae, Tobaegya, yɛɛ Gyɛdaya mɔɔ bɛhyele bɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu na bɛvi Babelonia bɛra la ɛkɛ ne, na kenle ko ne ala fa kɔ Zɛfanaya ara Dwosaya sua nu. Fa dwɛtɛ fufule ne nee ezukoa nvutuke ne yɛ belemgbunli kyɛlɛ na fa soa Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli Dwɔhyua, Gyɛhɔzadake ara nrenya ne, 12 na ka kile ye kɛ, ‘Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se: Bɛnlea, sonla ne mɔɔ ye duma a le Baka Ɛhane la ɛne. Ɔbakpazi wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ ɔde la na yeazi Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne. 13Yemɔ a ɔbazi Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne a, na bɛbali ye eni kɛ belemgbunli. Ɔbadɛnla ye belemgbunli ebia nu na yeazie ye menli ne. Ɔbanyia sɛlɛvolɛ ko wɔ ye belemgbunli ebia ne anwo, na bɛdabɛ bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛ nloa bazɛ bɛ nwo anzonudwolɛ nu.’ 14Belemgbunli kyɛlɛ ne ɛnrɛkpa Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu ɛlɛ, na ɔbayɛ ngakyelɛdeɛ yeamaa Hɛledae, Tobaegya, Gyɛdaya, yɛɛ Zɛfanaya ara Dwosaya.
15“Menli mɔɔ wɔ moa moa la baraboa Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne ɛzilɛ; na bɛbanwu kɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛzoa me bɛ nwo a. Saa bɛtie Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne ane na bɛyɛ tieyɛ bɛmaa ye a, bɛbanwu kɛ ɛhye mɔ amuala bazi.”

english_text:
A Question about Going without Eating
1On the fourth day of Chislev, the ninth month of the fourth year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord again spoke to me. 2-3It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
4-5It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests:
For 70 years you have gone without eating during the fifth and seventh months of the year. But did you really do it for me? 6And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment? 7My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
8-9So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another! 10Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
11-12But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry 13and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
14That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma tendɛ atia adalɛ ɛhɔnehyelɛ
1Maanle Maanle Belemgbunli Dalayɛse lile ɛvolɛ nna wɔ Pɛhyea ebia zo la, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele Zɛkalaya wɔ siane ngɔnla ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye “Kyeselɛve” la ye kenle nna ne azo.
2Bɛtɛlema ɛzoa Hyalizɛ nee Riligɛmɛlɛke nee bɛ sa zo kɛ bɛhɔzɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, 3na bɛbiza sɛlɛvolɛma mɔɔ wɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu nee Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma ne mɔ kɛ, “Yɛli nyane na yɛhye ɛhɔne wɔ siane nnu ne anu, kɛmɔ ɛvolɛ dɔɔnwo mɔɔ ɛraze ɛhɔ la yɛyɛ ye la ɔ?”
4Na Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 5Ɔse, “Biza menli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu nee sɛlɛvolɛma ne kɛ: Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛhyele ɛhɔne na bɛlile nyane wɔ siane nnu ne mɔ anu, wɔ ɛvolɛ abulasuu ye mɔɔ ɛze ɛhɔ la anu la, asoo mame me ti a bɛhyele ɛhɔne ne a? 6Mɔɔ bɛdi, bɛanlo la, asoo mame me ti ɔ? Se bɛlile, bɛnlonle bɛmanle bɛ nwo!
7“Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Gyɛlusalɛm le gbudugbudu na awie biala asa ɛyia ɔ nwo, mɔɔ ɛnee azuamgbole ɛbɔ ɛyia ye, na ye nyiakɛ nee ye adɔleɛ ndololeɛ nu kɔsɔɔti le menli ngome la, Ɛdɛnkɛma ammaa ye alumua kpɔmanvolɛma ambɔ edwɛkɛ ɛhye mɔ nolo angile bɛ ɔ?”
Anzosesebɛyɛlɛ ahatualɛ a le nlɔnuhɔlɛ
8Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele Zɛkalaya. 9Ɔse, “Medame, Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, mese: Bɛbua ndɛne nɔhalɛ nu, bɛyɛ ahunlunyele na bɛze bɛ nwo anwunvɔne ngoko ngoko; 10bɛmmasisi ahunlanvolɛ, menli mɔɔ ɛnlɛ bɛ ze mɔ, nyɛvolɛ anzɛɛ ehyianvolɛma; yɛɛ bɛ biala mmafa ɔ diema anwo adwenle ɛtane.”
11Noko menli ne kpole kɛ bɛnrɛdie, na bɛkpunyunle bɛ bati, bɛduoduale bɛ nzo, amaa bɛande edwɛkɛ ne. 12Bɛboɔboale bɛsolole, amaa bɛandie Nyamenle mɛla ne nee edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛzoa ye Sunsum ne yemaa yelua ye alumua kpɔmanvolɛma anwo zo yeha yehile bɛ la. Zɔhane ati Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma vale ɛya kpole, 13na ɔhanle kɛ, “Kɛmɔ menvɛlɛle na bɛandie la, bɛdabɛ bɛvɛlɛle la, medame noko meandie. 14Membɔle bɛ asande wɔ maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ bɛnze bɛ la anu. Na azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛgyakyile ye bɛ nzi la lale ɛkɛ ne mɔɔ awie ɛngɔ, ɛmba zolɛ a, na azɛlɛ kɛnlɛma ne dɔle mgbane.”

english_text:
The Lord's Promises to Zion
1The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
2I love Zion so much that her enemies make me angry. 3I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
4Very old people with walking sticks will once again sit around in Jerusalem, 5while boys and girls play in the streets. 6This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful. 7I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west, 8and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
9I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid. 10Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
11My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before. 12Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky. 13People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
14When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back. 15Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness. 16 But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace. 17Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things.
A Time of Celebration
18The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
19People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
20I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere. 21Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
22Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness. 23When this happens, ten people from nations with different languages will grab a Jew by his clothes and say, “Let us go with you. We've heard that God is on your side.” I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma bɔ ɛwɔkɛ kɛ ɔmaa Gyɛlusalɛm ayɛ kɛ ye dɛba ne la
1Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me. 2Ɔse, “Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, metwe Gyɛlusalɛm anwo nungule kpole kpalɛ, yɛɛ mefa ɛya a metwe ɔ nwo nungule ne a. 3Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mese: Mebazia meahɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, mebahɔ meahɔdɛnla Gyɛlusalɛm avinli, na bɛbavɛlɛ Gyɛlusalɛm nɔhalɛ suakpole, na bɛavɛlɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Boka ne Boka Nwuanzanwuanza. 4Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mese: Mrenya mrelera nee mraalɛ mrelera eza badɛnlɛdɛnla Gyɛlusalɛm gua ne mɔ azo, ko biala bava kpɔma a adia a, ɔluakɛ yeyɛ ɛrelera. 5Suakpole ne azo gua ne mɔ azo bayɛ ngakula mrenya nee mraalɛ ngome mɔɔ ɛlɛdi nwɔhoa a.
6“Na medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebiza kɛ: Saa ɔyɛ azibɛnwo ɔmaa bɛdabɛ Dwuuma mɔɔ bɛha la bɛ nye zo wɔ mekɛ ɛhye anu a, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ ɔyɛ medame noko azibɛnwo ɔ? 7Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mese: Bɛnlea, mebalie me menli ne meavi adɔleɛ nee aduduleɛ maanle ne mɔ anu, 8na meava bɛ meara meamaa bɛaradɛnla Gyɛlusalɛm. Bɛbayɛ me menli na meayɛ bɛ Nyamenle, wɔ nɔhalɛlilɛ nee tenleneyɛlɛ nu.”
9Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛtie edwɛkɛ ɛhye mɔ bɛavi me kpɔmanvolɛma anloa la, bɛnyia akɛnrasesebɛ, kɛmɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛwula Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Sua ne aze la bɛnyianle la, amaa bɛahola bɛazi Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne. 10Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ ɛnee mekɛ zɔhane ɛtɛdwule la, bɛmbɔ awie ɛkpa bɛndua ye kakɛ yɛɛ bɛmbɔ awie nane ɛkpa bɛndua ye kakɛ, yɛɛ awie biala ɛnva ɔ nwo kɔlɔnwo ɛngɔ ɛmba wɔ ye kpɔvolɛma asa anu, ɔluakɛ ɛnee meye ɛkpɔlɛ medo awie biala nee ɔ gɔnwo avinli. 11Na kɛkala me nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛha la ɛnrɛli ye kɛ mɔɔ alumua ne me nee bɛ lile la, medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a. 12Bɛbalua bɛ aleɛ anzonudwolɛ nu; vanye mbaka bazo, na azɛlɛ ne amaa bɛ aleɛ ahye, yɛɛ ɛbɔlɛ badɔ amaa bɛ. Mebamaa menli ɛhye mɔ abo zo amra mɔɔ ɛha la anyia ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ amuala. 13Na kɛmɔ bɛyɛ amowa ɛfenle wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ avinli la, zɔhane ala, O Dwuuma nee Yizilayɛma, yɛɛ mebalie bɛ na bɛayɛ nyilalɛ bɛamaa maanle maanle ne mɔ a. Yemɔti bɛmmasulo, na bɛnyia akɛnrasesebɛ.”
14Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛ ze mɔ hanle me ɛya la, menyianle adwenle kɛ me nee bɛ di ye ɛtane zo, na amgba noko menyɛle. 15Na kɛkala, medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, menyia adwenle bieko kɛ mekɛ ɛhye anu meyɛ boɛ meamaa Gyɛlusalɛm nee Dwudama amuala. Yemɔti bɛmmasulo. 16 Ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ la ɛne: Bɛha nɔhalɛ bɛhile bɛ nwo ngoko, bɛyia nu a bɛbua ndɛne nɔhalɛ nu na bɛmaa anzonudwolɛ ɛrɛla. 17Bɛmmafa bɛ gɔnwo mɔ anwo adwenle ɛtane, yɛɛ bɛmmadie ndane adalɛ biala bɛto nu, ɔluakɛ mekyi ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ amuala, medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.”
18Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me, ɔse, 19“Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mese: Ɛhɔne ne mɔɔ bɛkye ye siane nna ne, siane nnu ne, siane nsuu ne yɛɛ siane bulu ne mɔ anu la bayɛ anyelielɛ nee fɛlɛkolilɛ mekɛ amaa Dwudama na bɛado ɛkponle anyelielɛ nu. Yemɔti bɛhulo nɔhalɛ nee anzonudwolɛ.”
20Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Menli dɔɔnwo bara; 21menli vi azuamgbole dɔɔnwo azo bahɔ azuamgbole zo ahɔze kɛ, ‘Bɛmaa yɛha yɛ nwo waa yɛhɔ yɛhɔzɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma na yɛzonle Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma. Bɛrɛla bɛmaa yɛhɔ.’ 22Maanle maanle mɔɔ anwo yɛ se nee menli ngakyile ngakyile barakpondɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma abo zo bɛazonle ye wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, na bɛazɛlɛ ye moalɛ. 23Mekɛ ne anu mrenya bulu vi maanle maanle ne mɔ nee aneɛ ngakyile ne mɔ anu barazɔ Dwuunli tɛladeɛ nu na bɛaha kɛ, ‘Maa yɛ nee wɔ ɛhɔ, ɔluakɛ yɛde kɛ Nyamenle nee bɛ lua.’ ”

english_text:
Israel's Enemies Will Be Punished
1 This is a message
from the Lord:
His eyes are on everyone,
especially the tribes
of Israel.
So he pronounces judgment
against the cities
of Hadrach and Damascus.
2Judgment will also fall
on the nearby city
of Hamath,
as well as on Tyre and Sidon,
whose people are clever.
3Tyre has built a fortress
and piled up silver and gold,
as though they were dust
or mud from the streets.
4Now the Lord will punish Tyre
with poverty;
he will sink its ships
and send it up in flames.
5 Both Ashkelon and Gaza
will tremble with fear;
Ekron will lose all hope.
Gaza's king will be killed,
and Ashkelon emptied
of its people.
6A mob of half-breeds
will settle in Ashdod,
and the Lord himself
will rob Philistia of pride.
7No longer will the Philistines
eat meat with blood in it
or any unclean food.
They will become part
of the people of our God
from the tribe of Judah.
And God will accept
the people of Ekron,
as he did the Jebusites.
8God says, “I will stand guard
to protect my temple from those
who come to attack.
I know what's happening,
and no one will mistreat
my people ever again.”
The Lord Tells about the Coming King
9 Everyone in Jerusalem,
celebrate and shout!
Your king has won a victory,
and he is coming to you.
He is humble
and rides on a donkey;
he comes on the colt
of a donkey.
10 I, the Lord, will take away
war chariots and horses
from Israel and Jerusalem.
Bows that were made for battle
will be broken.
I will bring peace to nations,
and your king will rule
from sea to sea.
His kingdom will reach
from the Euphrates River
across the earth.
The Lord Promises To Rescue Captives
11 When I made a sacred agreement
with you, my people,
we sealed it with blood.
Now some of you are captives
in waterless pits,
but I will come to your rescue
12and offer you hope.
Return to your fortress,
because today I will reward you
with twice what you had.
13I will use Judah as my bow
and Israel as my arrow.
I will take the people of Zion
as my sword
and attack the Greeks.
The Lord Will Protect His People
14Like a cloud, the Lord God
will appear over his people,
and his arrows will flash
like lightning.
God will sound his trumpet
and attack in a whirlwind
from the south.
15The Lord All-Powerful
will protect his people,
and they will trample down
the sharpshooters
and their slingshots.
They will drink and get rowdy;
they will be as full as a bowl
at the time of sacrifice.
16The Lord God will save them
on that day,
because they are his people,
and they will shine on his land
like jewels in a crown.
17How lovely they will be.
Young people will grow there
like grain in a field
or grapes in a vineyard.
translation_text:
Maanle maanle mɔɔ zuozua Yizilayɛ la ndɛnebualɛ
1 Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ ne ɛne: Luk 10.13-14
Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ ne tia Heedelakema yɛɛ ɔbadwu Dɛmasekɛsema anwo zo. Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ nee Selea maanle ne suakpole ne ɛyɛ ye ɛdeɛ. 2Zɔhane ala yɛɛ Heemate mɔɔ wɔ Heedelakema ɛweɛne zo, Tayama yɛɛ Saedɛnema mɔɔ ze nrɛlɛbɛ la le Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdeɛ a. 3Tayama ɛzi aranemgbole na bɛboɔboa dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke nloa edukue edukue kɛ gua zo ndɛtɛlɛ. 4Noko nea, Ɛdɛnkɛma baza bɛ alie bɛ ninyɛne na yeavuandi bɛ anwonyia yeagua nyevile nu, na bɛado senle suakpole ne azo bɛayela ye.
5 Menli mɔɔ wɔ suakpole Ahyekɛlɔn azo la banwu ɛhye, na ɛzulolɛ baha bɛ. Gazama banwu ye, na bɛ nwo bafofo bɛ. Ɛkelɔnoma noko banwu ye, na bɛanwu kɛ bɛ anyelazo muala ɛwie. Gaza belemgbunli ne bawu, yɛɛ Ahyekɛlɔn bayɛ kulofenle (suadu). Emɔ 1.6-8; Zɛf 2.4-7 6Menli ngakyile baradɛnla Ahyedɔdo; na Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa Filisitiama adubɛnwo ne abɔ aze. 7Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Bɛnrɛli nane mɔɔ mogya wɔ nu nee bɛkyi aleɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛdi la bieko. Menli mɔɔ baha la bayɛ me menli; bɛbayɛ kɛ abusua ekpulike wɔ Dwuda, yɛɛ Ɛkelɔnoma bayɛ kɛ Gyibɛsema la. 8Akee mebadɛnla me sua ne anyunlu kɛ sinzavolɛ, amaa awie biala andia kilikili anze ɛkɛ. Awie ɛnrɛsisi bɛ bieko, ɔluakɛ medame me nye nwiɔ ɛnwu nyane mɔɔ bɛlɛnwu ye la.”
Kenlebie belemgbunli ne
9 O Zayɔnoma, bɛmaa bɛ nye ɛlie!
O Gyɛlusalɛmma, bɛdea nu kpole kpalɛ!
Bɛnlea, bɛ belemgbunli ne ɛlɛba bɛ ɛkɛ;
ɔlɛba ye konimlilɛ nu.
Ɔle bɛlɛvo yɛɛ ɔde asoaso zo,
asoaso ralɛ zo.
10 Ɛdɛnkɛma se,
“Mebabubu Yifelaem konle ehwili ne mɔ
na meaye bɛ konle mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm.
Mebabubu bɛ konle ɛda ne mɔ anu,
na ɔbamaa anzonudwolɛ aha maanle maanle ne mɔ.
Ye belemgbunlililɛ badwu ɛnwea ɛnwea,
ɔvi Azule Yufileti ne anloa yeahɔdwu ewiade awieleɛ.”
Nyamenle menli ne sia ayɛ kɛ bɛ dɛba ne la
11 Ɛdɛnkɛma se,
“Kɛmɔ me nee wɔ ɛyɛ ngyekyeleɛ
mɔɔ bɛva azubɔlɛ mogya bɛzɔ ɔ nloa la ati,
mebadwula wɔ menli ne mɔɔ bɛhye bɛ nuokɛ la,
mebaye bɛ meavi kuma ne mɔɔ nzule ɛnle nu la anu.
12Bɛzia bɛrɛla bɛ ɛvealeka ne,
O bɛmɛ pilizama mɔɔ bɛlɛ anyelazo a,
ɛnɛ meka meahile bɛ kɛ,
debie biala mɔɔ bɛminli ye la,
mebamaa bɛanyia ye mɔnwo.
13Ɔluakɛ meva Dwuda meyɛ me ɛda mekpo.
meva Yizilayɛ meyɛ me ɛda mbaka.
O Zayɔn, mebado bɛ mra mrenya kɛ dadeɛ,
meava meaha Gilikima senle,
na meanwɔha bɛ kɛ kovolɛ dadeɛ.”
14Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma bavinde bɛ ti zo anwuma;
ɔbatoto ye ɛda ne kɛ ɛsɛlɛmanye;
Awulae Nyamenle ne babɔ aweɛne tendenle ne anu,
na yealua nyiakɛ ahumuakyima ne anu yeara.
15Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bawowa bɛ;
bɛbahu totoabɔma ne bɛatietia bɛ nwo zo.
Bɛbayɛ begyebegye kɛ asɛɛ bɛbo nza;
bɛbaha bɛ kpɔvolɛma mogya bɛagua,
yeazonyi kɛ asɛɛ ɔgyi kɔpo nu
na bɛlɛwola bɛagua azukponle ne mgbɛne zo.
16Mekɛ ne anu Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne balie bɛ,
ɔluakɛ bɛle ye menli.
Bɛle kɛ belemgbunli abɔtile zo mgbɔba,
bɛbada ye azɛlɛ ne azo.
17Ɛhɛe, azɛlɛ ne bayɛ kpalɛ, ayɛ kɛnlɛma!
Zolɛ abɛlɛ nee nwanye fofolɛ
bamaa zolɛ mgbavolɛ nee mbɛlɛra anyia anwosesebɛ.

english_text:
A Bright Future for Judah and Israel
1I, the Lord, am the one
who sends storm clouds
and showers of rain
to make fields produce.
So when the crops need rain,
you should pray to me.
2 You can't believe idols
and fortunetellers,
or depend on the hope
you receive from witchcraft
and interpreters of dreams.
But you have tried all of these,
and now you are like sheep
without a shepherd.
3I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am fiercely angry
with you leaders,
and I will punish you.
I care for my people,
the nation of Judah,
and I will change
this flock of sheep
into charging war horses.
4From this flock will come leaders
who will be strong
like cornerstones and tent pegs
and weapons of war.
5They will join in the fighting,
and together they will trample
their enemies like mud.
They will fight,
because I, the Lord,
will be on their side.
And they will crush
the enemy cavalry.
6I will strengthen
the kingdoms of Judah
and Israel.
And I will show mercy
because I am the Lord,
their God.
I will answer their prayers
and bring them home.
Then it will seem as though
I had never rejected them.
7Israel will be like
a tribe of warriors
celebrating with wine.
When their children see this,
they will also be happy
because of me, the Lord.
8I will give a signal
for them to come together
because I have rescued them.
And there will be as many
as ever before.
9 Although I scattered my people
in distant countries,
they won't forget me.
Once their children are raised,
they will return—
10I will bring them home
from Egypt and Assyria,
then let them settle
as far as Gilead and Lebanon,
until the land overflows
with them.
11My people will go through
an ocean of troubles,
but I will overcome the waves
and dry up the deepest part
of the Nile.
Assyria's great pride
will be put down,
and the power of Egypt
will disappear.
12I'll strengthen my people
because of who I am,
and they will follow me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma bɔ ngoanelielɛ nwo ɛwɔkɛ
1Bɛbiza Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ ɔmaa ezule ɛdɔ wɔ nyenyensuo mekɛ nu. Ɛdɛnkɛma a maa anwomanyunlu yɛ dukuduku na ɔtɔ ezule ɔmaa menli, na ɔmaa awie biala egyinli kye a. 2Mmonle ananze ne mɔ ka ngoaseasɛm, ngonyiama bɔ adalɛ, yɛɛ menli mɔɔ ka ɛlalɛ la nwu adalɛ yekile, bɛfa bɛbɛlɛbɛla awie mɔ kɛ bɛfa bɛakyekye bɛ rɛle. Zɔhane ati menli ne duolua nuhua kɛ mboane; bɛnwu amaneɛ, ɔboalekɛ bɛnlɛ neavolɛ.
3Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Meva mboaneneavolɛma ne mɔ anwo ɛya kpole, na mebadea mgbanyima ne mɔ. Ɔluakɛ medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mebanlea me mboane ne, mɔɔ le Dwuda abo zo amra ne, na mebayɛ bɛ me konle mgbɔnwɔ mɔɔ anwo yɛ ɛzulolɛ a. 4Bɛ nuhua yɛɛ menli vi bara arabu maanle ne, arayɛ maanle mgbanyima nee safohyenlema na bɛazie me menli ne a. 5Bɛbɔ nuhua a, bɛbayɛ menli anwo ɛzulolɛ wɔ konle nu, bɛatietia bɛ agbɔvolɛ nwo zo wɔ guabile ne mɔ azo. Bɛbaho ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma nee bɛ lua, na bɛbali kpɔvolɛ konlema ne mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ la anwo zo konim.
6“Mebamaa Dwudama anwo ayɛ se,
yɛɛ mebalie Dwosefi sua nu amra.
Mebanwu bɛ anwunvɔne,
na me nee bɛ kɔsɔɔti azia ara sua nu.
Bɛbayɛ kɛ asɛɛ metɛkpole bɛ,
ɔluakɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a,
mebadie bɛ nzɛlɛlɛ.
7Yifelaemma bayɛ kɛ katakyiema,
na bɛali fɛlɛko kɛ menli mɔɔ ɛnlo nza la.
Bɛ mra banwu ye na bɛ nye alie,
na bɛali fɛlɛko wɔ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyɛ la anwo.
8“Mebavɛlɛ bɛ na meaboɔboa bɛ nloa,
ɔluakɛ melie bɛ,
na bɛ nwo bazo kɛ dɛba ne la.
9Mendele bɛ memkpondenle maanle maanle avinli bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ,
noko wɔ moa moa maanle ne mɔ anu lɔ, bɛbahakye me,
na bɛ nee bɛ mra bɛbadɛnla ngoane nu na bɛazia bɛara.
10Me nee bɛ vi Yigyibiti nee Aselea
bazia ara sua nu.
Mebava bɛ meahɔgua Geleade nee Lɛbanɔn azɛlɛ zo,
bɛbava azɛlɛ ne amuala, noko ɔnrɛza bɛ.
11Bɛbalua ngyegyelɛ nyevile nu,
na medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebabɔ nyevile azɛlɛkye ne mɔ,
na Azule Naele ne basesa, awe resee.
Aselea adubɛnloanu ne baha aze,
na Yigyibiti tumi ne bavi ɔ sa.
12Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma me ti,
mebamaa bɛ nwo ayɛ se;
bɛbazonle me na bɛadie me ne.”
Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛdendɛ a.

english_text:
Trouble for Israel's Enemies
1Lebanon, open your gates!
Let the fire come in
to destroy your cedar trees.
2Cry, you cypress trees!
The glorious cedars have fallen
and are rotting.
Cry, you oak trees of Bashan!
The dense forest
has been chopped down.
3Listen! Shepherds are crying.
Their glorious pastures
have been ruined.
Listen! Lions are roaring.
The forests of the Jordan Valley
are no more to be found.
Worthless Shepherds
4The Lord my God said to me:
Tend those sheep doomed for slaughter! 5The people who buy and butcher them go unpunished, while everyone who sells them says, “Praise the Lord! I'm rich.” Not even their shepherds have pity on them.
6Tend those sheep because I, the Lord, will no longer have pity on the people of this earth. I'll turn neighbor against neighbor and make them slaves of a king. They will bring disaster on the earth, and I'll do nothing to rescue any of them.
7So I became a shepherd of those sheep doomed to be slaughtered by the sheep dealers. And I gave names to the two sticks I used for tending the sheep: One of them was named “Mercy” and the other “Unity.” 8In less than a month, I became impatient with three shepherds who didn't like me, and I got rid of them. 9Then I said, “I refuse to be your shepherd. Let the sheep that are going to die, go on and die, and those that are going to be destroyed, go on and be destroyed. Then let the others eat one another alive.”
10On that same day, I broke the stick named “Mercy” to show that the Lord had canceled his agreement with all people. 11The sheep dealers who saw me knew at once that this was a message from the Lord. 12-13 I told them, “Pay me my wages, if you think you should; otherwise, forget it.” So they handed me my wages, a measly 30 pieces of silver.
Then the Lord said, “Throw the money into the treasury.” So I threw the money into the treasury at the Lord's temple. 14Then I broke the stick named “Unity” and canceled the ties between Judah and Israel.
15Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd. 16Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
17You worthless shepherd,
deserting the sheep!
I hope a sword
will cripple your arm
and blind your right eye.
translation_text:
Amumuyɛma azedɔlɛ
1O Lɛbanɔnoma, bɛbukebuke bɛ nlenkɛ ne mɔ,
amaa senle ne ayela bɛ sida mbaka ne mɔ!
2Sepelɛse mbaka, bɛzu bɛye awolɛ,
na sida mbaka ngɛnlɛma ne mɔ ɛzɛkye!
Beehyan oku mbaka, bɛzu bɛye awolɛ,
ɔluakɛ bɛzo kpɔkɛmile ne bɔkɔɔ!
3Bɛdie, mboaneneavolɛma ɛlɛsu ye awolɛ,
ɔluakɛ bɛ anyunlunyia ɛdɔ aze!
Bɛdie, awenade ne mɔ ɛlɛkpo,
ɔluakɛ Dwɔdan kpɔkɛmile ne ɛhakyi ɛsɛlɛ!
Mboaneneavolɛma nwiɔ ne
4Ɛdɛnkɛma me Nyamenle ne zele me kɛ, “Yɛ mboane ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ ɛlɛkɔ ahunleɛ la neavolɛ. 5Menli mɔɔ tɔ la ku bɛ fa bɛ nwo dwɔɔ kɔ, awie ɛnze bɛ ɛhwee, yɛɛ menli mɔɔ tɔne bɛ la ka kɛ, ‘Ayɛlɛyelɛ ɛha Ɛdɛnkɛma, menyia me nwo;’ yɛɛ bɛ neavolɛma mumua ne ɛnze bɛ anwunvɔne.”
6(Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Medame menrɛze awie biala anwunvɔne wɔ azɛlɛ ɛhye azo. Nea, mebamaa menli adɔ; ko biala badɔ ye mboaneneavolɛ ne asa anu, na ye mboaneneavolɛ ne adɔ ye belemgbunli ne asa anu, bɛava bɛazɛkye azɛlɛ ye, na menrɛlie biala.”)
7Yemɔti menyɛle mboane ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ ɛlɛkɔ ahunleɛ bɛamaa menli mɔɔ di mboane awule gua la neavolɛ. Menvale agbɔma nwiɔ; mendonle ko “Ɛlolɛ” yɛɛ ko ne noko mendonle ye “Koyɛlɛ”. 8Akee menyɛnenle mboane ne mɔ. Siane ko anu, menzɛkyele mboaneneavolɛma nsa. Me kunlu andwo bɛ nwo fee, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ noko bɛangulo me edwɛkɛ. 9Yemɔti menganle kɛ, “Menrɛyɛ bɛ neavolɛ. Mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ ɔwu la, bɛmaa ɔwu; mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛsɛkye ye la, bɛzɛkye ye na bɛgyakyi bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛha la bɛmaa bɛdabɛ bɛ ngome bɛkeka bɛ nwo ngoko ngoko bɛli.” 10Akee menvale me kpɔma ne mɔɔ medo ye “Ɛlolɛ” la na membubule nu, menvale menzɛkyele ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ me nee maanle maanle ne mɔ ɛkyekye la. 11Yemɔti mentulule ngyekyeleɛ ne kenle ko ne, na nwule ne mɔ mɔɔ di mboane gua, mɔɔ ɛnee ɛlɛnea me la nwunle kɛ ɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anloa edwɛkɛ. 12 Akee menganle mengilele bɛ kɛ, “Saa bɛdabɛ bɛnea na ɔle kpalɛ a, ɛnee bɛdua me kakɛ, na saa bɛnea na ɔnle kpalɛ a, ɛnee bɛmaa ɔha.” Na bɛduale me dwɛtɛ fufule abulasa.
13Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, “Fa kɔgua Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne gya ne anu.” Yemɔti menvale dwɛtɛ fufule ne, ezukoa kpole ne mɔɔ bɛdua bɛmaa me la mengɔnguale Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne gya ne anu. 14Akee membubule me kpɔma ne mɔɔ tɔ zo nwiɔ, mɔɔ medo ye “Koyɛlɛ” la anu mengilele kɛ mezɛkye mediemayɛlɛ mɔɔ la Dwuda nee Yizilayɛ avinli la.
15Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ, “Eza fa mboaneneavolɛ ninyɛne mɔɔ ɛnzonle bolɛ la. 16Ɔluakɛ nea, melɛmaa mboaneneavolɛ bie mɔɔ ɛndwenle mboane mɔɔ ɛlɛwu la anwo, ɔmkpondɛ mɔɔ ɛminli la, ɔnyɛ mɔɔ ɛboda la ayile, yɛɛ ɔmmaa mɔɔ te kpɔkɛ la aleɛ la ara. Ye ɛdeɛ ne a le kɛ, ɔbali mboane ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛlɔ la, yeafufo bɛ mbowule nu. 17Me mboaneneavolɛ mgbane zɔhane, mɔɔ kpo me mboane ne mɔ la, ye gyakɔ! Bɛbapepɛ ɔ sa wɔ konle nu na bɛadu ɔ nye fema ne. Ɔ sa badwe, yɛɛ ɔ nye fema ne bazi bɔkɔɔ.”

english_text:
Victory for Jerusalem
1This is a message from the Lord about Israel:
I am the Lord! I stretched out the heavens; I put the earth on its foundations and gave breath to humans. 2I have decided that Jerusalem will become a bowl of wine that makes the neighboring nations drunk. And when Jerusalem is attacked, Judah will also be attacked. 3But I will turn Jerusalem into a heavy stone that crushes anyone who tries to lift it.
When all nations on earth surround Jerusalem, 4I will blind every horse and make them panic, and every rider will be confused. But at the same time, I will watch over Judah. 5Then every clan in Judah will realize that I, the Lord All-Powerful, am their God, and that I am the source of their strength.
6At that time I will let the clans of Judah be like a ball of fire in a wood pile or a fiery torch in a hay stack. Then Judah will send the surrounding nations up in smoke. And once again the city of Jerusalem will be filled with people.
7But I will first give victory to Judah, so the kingdom of David and the city of Jerusalem in all of their glory won't be thought of more highly than Judah itself. 8I, the Lord God, will protect Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there will be as strong as David, and David's kingdom will rule as though my very own angel were its leader. 9I am determined to wipe out every nation that attacks Jerusalem.
Mourning for the One Pierced with a Spear
10 I, the Lord, will make the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem feel deep sorrow and pray when they see the one they pierced with a spear. They will mourn and weep for him, as parents weep over the death of their only child or their first-born. 11On that day the people of Jerusalem will mourn as much as everyone did for Hadad Rimmon on the flatlands near Megiddo. 12Everyone of each family in the land will mourn, and the men will mourn separately from the women. This includes those from the family of David, and the families of Nathan, 13Levi, Shimei, 14and all other families as well.
translation_text:
Kenlebie Gyɛlusalɛm ɛlielɛ
1Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ fane Yizilayɛma anwo la ɛne: Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ bɔle anwuma, ɔbɔle azɛlɛ, na ɔbɔle sonla sunsum mɔɔ wɔ ye nu la se, 2“Mebayɛ Gyɛlusalɛm kɛ kɔpo mɔɔ nwanye ɛyi ye tɛkɛɛ la; maanle maanle mɔɔ zuozua ye la baranlo bie na bɛabo kɛ tandi. Saa bɛfa ɛlɔnema bɛbabɛnra bɛyia Gyɛlusalɛm a, ɛnee bɛbɛnra bɛyia Dwuda azuamgbole kɔsɔɔti noko. 3Mekɛ ne anu, mebamaa Gyɛlusalɛm ayɛ kɛ bolɛ ɛnlomboɛ yeamaa maanle maanle ne mɔ. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛbɔ ɛhɔne kɛ bɛmaa ye zo la babodɛboda. Azɛlɛ ye azo maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti baboɔboa bɛ nloa atia ye. 4Mekɛ ne anu, medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mese, mebamaa ɛkpɔnwɔ biala anye zo ada ye na mɔɔ ka la agyibi. Na Dwudama ɛdeɛ, saa memaa maanle maanle ne mɔ mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ anye si a, mebabuke me nye na meanlea bɛ. 5Na akee Dwuda mbusua ekpulike ekpulike ne mɔ baha ahile bɛ nwo ngoko kɛ, ‘Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛ Nyamenle ne ati, Gyɛlusalɛm lɛ anwosesebɛ.’
6“Mekɛ ne anu mebamaa Dwuda mbusua ekpulike ekpulike ne mɔ adɔlɔ woonwu kɛ siase mɔɔ gyi senle zo wɔ mbaka avinli, bɛayɛ kɛ tɛkɛ mɔɔ la nya avinli ɛlɛsɔ la. Bɛbazɛkye menli mɔɔ wɔ bɛ bɛne zo nee bɛ fema zo la amuala, na Gyɛlusalɛmma ɛdeɛ, bɛbadɛnla bɛ bo zo ne ala, wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm.
7“Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebamaa Dwuda ɛlɔnema alumua ali konim, amaa Devidi abo zo amra nee Gyɛlusalɛmma annyia bɛ nyunlu andɛla Dwudama. 8Mekɛ ne anu mebawowa Gyɛlusalɛmma, amaa mɔɔ anwo ɛngyinla ye fee bɔbɔ wɔ bɛ avinli la anwo ayɛ se kɛ Devidi. Devidi abo zo amra bayɛ kɛ Nyamenle; bɛbayɛ kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ bɛali menli ne ati. 9Na mekɛ ne anu maanle biala mɔɔ kɛra Gyɛlusalɛm anwo zo la, mebazɛkye ye.
10 “Mebamaa Devidi abo zo amra ne nee Gyɛlusalɛmma aze anwunvɔne dɔɔnwo, na bɛanyia sunsum mɔɔ bɛfa bɛyɛ nzɛlɛlɛ la, amaa bɛnea sonla mɔɔ bɛboda ye la a bɛali nyane bɛamaa ye, kɛmɔ sonla su ɔ ra nrenya kokye mɔɔ ɔlɛ na ɔkɛwu la; bɛbazu ye kɛ sonla mɔɔ ye belamunli ralɛ kɛwu na ɔlɛsu ye la. 11Mekɛ ne anu nyanelilɛ mɔɔ bara Gyɛlusalɛm la bayɛ kɛ nyane ne mɔɔ bɛlile wɔ Heedadelemɔn mɔɔ wɔ Mɛgedo fienemgbole nu la. 12-14Nyanelilɛ bara maanle ne anu amuala. Abusua ekpulike ko biala ɔdaye ɔ ngome ɔbali ye nyane ɛdeɛ. Devidi abo zo amra, Neetan abo zo amra, Livae abo zo amra, Hyemɛyae abo zo amra, yɛɛ mbusua ekpulike ekpulike mɔɔ ɛha la amuala bali nyane bɛ ti bɛ ti, abusua ekpulike ko biala anu mrenya bali bɛ nyane ɛdeɛ ngome na bɛ mraalɛ noko ali bɛ nyane ɛdeɛ ngome.

english_text:
Getting Rid of Idols and False Prophets
1In the future there will be a fountain, where David's descendants and the people of Jerusalem can wash away their sin and guilt.
2The Lord All-Powerful says:
When that time comes, I will get rid of every idol in the country, and they will be forgotten forever. I will also do away with their prophets and those evil spirits that control them. 3If any such prophets ever appear again, their own parents must warn them that they will die for telling lies in my name—the name of the Lord. If those prophets don't stop speaking, their parents must then kill them with a sword.
4Those prophets will be ashamed of their so-called visions, and they won't deceive anyone by dressing like a true prophet. 5Instead, they will say, “I'm no prophet. I've been a farmer all my life.”
6And if any of them are asked why they are wounded, they will answer, “It happened at the house of some friends.”
A Wounded Shepherd and Scattered Sheep
7 The Lord All-Powerful said:
My sword, wake up! Attack
my shepherd and friend.
Strike down the shepherd!
Scatter the little sheep,
and I will destroy them.
8Nowhere in the land
will more than a third of them
be left alive.
9Then I will purify them
and put them to the test,
just as gold and silver
are purified and tested.
They will pray in my name,
and I will answer them.
I will say, “You are my people,”
and they will reply,
“You, Lord, are our God!”
translation_text:
1“Mekɛ ne anu bɛbabuke nzufeanvea bɛava bɛanrinzi Devidi abo zo amra nee Gyɛlusalɛmma amuala ɛtane nee evinli biala bɛagua. 2Mekɛ ne anu, medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mese, mebaminliminli mmonle mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu nee bɛ aluma kɔsɔɔti abo zo, amaa bɛangakye bɛ bieko; eza mebadu kpɔmanvolɛma adalɛ nee sunsum ɛtane ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti meavi azɛlɛ ne azo. 3Na saa awie biala finde kɛ ɔle Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ a, ɔ ze nee ɔ nli mɔɔ wole ye la baze ye kɛ, ‘Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛku wɔ, ɔluakɛ ɛfa Ɛdɛnkɛma duma ɛbɔ adalɛ.’ Na ɔ ze nee ɔ nli bawɔ ye atwɛ ahu ye nee ye Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne. 4Mekɛ ne anu Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ biala mɔɔ baha Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ, yeaha ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ edwɛkɛ la baze nwolɛ nyiane. Ɔnrɛva ɛdanlɛ mɔɔ bɛnwo ye futuu la ɔnrɛheda ɔ ti zo ɔnrɛbɛlɛbɛla menli. 5Ɔbaha kɛ, ‘Menle Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ, mele ɛyazonlɛnli, ɔluakɛ sumunli me ngakula nu ɛbɔ nu egyinli ala a meyɛ a.’ 6Na saa awie biza ye kɛ, ‘Na nganlɛ ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ wɔ ɛ nzi la noko ɛ?’ a, ɔbaha kɛ, ‘Bɛle nganlɛ mɔɔ me gɔnwo mɔ mɔɔ mengɔle bɛ sua nu la bɔle me a.’ ”
Nyamenle se bɛhu ye mboaneneavolɛ ne
7 Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Dwazo, konle dadeɛ, dwazo ku me mboaneneavolɛ ne, ku ahenle ne mɔɔ gyi me nwo ɛke la. Bɔ mboaneneavolɛ ne ku ye maa mboane ne mɔ ɛbɔ asande. Medame mebava me sa meazie ngyikyi ne mɔ anwo. 8Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mese, azɛlɛ ye amuala, mebahyɛ nu nsa na meazɛkye nwiɔ, meaminli bɛ bo zo. Nuhua ɛkpɔ ko ala a baha a. 9Ekpunli ko ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa bɔbɔ la, mebagua bɛ senle nu meadu bɛ nuhua, kɛmɔ bɛtu dwɛtɛ fufule nu la, na meazɔ bɛ meanlea, kɛmɔ bɛsɔ ezukoa nvutuke bɛnea la. Bɛbabɔ me duma bɛavɛlɛ me, na mebalie bɛ zo. Mebaha kɛ, ‘Bɛle me menli’ na bɛbaha kɛ, ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma le me Nyamenle.’ ”

english_text:
War and Victory
1The Lord will have his day. And when it comes, everything that was ever taken from Jerusalem will be returned and divided among its people. 2But first, he will bring many nations to attack Jerusalem—homes will be robbed, women raped, and half of the population dragged off, though the others will be allowed to remain.
3The Lord will attack those nations like a warrior fighting in battle. 4He will take his stand on the Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem, and the mountain will split in half, forming a wide valley that runs from east to west. 5Then you people will escape from the Lord's mountain, through this valley, which reaches to Azal. You will run in all directions, just as everyone did when the earthquake struck in the time of King Uzziah of Judah. Afterwards, the Lord my God will appear with his holy angels.
6It will be a bright day that won't turn cloudy or cold. 7And the Lord has decided when it will happen—this time of unending day.
8 In both summer and winter, life-giving streams will flow from Jerusalem, half of them to the Dead Sea in the east and half to the Mediterranean Sea in the west. 9Then there will be only one Lord who rules as King and whose name is worshiped everywhere on earth.
10-11 From Geba down to Rimmon south of Jerusalem, the entire country will be turned into flatlands, with Jerusalem still towering above. Then the city will be full of people, from Benjamin Gate, Old Gate Place, and Hananel Tower in the northeast part of the city over to Corner Gate in the northwest and down to King's Wine Press in the south. Jerusalem will always be secure and will never again be destroyed.
12Here is what the Lord will do to those who attack Jerusalem: While they are standing there, he will make their flesh rot and their eyes fall from their sockets and their tongues drop out. 13The Lord will make them go into a frenzy and start attacking each other, 14-15until even the people of Judah turn against those in Jerusalem. This same terrible disaster will also strike every animal nearby, including horses, mules, camels, and donkeys. Finally, everything of value in the surrounding nations will be collected and brought to Jerusalem—gold, silver, and piles of clothing.
16 Afterwards, the survivors from those nations that attacked Jerusalem will go there each year to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters. 17No rain will fall on the land of anyone in any country who refuses to go to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful. 18-19This horrible disaster will strike the Egyptians and everyone else who refuses to go there for the celebration.
20-21At that time the words “Dedicated to the Lord” will be engraved on the bells worn by horses. In fact, every ordinary cooking pot in Jerusalem will be just as sacred to the Lord All-Powerful as the bowls used at the altar. Any one of them will be acceptable for boiling the meat of sacrificed animals, and there will no longer be a need to sell special pots and bowls.
translation_text:
Gyɛlusalɛm nee maanle maanle ne mɔ
1Bɛdie, Ɛdɛnkɛma kenle ne ɛlɛba, mɔɔ ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛrawua wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm ɛke la bɛbahyɛ wɔ bɛ nye zo ɛke ala. 2Mebaboɔboa maanle maanle ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti anloa meamaa bɛ nee Gyɛlusalɛm aho na bɛava suakpole ne. Bɛbave bɛ ninyɛne na bɛafunlofunla bɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ. Bɛbahye suakpole ne azo amra foa ko bɛahɔ nlɔnu, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛha la, bɛbadɛnla ɛkɛ ne. 3Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma bahɔ na ɔ nee maanle maanle ne mɔ ahɔho, kɛmɔ ɔyɛ a konle nu ɔyɛ la. 4Mekɛ ne anu ɔbava ɔ gyakɛ yeazie Ɔlivi Boka ne mɔɔ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm aduduleɛ la azo, na boka ne bakpuke nwiɔ, ɔvi aduduleɛ yeahɔdɔ adɔleɛ, yeaye bɔnza tɛtɛlɛ kpalɛ yeado ɛkɛ; ɛhye bamaa boka ne foa ko ahɔli sɔlɔ na foa ko arali nyiakɛ. 5Bɛbanriandi bɛahɔ me awoka ne mɔ bɔnza ne anu, ɔluakɛ bɔnza ne anu badɛlɛ toonwo adwu Ezɛle. Bɛbanriandi, kɛmɔ bɛ nlenya mɔ nriandile azɛlɛkpusulɛ mekɛ ne anu wɔ Dwuda Belemgbunli Ɛzaya mekɛ zo la. Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne bara, na ɔ nee Nyamenle menli ne mɔ amuala ara.
6Kenle zɔhane, wuluwulu ɛnrɛra yɛɛ ɛyɛlɛ ɛnrɛra. 7Ɔbayɛ kenle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɔdaye ala a ɔze a. Aleɛ ɛnrɛdwo na aleɛ ahye, ɔluakɛ aledwolɛ bayɛ wienyi kɛ alehyenlɛ la.
8 Mekɛ ne anu, ngoane nzule bazenze avi Gyɛlusalɛm, foa ko bazenze ahɔgua aduduleɛ nyevile ne anu na foa ko noko ahɔgua adɔleɛ nyevile ne anu. Fɔsɛlɛ nu o, wawaa nu o, kɛ ɔsi ɔsenze la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔbazenze mekɛ biala a. 9Ɛdɛnkɛma bali azɛlɛ ye kɔsɔɔti azo belemgbunli; mekɛ ne anu awie biala bazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ yemɔ a ɔle Nyamenle kokye ne a yɛɛ ye duma ko.
10Azɛlɛ ne kpokpoti, ɔvi Giba mɔɔ kɔdwu Relemɔn mɔɔ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm nyiakɛ la bayɛ fienemgbole. Na Gyɛlusalɛm bagyinla kpundii wɔ ɔ bo zo ne wɔ boka zo, ɔvi Bɛngyaman Anlenkɛ Kpole nloa yeahɔ anlenkɛ kpole dɛba ne anwo, yeahɔdwu Muleɛ Anlenkɛ Kpole ne anloa, na ɔvi Hananili Tawa ne anwo yeahɔdwu belemgbunli ne nwanyeyɛlɛ ɛleka ne mɔ. 11 Menli bayi zo gbudugbudu, ɔluakɛ munzule biala ɛnrɛra zolɛ. Gyɛlusalɛmma badɛnla mɔɔ awie ɛngyegye bɛ a.
12Akee ewule mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bava ado maanle maanle mɔɔ kɛva konle kɛdoa Gyɛlusalɛm la anwo la ɛne: bɛ nwonane bakpɔlɔ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛde ngoane nu la, bɛ nye bakpɔlɔ bɛ nye mbɔne ne mɔ anu, yɛɛ bɛ tafinlima bakpɔlɔ bɛ nloa anu.
13Mekɛ ne anu Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa sulosulo adɔ bɛ nwo na bɛ nye zo ada bɛ, amaa bɛadwazo bɛdabɛ bɛ ngome bɛ nwo zo ngoko ngoko. 14Dwudama bɔbɔ baho atia Gyɛlusalɛmma. Bɛbave anwonyia mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la amuala; ezukoa nvutuke, dwɛtɛ fufule, yɛɛ adɛladeɛ ngɛnlɛma dɔɔnwo mɔɔ zonle bo zolɛ.
15Ewulenzane badɔ mgbɔnwɔ, mgbɔnwɔndua, afunlumu, asoaso, yɛɛ nane biala mɔɔ wɔ kpɔvolɛ ne azokoɛleɛ la avinli.
16Akee awie biala mɔɔ wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛra Gyɛlusalɛm anwo zo ɛlɛ la anu, mɔɔ kɛvi ɛsalɛ la bahɔ Gyɛlusalɛm ɛvolɛ biala ahɔzonle Belemgbunli ne, Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, na yeali ye Kpɔda Bo Ɛdɛnlanlɛ Ɛvoyia ne. 17Na saa azɛlɛ ye azo abusua ekpulike bie wɔ ɛkɛ na yeangɔ Gyɛlusalɛm yeangɔnzonle Belemgbunli ne, Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a, ezule ɛnrɛdɔ bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo. 18Saa Yigyibitima kpo na bɛangɔnva bɛ nwo bɛangile a, ewulenzane ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma fa to maanle maanle mɔɔ angɔnli Kpɔda Bo Ɛdɛnlanlɛ Ɛvoyia ne bie la anwo la ado bɛ avinli. 19Ɛhye a bayɛ Yigyibitima nee maanle maanle ne mɔ mɔɔ kɛkpo na bɛangɔnli Kpɔda Bo Ɛdɛnlanlɛ Ɛvoyia ne la ndeanlɛ a. 20Mekɛ ne anu bɛbahɛlɛ ɛhye wɔ mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ dɔne ne mɔ anwo kɛ, “Bɛdu bɛzie ahane bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma.” Siase mɔɔ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu la bayɛ kɛ azukponle ne azo dwora; 21yɛɛ siase biala mɔɔ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm nee Dwuda la, bɛbadu bɛazie ahane bɛamaa Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, amaa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛra kɛ bɛbabɔ azu la ava ado bɛ azubɔlɛ aleɛ ne. Awie ɛnrɛli gua wɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu wɔ mekɛ ne anu.

english_text:
1I am Malachi. And this is the message that the Lord gave me for Israel.
The Lord's Love for Israel
2 Israel, I, the Lord, have loved you. And yet you ask in what way have I loved you. Don't forget that Esau was the brother of your ancestor Jacob, but I chose Jacob 3instead of Esau. And I turned Esau's hill country into a barren desert where jackals roam. 4Esau's descendants may say, “Although our nation Edom is in ruins, we will rebuild it.”
But I, the Lord All-Powerful, promise to tear down whatever they build. Then everyone will know that I will never stop being angry with them as long as they are so sinful.
5Israel, when you see this, you will shout, “The Lord's great reputation reaches beyond our borders.”
Judgment against Priests
6I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something to say to you priests. Children respect their fathers, and servants respect their masters. I am your father and your master, so why don't you respect me? You priests have insulted me, and now you ask, “How did we insult you?”
7You embarrass me by offering worthless food on my altar. Then you ask, “How have we embarrassed you?” You have done it by saying, “What's so great about the Lord's altar?”
8 But isn't it wrong to offer animals that are blind, lame, or sick? Just try giving those animals to your governor. That certainly wouldn't please him or make him want to help you. 9I am the Lord God All-Powerful, and you had better try to please me. You have sinned. Now see if I will have mercy on any of you.
10I wish someone would lock the doors of my temple, so you would stop wasting time building fires on my altar. I am not pleased with you priests, and I refuse to accept any more of your offerings. 11From dawn until dusk my name is praised by every nation on this earth, as they burn incense and offer the proper sacrifices to me. 12But even you priests insult me by saying, “There's nothing special about the Lord's altar, and these sacrifices are worthless.”
13You get so disgusted that you even make vulgar signs at me. And for an offering, you bring stolen animals or those that are lame or sick. Should I accept these? 14Instead of offering the acceptable animals you have promised, you bring me those that are unhealthy. I will punish you for this, because I am the great King, the Lord All-Powerful, and I am worshiped by nations everywhere.
translation_text:
1Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ ɔluale Malakae anwo zo ɔvale ɔmanle Yizilayɛma la ɛne:
Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhulolɛ mɔɔ ɔkulo Yizilayɛma la
2 Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mehulo bɛ.”
Noko bɛmɛ bɛse, “Kɛ wɔzi wɔhulo yɛ ɛ?”
Ɛdɛnkɛma biza bɛ kɛ, “Asoo tɛ Yisɔ adiema a le Gyekɔbo? Noko mehulo Gyekɔbo, Emɔ 1.11-12; Oba 1-14 3na mekpɔ Yisɔ. Memaa ye awoka zo azɛlɛ ɛhakyi ɛsɛlɛ na meva ye agyadeɛ muala mewula ɛsɛlɛ zo boboduma ne mɔ asa anu.”
4Saa Yidɔmma ka kɛ, “Bɛzɛkye yɛ maanle ye bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko yɛbazia yɛakyekye ye fofolɛ” a, ɛnee kɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne, “Bɛbakyekye bɛ azua ne mɔ, na mebagologolo bɛ meagua. Bɛbavɛlɛ bɛ azɛlɛ ne ‘Amumuyɛ Azɛlɛ’ na bɛavɛlɛ bɛdabɛ mumua ne ‘Menli mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva bɛ nwo ɛya mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ a.’ ”
5Bɛdabɛ bɛbanwu ye bɛ nye zo na bɛaha kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma anwo yɛ ɛzulolɛ wɔ Yizilayɛ anzi lɔ!”
Ɛdɛnkɛma twi sɛlɛvolɛma anyunlu
6Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma biza bɛ kɛ, “Ralɛ di ɔ ze eni yɛɛ akɛlɛ di ɔ menle eni. Na saa mele bɛ ze a, ɛnee eni mɔɔ bɛdi me la a le boni? Yɛɛ saa mele bɛ menle a, ɛnee ɛzulolɛ mɔɔ bɛsulo me la wɔ nienwu? Bɛmɛ sɛlɛvolɛma bɔbɔ yɛɛ bɛsɛkye me duma a. Noko bɛmɛ bɛbiza kɛ, ‘Ɛnee kɛ yɛzi yɛzɛkye wɔ duma ɛ?’ 7Bɛfa aleɛ mɔɔ nwolɛ ɛnde la bɛgua me azukponle zo. Noko bɛbiza kɛ, ‘Kɛ yɛzi yɛgua ɛ nwo evinli ɛ?’ Bɛ adwenle a le kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma azukponle ne bɔbɔ, ɔnle kɛ bɛdi ye eni. 8 Asoo saa bɛfa nane mɔɔ anye ɛzi la bɛba kɛ bɛva bɛbɔ azu bɛmaa me a, ɛnee bɛdabɛ bɛnea a bɛtɛbɔle munzule? Yɛɛ saa bɛfa nane mɔɔ ɛbubu anzɛɛ ewule ɛha ye la bɛba kɛ bɛva bɛbɔ azu bɛmaa me a, asoo ɛnee bɛtɛbɔle munzule? Bɛva ninyɛne zɔhane mɔ bɛhɔhyɛ bɛ amɛnlado ne. Asoo bɛnea a ɔ kunlu kɛdwo bɛ nwo anzɛɛ ɔ nye kɛlie bɛ nwo?”
9Bɛmɛ sɛlɛvolɛma, bɛzɛlɛ Nyamenle bɛmaa ɔ nye ɛlie yɛ nwo na ɔlo yɛ. Asoo bɛnea a ɔkɛlie bɛ sa nu azubɔdeɛ mɔɔ le zɛhae la? 10Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Anrɛɛ bɛ nuhua ko ahɔtoto Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne nlenkɛ ne mɔ anu amaa bɛanzɔ senle wɔ me azukponle ne azo mgbane mgbane. Me kunlu ɛndwo bɛ nwo yɛɛ menrɛlie bɛ sa nu azubɔdeɛ biala. 11Me duma le kpole wɔ maanle maanle avinli ɔvi sɛnzɛne aduduleɛ kɔdwu adɔleɛ. Ɛleka biala bɛkpu ɛyɛlɛ evuanlɛ na bɛfa azubɔdeɛ mɔɔ anwo te la bɛmaa me, ɔluakɛ me duma ne le kpole wɔ maanle maanle avinli. 12Na bɛmɛ, saa bɛka kɛ ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma azukponle ne anwo ɛnde yɛɛ kpanwo ne ɛnle kpalɛ’ a ɛnee bɛgua azukponle ne anwo evinli. 13Bɛmɛ, bɛ edwɛkɛ a le kɛ, ‘Duzu ɛvɛlɛ a le ɛhye?’ Bɛka ɛhye na bɛakpobi bɛ nloa.
“Saa bɛbabɔ azu a bɛfa nane mɔɔ bɛwuale, anzɛɛ ɛbubu anzɛɛ ewule ɛha ye la a bɛyɛ azubɔdeɛ bɛbɛlɛ me a. Asoo medie ɛhye a ɔyɛ boɛ? 14Munzule ɛha nzisi sonla ne mɔɔ lɛ boane nyinli wɔ ye nyɛmoa nu, ɔkɛva ɔkɛbɔ ɛwɔkɛ, na akee ɔkɛva ɛtane bie ɔkɛrabɔ azu ɔkɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma la, ɔluakɛ mele belemgbunli kpole, yɛɛ maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti sulo me.”

english_text:
True and False Priests
1I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something else to say to you priests. 2You had better take seriously the need to honor my name. Otherwise, when you give a blessing, I will turn it into a curse. In fact, I have already done this, because you haven't taken to heart your duties as priests. 3I will punish your descendants and rub your faces in the manure from your animal sacrifices, and then be done with you.
4 I am telling you this, so I can continue to keep my agreement with your ancestor Levi. 5 I blessed him with a full life, as I had promised, and he kept his part of the agreement by honoring me and respecting my name. 6He taught the truth and never told lies, and he led a lot of people to turn from sin, because he obeyed me and lived right.
7You priests should be eager to spread knowledge, and everyone should come to you for instruction, because you speak for me, the Lord All-Powerful. 8But you have turned your backs on me. Your teachings have led others to do sinful things, and you have broken the agreement I made with your ancestor Levi. 9So I caused everyone to hate and despise you, because you disobeyed me and failed to treat all people alike.
A Broken Agreement
10Don't you know that we all have God as our Father? Didn't the one God create each of us? Then why do you cheat each other by breaking the agreement God made with your ancestors? 11You people in Judah and Jerusalem have been unfaithful to the Lord. You have disgraced the temple that he loves, and you have committed the disgusting sin of marrying the worshipers of other gods. 12I pray that the Lord will no longer let those who are guilty belong to his people, even if they eagerly decide to offer the Lord a gift.
13And what else are you doing? You cry noisily and flood the Lord's altar with your tears, because he isn't pleased with your offerings and refuses to accept them. 14And why isn't God pleased? It's because he knows that each of you men has been unfaithful to the wife you married when you were young. You promised that she would be your partner, but now you have broken that promise. 15Didn't God create you and your wife to become like one person? And why did he do this? It was so you would have children, and then lead them to become God's people. Don't ever be unfaithful to your wife. 16The Lord God All-Powerful of Israel hates anyone who is cruel enough to divorce his wife. So take care never to be unfaithful!
17You have worn out the Lord with your words. And yet, you ask, “How did we do that?”
You did it by saying, “The Lord is pleased with evil and doesn't care about justice.”
translation_text:
1Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Akee bɛmɛ sɛlɛvolɛma, bɛ mɛla a le ɛhye: 2Saa bɛnrɛdie me edwɛkɛ, bɛnrɛva bɛnrɛzie bɛ ahonle nu kɛ bɛwula me duma ne anyunlunyia a, mebamaa munzule ara bɛ nwo zo na meamaa bɛ nyilalɛ ahakyi munzule. Nɔhalɛ, memaa bɛ nyilalɛ ɛhakyi munzule dɛbadɛba, ɔboalekɛ bɛambu me edwɛkɛ ne bie. 3Mebahwi bɛ bo zo amra anyunlu, na meava bɛ azubɔlɛ nane ne mɔ ebinli meakpuda bɛ nyunlu, na meaye bɛ meavi me nye zo. 4 Ɛhye yɛɛ bamaa bɛanwu kɛ medame yɛɛ meva mɛla ɛhye memaa bɛ a, amaa ngyekyeleɛ mɔɔ me nee Livae yɛkyekyele la anzɛkye.
5 “Ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ me nee ye yɛle la le ngoane nee anzonudwolɛ ngyekyeleɛ, yɛɛ menvale memanle ye amaa yeazulo, yɛɛ ɔzulole me noko. Ɔte me duma a, ɔ nwo wozo ye. 6Ye ngilehilelɛ le fɔɔnwo yɛɛ yeambɔ adalɛ biala. Ɔ nee me luale anzonudwolɛ nu na ɔbɔle ɛbɛla mɔɔ tenrɛ la, na ɔmanle menli dɔɔnwo gyakyile ɛtaneyɛlɛ. 7Ɔluakɛ ɔwɔ kɛ ndelebɛbo finde sɛlɛvolɛ biala anloa edwɛkɛ nu, yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ menli fa ɛzukoalɛdeɛ wɔ ye ɛdendɛlɛ nu, ɔboalekɛ ɔle Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ.
8“Noko bɛmɛ, bɛvi adenle ɛhye azo bɛye bɛ nwo yɛɛ bɛva bɛ ngilehilelɛ bɛmaa menli dɔɔnwo ɛdu koti; bɛtulu ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ me nee Livae kyekyele la. 9Zɔhane ati medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mese, meye bɛ nyunlu nwoma mɔɔ awie biala ɛmbu bɛ a, amaa bɛagua bɛ nyunlu aze wɔ menli nu, ɔboalekɛ bɛanlua me adenle ne anu bɛangilehile; bɛnea sonla nyunlu na bɛahilehile.”
Menli ne anli nɔhalɛ ammaa Nyamenle
10Yɛ muala yɛ ze ɛnle ko ɔ? Tɛ Nyamenle ko ne ala a bɔle yɛ muala ɔ? Duzu ati a yɛnli nɔhalɛ yɛmmaa yɛ nwo, na ɔlua zo yɛgua yɛ ze mɔ ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ bɛ nee Nyamenle yɛle la anwo evinli a? 11Dwudama anli nɔhalɛ, bɛbɔ munzule wɔ Yizilayɛ amuala nee Gyɛlusalɛm. Dwudama ɛva evinli ɛha Ɛleka Nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye die ɛkɛ ne la. Bɛhɔgya mraalɛ mɔɔ sonle nyamenle gyɛne la. 12Sonla mɔɔ yɛ ɛhye mɔ la, saa yemɔ a ɔdi nwolɛ ɛzonle, anzɛɛ ɔdi daselɛ, anzɛɛ saa ɔfa nwolɛ azubɔdeɛ ɔba Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu bɔbɔ a, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye ye ɛvi Gyɛkɔbo sua nu.
13Debie bieko mɔɔ eza bɛyɛ la ɛne: Bɛtwi monle wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma azukponle ne azo. Bɛsu na bɛdi nyane bɛ nuhua kɛ ɛnɛ ɔnlie bɛ azubɔlɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ, yɛɛ ɔ nye ɛnlie nwolɛ. 14Bɛbiza kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɔnlie ɛ?” Ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma di ngyekyeleɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ mraalɛ mɔɔ bɛgyale bɛ bɛ mgbavolɛ nu la yɛle la anwo daselɛ. Bɛanli nɔhalɛ bɛammaa bɛ, noko bɛ mraalɛ ɔ, yɛɛ ngyekyeleɛ ne kile kɛ bɛle bɛ ye mɔ. 15Asoo Ɛdɛnkɛma anga bɛ ambɔ nu anyɛ bɛ ko wɔ sunsum nee nwonane nu? Na duzu a ɛnee ɔkpondɛ a? Ɔkpondɛ Nyamenle nu mralɛ. Yemɔti bɛnlea bɛ nwo boɛ kpalɛ na bɛmmabɔ bɛ mraalɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛgya bɛ bɛ mgbavolɛ nu la ewole. 16Yizilayɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ne se, “Mekyi ewolebɔlɛ, yɛɛ mekyi nrenya mɔɔ fa anyebolo bɔ ɔ ye ewole la. Medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a. Yemɔti bɛnlea bɛ nwo boɛ na bɛli nɔhalɛ bɛmaa bɛ ye mɔ.”
Ndɛnebualɛ Kenle ne ɛbikye
17Bɛva bɛ ɛdendɛlɛ bɛgyegye Ɛdɛnkɛma, na akee bɛbiza kɛ, “Kɛ yɛzi yɛgyegye ye ɛ?” Bɛ edwɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛka la a le kɛ, “Awie biala mɔɔ di ɛtane la le kpalɛ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye zo, yɛɛ ɔ nye die bɛ nwo.” Eza bɛbiza kɛ, “Na Nyamenle ne mɔɔ di pɛlepɛle la wɔ nienwu?”

english_text:
The Promised Messenger
1 I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will send my messenger
to prepare the way for me.
Then suddenly the Lord
you are looking for
will appear in his temple.
The messenger you desire
is coming with my promise,
and he is on his way.
A Day of Change
2 On the day the Lord comes, he will be like a furnace that purifies silver or like strong soap in a washbasin. No one will be able to stand up to him. 3The Lord will purify the descendants of Levi, as though they were gold or silver. Then they will bring the proper offerings to the Lord, 4and the offerings of the people of Judah and Jerusalem will please him, just as they did in the past.
Don't Cheat God
5The Lord All-Powerful said:
I'm now on my way to judge you. And I will quickly condemn all who practice witchcraft or cheat in marriage or tell lies in court or rob workers of their pay or mistreat widows and orphans or steal the property of foreigners or refuse to respect me.
6 Descendants of Jacob, I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I never change. That's why you haven't been wiped out, 7even though you have ignored and disobeyed my laws ever since the time of your ancestors. But if you return to me, I will return to you.
And yet you ask, “How can we return?”
8You people are robbing me, your God. And, here you are, asking, “How are we robbing you?”
You are robbing me of the offerings and of the ten percent that belongs to me. 9That's why your whole nation is under a curse. 10 I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I challenge you to put me to the test. Bring the entire ten percent into the storehouse, so there will be food in my house. Then I will open the windows of heaven and flood you with blessing after blessing. 11I will also stop locusts from destroying your crops and keeping your vineyards from producing. 12Everyone of every nation will talk about how I have blessed you and about your wonderful land. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
13You have said horrible things about me, and yet you ask, “What have we said?”
14Here is what you have said: “It's foolish to serve the Lord God All-Powerful. What do we get for obeying God and from going around looking sad? 15See how happy those arrogant people are. Everyone who does wrong is successful, and when they put God to the test, they always get away with it.”
Faithfulness Is Rewarded
16All those who truly respected the Lord and honored his name started discussing these things, and when God saw what was happening, he had their names written as a reminder in his book.
17Then the Lord All-Powerful said:
You people are precious to me, and when I come to bring justice, I will protect you, just as parents protect an obedient child. 18Then everyone will once again see the difference between those who obey me by doing right and those who reject me by doing wrong.
translation_text:
1 Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Nea, mebazoa me ɛbɔfoɔ meamaa yeahɔziezie adenle ne anu yeamaa me. Na arɛlevilɛ nu ala bɛbanwu Awulae ne mɔɔ bɛlɛkpondɛ ye la kɛ ɔlɛkɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu. Ngyekyeleɛ ne anwo ɛbɔfoɔ ne mɔɔ bɛ nye la ye ade la ɛlɛba.”
2 Kenle mɔɔ ɔkɛra la, nwane a kɛhola gyinla a, yɛɛ saa ɔye ɔ nyunlu a, nwane a kɛnyia gyinlagyakɛ a? Ɔluakɛ ɔbayɛ kɛ dwinvolɛ senle mɔɔ ɔfa ɔtu ninyɛne nu anzɛɛ saminla anloa ɛsesebɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛkpo ninyɛne la. 3Ɔbadɛnla aze kɛ dwinvolɛ mɔɔ tu dwɛtɛ fufule nu la. Ɔbadu Livaema anu na yeabolo bɛ nwo kɛ ezukoa nvutuke anzɛɛ yeahwi bɛ nwo kɛ dwɛtɛ fufule, kɔdwu mekɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛva nɔhalɛ azubɔlɛ ninyɛne bɛkɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma la. 4Ɛhye bamaa Dwudama nee Gyɛlusalɛmma azubɔlɛ ninyɛne ayɛ anyenzɔlɛ amaa Ɛdɛnkɛma, kɛmɔ ɛnee ɔde wɔ ɛvolɛ dɔɔnwo mɔɔ ɛraze ɛhɔ la.
5Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Mebahwe meabikye bɛ na meabua bɛ ndɛne. Mebadea ngonyiama, awuvolɛvalɛma nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛka ndane mgbane mgbane la ndɛndɛ zo. Mebadea bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛsisi gyimayɛvoma wɔ bɛ kakɛdualɛ nu, bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛsisi ahunlanvolɛ nee nrisa, bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛmbu nyɛvolɛ yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnzulo me la.”
Ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ko ɛdualɛ ne
6Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mengakyi ɛlɛ. Yemɔti bɛmɛ Gyekɔbo abo zo amra, bɛ bo zo ɛtɛbɔle bɔkɔɔ. 7Sumunli bɛ nlenya mɔ mekɛ zo yɛɛ bɛvale me mɛla zo ɛtietialɛ a, yɛɛ bɛnli zolɛ. Bɛzia bɛrɛla me ɛkɛ ne, na medame noko menwɔra bɛ nwo ɛkɛ. Noko bɛbiza kɛ, ‘Ɛnee kɛ yɛyɛ yɛzia yɛ nzi ɛ?’ 8Asoo sonla kola wua Nyamenle? Noko bɛmɛ, ɛwualɛ ala a bɛwua me a. Na bɛbiza kɛ, ‘Ɛnee kɛ yɛsi yɛwua wɔ ɛ?’ Bɛwua me wɔ bɛ azubɔlɛ nu nee ninyɛne ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛkyɛ nu bulu bɛtu ɛkpɔ ngoko bɛmaa me la anu. 9Bɛbɔ munzule, bɛdabɛ maanlema amuala, ɔluakɛ bɛlɛwua me. 10 Ɛkpɔ ne mɔ mɔɔ le me ɛdeɛ la, bɛva bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛrɛla bɛragua ɛleka mɔɔ mesie me ninyɛne ne la, amaa aleɛ ara me sua nu. Bɛzɔ me bɛnlea wɔ ɛhye anwo na bɛnlea saa menrɛbuke anwuma nlenkɛ menrɛgua nwolɛ menrɛmaa bɛnrɛnyia nyilalɛ dɔɔnwo a. 11Menrɛmaa ngɛkɛba ɛnrɛli bɛ aleɛ, yɛɛ bɛ vanye mbaka ɛnrɛkpolo bɛ ndotolo nee ma ɛnrɛgua. 12Na maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti baha kɛ Nyamenle ɛlo bɛ, ɔluakɛ bɛ maanle nu bayɛ anyelielɛ.”
Nyamenle anwunvɔnezelɛ ne anwo ɛwɔkɛ
13Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Bɛheha ɛtane ɛtane bɛtietia me! Noko bɛbiza kɛ, ‘Duzu edwɛkɛ a yɛha yɛtia wɔ a?’ 14Bɛha kɛ, ‘Nyamenle ɛzonlenlɛ le debie mgbane. Duzu nvasoɛ yɛɛ yɛnyia ye wɔ ye ɛhulolɛdeɛ zo ɛlilɛ nwo, nee yɛ nwo alɔbɔlɛ alɔbɔlɛ mɔɔ yɛyɛ wɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu, kɛ asɛɛ nyane bie ɛdo yɛ la anwo a? 15Noko nea, ɛnɛ, yɛfa sonla mɔɔ le mgbanyizonle la kɛ Nyamenle ɛyila ye. Menli mɔɔ di ɛtane la kpazi, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛ ɛtane bɛsɔ Nyamenle bɛnea la anwo dwɔɔ.’ ”
16Na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛsulo Ɛdɛnkɛma la dule bɛ nwo azukue. Ɛdɛnkɛma diele bie, yɛɛ ɔdele ɔ muala. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛsulo Ɛdɛnkɛma na bɛdwenle ɔ nwo la, bɛhɛlɛle bɛ muala aluma wɔ ngakyelɛ buluku nu, ɔla Nyamenle anyunlu. 17Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Bɛbayɛ me ɛdeɛ. Bɛbayɛ me agyadeɛ mɔɔ anwo hyia a, wɔ kenle mɔɔ menwɔha me nwo la. Mebanwu bɛ anwunvɔne, kɛmɔ sonla nwu ɔ ra mɔɔ sonle ye la anwunvɔne la. 18Na akee bɛbanwu ngakyile mɔɔ wɔ sonla mɔɔ di pɛlepɛle nee mɔɔ yɛ amumuyɛ la avinli la, nee ngakyile mɔɔ wɔ sonla mɔɔ sonle Nyamenle nee mɔɔ ɛnzonle Nyamenle la avinli la.”

english_text:
The Day of Judgment
The Lord said:
1The day of judgment is certain to come. And it will be like a red-hot furnace with flames that burn up proud and sinful people, as though they were straw. Not a branch or a root will be left. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken! 2But for you that honor my name, victory will shine like the sun with healing in its rays, and you will jump around like calves at play. 3When I come to bring justice, you will trample those who are evil, as though they were ashes under your feet. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
4Don't ever forget the laws and teachings I gave my servant Moses on Mount Sinai.
5 I, the Lord, promise to send the prophet Elijah before that great and terrible day comes. 6He will lead children and parents to love each other more, so that when I come, I won't bring destruction to the land.
translation_text:
Ɛdɛnkɛma Kenle ne ɛlɛba
1Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, “Bɛnlea, kenle ne ɛlɛba; ɔbazɔ kɛ fonlomo senle. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛmemaa bɛ nwo zo nee amumuyɛma bayela kɛ ewula. Bɛ ndinli bɔbɔ ɛnrɛha na yeayɛ bɛ ngane. 2Na bɛmɛ mɔɔ bɛsulo me la, pɛlepɛle sɛnzɛne mɔɔ le ayile la badudu bɛ nwo zo. Na bɛbavinde wienyi nu na bɛawuluwulu kɛ nlankɛ mralɛ mɔɔ bɛye bɛ bɛvi tunli nu la. 3Na bɛbatietia amumuyɛma anwo zo. Amumuyɛma bayɛ kɛ nzonle wɔ bɛ gyakɛ abo wɔ kenle mɔɔ mebaha me nwo la. 4Bɛhakye me mɛla nee me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ menvale memanle me sonvolɛ Mosisi wɔ Hɔlɛbe kɛ ɔva ɔmaa Yizilayɛma amuala la.
5 “Mebazoa Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ Yilaegya bɛ nwo kolaa na Ɛdɛnkɛma kenle kpole anu ɛzulolɛ ne ara. 6Ɔbamaa selɛma ahulo bɛ mra na mralɛ ahulo bɛ ze mɔ; saa tɛ ye zɔhane a, anrɛɛ mebara na meamaa munzule ava azɛlɛ ye.”

english_text:
The Ancestors of Jesus
(Luke 3.23-38)
1Jesus Christ came from the family of King David and also from the family of Abraham. And this is a list of his ancestors. 2-6aFrom Abraham to King David, his ancestors were:
Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Judah and his brothers (Judah's sons were Perez and Zerah, and their mother was Tamar), Hezron;
Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, Boaz (his mother was Rahab), Obed (his mother was Ruth), Jesse, and King David.
6b-11 From David to the time of the exile in Babylonia, the ancestors of Jesus were:
David, Solomon (his mother had been Uriah's wife), Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Jehoram;
Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, Josiah, and Jehoiachin and his brothers.
12-16From the exile to the birth of Jesus, his ancestors were:
Jehoiachin, Shealtiel, Zerubbabel, Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Zadok, Achim;
Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan, Jacob, and Joseph, the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus, who is called the Messiah.
17There were 14 generations from Abraham to David. There were also 14 from David to the exile in Babylonia and 14 more to the birth of the Messiah.
The Birth of Jesus
(Luke 2.1-7)
18 This is how Jesus Christ was born. A young woman named Mary was engaged to Joseph from King David's family. But before they were married, she learned that she was going to have a baby by God's Holy Spirit. 19Joseph was a good man and did not want to embarrass Mary in front of everyone. So he decided to quietly call off the wedding.
20While Joseph was thinking about this, an angel from the Lord appeared to him in a dream. The angel said, “Joseph, the baby that Mary will have is from the Holy Spirit. Go ahead and marry her. 21 Then after her baby is born, name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”
22So the Lord's promise came true, just as the prophet had said, 23 “A virgin will have a baby boy, and he will be called Immanuel,” which means “God is with us.”
24After Joseph woke up, he and Mary were soon married, just as the Lord's angel had told him to do. 25 But they did not sleep together before her baby was born. Then Joseph named him Jesus.
translation_text:
Gyisɛse Kelaese abusua ɛlɔnwɔne ne
(Luk 3.23-38)
1 Gyisɛse Kelaese abusua ɛlɔnwɔne ne ɛne. Gyisɛse le Devidi angabɛnzo yɛɛ Devidi le Ebileham alɔnra.
2Ebileham wole Ayezeke, Ayezeke wole Gyekɔbo, Gyekɔbo wole Dwuda nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ. 3Dwuda wole Pɛlɛze nee Zila (bɛfɛlɛ bɛ nli Teemaa), Pɛlɛze wole Hɛzelɔn, Hɛzelɔn wole Relam, 4Relam wole Amenadabe, Amenadabe wole Nahyɔn, Nahyɔn wole Salemɔn, 5Salemɔn wole Bowaze, (bɛfɛlɛ ɔ nli Releehabe); Bowaze wole Obɛde (bɛfɛlɛ ɔ nli Wulutu), Obɛde wole Gyɛsi, yɛɛ 6Gyɛsi wole Belemgbunli Devidi.
Devidi wole Sɔlɔmɔn (ɔ nli a le raalɛ ne mɔɔ Yulaya gyale ye bie la), 7Sɔlɔmɔn wole Rilihɔbowam; Rilihɔbowam wole Abaegya, Abaegya wole Esa, 8Esa wole Gyɛhɔhyafate, Gyɛhɔhyafate wole Gyɛholam, Gyɛholam wole Ɛzaya, 9Ɛzaya wole Dwotam, Dwotam wole Ehaze, Ehaze wole Hɛzikaya, 10Hɛzikaya wole Manasɛ, Manasɛ wole Amɔn, Amɔn wole Dwosaya, 11Dwosaya wole Gyɛhɔyakɛn nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ. Mekɛ ɛhye anu yɛɛ Babelɔnoma hyele Dwuda maanlema dɔɔnwo hɔle nlɔnu a.
12Bɛvale bɛ bɛhɔle Babelɔn la nzinlii Gyɛhɔyakɛn wole Hyealeteɛle, Hyealeteɛle wole Zɛlɛbabɛle, 13Zɛlɛbabɛle wole Abayude, Abayude wole Yilayakem, Yilayakem wole Ezɔ, 14Ezɔ wole Zeedɔko, Zeedɔko wole Ekem, Ekem wole Yilayɛde, 15Yilayɛde wole Ɛlieza, Ɛlieza wole Matan, Matan wole Gyekɔbo, 16Gyekɔbo wole Dwosefi, mɔɔ ɔ ye a le Mɛle mɔɔ wole Gyisɛse, mɔɔ le Kelaese ne la.
17Zɔhane ati, ɔvi Ebileham anwo zo toonwo mɔɔ badwu Devidi anwo zo la le awolɛndoazo bulu nee nna, yɛɛ ɔvi Devidi anwo zo toonwo mɔɔ badwu mekɛ mɔɔ bɛhyele Dwuda maanlema bɛhɔle Babelɔn la le awolɛndoazo bulu nee nna, yɛɛ ɔvi mekɛ zɔhane mɔɔ badwu Kelaese ne awolɛ nu la le awolɛndoazo bulu nee nna.
Gyisɛse Kelaese awolɛ ne
(Luk 2.1-7)
18 Kɛ Gyisɛse Kelaese awolɛ ne yɛle la ɛne. Mekɛ mɔɔ Dwosefi yiale Mɛle, mɔɔ le Gyisɛse ɔ nli ne, na ɔtɛnyianle ɔtɛyɛle ɔ nwo debie la bɛnwunle kɛ Mɛle lua Sunsum Nwuanzanwuanza ne anwo zo ɛva ɛkolɛ. 19Kɛmɔ ɛnee Dwosefi le sonla mɔɔ di pɛlepɛle na yeangulo kɛ ɔkɛbɔ ye anyiemgba la, ɔdwenlenle nwolɛ kɛ ɔfa ahane yeahɔye ɔ nloa wɔ ɔ nwo. 20Na mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Dwosefi ɛlɛdwenledwenle ɛhye anwo la, Awulae soanvolɛ yele ɔ nwo hilele ye wɔ ɛlalɛ nu na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Dwosefi, Devidi alɔnra, mmasulo kɛ ɛkɛva Mɛle ɛkɛyɛ ɛ ye, ɔluakɛ ɔlua Sunsum Nwuanzanwuanza ne anwo zo a yenrenzɛ a. 21 Ɔbawo ralɛ nrenya na wɔado ye duma Gyisɛse, ɔboalekɛ ɔbalie ye menli ne yeavi bɛ ɛtane nu.”
22Ɛhye mɔ amuala zile amaa mɔɔ Awulae luale ye kpɔmanvolɛ ne anwo zo hanle la ayɛ nɔhalɛ kɛ, 23 “Bɛlɛra mɔɔ ɛnze nrenya la banrenzɛ awo ralɛ nrenya na bɛbavɛlɛ ye Yemanoɛle.” (Ɔ bo a le “Nyamenle nee yɛ de.”)
24Ɛhye ati mɔɔ Dwosefi vi nla nu dwazole la, ɔyɛle ye kɛmɔ Awulae soanvolɛ ne zele ye la na ɔgyale Mɛle. 25 Noko yeanva ɔ nwo yeanga Mɛle toonwo ɔhɔkpulale mekɛ mɔɔ ɔwole ye belamunli ralɛ nrenya ne la. Na Dwosefi donle ye Gyisɛse.

english_text:
The Wise Men
1When Jesus was born in the village of Bethlehem in Judea, Herod was king. During this time some wise men from the east came to Jerusalem 2and said, “Where is the child born to be king of the Jews? We saw his star in the east and have come to worship him.”
3When King Herod heard about this, he was worried, and so was everyone else in Jerusalem. 4Herod brought together the chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses and asked them, “Where will the Messiah be born?”
5They told him, “He will be born in Bethlehem, just as the prophet wrote,
6 ‘Bethlehem in the land
of Judea,
you are very important
among the towns of Judea.
From your town
will come a leader,
who will be like a shepherd
for my people Israel.’ ”
7Herod secretly called in the wise men and asked them when they had first seen the star. 8He told them, “Go to Bethlehem and search carefully for the child. As soon as you find him, let me know. I also want to go and worship him.”
9The wise men listened to what the king said and then left. And the star they had seen in the east went on ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. 10They were thrilled and excited to see the star.
11When the men went into the house and saw the child with Mary, his mother, they knelt down and worshiped him. They took out their gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh and gave them to him. 12Later they were warned in a dream not to return to Herod, and they went back home by another road.
The Escape to Egypt
13After the wise men had gone, an angel from the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Get up! Hurry and take the child and his mother to Egypt! Stay there until I tell you to return, because Herod is looking for the child and wants to kill him.”
14That night, Joseph got up and took his wife and the child to Egypt, 15 where they stayed until Herod died. So the Lord's promise came true, just as the prophet had said, “I called my son out of Egypt.”
The Killing of the Children
16When Herod found out that the wise men from the east had tricked him, he was very angry. He gave orders for his men to kill all the boys who lived in or near Bethlehem and were two years old and younger. This was based on what he had learned from the wise men.
17So the Lord's promise came true, just as the prophet Jeremiah had said,
18 “In Ramah a voice was heard
crying and weeping loudly.
Rachel was mourning
for her children,
and she refused
to be comforted,
because they were dead.”
The Return from Egypt
19After King Herod died, an angel from the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph while he was still in Egypt. 20The angel said, “Get up and take the child and his mother back to Israel. The people who wanted to kill him are now dead.”
21Joseph got up and left with them for Israel. 22But when he heard that Herod's son Archelaus was now ruler of Judea, he was afraid to go there. Then in a dream he was told to go to Galilee, 23 and they went to live there in the town of Nazareth. So the Lord's promise came true, just as the prophet had said, “He will be called a Nazarene.”
translation_text:
Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma nsa ne
1Bɛwole Gyisɛse wɔ sua ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Bɛtelɛhɛm la azo, wɔ Dwudiya maanzinli nu, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Hɛlɔdo a di belemgbunli la. Nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma bie vi aduduleɛ rale Gyɛlusalɛm 2rabizale kɛ, “Nienwu a yɛkɛnwu Dwuuma belemgbunli ne mɔɔ bɛwo ye la a? Ɔluakɛ yɛnwunle ye ɛwɔlɔra ne mɔɔ dule la wɔ aduduleɛ nehane, na yɛra kɛ yɛbazonle ye.”
3Belemgbunli Hɛlɔdo dele ɛhye la ye adwenle zɛkyele, na Gyɛlusalɛm amra amuala noko atiakunlu zɛkyele. 4Ɔyieyiale sɛlɛvolɛ mgbanyinli ne nee mɛla kilehilevolɛma ne mɔ amuala na ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Nienwu a ɔwɔ kɛ bɛwo Kelaese ne a?”
5Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Wɔ Bɛtelɛhɛm mɔɔ wɔ Dwudiya la. Zɔhane yɛɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne hɛlɛle a. Ɔse,
6 ‘Na wɔmɔ Bɛtelɛhɛm, mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda maanle nu,
ɛnle ekyi wɔ Dwuda maanle nu azuamgbole avinli;
ɔluakɛ wɔ ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ mɔɔ barali Yizilayɛma ati
anlea me menli ne anwo zo la vi bara a.’ ”
7Yemɔti Belemgbunli Hɛlɔdo vɛlɛle nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma ne mɔ ahane na ɔbizebizale bɛ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛwɔlɔra ne vindele la. 8Ɔwiele la ɔhilele bɛ kɛ bɛhɔ Bɛtelɛhɛm, na ɔvale ɔzɔle zo kɛ, “Bɛhɔ na bɛhɔdɔ alagye bɛkpondɛ kakula ne, saa bɛnwu ye a bɛrabɔ me amaneɛ, amaa medame noko meahɔzonle ye bie.”
9Bɛdiele belemgbunli ne edwɛkɛ ne bɛwiele la bɛhɔle. Bɛkɔ la bɛnwunle ɛwɔlɔra ne mɔɔ bɛnwunle ye wɔ aduduleɛ la bieko; ɔlile bɛ nyunlu toonwo ɔhɔgyinlanle ɛleka mɔɔ kakula ne wɔ la anwuma. 10Bɛnwunle ɛwɔlɔra ne la bɛlile fɛlɛko kpole. 11Bɛwolole sua ne anu na bɛnwunle kakula ne nee ɔ nli Mɛle, na bɛbutule bɛzonlenle ye. Akee bɛzianyinli bɛ awɔlɛ ne mɔ anu na bɛhyɛle ye ezukoa nvutuke, ɛyɛlɛ, yɛɛ alufuanlɛ.
12Na Nyamenle hanle bɛ ɛlalɛ kɛ bɛmmasia bɛkɔ Belemgbunli Hɛlɔdo anwo lɔ bieko, yemɔti bɛvale adenle gyɛne zo bɛziale bɛhɔle bɛ maanle nu.
Bɛfa Gyisɛse bɛanriandi bɛahɔ Yigyibiti maanle nu
13Mɔɔ bɛhɔle la, Awulae soanvolɛ yele ɔ nwo hilele Dwosefi wɔ ɛlalɛ nu na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Belemgbunli Hɛlɔdo barakpondɛ kakula ye ahu ye, yemɔti dwazo na fa ye nee ɔ nli nriandi kɔ Yigyibiti maanle nu kɔdɛnla ɛkɛ ne kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ menwɔze wɔ kɛ akee ɛvi ɛkɛ ne la.”
14Dwosefi dunwuele la ɔvale kakula ne nee ɔ nli na nɔe ne ala ɔzile nu ɔhɔle Yigyibiti; 15 ɔdɛnlanle ɛkɛ ne toonwo ɔhɔkpulale mekɛ mɔɔ Hɛlɔdo wule la. Ɛhye zile amaa edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ Awulae luale ye kpɔmanvolɛ ne anwo zo hanle la ayɛ nɔhalɛ kɛ, “Menvɛlɛle me ra ne menvile Yigyibiti.”
Ngakula ne mɔ ɛhunlɛ
16Mɔɔ Belemgbunli Hɛlɔdo nwunle kɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma ne mɔ ɛbɛlɛbɛla ye la, ɔvale ɛya kpole, na ɔvale ye adwenle ɔbubule ɔvile mekɛ mɔɔ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma ne rahanle edwɛkɛ ne hilele ye la, na ɔmanle bɛhɔhunle ngakula mrenya ngyikyi ngyikyi mɔɔ wɔ Bɛtelɛhɛm nee azua mɔɔ zuozua Bɛtelɛhɛm, na bɛli ɛvolɛ nwiɔ nee mɔɔ ɛtɛdwule ɛvolɛ nwiɔ la amuala, kɛmɔ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma ne zile hilele mekɛ ne la.
17Ɛhye manle edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ Gyɛlɛmaya hanle la yɛle nɔhalɛ kɛ:
18 “Bɛdele menli ne wɔ Releema
kɛ bɛlɛsu bɛaye awolɛ.
Relahyɛle ɛlɛsu ɔ mra, bɛkpɔda ye a ɔndie,
ɔluakɛ ɔ mra ne mɔ ɛwie wu.”
Bɛvi Yigyibiti maanle nu bɛzia
19Mɔɔ Belemgbunli Hɛlɔdo wule la, Awulae soanvolɛ hanle Dwosefi ɛlalɛ wɔ Yigyibiti na 20ɔzele ye kɛ, “Dwosefi, fa kakula ne nee ɔ nli sia kɔ Yizilayɛ azɛlɛ zo, ɔluakɛ menli mɔɔ kpondɛ kakula ne ahu ye la ɛwu.” 21Yemɔti Dwosefi dwazole vale kakula ne nee ɔ nli rale Yizilayɛ.
22Na mɔɔ Dwosefi dele kɛ Aakɛleeyɛse a ɛli ɔ ze Hɛlɔdo agya na yemɔ a ɔdi belemgbunli wɔ Dwudiya la, ɔzulole kɛ ɔkɛhɔ ɛkɛ ne. Bɛhakyele ye ɛhye wɔ ɛlalɛ nu, zɔhane ati ɔhɔle Galeli maanzinli nu, 23 na ɔhɔdɛnlanle sua ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Nazalɛte la azo. Ɛhye manle mɔɔ Nyamenle luale ye kpɔmanvolɛma ne mɔ anwo zo hanle la yɛle nɔhalɛ kɛ, “Bɛbavɛlɛ ye Nazalɛtenli.”

english_text:
The Preaching of John the Baptist
(Mark 1.1-8; Luke 3.1-18; John 1.19-28)
1Years later, John the Baptist started preaching in the desert of Judea. 2 He said, “Turn back to God! The kingdom of heaven will soon be here.”
3 John was the one the prophet Isaiah was talking about, when he said,
“In the desert someone
is shouting,
‘Get the road ready
for the Lord!
Make a straight path
for him.’ ”
4 John wore clothes made of camel's hair. He had a leather strap around his waist and ate grasshoppers and wild honey.
5From Jerusalem and all Judea and from the Jordan River Valley crowds of people went to John. 6They told how sorry they were for their sins, and he baptized them in the river.
7 Many Pharisees and Sadducees also came to be baptized. But John said to them:
You bunch of snakes! Who warned you to run from the coming judgment? 8Do something to show you have really given up your sins. 9 And don't start telling yourselves that you belong to Abraham's family. I tell you that God can turn these stones into children for Abraham. 10 An ax is ready to cut the trees down at their roots. Any tree that doesn't produce good fruit will be chopped down and thrown into a fire.
11I baptize you with water so you will give up your sins. But someone more powerful is going to come, and I am not good enough even to carry his sandals.
